provenance.section: Honesty ledger

content:
Captured to `Research/Taste-Profile/sources/`:

- **LCD "All My Friends" = one loop, additive build.** Two pianos play one interlocking
  figure (Steve Reich *Music for 18 Musicians* lineage) and **that double-piano loop runs
  essentially unchanged through the whole ~7:45 track**, with a deliberate slur left in. James
  Murphy's method is **additive** — lock a tempo + a tiny core, then enter layers one at a
  time across minutes; the unchanging loop lets each new layer register. Aimed at the feeling
  of Joy Division's "Transmission" / Arthur Russell's "Go Bang." (`lcd-all-my-friends-piano-loop-build.md`)
- **LCD "Dance Yrself Clean" = withholding, then explosion.** ~3 min of a sparse two-chord
  vamp (bass toll + tapped percussion/cowbell + hurdy-gurdy organ + muted close vocal), then a
  **cued drop** into a huge **fuzzy/distorted synth-arp** wall + full drum-machine groove. The
  build is **arrangement, not a filter sweep** (contrast Daft Punk) — layers withheld then
  slammed in at one boundary; the drop arp is run **hot/saturated**, on-aesthetic for the rig.
  (`lcd-dance-yrself-clean-build-explosion.md`)
- **LCD method = resample the synth for the drums + analog imperfection.** Murphy
  **synthesizes drum hits on a polysynth and resamples them** to build the rhythm track — the
  "Get Innocuous!" kit was built from a **Yamaha CS-60** and sampled back in. Drum sources:
  TR-808 (heavy), TR-909, CR-78, Simmons SDS-V; DBX 162SL bus comp for glue. Philosophy:
  **"analog and imperfect over synthetic and streamlined"** — vintage gear is a small part; the
  *method* (tight palette → resample → loop → layer additively, human looseness left in) is the
  thing. Tyler Pope's discipline: "one drum machine + one synth" (CR-78 + ARP Odyssey).
  (`lcd-murphy-resample-synth-drums-analog-imperfection.md`, `lcd-tyler-pope-one-machine-one-synth-gear.md`)
- **Daft Punk filter-house = one loop, vary the timbre not the notes.** A 2–4-bar disco/funk
  loop (or a short synth figure) repeats through the whole track; the story is told by
  **filter-cutoff automation** (lowpass/highpass opening over a build), plus phasing/flanging
  and **cutting up the loop** into different slices. **"Around the World" bass** = sawtooth,
  filter cutoff low (~2.7 on a 0–10 scale), **resonance high (not screeching, ~6.9 in TAL
  U-NO-LX)**, small env→filter, **ADSR attack 1 / decay 6 / no sustain** = the pluck. **Lead**
  = square, filter ~3, reso ~6, env-mod halfway, attack ~2 = "funky wah-wah." Tempo-synced
  stereo delay (1/8 L, dotted-1/8 R, ~25% mix, ~40% fb). Drums = "dirty 909-type with shuffle."
  (`daft-punk-around-the-world-bass-macprovideo.md`, `daft-punk-homework-synths-reverbmachine.md`, `splice-filter-house-techniques.md`)
- **Daft Punk "Da Funk" lead = distorted, band-passed, portamento mono line.** Originally an
  **MS-20** (distorted filter envelope into the high-pass) or a Juno-106/MKS-80 into an Ibanez
  Fat Cat — reads like an overdriven guitar; melody moves in **perfect fourths**. Recreation
  spec: sawtooth + **GLIDE/portamento ~10 o'clock**, VCA full, filter-env "wah" attack. The
  303 bassline = a real TB-303 acid pattern. (`daft-punk-da-funk-lead-portamento-moog.md`,
  `daft-punk-homework-synths-reverbmachine.md`)
- **Daft Punk vocals = NO single vocoder.** Three families per song: **talkbox** (a tube into
  the mouth modulating a Juno-106 — "Around the World"; Heil/Rocktron Banshee), **vocoder**
  (Roland SVC-350 / DigiTech Talker / Sennheiser VSM201), **harmonizer/Auto-Tune** (DigiTech
  Vocalist; Auto-Tune on "One More Time"). **The rig has neither talkbox nor vocoder** → the
  robot-voice patches are flagged approximate. (`daft-punk-talkbox-vocoder-per-song-bjango.md`)
- **Filter-house grit + pump.** The lo-fi crunch = a loop recorded into an **SP-1200 at 45 rpm
  then pitched down** (juicy artifacts → approximate with bitcrush); the **pump** = a quarter-
  note **kick triggers sidechain compression** on the loop. Pump settings: **attack 1–10 ms,
  release 150–250 ms @ ~120 BPM, ratio 4:1–10:1, 6–12 dB gain reduction.**
  (`splice-filter-house-techniques.md`, `sidechain-pump-settings-house-techno.md`)
- **Postal Service "Such Great Heights" = glitchy programmed beat, NO pump.** Jimmy Tamborello's
  **Kurzweil K2000RS** generated the beeping melodies + glitchy rhythms; sequenced in **Cubase**
  with **NI Battery** kits; FX = a **Line 6 delay** + **Alesis MIDIverb**. Crucially: **"none of
  that [sidechain] on the album"** — the clatter is raw programmed beats + delay, the
  un-pumped counterpoint to Daft Punk. Glitch lineage (Dntel): "every song had something
  broken-sounding in it" — sequence tight beeps/clicks, then add the broken element.
  (`postal-service-give-up-tamborello-gear-musicradar.md`, `dntel-tamborello-glitch-tools-westword.md`)

content:
### Elektron Digitakt 2 — sample sequencer  (3 patches)

| # | Patch | Ref (electronic sound) | Prov |
|---|-------|------------------------|------|
| DT2-E1 | **Filter-House Loop (open/close cutoff sweep)** ⭐ | Daft Punk "Around the World"/"Da Funk" filter-house | 🟣 |
| DT2-E2 | **Sidechain-Pump Bus (LFO-ramp duck)** ⭐ | Filter-house / LCD 4-on-the-floor breathing | 🟣 |
| DT2-E3 | **Glitch Beat under Soft Vox (Postal Service, un-pumped)** ⭐ | Postal Service "Such Great Heights" K2000 clatter | 🟣 |

- **DT2-E1:** Load a 2–4-bar disco/funk-style loop (or resample a VG-800/banjo figure) on one
  track, `SRC` ONESHOT/`LOOP ON`, track length = loop length so it never changes (the
  filter-house rule — vary timbre, not notes). FX page: **multimode filter**, start `FREQUENCY`
  low + `RESONANCE` high-but-not-screaming. **LFO → filter FREQUENCY**, `WAVE = TRIANGLE`,
  `MULT` tempo-synced very slow (one cycle over many bars) so the cutoff **opens over the
  build**; or p-lock/hand-ride `FREQUENCY` for a manual sweep. Add a touch of `BIT REDUCTION`
  for the SP-1200 grit. Send a slap of `DELAY` (tempo-synced). The single signature filter-house
  move. **Ref:** `daft-punk-homework-synths-reverbmachine.md`, `splice-filter-house-techniques.md`.
- **DT2-E2:** On any track that should "breathe" with the kick (the loop/bass/pad): **LFO →
  track LEVEL (AMP volume)**, `WAVE = RAMP` (saw that snaps down on the beat then rises),
  `MULT` synced so **one LFO cycle = one beat** (1/4), `DEP` high (deep duck), `MODE = TRIG`
  retriggered on the downbeat. The ramp's down-then-recover shape **fakes the sidechain pump**
  — the DT2 has no true sidechain key. Set the kick on the same step the ramp resets. **Ref:**
  `sidechain-pump-settings-house-techno.md`, `splice-filter-house-techniques.md`.
- **DT2-E3:** Resample a VG-800/OP-1 **blip/beep** (single tone) and chop it; program a **fast,
  clattery 16th beat** of beeps + clicks. **NO pump** (Postal Service had none). Add the broken
  element: a `BIT REDUCTION` p-lock on a few steps, **conditional/probability trigs** (60–80% or
  1:2) + micro-timing nudges for the Dntel cut-up feel, short retrigs (`RTRG`) on one step. Send
  a `DELAY` slap (the Line 6 / MIDIverb role); keep it dry-forward so a soft lead sits on top.
  **Ref:** `postal-service-give-up-tamborello-gear-musicradar.md`, `dntel-tamborello-glitch-tools-westword.md`.

### Elektron Octatrack MkII — performance sampler  (3 patches)

| # | Patch | Ref (electronic sound) | Prov |
|---|-------|------------------------|------|
| OT-E1 | **Filter-House Crossfader Open/Close** ⭐ | Daft Punk filter-house cutoff automation | 🟣 |
| OT-E2 | **4-on-the-Floor Sidechain-Pump Loop** ⭐ | Filter-house / LCD pump (input comp + LFO duck) | 🟣 |
| OT-E3 | **One-Loop Additive Long Build (All My Friends)** ⭐ | LCD "All My Friends" / "Dance Yrself Clean" build | 🟣 |

- **OT-E1:** Put the disco/funk loop (or a resampled banjo/VG figure) on a **Flex** track,
  `LOOP ON`. **FX1 = multimode resonant filter**, FX2 = delay. **Scene A** (fader left) =
  filter **closed** (`CUTOFF` low, `RESONANCE` up); **Scene B** (fader right) = filter **open**
  (`CUTOFF` high). Throwing the crossfader A→B **is** the filter-house build; add a slow
  **LFO → FX1 cutoff** under it for motion, and **Lo-Fi (bit reduction)** for SP-1200 grit. The
  OT's crossfader is the most natural filter-house controller on the rig. **Ref:**
  `splice-filter-house-techniques.md`, `daft-punk-homework-synths-reverbmachine.md`.
- **OT-E2:** Loop on a Flex/Static track; **kick on Track for the 4-on-the-floor**. Two ways to
  pump: (a) route the loop through an **input compressor** (the OT has one per input pair) — the
  OT factory template even ships "sidechain pumping on every pattern (default 4-on-the-floor)";
  (b) **LFO → AMP volume** on the loop track, `WAVE = RAMP`, synced 1/4, `DEP` high, retrigged on
  the kick step. Pump targets from house practice: deep, fast attack, recover before the next
  beat. The pump is an **emulation** (no true sidechain key) — flagged. **Ref:**
  `sidechain-pump-settings-house-techno.md`, OT patch #? input comps.
- **OT-E3:** Lock **ONE loop** (piano-ish / banjo / VG figure) on a Flex track, `LOOP ON`, and
  **never change it** (the "All My Friends" rule). Build the song by **adding tracks across
  minutes** — percussion, bass, pad — each entering one at a time, muted/unmuted live with
  `[FUNC]+[TRACK]`. Stage the **"Dance Yrself Clean" explosion** as a **cued Part switch** (or
  Pattern change at the next boundary) that drops in a distorted VG-800 saw arp + full kick on
  the downbeat. Build = arrangement, not a filter sweep. Keep the deliberate loop slur in.
  **Ref:** `lcd-all-my-friends-piano-loop-build.md`, `lcd-dance-yrself-clean-build-explosion.md`.

### Akai MPC Sample (AC50) — sampler/groovebox  (3 patches)

| # | Patch | Ref (electronic sound) | Prov |
|---|-------|------------------------|------|
| MPC-E1 | **4-on-the-Floor 909/808 Kit + Cowbell** ⭐ | LCD / filter-house drum-machine backbone | 🟣 |
| MPC-E2 | **Resample-the-Synth-for-Drums (Get Innocuous kit)** ⭐ | LCD "Get Innocuous!" CS-60-built kit | 🟣 |
| MPC-E3 | **Glitchy Beep-Beat (Postal Service, un-pumped + dry)** ⭐ | Postal Service "Such Great Heights" K2000 beat | 🟣 |

- **MPC-E1:** Build a kit of 909/808-style samples on one pad bank: kick (center), snare/clap,
  **closed + open hat in one Mute Group** (closed chokes open), **cowbell** (the LCD/DFA staple),
  ride/perc. **Tune drums to the song key** (Tune page Semi −24…+24 / Fine ±90¢; kick = root,
  snare = minor 3rd) so they lock to the baritone sub-bed. Program a **four-on-the-floor** kick
  + offbeat hats; add **Swing 54–58%** (the "shuffle" of dirty 909 house). **Transient Knob FX**
  on the kick (Attack +30–60%, Sustain −20%) for snap. Pan kick/snare center, hats/perc to the
  sides. **Ref:** `splice-filter-house-techniques.md`, `lcd-tyler-pope-one-machine-one-synth-gear.md`.
- **MPC-E2:** The signature DFA method on the AC50. **Synthesize** a kick/snare/cowbell from the
  **VG-800 SYNTH** (or OP-1) — one polysynth's voices — and **Resample (Pad 11)** each into the
  sampler (resample is silent the first try — do it twice). Tune to key, shape with Amp Env
  (Attack 0, short Decay-From-Start) + Transient FX, then **loop and layer additively** like
  "All My Friends." This is the "one synth → the whole kit" backbone, AC50-mapped. **Ref:**
  `lcd-murphy-resample-synth-drums-analog-imperfection.md`.
- **MPC-E3:** Resample a **VG-800/OP-1 beep** and chop it into pitched beeps; sequence a **fast,
  slightly-clattery** beat. **NO compression/pump** (Tamborello: "none of that on the album").
  Add the broken element with the **LoFi Bitcrush FX** (24→~6-bit) on a couple of hits and loose
  16th-note timing; send the bus to the **Delay FX** (the Line 6 / MIDIverb role). Keep it
  **dry-forward** under a soft lead. The un-pumped counterpoint to MPC-E1/MPC-E2. **Ref:**
  `postal-service-give-up-tamborello-gear-musicradar.md`, `dntel-tamborello-glitch-tools-westword.md`.

### TE OP-1 Field — synth/sampler  (3 patches)

| # | Patch | Ref (electronic sound) | Prov |
|---|-------|------------------------|------|
| OP1-E1 | **Da Funk Portamento Mono Lead** ⭐ | Daft Punk "Da Funk" glided band-passed lead | 🟣 |
| OP1-E2 | **Around-the-World Acid-Pluck Bass** ⭐ | Daft Punk "Around the World" sawtooth pluck bass | 🟣 |
| OP1-E3 | **Talkbox/Vocoder Robot-Voice (carrier source)** · INDEX-ONLY approximate | Daft Punk talkbox/vocoder vocals | 🟣 |

- **OP1-E1:** A distorted, glided mono lead. Engine **Voltage** (AM/biting, "good for evolving")
  or **Digital** for the band-passed squelch; **portamento/glide ON** (slide between notes is
  signature — Da Funk moves in perfect fourths); short filter-env "wah" attack; FX **nitro** (on)
  for the overdriven-guitar grit; LFO **value** for a touch of movement; Octave 0. Mono playing.
  Print to **Porta** tape for the degrade lean. Banjo-as-lead can carry this line via the VG
  (see VG-E1). **Ref:** `daft-punk-da-funk-lead-portamento-moog.md`.
- **OP1-E2:** A bouncing acid-pluck bass. Engine **Cluster** or **Dr Wave** at **Octave −1/−2**
  (saw character), **short DECAY / no SUSTAIN** envelope (the "subtle pluck"), filter cutoff low
  + resonance high (the acid signature), FX **filter** or **nitro**. Sequence a short repeating
  bass figure (the part doesn't change — the *filter* does). Ride the filter open over a build.
  **Ref:** `daft-punk-around-the-world-bass-macprovideo.md`, `daft-punk-homework-synths-reverbmachine.md`.
- **OP1-E3 · INDEX-ONLY · APPROXIMATE:** The OP-1 has **no vocoder/talkbox**. Closest fake:
  use it as the **carrier** — a sustained **Cluster/Dr Wave** saw note — and modulate its filter
  rhythmically (value-LFO or hand-ride) in time with a spoken/sung phrase, OR use the **Synth
  Sampler** to one-note-sample a voice and play it chromatically for a robotic-choir flavor.
  This reproduces the *result* (a moving, formant-ish robot tone), **not** the talkbox/vocoder
  method. Flagged approximate. **Ref:** `daft-punk-talkbox-vocoder-per-song-bjango.md`.

### Novation 61SL MkIII — controller / sequencer  (2 patches)

| # | Patch | Ref (electronic sound) | Prov |
|---|-------|------------------------|------|
| 61SL-E1 | **Filter-Cutoff Ride + Pump-CC Template** ⭐ | Daft Punk filter-house cutoff automation; LCD pump | 🟣 |
| 61SL-E2 | **Dance-Yrself-Clean Cued-Explosion Session** ⭐ | LCD "Dance Yrself Clean" withhold-then-drop build | 🟣 |

- **61SL-E1:** A standalone template/session that **rides the filter** of whatever holds the
  loop (VG-800 SYNTH cutoff via its CONTROL ASSIGN CCs, or a soft synth, or an Elektron FX CC).
  **enc1 → filter CUTOFF** CC (slow open/close = the filter-house build); **fader1 → a pump-CC**
  (or record a CC automation lane that ramps down on each beat = the duck); **enc2 → RESONANCE**.
  Set Low/High to scale; Fader Pickup ON. SL = **clock master** (Tx On) so the loop and any
  synced delays follow one tempo (4-on-the-floor). The hands-on filter-house controller. **Ref:**
  `splice-filter-house-techniques.md`, `daft-punk-homework-synths-reverbmachine.md`, `sidechain-pump-settings-house-techno.md`.
- **61SL-E2:** A standalone **Session** staging the LCD withhold-then-explosion. **Part 1** =
  the sparse quiet vamp (a held organ/baritone drone + a tapped-percussion pattern, low density,
  sustained for ~3 min). **Part 2** = the full drop (distorted VG-800 saw arp + full kick
  groove). Use **Sequence Transpose** / a **cued Session or pattern switch** at the boundary to
  **slam Part 2 in on the downbeat** (the explosion is arrangement, not a filter sweep). SL =
  clock master driving the Elektrons/MPC. **Ref:** `lcd-dance-yrself-clean-build-explosion.md`,
  `lcd-all-my-friends-piano-loop-build.md`.

### Roland VG-800 — guitar-synth modeler (banjo/baritone source)  (3 patches)

| # | Patch | Ref (electronic sound) | Prov |
|---|-------|------------------------|------|
| VG-E1 | **Da Funk Band-Passed Portamento Lead (banjo-as-lead)** ⭐ | Daft Punk "Da Funk" distorted glided lead | 🟣 |
| VG-E2 | **Around-the-World Acid Filter-Bass (baritone)** ⭐ | Daft Punk "Around the World" acid-pluck bass | 🟣 |
| VG-E3 | **Talkbox/Vocoder Carrier (filter-modulated synth)** · INDEX-ONLY approximate | Daft Punk talkbox vocal (Juno carrier) | 🟣 |

- **VG-E1:** Banjo via GK-5 as a Da Funk lead. `INST TYPE = SYNTH`, `SYNTH TYPE = SOLO` (or
  GR-300 for more grit). **PITCH-glide/portamento ON** (the Da Funk slide — moves in 4ths);
  `FILTER CUTOFF` mid + `TOUCH SENS` up = pick-triggered filter "wah" (the band-passed,
  overdriven-guitar voice); `RESONANCE` moderate. `NORMAL MIX` low. Into the rig's distortion
  (MXR 108 / Hizumitas) for the overdriven-guitar read — on-aesthetic. Banjo-as-lead carries the
  Da Funk line. **Ref:** `daft-punk-da-funk-lead-portamento-moog.md`, `daft-punk-homework-synths-reverbmachine.md`.
- **VG-E2:** Baritone JM (or banjo) as the bouncing acid bass. Switch to **BASS mode**,
  `INST TYPE = SYNTH`, `SYNTH TYPE = FILTER BASS`. `FILTER CUTOFF ~50` (low), `FILTER RESO ~60`
  (high — the acid signature), `TOUCH SENS ~40`, **`FILTER DECAY ~25` (snappy = the pluck / "no
  sustain")**, `COLOR 70–90` (weight). Optional `ALT TUNE = -12 STEP` for a sub-octave. Play a
  short repeating figure; ride `FILTER CUTOFF` open over the build (or have the 61SL/Elektron do
  it). The VG's acid-bass is the closest hardware "Around the World" bass. **Ref:**
  `daft-punk-around-the-world-bass-macprovideo.md`, `daft-punk-homework-synths-reverbmachine.md`.
- **VG-E3 · INDEX-ONLY · APPROXIMATE:** The VG-800 has **no vocoder/talkbox**. Closest fake:
  `INST TYPE = SYNTH` (saw/GR-300) as the **carrier**, then have the **61SL/Digitakt send a
  sequenced CC to the VG's FILTER CUTOFF** (CONTROL ASSIGN, CC#1–31 window) so the filter opens
  and closes rhythmically in time with a phrase — an **envelope/filter** robot voice, not a
  bank-of-bandpass vocoder. The VG's `ALT TUNE HARMONY` / `12-STRING` blocks add a harmonizer-
  choir flavor. Reproduces the *result*, not the method. Flagged approximate. **Ref:**
  `daft-punk-talkbox-vocoder-per-song-bjango.md`.

  the user's gear — they used CS-60/SH-101/808/909, Juno-106/MKS-80/TB-303/SP-1200, and a

- **Emulated 🟣:** 16 — **all on gear sheets** (3 Digitakt 2, 3 Octatrack MkII, 3 MPC Sample,

- **Approximation flags:** (1) **No vocoder/talkbox** on the rig — the robot-voice patches only
  mimic the *result* via filter modulation/harmonizer; true vocoder is not achievable. (2) The
  **sidechain pump** is faked with an **LFO-ramp on track volume** (or the OT's input
  compressors) — there is no DAW-style sidechain key on the Elektrons/MPC. (3) Daft Punk's
  filter-house was a **sampled disco loop**; the rig recreates the *timbre-variation method*
  (filter sweeps + bitcrush grit), not the original samples. (4) LCD's drums were a **resampled
  polysynth** — the rig reproduces the *method* (synthesize → resample → loop) on the AC50/
  Elektrons, not LCD's CS-60. All flagged inline.

provenance.section: Honesty ledger

content:
Captured to `Research/Taste-Profile/sources/`:

- **The vocal halo IS a Prismizer/Messina.** Bon Iver's "22 (OVER S∞∞N)" / "715 - CRΣΣKS" halo =
  Chris Messina's custom rig: voice → **Ableton + TWO Auto-Tunes** (one tunes hard, one outputs the
  **tonic**), tonic + a **MIDI keyboard** feed an **Eventide H8000** harmony program that spits up
  to **4 (semi-random) harmony notes**; the sum of dry + tuned + tonic + 4 harmonies = the choir-of-
  one-voice. The H8000's **artifacts/distortion are kept**; on "715" they **"hit it harder for more
  distortion."** ("It's not a thing… many things working together.")
  (`messina-prismizer-22-a-million-chain.md`, `messina-715-creeks-one-take.md`)
- **The Prismizer proper** = **Antares Harmony Engine Evo** run as a **MIDI-controlled instrument**
  (Harmony Source = MIDI Omni), **chords played live** over the vocal → 4 pitched layers, with a
  **LONG glide** (the slur) and **throat-length/formant** per register (shorter = cartoonish-up,
  longer = down). Prism + harmonizer; Francis Starlite's invention. (`prismizer-harmony-engine-recipe.md`)
- **Intimacy = close, dry, layered.** *For Emma* = one **SM57** for guitar AND voice, **stacked
  falsetto layers** to build a self-choir; later records = **SM7**, different distances per layer.
  The voice is **close and dry-forward**, space added later — never a hall swallowing it.
  (`bon-iver-sm7-close-mic-layered-falsetto.md`)
- **Sufjan's banjo** = **Deering Goodtime** (open-back), **played like a 4-string guitar**, mostly
  **fingerpicked rolling arpeggios** (folk, not Scruggs). Banjo leads *Seven Swans*; on *Carrie &
  Lowell* it enters under "Should Have Known Better." **Honesty correction:** "Death with Dignity"
  is fingerpicked **guitar**, not banjo. (`sufjan-banjo-deering-four-string-fingerpick.md`)
- **Carrie & Lowell room** = literally **iPhone Voice Memos** in hotel rooms (A/C hiss left in),
  produced by **Thomas Bartlett** who kept it sparse — the lo-fi capture IS the intimacy; reverb is
  a halo, not a hall; harmonies "echoes of the past." (`sufjan-carrie-lowell-iphone-bartlett-intimate.md`)
- **Big Thief "Not"** = **live in the room, no overdubs, live vocal** (Sonic Ranch; producer
  **Andrew Sarlo**). *Two Hands* is the deliberately raw "earth twin" to *U.F.O.F.*'s spectral
  overdubs. Sarlo: capture-the-performance, **leave the accidents in** (kept an accidental fade-in),
  and **EchoBoy slapback to "mimic my Space Echo"** on the vocal. (`big-thief-not-live-room-sarlo.md`,
  `andrew-sarlo-echoboy-imperfection-philosophy.md`)

> **Cluster tension worth naming.** Two modes live here: the **bare/raw** mode (Big Thief "Not,"
> Sufjan's whisper + iPhone) and the **halo/spectral** mode (Bon Iver, U.F.O.F. overdubs). The
> making-aesthetic tie-breaker pushes toward sustained/degraded — so most patches below build the
> halo/wall, but the **degrade is the intimate "recorded-wrong" kind (cassette/iPhone), not doom
> fuzz**, and CB Clean + a present dry source stays underneath. Keep the voice close.

provenance.section: How the artists actually get these sounds (research summary)

content:
### Walrus QI Etherealizer — the hardware Prismizer-halo approximation  (3 patches)

> The named hardware approximation of the vocal halo. It chases the RESULT (a pitched harmony cloud
> around one voice) — it CANNOT be MIDI-played into chords like the real Prismizer, so the cloud is
> fixed/drifting, not played harmony. RIG-CRITICAL: pad/reamp the VG-800 line level (no level switch).

| # | Patch | Ref (artist sound) | Prov |
|---|-------|--------------------|------|
| QI-TB1 | **Prismizer Halo Freeze Cloud** ⭐ | Bon Iver "22 (OVER S∞∞N)"/"715" Prismizer halo | 🟣 |
| QI-TB2 | **Layered-Falsetto Self-Choir Pad** ⭐ | Bon Iver stacked-SM7 falsetto self-choir | 🟣 |
| QI-TB3 | **iPhone-Intimate Faint Wash** ⭐ | Carrie & Lowell close/dry voice, halo-not-hall | 🟣 |

- **QI-TB1:** Flow **Parallel** (live banjo stays present on top, like the dry vocal). Grain mode
  **Grain Cloud**, Grain Mix **1–2:00**, X **~11:00**, **Playback x2 (+1 oct)** for the bright
  prism-up layer. Chorus **Tri**, Mix **~11:00**, Rate **9**, Depth **11** (the slur/glide stand-in
  for the Prismizer's long glide). Delay Mix off. Space **10–11:00** (modest — Dark Star owns space).
  Tone **~1:00** (roll the banjo ice-pick). Play a chord/banjo roll → **short-press Freeze** = the
  grain cloud loops = a pitched harmony cloud around the held note; play the lead over it. For the
  "715 hit-it-harder" distortion, push the VG-800/Board-1 source hot before the (padded) input.
  **Approximation flag:** fixed pitched cloud, NOT MIDI-played 4-note harmony — chases the result.
- **QI-TB2:** Flow **Parallel**. Grain **Grain Cloud**, Mix **noon**, Playback **x1** (unison
  thickening, not an interval). Chorus **Tri**, Mix **~1:00** (dominant — the "many voices"),
  **Rate ~10, Depth ~1:00** (lush detune = the stacked-layer beating). Tone **noon**. Space
  **9–10:00**. Freeze a sung/banjo chord → the looping unison-grain + heavy chorus = a self-choir of
  one source. The unison-x1 + chorus is the literal stand-in for "stack falsetto layers."
- **QI-TB3:** Flow **Parallel**, **Mix/Dry HIGH** (mostly dry — the voice stays close/present).
  Grain Mix **~10:00** (faint), **Grain Cloud**, x1. Chorus low (**~9:00**). Delay off. Space
  **9:00** (a halo, not a hall). Tone **~11:00**. The texture sits *behind* a dry-forward source —
  the documented Carrie & Lowell "close, dry, space-added-faintly" balance. The restraint patch.
- **Refs:** `messina-prismizer-22-a-million-chain.md`, `prismizer-harmony-engine-recipe.md`,
  `bon-iver-sm7-close-mic-layered-falsetto.md`, `sufjan-carrie-lowell-iphone-bartlett-intimate.md`

### Roland VG-800 — banjo-as-lead + the played-harmony halo  (3 patches)

> The string source. VG-TB1 is the closest the rig gets to the Prismizer *method* — a played
> diatonic harmony voice on the banjo — but it's ONE fixed interval, not 4 MIDI-played notes.

| # | Patch | Ref (artist sound) | Prov |
|---|-------|--------------------|------|
| VG-TB1 | **Banjo Halo Harmony Drone** ⭐ | Bon Iver halo / Sufjan layered-harmony "echoes" | 🟣 |
| VG-TB2 | **Sufjan Fingerpicked Banjo Lead** ⭐ | Sufjan Deering Goodtime, banjo-as-lead, Seven Swans | 🟣 |
| VG-TB3 | **iPhone-Intimate Clean Acoustic Bed** ⭐ | Carrie & Lowell fingerpicked guitar/banjo, Big Thief "Not" dry | 🟣 |

- **VG-TB1:** Recall **GK SETTING slot 1 (EBM5 BANJO)**. `INST = E.GUITAR` (or VIO for attackless).
  `ALT TUNE SW = ON`, `ALT TUNE MODE = HARMONY`, `HARMONY = +1 oct` **or** a `USER SCALE` diatonic
  **3rd/5th** (set `KEY` to the tune's key). `NORMAL MIX ~30%` (keep the dry banjo under the
  harmony). Optional `SUSTAIN`/`SLOW GEAR` for a drone entry. This is the rig's nearest analogue to
  the Prismizer's *played* harmony — a banjo lead with a fixed diatonic voice stacked on it.
  **Approximation flag:** one fixed interval, NOT the 4-note MIDI-played, formant-shifted cloud —
  layer QI-TB1/QI-TB2 downstream for the cloud, this for the played voice. (Builds on VG sheet #30.)
- **VG-TB2:** Recall **EBM5 BANJO**. `INST = E.GUITAR` or `ACOUSTIC`, **5th string excluded**
  (`STRING MUTE 5` / `STRING LEVEL 5 = 0`, keep the real 5th drone via `NORMAL MIX ~20–40%`) =
  Sufjan's "banjo as a 4-string guitar." Bright/clean, no dirt, `NORMAL MIX` moderate so the real
  pluck/finger noise stays. Onboard REV/DLY off. Fingerpick rolling arpeggios — the lead voice for
  the whole cluster.
- **VG-TB3:** `INST = ACOUSTIC` (J-45 / D-28). `ALT TUNE TYPE = OPEN D` or `OPEN G` (circular open
  tunings, Sufjan-style) **or** standard. Minimal/no dirt, `NORMAL MIX` low, onboard FX off — a
  pristine, present, close source. Keep ACOUSTIC RESONANCE OFF if you want downstream per-string
  pan. Feed this into the iPhone-degrade chain (Chroma CASSETTE) or leave dry for the "Not" raw bed.
- **Refs:** `sufjan-banjo-deering-four-string-fingerpick.md`,
  `prismizer-harmony-engine-recipe.md`, `big-thief-not-live-room-sarlo.md`

### Hologram Microcosm — orchestral/electronic wash around a single voice  (2 patches)

| # | Patch | Ref (artist sound) | Prov |
|---|-------|--------------------|------|
| MC-TB1 | **Glacial Halo Bed (Haze)** ⭐ | Bon Iver/U.F.O.F. spectral wash around the voice | 🟣 |
| MC-TB2 | **Banjo Fingerpick Onset-Halo (Strum/Mosaic)** ⭐ | Sufjan fingerpicked banjo → harmony "echoes" cloud | 🟣 |

- **MC-TB1:** Global Config baseline (Stereo in, Line, Buffered+Trails). Engine **HAZE (Granules)
  variation B or D** (the glacial grain-wash; D = +half-speed octave-down for body). Activity
  **~1:00** (density), Shape **~1:00** (slow envelope), Filter **11–12** (tame banjo top), Space
  **~2:00** (mostly wet), Mix **~11:00** (sits *behind* the dry voice — like the faint C&L wash). A
  glacial diffuse bed around a single close source; hand it to QI-TB3 / Dark Star. (Microcosm sheet
  #11 / #27.) **Keep Mix modest** — this is the halo-not-hall move, not a takeover.

  pluck overlap into phasing/cascading runs) **or MOSAIC A** (octave-up harmony loops). Feed
  fingerpicked banjo plucks; the engine chains them into a cloud of pitched copies = a granular
  stand-in for the "intertwining harmony echoes." Filter **noon** (tame 2–4 kHz), Mix **noon** (dry
  banjo lead present). For the brighter prism-up colour use Mosaic A (octave-up). (Microcosm #13 / #6.)

### OBNE Dark Star V3 — pitched halo + orchestral wash terminus  (2 patches)

> Dark Star's dual ±2-oct shifters give two FIXED pitched voices — a hardware echo of the halo's
> pitched copies (not played harmony). Board-2 terminus: Stereo, trails on.

| # | Patch | Ref (artist sound) | Prov |
|---|-------|--------------------|------|
| DS-TB1 | **Halo Shimmer Pad (dual-pitch glide)** ⭐ | Bon Iver Prismizer halo / pitched-up cloud | 🟣 |
| DS-TB2 | **Orchestral Halo Freeze Bed** ⭐ | Bon Iver/Sufjan orchestral-electronic wash around one voice | 🟣 |

- **DS-TB1:** Routing **Stereo**, trails on. **Pitch 1 = +1 oct (L) · Pitch 2 = detune just off
  unity (R)** (a bright prism-up voice + a chorused near-unity drop — mirrors the Prismizer's
  up-harmony + slurred body). Use the **"a in Dark"** off-noon trick to seat unity, then nudge Pitch
  2 a hair for chorused width. **Crush = ~12** (clean — this is the intimate, not doom lane, but pull
  to ~11 for a light degraded edge). **Filter = ~1 (HPF, glassy)** so the up-voice floats; favor the
  **LPF side** if it ice-picks over banjo. Decay **mid-high**, Multiply **low-mid** (no runaway),
  Mix **mostly wet but under the dry voice**. (Dark Star sheet #4 / #6 / #25.) **Approximation flag:**
  two fixed pitched voices, not the played 4-note halo.
- **DS-TB2:** Build a wide pad (**Pitch 1 = +1 oct, Pitch 2 = −1 oct** opposed split = orchestral
  spread; or both detuned for a chorused cloud), **Decay high**, **Lag low**, **Multiply ~noon**,
  **Mix high**, **Crush ~11** (faint lo-fi). Assign **Aux = Hold**; play a banjo roll / VG pad →
  **freeze** → a static orchestral halo bed; solo the banjo over it. ⚠️ Hold passes new notes
  BONE-DRY — that's fine here (the dry banjo lead sits in front, exactly the close-voice-over-halo
  balance). (Dark Star sheet #13 / #24.)
- **Refs:** `messina-prismizer-22-a-million-chain.md`, `prismizer-harmony-engine-recipe.md`,
  `sufjan-carrie-lowell-iphone-bartlett-intimate.md`

provenance.section: Honesty ledger

content:
Captured to `Research/Taste-Profile/sources/`:

- **Will Toledo's lo-fi is a BUDGET-DAW degrade, not a tape degrade.** Audacity → GarageBand →
  Logic on a Mac laptop; vocals "singing or screaming into" the **bundled laptop microphone** (in
  his car, for privacy) — the blown-out distorted vocal = *a cheap mic overloaded by a screamed
  source*, not a fuzz. Guitars were **direct-in, amp-sim added after** ("I never recorded mic-and-amp
  until the studio… always direct input"). He layered "part after part… as big as possible" and
  kept the warts: "I just would really screw with stuff until it started to sound interesting."
  (`car-seat-headrest-toledo-diy-lofi-method.md`)
- **The crunchy-dry guitar tone is a quiet source clipped + boosted.** Early-'90s Mexican
  **Telecaster → Boss DS-2 Turbo Distortion → vintage Supro / Vox AC15 / Fender '65 Twin Reverb**,
  "recorded relatively quietly and boosted in the mix" = "crunchy and dry." The DS-2 "keeps breaking"
  — a cheap, half-failing, mid-spiky, gated-ish dirt box. Bright single-coil + dry (no verb) +
  mid-forward. "Something Soon" (Teens of Style) was **all Toledo's own bedroom work** — a pro mixer
  was brought in *only for drums and bass.*
  (`car-seat-headrest-crunchy-dry-distortion-tone.md`, `csh-something-soon-amps-mixing.md`)
- **Modest Mouse's jangle is a CLEAN amp + bright single-coils + pedals.** Documented direction: a
  **Fender Twin Reverb** clean with headroom (reverse-engineered EQ leans bright/mid: Treble 7 /
  Mid 5–6 / Bass 4 / Reverb 6, vibrato off), **Telecaster / Mustang / Wicks (P-90)** on the bright
  pickup. The lead is **double-tracked → natural thick chorus**; **delay = one clear repeat,
  feedback 0, mix ~30–40%**; modulation (Brock-named **Seymour Duncan stereo TREMOLO**, not lush
  chorus) used sparingly; moderate reverb for space. Bright, bouncy, brittle, articulate.
  (`modest-mouse-brock-jangly-clean-tone-gear.md`)
- **The early "recorded-wrong" sound is a Calvin-Johnson capture philosophy.** *The Lonesome
  Crowded West* (1997) was tracked in ~2 weeks at Moon Studios with Calvin Johnson "letting the
  tape roll" — hands-off, capture spontaneity, leave the warts. Brock's microtonality / odd tunings
  and strained vocals are left raw. Lo-fi by *capture*, not by extreme degrade gear.
  (`modest-mouse-lonesome-crowded-west-production.md`)
- **Anti-precious is the method (Brock, verbatim).** "I quit trying to find my favorite fucking
  guitar. Now I find the nearest guitar… all the precious pairing of instruments and amps is just
  time spent not writing." Favorite recordings came from "shit that couldn't even be tuned" — the
  tuning-instability and warts ARE the identity. His "basic pedals for years = a blues driver and a
  digital delay"; the movement is a **stereo TREMOLO** (Seymour Duncan Shape Shifter, a "must-have"),
  not lush chorus. (`brock-anti-precious-stereo-tremolo-amp-settings.md`)
- **The five signature sounds, pinned to method + flagged for the rig.** (1) bedroom/4-track
  cassette degrade → laptop/fast-capture (rig: PORTA424 + Gen Loss + 424); (2) clipped/overloaded
  preamps → "recorded quiet, boosted" reveals clipping (rig: Colour Box broken-console); (3)
  room-mic'd amps bleeding → left-in room (rig: *approximated* — this is a dry-forward print rig);
  (4) vocals pushed into distortion → cheap mic overloaded (rig: *character only* — no vocal path,
  ported to a string source); (5) jangly brittle clean + odd tunings → bright clean + double-track
  + sparing tremolo (rig: bright edge-of-breakup + Deco doubletracker, tremolo *approximated*).
  (`lofi-prolific-blown-out-vocals-and-warts.md`)

### MXNHLT PORTA424 — cassette channel-strip (degrade terminus)  (3 patches)

| # | Patch | Ref (lo-fi sound) | Prov |
|---|-------|-------------------|------|
| P424-LF1 | **Bedroom 4-Track Demo Print** ⭐ | CSH *Twin Fantasy* / Toledo laptop-cassette bedroom degrade | 🟣 |

- **P424-LF1:** Input Trim **12–1:00** (the breakup gate — audible-but-musical demo grit) · Treble
  **10:00** (shelved down — laptop/cassette dullness) · Bass **12–1:00** · Channel Fader **~80%** ·
  Master **down** to compensate · **9V** (earlier, trashier breakup = the budget-source feel) ·
  Placement **end of chain** (or front-of-chain as the "amp" per K_YEON_J's documented placement).
  This is the cassette half of Toledo's budget-DAW degrade — pair with Gen Loss GL-LF1 upstream for
  a double-cassette bounce.
- **P424-LF2:** Input Trim **10–11:00** (gentle — keep the jangly attack, just add tape) · Treble
  **12:00** (leave the brittle top — do NOT shelve it away; the brittleness IS the sound) · Bass
  **11–12:00** (slightly down — keep it thin/brittle, not warm) · Channel Fader **~72%** · Master
  **unity** · **18V** (headroom — coloration not destruction on the jangle). The cluster's one patch
  that resists the degrade tie-breaker only partway: keep it *brittle*, not pristine.
- **P424-LF3:** Input Trim **MAXED** (~3–4:00 — the overloaded-cheap-mic clip) · Treble **1:00**
  (spiky — a screamed source is harsh) · Bass **12:00** · Channel Fader **~90%** · Master **well
  down** (loud) · **9V** (maximum trash/compression). Run on a banjo/baritone/VG-800 source as the
  *character* of "screamed into a laptop mic." **APPROXIMATION:** no vocal path on this rig — this

provenance.section: Honesty ledger

content:
Captured to `Research/Taste-Profile/sources/`:

- **Swans = no pedals on the wall (volume + sustain + repetition + layering).** Gira uses "only volume
  and sustain" — a Gibson Lucille (controls taped except volume) + a holey Guild acoustic (Fishman
  pickup, thumbed "between a bass and a guitar") into a bass-heavy rig (Orange Thunderverb + a
  **Gallien-Krueger 1000 bass head** + Mesa 4x12s chained). The wall is built by finding chords with
  "potential," playing them **repeatedly**, listening for the **ghost notes / overtones**, then
  **layering sustained voices underneath**. (`gira-swans-no-pedals-overtones-crescendo.md`)
- **Westberg's second wall voice = "a vast, sustaining chordal sound."** Ibanez AS-200 (body
  resonance/feedback) → **Boss DS-1** ("aggressive, grinding") → **MXR Dyna Comp + a volume pedal** (the
  swell/build tools) → Orange Thunderverb. Loud on purpose: the sustain/feedback bloom is a volume
  phenomenon — "like **four church choirs singing at once**." "Bring the Sun" live repeats the same
  chord/beat ~6–7 min into the climax. → the wall is TWO stacked dirt voices + compression + a volume
  swell + repetition. (`westberg-swans-sustaining-chordal-wall-gear.md`)
- **The Swans crescendo is a duration/dynamics event, not a tone.** "Bring the Sun" live: a **drone
  barely audible** (tape loops + gong) → a motorik/kraut **pulse** emerges → instruments stacked one at
  a time over minutes → "warm guitar/bass hum" under "monotonous, **icy stabs** of Gira's guitar" →
  "pulverising, almost kraut-rock crescendo." "The Seer" was tracked then overdubbed for **five months**.
  (`swans-seer-bring-the-sun-crescendo-build.md`)
- **Joy Division's cold/separated space = Hannett's AMS rack + obsessive isolation.** Each drum recorded
  **separately** (zero bleed); kit **deadened**; a **very fast delay on the snare**; the **AMS 15-80S**
  delay "set to some minute period" on the drums; reverb re-amped through an Auratone on a basement
  toilet; **extreme panning** (delay-tails to the opposite side = "cavernous"); **backwards guitar**
  opens "New Dawn Fades"; guitars set **back behind reverb**. Character: cold, clinical, separated, with
  **predelay** so the dry source and the space never blur.
  (`hannett-joy-division-cold-gated-space.md`)
- **The AMS gear names the target parameters.** The AMS RMX16 has **Predelay**, **Nonlin** (the gated,
  abruptly-cut reverb), and **Reverse** programs, and a clean/cold/hard-edged digital character (not a
  warm plate). → aim the Dark Star / QI emulations at **Lag/predelay + cold HPF filter + abrupt/short or
  gated decay + reverse grains**, not a lush warm hall. (`hannett-ams-rmx16-nonlin-gated-reverb.md`)
- **Joy Division's guitar itself is dark, treble-cut, low-gain, rhythmic.** A representative "She's Lost
  Control" Vox AC30 dial = **Gain 3 · Bass 8 · Mid 4 · Treble 2 · Presence 1** — bass up, treble +
  presence cut hard. The documented move: **use an EQ pedal to take away most of the guitar's treble**
  for the "dark, percussive, rhythmic" tone, then the huge cold reverb sits over it.
  (`joy-division-sumner-amp-settings-treble-cut.md`)
- **BC,NR = a chamber-rock build: restrained brittle texture → sudden late slab.** Luke: "It's more
  about the **dynamics** and filling out another melodic space" than riffing. The fuzz is an **Op Amp Big
  Muff** ("Sunglasses" opens with "a blast of fuzz"); stacked dirt = a **JFET clean-boost into the
  Maxon**; "Basketball Shoes" "kicks the door in two-thirds through with **slabs of distortion and a riff
  that nods to Black Sabbath**." Tension/release is the engine — they "shake as if on the verge of
  exploding" then only **half** the instrumental amps up. The 2021 "Sunglasses" adds a "minute-long
  **droning** guitar intro." (`bcnr-diy-guitar-fuzz-dynamics.md`, `bcnr-sunglasses-fuzz-climax.md`,
  `bcnr-basketball-shoes-sabbath-slab-climax.md`)

**The throughline:** all three build from near-silence/restraint to an overwhelming sustained wall via
**repetition + layering + a late dynamic slab**, pairing a **dark low wall** with a **brittle high
voice**, and Joy Division adds a **cold, predelayed, separated** spatial signature. The user's rig
renders this as: a sustained-fuzz wall (Hizumitas/Longsword/108), a brittle/icy texture voice, a
baritone low bed (VG-800), and cold predelayed/reverse space (Dark Star / QI) — performed as a dynamics
arc, never set-and-forget.

### Longsword — op-amp distortion / studio EQ / boost  (3 patches)
→ `Gear/Longsword/presets/Longsword-Patches.md`

  Sabbath-class scooped slab, not BC,NR's exact pedal.
- **LS-PP2:** DIODE up (MOSFET, soft) · Drive ~10:00 (low — JD is low-gain) · Level ~noon · **Low

### OBNE Dark Star V3 — cold predelayed space / frozen drone  (3 patches)
→ `Gear/OBNE Dark Star V3/presets/Dark-Star-V3-Patches.md`

| # | Patch | Ref (post-punk sound) | Prov |
|---|-------|-----------------------|------|

- **QI-PP3:** Flow **Parallel**. Grain Mix ~1:00, **Grain Cloud**, Playback **x.5 (−1 oct)** or x1. Chorus
  Mix ~10:00 (Tri, subtle). Delay Mix off/~9:00. **Space ~11:00 (modest)**. Tone ~12:00. Hit a sustained
  chord → **short-press Freeze** → hold the looping pad as the **minute-long droning intro** under a
  restrained brittle texture (108-PP2), before the slab kicks in. A frozen chamber-rock bed that fills
  melodic space (Luke's "filling out another melodic space"), distinct from the Dark Star's octave-down
  drone (DS-PP3) — run one or the other, or layer them quietly. ⚠️ Approximation: BC,NR's intro is a
  sustained guitar drone into Orange amps; this freezes a grain pad to occupy that pre-climax space.

provenance.section: Per-gear patch tables (the merge step appends these to each gear sheet)

content:
- **The Swans crescendo arc (one player, full board — the arc IS the patch):** *(1)* Near-silence —
  banjo/baritone drone → **Dark Star DS-PP2** frozen bed (Aux Hold) + **QI QI-PP1** frozen grain loop,
  barely audible. *(2)* Pulse — clock-locked motorik 16ths from Digitakt/MPC under a **Longsword LS-PP3**
  drone-bed feeder. *(3)* Grind + stabs — **108 108-PP1** grinding bite + **108-PP2 / Hizumitas HZ-PP3**
  brittle icy stabs over the warm bed (Gira's "icy stabs over warm hum"). *(4)* Crescendo — kick
  **Hizumitas HZ-PP1** sustaining chordal wall + VG-800 baritone, **QI QI-PP1** long-press Freeze → Space
  100% + Tap/Osc snowball → overwhelming wall ("four church choirs"). *(5)* Collapse/fade.
- **Joy Division cold space (Disorder/Atmosphere):** dark treble-cut source — **Longsword LS-PP2** (the
  EQ-pedal-cuts-treble move) or **Hizumitas HZ-PP3** dark rhythm — playing rhythmic stabs (add **108
  108-PP2** buffer-off icy stab for the brittle high) → **Dark Star DS-PP1** cold predelayed/gated space
  (long Lag, HPF, clean Crush, Spread CCW for the cavernous cross-pan). Keep the guitar dry-forward and
  set BACK behind the reverb. Drop a BF-3 gate after the Dark Star for the Nonlin/gated cut-off. Resist
  the degrade tie-breaker — this one is COLD and CLEAN.
- **Backwards guitar (New Dawn Fades):** ringing note → **QI QI-PP2** REVERSE grain (the literal reverse)
  → **Dark Star DS-PP1** cold space.
- **BC,NR "Sunglasses"/"Basketball Shoes" build:** *droning intro* — **Dark Star DS-PP3** octave-down
  drone and/or **QI QI-PP3** frozen pad. *Tension* — restrained brittle texture (Hizumitas HZ-PP3 /
  108-PP2), half the rig amping. *Slab* — **108-PP1** grind pre-stage → **Hizumitas HZ-PP2** Big-Muff slab
  and/or **Longsword LS-PP1** op-amp Sabbath slab, Boost footswitch ON as the door-kick. A late, partial,
  sudden drop — tension/release, not one blow-out.

provenance.section: Chain recipes (putting it together)

content:
- **Documented 🟢:** **0.** No post-punk artist setting exists for any of the user's gear — **Gira uses
  no pedals** (volume + sustain + overtones + layering), **Westberg uses an Ibanez AS-200 → Boss DS-1 →

  and **BC,NR use an Op Amp Big Muff / Z.Vex / Maxon** into Orange amps. Every Ref names the real

- **Emulated 🟣:** **14 — all on gear sheets:** 3 Hizumitas, 2 MXR 108, 3 Longsword, 3 Dark Star V3,
  3 QI Etherealizer. (No index-only patches this cluster — every target unit has a sheet.)
- **Approximation flags (where the rig can only get close):**
  - **Swans wall** — Gira's overtone-and-layering method is unreproducible as a pedal setting; the rig
    chases the *result* (sustain + bass weight + freeze-layering + a dynamics arc). The crescendo is a
    whole-board performance, not a single patch. The "vast sustaining chordal" two-voice stack (Gira +
    Westberg's DS-1) is approximated by 108-into-Hizumitas; "four church choirs" = freeze/Multiply
    (Dark Star) + freeze pads (QI), not multiple live instruments.
  - **Hannett's cold space** — the AMS character (predelay + Nonlin gate + cold digital reverse) is
    approximated by Dark Star Lag + HPF + clean Crush + short/controlled decay; the rig has **no true
    non-linear gated-reverb mode** (add the BF-3 downstream for a literal gated reverb). JD's
    **treble-cut guitar** is a Vox AC30 + a separate EQ pedal; the Longsword's active EQ does it in one

    gets the *sonic signature*.
  - **Backwards guitar** — QI-PP2 (REVERSE grain) is the literal reverse but is granular, not a
    captured-and-reversed take; the Dark Star can only do a swell-in feel (Multiply+Lag regeneration).
  - **BC,NR slab** — the Op Amp Big Muff is a different fuzz than the Hizumitas (muff-lineage but voiced

  - **VG-800 line level into the QI** must be padded/reamped (no level switch — it clips hot). Flagged

provenance.section: Honesty ledger

content:
- **Anti-precious is the method, verbatim (Guitar World):** *"I quit trying to find my favorite fucking
  guitar. Now I find the nearest guitar"*; *"all the precious pairing of fucking instruments and amps… is
  just time spent not writing."* He grabs whatever amp is nearby at Dave Sardy's studio. Favorite
  recordings came from *"shit that couldn't even be tuned."* → capture-over-perfect; the warts and
  tuning-instability ARE the sound. (He used to remove the locking nuts from Floyd Rose guitars, courting
  the detune.)
- **The jangle = bright single-coil into a clean Fender, pedals do the dirt.** Equipboard-listed amp
  direction (reverse-engineered, not spoken): tube Fender, **input volume ~7–8, Treble ~7, Mid ~5.5,
  Bass ~4, Reverb ~3–8, Master ~8** — a loud-clean headroom platform with bright/biting treble and tight
  bass. Brock has used the **middle single-coil pickup live** and a **Filtertron bridge** historically;
  the brightness + attack of single coils/Filtertron into a clean Twin IS the brittle jangle.
- **"Basic pedals for years = a blues driver and a digital delay."** The whole early/core jangle is a
  low-gain blues-driver edge-of-breakup + one clear delay repeat — NOT a wall of effects. Add Pro Co RAT
  for heavier parts.
- **Modulation = STEREO TREMOLO, not chorus-soup.** Brock names the **Seymour Duncan Shape Shifter Stereo
  Tremolo** a "must-have" and a **LEM (Mastro Valvola) stereo tremolo**; he gravitates to stereo configs
  for their *"trippiness."* The signature movement on the clean jangle is choppy/throbbing stereo
  amplitude tremolo + the double-tracked thickness — NOT lush chorus.
- **Recent guitars:** Wicks customs (P-90s), Koll Duo Glide / Spectro Glide 12-string, Fender baritones,
  a rubber-string bass ukulele. Recent rig leans baritone-low and 12-string-jangle.

provenance.section: Distilled (HOW the jangly brittle clean is made — gear + philosophy)

content:
- The clean jangle is the ONE place the cluster resists the degrade tie-breaker — but render it as a
  *brittle, slightly-broken* clean, not pristine: low-gain edge-of-breakup (Kilt 10 Crunch, Oxford
  low-gain shoegaze, 424 Gain-1-low) kept BRIGHT + DRY, banjo-as-lead carrying the single-note line.
- **No true stereo-tremolo box** is in the 8 target units → the **Deco V2 doubletracker** (Wide-Stereo
  + low Wobble) is the nearest APPROXIMATION for the double-tracked "natural thick chorus" + wobble. Flag
  it: Deco gives doubling/warble, not throbbing amplitude tremolo. (The rig's BF-3 / a real tremolo
  elsewhere would be the true match, but those aren't in this cluster's target list.)
- **Odd tunings / "couldn't even be tuned"** = a PLAYING choice (banjo / VG-800 detune / tuning models);
  the pedals keep the dissonance brittle + audible (bright drive, light cassette print), not smoothed.

provenance.section: Translation note (for THIS rig)

content:
- **Guitars:** early-'90s **Mexican Fender Telecaster** (main — bright, twangy, biting highs;
  the cluster's brittle-jangle source); **Squier Mini Strat** ($100 practice); Yamaha acoustics.
  Toledo deliberately uses cheap/light guitars — anti-precious, demo-grade instruments.
- **Dirt:** **Boss DS-2 Turbo Distortion** is the primary effect — a cheap, aggressive, mid-spiky
  distortion that he says "keeps breaking." That half-failing quality (a dirt box on its last
  legs) is part of the lo-fi character.
- **Amps:** **vintage Supro** (Teens of Denial studio crunch), **Fender Twin Reverb** (reverb
  source), **Fender Cyber Twin PR393** (live, a modeler).
- **The signature recipe** ("Fill in the Blank" etc.): **Telecaster → Boss DS-2 → Supro,
  recorded relatively QUIETLY and boosted in the mix.** Result = "crunchy and dry." The *dry*
  (little reverb on the dirt) + *boosted-quiet-source* = the clipped, in-your-face, mid-forward,
  slightly-broken-up demo-crunch. NOT a saturated wall — a brittle, dry, overloaded crunch.
- **Other:** Red Panda Particle (granular delay), TC PolyTune, D'Addario .010–.046, Dunlop
  mediums. The layered-crunchy-guitar wall is many DS-2/Tele direct-in passes stacked.

provenance.section: Distilled

  On the rig: a drive pushed by a near-line VG-800 source (Kilt / Oxford / Longsword) kept DRY
  (no verb), mid-forward, with the *level* boosted after — or the **Colour Box** broken-console
  preamp fuzz (STEP high, PRE-VOL up) which is literally "boost a quiet source into clipping."

provenance.section: Translation note

content:
- **The chain was a laptop, not a studio.** Toledo started in **Audacity** (free), moved to a Mac
  laptop running **GarageBand**, eventually **Logic Pro**. There was no console, no tape machine,
  no outboard. The degrade is a *budget-DAW* degrade, not a tape-deck degrade.
- **Vocals tracked into the LAPTOP MIC, in the car.** Verbatim: "I was using the laptop
  microphone. I would just be singing or screaming into it." For ~3 years he used the bundled
  cheap computer mic. The band name = recording vocals in his car for privacy at his parents'
  house. The blown-out, clipped, distorted vocal = a cheap mic overloaded + screamed into, NOT a
  designed fuzz.
- **Guitars were DIRECT-IN, amp/effects added after.** "I never really recorded mic-and-amp until
  we were doing this record in the studio; I was always doing it direct input." For the laptop
  era: plug straight in or use a preamp setting, amp-sim the tone afterward. (This is *exactly*
  the user's VG-800 → console/tape → print workflow.)
- **Layer to wall, leave the warts.** "I would record part after part and try to make it all as
  big as possible." Density built from many cheap layers — a bedroom wall-of-sound. He kept the
  production warts: "I just would really screw with stuff until it started to sound interesting."
  Starting with *bad* source forced the creative manipulation — imperfection is identity.
- **"Crunchy and dry," recorded quiet + boosted.** On the remade *Twin Fantasy* / Teens-era
  "Fill in the Blank": **Telecaster → Boss DS-2 Turbo Distortion → vintage Supro amp**, "recorded
  relatively quietly and just kind of boosted it in the mix" = the clipped, dry, mid-forward
  crunch. The DS-2 "keeps breaking" (his words) — a cheap, half-broken dirt box.
- **Live tone = Fender Cyber Twin** (a modeler-amp — "a computer with different settings"), which
  he chose *because it mirrors how he recorded* (direct, recallable, no mic'ing). Other gear:
  early-'90s Mexican **Telecaster** (main), **Red Panda Particle** (granular delay), DS-2.
- **The remake proves the point in reverse.** The 2018 *Twin Fantasy (Face to Face)* re-recorded
  the 2011 bedroom record in a full studio — Toledo: the original was lo-fi "due to lack of
  resources," not aesthetic choice, but the *spirit* (layered, blown-out, direct, demo-is-the-song)
  is what fans love. Both versions are the cluster's signature: bedroom-DAW degrade + crunchy
  direct-in guitars + overloaded screamed vocals + dense cheap layering.

content:

provenance.section: Translation note (for THIS rig)

content:

  differently — NOT one patch. Documented stack: **Moog Minimoog Voyager PE** (lead unison

  drift is the wash. Recreate with Prophet-V / Mini V soft synths, layered + chorus/reverb for
  width (Reverb News).
- **The phasing arpeggios** (Jonny singled out Ful Stop for its "good phasing arpeggios," 2018
  Guardian) = **EHX Small Stone V4** on a Telecaster Plus, into **Boss RE-20 Space Echo** + a
  digital reverb, clean Vox AC30. The arpeggios sit in the back half UNDER the synth wash.

provenance.section: Translation note

content:
- **Idioteque:** built from a drum-machine pattern Jonny made with a **modular synth**; he felt
  it "needed chaos" and brought in found sounds + sampling.
- **Everything in Its Right Place:** **Ed cut up Thom's Rhodes in real time** and created
  effects on the fly; the album opens with a **sampled Yorke vocal snippet** laid across pulsing

  uncorrected. Loops are mistreated, stretched, pulled out of phase. **Everything breathes wrong

provenance.section: Distilled

content:
This line — "loops mistreated, stretched, pulled out of phase… breathes wrong on purpose" — IS
the user's making aesthetic verbatim. Direct rig maps:
- **Cut-up Rhodes / vocal snippet in real time** → MOOD Slip (real-time re-pitch/reverse on a
  micro-loop) + Blooper Scrambler (cut a loop into a grid pattern).
- **Loops stretched / out of phase** → MOOD Stretch (Frozen Grain Wall) + Blooper Stability
  (tape-age wobble = "out of phase / breathes wrong").
- **Granular breaks / rhythmic artifacts** → Blooper Dropper (granular flutter) + Stepped
  Trimmer glitchprint; Big Time CLUSTER + 0.5X crush.

content:

provenance.section: Translation note

content:
### Ondes Martenot (Jonny's signature lead voice)
- Featured on **"The National Anthem"** and **"How to Disappear Completely"** (Kid A), "Where I
  End and You Begin," etc. On "Motion Picture Soundtrack" a "synthy choir" = **Mellotron +
  ondes Martenot**.
- Playing feel: a **ring controls pitch with a ribbon for seamless glides**; an **intensity key
  responds to finger pressure like a violin bow**, shaping attack/decay in real time. Greenwood:
  "I've always wanted to play an instrument that was like singing, and there's nothing closer."
- Sound in tracks: "swooping between ghostly strings," "howling in parallel" with guitar
  feedback. A vocal/violin-like, gliding, swelling MONOPHONIC lead — slow portamento, expressive
  swell, no fixed pitch grid.

### Polysynth roster (the wash/pad sound)
- **Prophet-series (Sequential/DSI) dominate** — more tracks than any other brand. Prophet 5 =
  "Everything in Its Right Place" + heavy on AMSP & In Rainbows; Prophet 08 = AMSP. Moog Model D
  for bass ("Lotus Flower"). Juno-60, Voyager PE on AMSP.
- KoG's tonal point: "the most significant factor in a subtractive synth's tone is the tone of
  its **filter**" — Curtis-chip Prophet filter = the signature. (Specific detune/unison/mod
  depths not documented at this source.)
- Suggested affordable mono for Radiohead leads: **Korg MS-20 mini** ("traditional synth bass
  and lead… as well as experimental effects").

content:

content:
Neither artist used "lo-fi gear" as an aesthetic *device* the way the rig does — they used **cheap
gear and fast capture out of necessity**, and the warts became identity. So **every rig patch in
this cluster is 🟣 designed-to-emulate the RESULT** (the blown-out, brittle, recorded-wrong sound),
never a found artist setting. The honest move: chase the sound, name the record, flag the method gap.

provenance.section: The load-bearing finding

content:

- **Room-mic bleed** → this rig is a dry-forward direct/print rig; "room" is faked with tape glue +

- **Stereo tremolo (Brock)** → no tremolo box in the target list; Deco wobble/Wide-Stereo doubler

- **Odd tunings / microtonality** → a PLAYING choice (banjo / VG-800 tuning models), not a pedal
  setting; the pedals only keep the dissonance brittle and audible.

provenance.section: Approximation flags (be explicit in the index)

content:
- **The core is a CLEAN amp + pedals, not amp gain.** Documented direction: **Fender Twin Reverb**
  set clean with headroom — Guitar-Chalk reverse-engineered settings: **Volume 5** (clean, slight
  pick-dynamic breakup), **Treble 7** (bright/biting so single-note riffs cut), **Middle 5**,
  **Bass 4** (tight, minimize boom), **Reverb 6** (moderate ambient space), vibrato OFF. The tone
  philosophy: "crisp, articulate single-coil attack with dynamic picking; clean platform with
  slight breakup, pedals do the dirt."
- **Guitars = bright single-coil / P-90.** **Fender Telecaster** (main for years — twangy, biting
  highs), **Fender Mustang/Jazzmaster** (early/offset), **Koll** and **custom Wicks** guitars
  (Wicks w/ P-90s = the "Float On" lead). Bridge / middle single-coil selected for the brittle
  jangle. The brightness + attack of single coils into a clean Twin IS the jangle.
- **Pedals (verified):** Pro Co **RAT** (gritty OD for heavier parts), **Line 6 DL4** (looping +
  experimental delay), **EHX POG** (octave/organ drones), **EarthQuaker Avalanche Run** (delay),
  **EarthQuaker Levitation** (reverb), **DigiTech Whammy** (pitch), **Boomerang chorus/delay**,
  **Seymour Duncan Shape Shifter STEREO TREMOLO** (a Brock-named "must-have" — the stereo-tremolo
  trippiness is central to his recent jangle), **LEM (Mastro Valvola)** stereo tremolo.
- **The jangle recipe (from "Float On"):** very clean amp, HIGH volume for headroom, EQ leaning
  mid/high (Bass 4 / Mid 6 / Treble 7); **delay = ONE clear repeat, feedback 0, mix ~30–40%**;
  the lead is **double-tracked → natural thick chorus**; modulation (tremolo/chorus) used
  SPARINGLY; moderate reverb for space without washing out clarity. Bright, bouncy, articulate.
- **Modulation, not chorus-soup.** Brock's signature movement is increasingly **stereo TREMOLO**
  ("the trippiness of stereo") rather than lush chorus — choppy/throbbing amplitude movement on a
  clean jangle. Double-tracking gives the chorusy thickness; tremolo gives the wobble.
- **Anti-precious recording.** Guitar World (Golden Casket): "I quit trying to find my favorite
  guitar… all the precious pairing of instruments and amps is just time spent not writing." He
  uses whatever's nearest at Dave Sardy's studio. The lo-fi-prolific ethos = capture > perfect.

provenance.section: Distilled (HOW the jangle is made)

content:
- The clean jangle is the ONE place the cluster resists the rig's degrade tie-breaker — but the
  tie-breaker still applies: render it as a *brittle, slightly-broken* clean (lo-fi jangle), not a
  pristine one. On the rig: a low-gain edge-of-breakup drive (Kilt Crunch, Oxford low-gain, 424
  Gain-1-low) kept BRIGHT + DRY, banjo-as-lead carrying the jangly single-note line, then the
  **Deco V2 doubletracker** for the double-tracked "natural thick chorus" + tape wobble standing in
  for the stereo tremolo. The brittle top can be made "recorded-wrong" through PORTA424/424 print.
- The cluster has no true stereo-tremolo box in the target list — Deco's wobble + Wide-Stereo
  doubler is the closest *approximation* (flag it).

provenance.section: Translation note

content:
- **Tracked fast, live, hands-off.** Recorded **May 22 – June 7, 1997** (≈2 weeks) at **Moon
  Studios, Olympia** (+ Avast! and Jon & Stu's, Seattle). Produced by **Calvin Johnson** (K
  Records / Beat Happening) with Brock + Scott Swayze; engineered by Swayze.
- **Calvin Johnson's method = let the tape roll, capture spontaneity.** Verbatim: "the important
  thing is to get a good atmosphere… set an environment where people feel comfortable… it's a
  special place, let's make a special record." Hands-off, anti-polish — capture the room and the
  performance warts, don't fix them. This is the "demo-is-the-song" / production-warts-audible
  ethos in production form.
- **The result:** brittle, dry, room-y, jangly clean guitars next to blown-out distorted bursts;
  Brock's strained/cracking vocals pushed; dynamics and odd-tuning dissonance left raw. Lo-fi by
  capture philosophy more than by extreme degrade gear — a *cheap-room, fast, honest* sound.
- **Brock on it:** Calvin's presence "gave me a confidence I needed" — i.e. permission to leave it
  rough. The fatigue/resentment of constant van touring is *in* the take (Brock's framing).
- **Microtonality / odd tunings:** Brock is documented for microtonality and unusual tunings —
  notes that sit "wrong" against the standard system. ("Dramamine" is standard E-tuning with slide
  guitar by Steve Wold; the microtonal/odd character comes more from bends, slide, and detuned
  passages elsewhere than from one alt tuning.) The slightly-out, brittle dissonance is signature.

provenance.section: Distilled (HOW the early "recorded-wrong" sound was made)

content:
- "Let the tape roll, capture the warts" doesn't map to a knob — it maps to a *workflow choice*:
  commit a take through a degrade chain (Colour Box → PORTA424 / 424 print) rather than fixing it.
  The rig's console-to-tape arc IS Calvin Johnson's "let the tape roll" in pedal form.
- The brittle dry room sound = bright drive kept dry + a light cassette/console print, not a long
  verb. The odd-tuning/microtonal dissonance is a *playing* choice (the banjo/VG-800 can detune /
  use the VG's tuning models); the rig's job is to keep that dissonance brittle and audible, not
  smooth it.

provenance.section: Translation note

content:
- Jonny's "randomised stutter Max/MSP patch" — **as heard on "Go To Sleep"** (also the family
  of glitch/stutter heard live on There There etc.) — is the most-documented Max/MSP use.
- **How it works (mechanics, from King of Gear):** the patch is always active once open; a
  **random generator runs**, and "when it hits a certain value the patch loops some audio for
  'x' amount of time." Whether you hear the glitch vs the dry signal is decided *randomly by
  the patch.*
- **Routing:** Jonny's laptop sits in an effects loop controlled by a **Boss LS-2** — the very
  FIRST pedal in his chain. He stomps the LS-2 to fold the patch in, then "plays a lot of
  notes to ensure the patch always has information to loop."
- **Feral Glitch pedal** (built by the King of Gear founder) recreates it: a left toggle picks
  **random vs fixed** stutter mode; a second toggle **kills or passes the dry signal**; two
  knobs set **effect time/length** (= max possible length in random mode) and **effect
  volume**; plus bypass + engage footswitches. (Kickstarter, ~$260.)

provenance.section: Distilled

content:
This is the **glitch/stutter** half of the art-rock lens, and it maps almost 1:1 onto the
**Blooper Scrambler (B5)** — jump points lock to a 16-slice grid; CW = repeating sequence,
CCW = **random** (= Jonny's random generator); "lowest random setting" = Skip Protection
(occasional disturbance). The "play a lot of notes so it has something to loop" approach is
exactly how you feed Blooper a dense source then let Scrambler chop it. DRY KILL dip = the
Feral's "kill dry" toggle. Honest: Blooper's randomness is per-toggle regen, not a free-running
generator, but the audible result is the same family.

provenance.section: Translation note

content:
- **Layered/doubled arpeggios:** Jonny played "cascading arpeggios on his Telecaster through a
  **Fender Deluxe**, **doubled them an octave higher**, then Ed added a **third layer on
  Jazzmaster**." Three stacked arpeggio layers = the jangle wall. (Note: the SongProfile lists a
  '75 Starcaster → AC30 for Jonny — sources conflict on the exact guitar/amp; the *layering
  method* is the consistent, load-bearing fact.)
- **Phil Spector wall of sound:** the guitars were "inspired by Phil Spector's wall of sound,"
  designed to "build like a tidal wave" / "crushing emotional weight." Ed O'Brien's own framing.
- **5/4 against 4/4 (Steve Reich phasing):** Jonny's arpeggio runs a **5-note pattern against
  the 4/4** — "two clocks that refuse to agree," a phasing mismatch (Reich-inspired) that gives
  the song its floaty, groundless momentum.
- **The room:** recorded at **St Catherine's Court**, candle-lit 16th-c. mansion, **in the
  ballroom at 3am because the natural reverb was almost supernatural** — the room IS a reverb.
- **Extra textures:** "a xylophone out of the attic"; Rhodes electric piano + Mellotron layers
  (per SongProfile); **outro = a dying ZX Spectrum that "chirps like a broken modem"** —
  random in-key bleeps, plus the sound of the program saving.

provenance.section: Distilled

content:
The "Let Down" cascading-arpeggio jangle-delay is the marquee target:
- **Big Time** = the multi-tap cascade engine. Bright, clean-ish repeats (HiFi/Focus, modest
  COLOR), a dotted/16th subdivision, and SPREAD ping-pong = the doubled/tripled arpeggio
  shimmer from one banjo/guitar line. The 5/4-vs-4/4 phasing can be faked by a delay
  subdivision that DOESN'T line up with the song's 4/4 (e.g. dotted-8th or a 5-against-4 tap).
- **Blooper** = literal layering — record the arpeggio, overdub an octave-up copy (Pitcher /
  Stepped Speed octave-up) for the "doubled an octave higher" move, then a third pass.
- **The ballroom reverb** = Big Sky/H90 hall with long pre-delay (index-only gear).
- **ZX Spectrum outro bleeps** = Blooper Scrambler random / MOOD micro-loop glitch.

provenance.section: Translation note (the centerpiece of this wave)

content:
Three pedalboards in series, signal flows **Front/Strings → Middle/Texture →
End/Time→Tape**. Sources include guitar, **banjo and baritone via Roland GK-5 →
Boss/Roland VG-800** (the VG models/synths the strings; banjo is treated as a
lead voice, not a novelty). Two cornerstones:

- **CB Clean = always-on favorite** — the unity-gain glue cornerstone; most
  signature beds start by assuming Clean is already in the chain.
- **CB Big Time = centerpiece** — minimal chains *into* it; played live with
  OP-1 / Digitakt / MPC. Favor centerpiece + integration recipes.
