content:
Jet-Flange Swell (Tap-Synced)
Device: Boss BF-3

Settings:
- MODE: Standard (or Ultra for more edge)
- MANUAL: 12:00
- RES: 1:00

- RATE: ~9–10:00 (or tap-sync)
- Input: GUITAR IN
- Output: OUTPUT A (mono)
- Pedal footswitch (tap-tempo): Hold ≥2 s → indicator blinks → tap the beat (touch RATE to return to knob)

## Concept

A bigger, more pronounced sweeping rush on the doom wall — the dramatic crescendo jet. Deep DEPTH and high-ish RES make the sweep rise through a sustained wall, and the RATE can be set by hand (~9–10:00) or tap-synced so the swell lands exactly on the song's beat. For builds: let the wall sit, then let this rise through it.

## How to play it

1. Set MODE to Standard (or Ultra for more edge), MANUAL 12:00, RES 1:00, DEPTH 2:00, RATE ~9–10:00.
2. To tempo-sync: hold the pedal switch ≥2 s until the indicator blinks, then tap the beat. Touch the RATE knob to return to manual rate.
3. Build the wall, then engage so the jet swell rises through it as a crescendo.

## Notes

- Rig-tuned (designed) from the dossier's own starting points — not a found recipe.
- Higher RES = output spike; trim into the Somersault.

content:
Stereo Rotary / Leslie Spin
Device: Boss BF-3

Settings:
- MODE: Gate/Pan
- MANUAL: 12:00 (wide-swirl Classic-Jet values) — or Messano's slicer values for a choppier pan
- RES: ~3–4:00 (wide swirl) — or low for choppier pan
- DEPTH: 12:00 (wide swirl)
- RATE: 12:00 (wide swirl)
- Input: GUITAR IN
- Output: OUTPUT A + OUTPUT B (STEREO — required)

## Concept

The "real" Gate/Pan: with both outputs patched into a stereo path, the same mode alternately pans L/R for a lush rotary/Leslie swirl instead of a mono chop. A wide rotating wash on the final stereo wall. Use the Classic-Jet knob values for a wide swirl, or Messano's slicer values for a choppier pan.

## How to play it

1. Set MODE to Gate/Pan and patch BOTH OUTPUT A and OUTPUT B into a stereo path.
2. For a wide swirl use the Classic-Jet knobs (MANUAL 12:00, DEPTH 12:00, RATE 12:00, RES ~3–4:00); for a choppier pan use Messano's slicer values instead.
3. Play a sustained stereo wall through it for a rotating Leslie-style wash.

## Notes

- Currently unavailable in the mono Board-1 slot — needs OUTPUT B / a post-CE-2W repatch; in the default mono slot it collapses to the Gate Slicer (Mono Chop).
- The H90/Chroma do stereo rotary-flange better, so this is a "when a part demands it" repatch, not a default.

content:
Subtle Drift on the Wall
Device: Boss BF-3

Settings:
- MODE: Standard
- MANUAL: ~11:00
- RES: ~8–9:00 (relatively low)
- DEPTH: 10:00–12:00
- RATE: ~7–8:00 (as slow as possible while still audibly moving)
- Input: GUITAR IN
- Output: OUTPUT A (mono)

## Concept

Slow, breathing movement that keeps a saturated wall intact instead of announcing itself — the always-on "flanging chorus" bloom for drone and shoegaze beds. Low RES, very slow RATE, and moderate DEPTH give a gentle, set-and-forget drift over a Hizumitas/Longsword wall. This is the BF-3's most defensible role in the rig: subtle motion on the saturated source, set once and left to breathe.

## How to play it

1. Set MODE to Standard, RES low (~8–9:00), RATE as slow as possible while still audibly moving (~7–8:00), DEPTH 10:00–12:00, MANUAL ~11:00.
2. Build the dirt stack into a sustained wall first.
3. Engage the BF-3 once the wall is already sustaining so it gently breathes underneath rather than sweeping.

## Notes

- Post-punk/shoegaze "flanger all the time" drift (Swans/Mogwai energy).
- MANUAL value (~11:00) is rig-inferred — BOSS leaves it unstated in the source Tape Warble recipe.

content:
Ultra Chaos (Recorded-Wrong)
Device: Boss BF-3

Settings:
- MODE: Ultra
- MANUAL: irrelevant (no function at max DEPTH — not broken)
- RES: maxed (5:00)
- DEPTH: MAX (full CW)
- RATE: 1–2:00
- Input: GUITAR IN
- Output: OUTPUT A (mono)

## Concept

The "broken," metallic, ring-mod-adjacent scoop that sounds like the signal was captured on the wrong machine — self-oscillating against the fuzz feedback. Ultra mode with maxed RES and DEPTH full CW pushes the flanger into its deepest, most ferocious voice. The signature doom/art-rock degrade texture: pair it into the granular pedals downstream for full collapse.

## How to play it

1. Set MODE to Ultra, RATE 1–2:00, DEPTH full CW, RES maxed (5:00).
2. Ignore MANUAL — it has no function at max DEPTH (this is expected, not a fault).
3. Engage against a sustained fuzz wall so it self-oscillates and scoops; feed into the granular pedals to degrade further.

## Notes

- Designed — highest signature-fit (art-rock glitch + lo-fi "recorded-wrong" + post-punk brittle).
- MANUAL is dead at max DEPTH by design — not broken.
- Big additive level spike: trim hard into the Somersault/CE-2W.
- BOSS officially endorses Ultra as the deeper/more-ferocious voice.

content:
VG-800 Pad Rotor Wash
Device: Boss BF-3

Settings:
- MODE: Standard (or Ultra for a thicker scoop)
- MANUAL: ~11:00
- RES: ~10:00–12:00
- DEPTH: ~11:00–12:00 (moderate)
- RATE: ~7–8:00 (very slow)
- Input: GUITAR IN (VG-800 summed output)
- Output: OUTPUT A (mono)

## Concept

Slow flange on a continuous VG-800 synth/string pad. Because a pad sustains indefinitely, the comb filter gets unlimited material to chew on, producing an evolving, rotor-like wash — one of the best drone tricks available in this slot. Banjo/baritone via GK-5 → VG-800 pad models feed the BF-3, and the sustained pad carries the motion under the lead.

## How to play it

1. Set MODE to Standard (or Ultra for a thicker scoop), RATE very slow (~7–8:00), DEPTH moderate (~11:00–12:00), RES ~10:00–12:00, MANUAL ~11:00.
2. Run the VG-800 summed output into GUITAR IN with a sustained pad model.
3. Hold the pad and let the slow flange evolve into a rotor wash; play the banjo/baritone lead over it.

## Notes

- Rig-specific (designed). Indie-folk/art-rock drone fit; banjo-as-lead-friendly when the VG-800 carries a sustained pad under the lead.
- Keep RES moderate so polyphonic patches don't artifact harshly — unless that's wanted (on this aesthetic, the artifact is a feature).

Pure modulated chorus with no dry mixed back in — much more dramatic/"underwater" for a wet-only patch into the Deco. The fully-wet voice when you want all modulation, no anchor.

## Notes

- ⭐ Signature: drone/shoegaze fully-wet wall.
- The dummy-plug routing is the load-bearing "control" here — plugging anything into OUTPUT B flips A from mixed to wet-only.
- CE-1 Vibrato needs no trick (dry already removed).

content:
Baritone Shimmer (Home Turf)
Device: Boss CE-2W

Settings:
- MODE: Standard
- RATE: 10:00
- DEPTH: 11:00 (kept modest to protect the fundamental)
- OUTPUT: A+B wet/dry split (B keeps a dry low-end anchor)

## Concept

Adds classic shimmer to the baritone (via VG-800) without thinning the low end — the gentle BBD top-roll flatters the darker voice. Modest DEPTH so the lows don't pitch-warble into mud. The dry B leg is the low-end anchor — the same logic that makes the wet/dry split better than a fully-wet chorus on bass.

## How to play it

1. Set MODE to Standard (switch left, CE-2 voicing).
2. RATE to 10:00, DEPTH to 11:00 (kept modest to protect the fundamental).
3. Route OUTPUT A+B wet/dry split (OUTPUT B keeps a dry low-end anchor under the modulation).
4. If lows still thin in Standard, switch to CE-1 Chorus (documented as having less low-end loss) at the same dials.

## Notes

- ⭐ Signature: baritone-weight cluster.
- DESIGNED — no published baritone CE-2W numbers exist.

content:
Both at Noon (Baseline Reference)
Device: Boss CE-2W

Settings:
- MODE: Standard
- RATE: 12:00
- DEPTH: 12:00
- OUTPUT: A only (mono, chorus+dry mixed)

## Concept

The canonical CE-2W reference tone — rich, chiming, sparkling classic Boss chorus. Both RATE and DEPTH at noon in Standard (CE-2) mode is your calibration starting point and the go-to for clean rhythm and arpeggios. Hear this first; it's the dial all the other patches are judged against.

## How to play it

1. Set MODE to Standard (switch left, CE-2 voicing).
2. RATE to 12:00, DEPTH to 12:00.
3. For the pure reference, use OUTPUT A only (mono — chorus and dry mixed).
4. For the wet/dry stereo spread, plug both A and B (A = wet/chorus only, B = dry only).
5. From here, back DEPTH/RATE down for the subtle states, push them up for the icy/agitated ones.

## Notes

- Not signature-weighted, but the reference everything else is measured against.
- Bypass is buffered — it always feeds both outs (dry), so the split survives bypass.

Device: Boss CE-2W

Settings:
- MODE: CE-1 Chorus
- RATE: 10:00
- DEPTH: 2:00
- OUTPUT: A+B hard-panned (A wet → amp/Deco L, B dry → amp/Deco R)

## Concept

Boss's own "living wall of sound" two-amp stereo recording technique — deeper pitch modulation, slightly darker character, hard-pan the wet/dry legs, leave a dry track up the middle. The drone/shoegaze foundation feeding the Deco + Board 2. The divergent wet/dry pair feeds the Deco's tape sim two different inputs → free degraded asymmetry (the channels evolve differently under the Deco's wobble/saturation).

## How to play it

1. Set MODE to CE-1 Chorus (middle).
2. RATE to 10:00, DEPTH to 2:00.
3. Route OUTPUT A (wet) → amp/Deco L and OUTPUT B (dry) → amp/Deco R, hard-panned.
4. Optionally add a 3rd dry track up the middle.

## Notes

- ⭐ Signature: post-punk/art-rock drone-wall foundation.
- Numbers are quoted straight from Boss's 2015 session (two Victory amps, hard-panned).

Bright, pronounced '80s jangle-pop chorus for rhythmic arpeggios that cut through — the Pretenders flavor of the classic compact CE-2. Clean, mid-forward, rhythmic. Use the A+B split for the wide '80s stereo spread.

- COLOR: LOW ~25–35% (fuzz already supplies saturation — bring up only until repeats just begin to compress)

## Concept

EQD Hizumitas (or any sustaining fuzz) → Big Time minimal chain: hold one note for an endless ambient/drone wall. Compressed STATE holds the sustaining fuzz together and prevents runaway; Focus voicing shaves highs and lows to keep the muff wall defined. Because the fuzz already supplies saturation, COLOR stays low — too much COLOR plus a hot fuzz makes the limiter clamp to porridge.

## How to play it

1. Run Hizumitas (mono) → **IN-L**, which auto-engages **MISO** (mono-in/stereo-out).
2. Pre-shape the muff with the Hizumitas Filter knob (scooped ↔ thick) before the delay.
3. Hold one note and let the wall build endlessly.
4. Bring COLOR up only until the repeats just begin to compress — no further.

## Notes

- Keep COLOR modest — too much COLOR + hot fuzz = limiter clamps to porridge. Compressed is the safe state under sustain.
- **MXR 108 fuzz variant:** use Saturated + CLUSTER higher for spitty rhythmic stabs the multi-taps echo.

Device: Chase Bliss Big Time

Settings:
- Slot/Bank: Save to a free internal slot via CC27
- MODE: Short
- STATE: Compressed (keeps the dense cascade articulate, Spector-wall glue without mush)
- VOICING: HiFi (or Focus) — keep the jangle bright and chimey
- SCALE: Off
- MOTION: Sine subtle (gentle tape-style shimmer on the layers)
- 0.5X: OFF (this one stays clean/bright)
- COLOR: ~30–35% (modest after Gen Loss — bright repeats, not saturated)
- TIME: dotted-8th vs 4/4 (or 5-against-4 tap for the 5/4 Reich phasing)
- CLUSTER: ~45–55% (multi-tap = the doubled/tripled arpeggio layers from one line)
- TILT EQ: above noon (cut mud, keep the chime)
- FEEDBACK: ~40% (cascade rings on, doesn't wash out)
- WET: ~40%
- TEXTURE: low (alt — clean)
- DIFFUSE: low-mid (alt — a little air)
- RATE: subtle (alt under TIME)
- DEPTH: subtle (alt under CLUSTER)
- SPREAD: ping-pong (the L/R doubling that reads as stacked-layer width)

## Concept

Track-B emulation of the OK Computer marquee — Jonny's cascading arpeggio doubled an octave up plus a third Jazzmaster layer into a Phil-Spector wall. One banjo/guitar arpeggio line feeds a shimmering multi-tap cascade. Compressed keeps the dense cascade articulate (Spector-wall glue without mush); HiFi/bright keeps the jangle chimey — the opposite of the lo-fi patches. **Designed-to-emulate** — no Big Time artist setting is documented, and Radiohead never used a Big Time.

## How to play it

1. Feed a single banjo arpeggio (GK-5 → VG-800); the taps build the octave-stack illusion.
2. Set TIME to **dotted-8th vs the 4/4**, or a **5-against-4 tap** to fake the 5/4 Reich phasing — the taps deliberately don't line up with the pulse.
3. Clock-lock to DT2/MPC via CC54 for the grid.
4. For the real doubled-octave layer, print an octave-up copy on Blooper (see Blooper TB2) and run both into this.
5. Run into a long hall (H90/Big Sky) = the St Catherine's ballroom.

## Notes

- The 5-against-4 tap is the trick that gives "two clocks that refuse to agree."
- HiFi/bright is intentional — this is the one patch that resists the degrade tie-breaker because the *jangle* is the hook.
- Numeric fader positions are designed starting points; on recall the flying faders override these.

Settings:
- Slot/Bank: Save to a free internal slot via CC27; recall by PC on DT2 pattern change
- MODE: Short
- STATE: Compressed (punchy, articulate in a dense mix)
- VOICING: Focus (or Warm for darker)

- MOTION: Off (or Sine subtle)
- 0.5X: ON (built-in lo-fi crush)
- COLOR: ~40%
- TIME: MIDI clock (slave) — subdivision via CC54
- CLUSTER: ~⅓–½ (multi-tap pattern = the groove)
- TILT EQ: slightly up
- FEEDBACK: ~35% (articulate, not washy)
- WET: ~40%
- TEXTURE: ~40% (alt — gentle comp)
- DIFFUSE: low (alt under FEEDBACK)
- SPREAD: widen (or ping-pong for the added taps)

## Concept

A clock-locked multi-tap groove — the body of a song carried on one delay. Slaved to DT2/MPC MIDI clock, with CLUSTER set as the "free arrangement" fader generating the multi-tap rhythmic pattern. Compressed STATE keeps the taps punchy and articulate in a dense mix; the 0.5X crush supplies the lo-fi color.

## How to play it

1. Slave to MIDI clock: set **CC111 = 0** (clock ignore off, so the pedal follows).
2. Set the subdivision via **CC54** (dotted-8th / 16th), or use Options → hold SCALE → TIME.
3. Dial CLUSTER to ⅓–½ to set the multi-tap pattern — this is the groove.
4. P-lock COLOR/TIME/etc. via **CC14–19** from the DT2 for grid-quantized moves on pattern changes.
5. Save to a free internal slot via CC27 and recall by PC when the DT2 pattern changes.

## Notes

- Compressed keeps the multi-taps punchy; CLUSTER is the "free arrangement" fader here.
- ⚠️ MPC Sample distorts when slaved on fw 1.2.1 — run MPC as master (Big Time follows) or verify the 1.3.x fix.

Device: Chase Bliss Big Time

Settings:
- Slot/Bank: Save to a free internal slot via CC27
- MODE: Long (long musical trails behind the lead)
- STATE: Compressed (sagging trails that react to playing — duck under attack, bloom after)
- VOICING: Focus (defined, vocal-like)
- SCALE: Off
- MOTION: Sine slow + shallow (vibrato/shimmer on the tails, the Ondes' bowed swell)
- 0.5X: OFF
- COLOR: ~35%
- TIME: long (musical, dotted or quarter)
- CLUSTER: low (~15% — clean single repeats, the line is the melody)
- TILT EQ: noon → up (keep the lead present)
- FEEDBACK: ~50% (long singing trails)
- WET: ~40%
- TEXTURE: ~50% (alt — Compressed ducking, trails get out of the way of the attack)
- DIFFUSE: low (alt under FEEDBACK)
- SPREAD: widen

## Concept

Track-B emulation of Jonny's Ondes-Martenot lead voice (Kid A: "How to Disappear Completely," "The National Anthem") translated to the banjo-as-lead — a gliding, swelling, singing single-note line over clean sustaining repeats. The Ondes is monophonic and voice-like, so CLUSTER stays low and the Compressed trails breathe around a single line, ducking under the attack and blooming after. **Designed-to-emulate** — no Big Time artist setting is documented, and Radiohead never used a Big Time.

## How to play it

1. Keep CLUSTER low (~15%) — clean single repeats; the *line* is the melody.
2. Pair with **CB Clean's Dynamic Volume Swell** so the banjo pluck swells in like the Ondes' intensity key.
3. Add portamento/glide on the VG-800 for the ribbon-glide character.
4. Let the long Compressed trails duck under the attack and bloom in the gaps.

## Notes

- The glide + swell come from upstream (VG-800 portamento + Clean swell); Big Time supplies the long, ducking, singing tail.
- MOTION Sine slow + shallow adds the vibrato/shimmer evoking the Ondes' bowed swell.
- Numeric fader positions are designed starting points; on recall the flying faders override these.

content:
One-Stomp Climax
Device: Chase Bliss Big Time

Settings:
- Slot/Bank: Save to a free internal slot via CC27
- MODE: Long (OVERLOAD only works in Long)
- STATE: Saturated
- VOICING: Analog
- SCALE: Off
- MOTION: Sine slow
- COLOR: ~35% (headroom so the ramp has somewhere to go)
- TIME: long
- CLUSTER: ~50%
- TILT EQ: pushed DOWN (boost lows → longer/louder tails feeding the climb)
- FEEDBACK: ~55% (base) — the ramp takes it to max
- WET: set conservatively (the ramp is scary loud)
- DIFFUSE: high (alt under FEEDBACK)
- TEXTURE: mid (alt under COLOR)
- SPREAD: widen
- RIGHT footswitch (hold): OVERLOAD — ramps COLOR+FEEDBACK toward max into a wall; release to fall back
- MODE button (hold): Panic reset to a clean simple delay (safety net)

## Concept

The build/drop on one footswitch: hold the RIGHT footswitch in Long mode and the **OVERLOAD** ramp drives COLOR and FEEDBACK toward max, detonating a part's climax into a wall; release to collapse. COLOR and FEEDBACK sit with headroom so the ramp has somewhere to go, and TILT EQ is pushed down to boost lows that feed the climb.

## How to play it

1. Set the base state (MODE Long — OVERLOAD only works in Long).
2. At the climax, **hold the RIGHT footswitch** → OVERLOAD ramps COLOR+FEEDBACK toward max into a wall.
3. Release to fall back / collapse.
4. Safety: hold the **MODE button** to panic-reset to a clean simple delay if it gets out of hand.

## Notes

- The manual warns "beware volume levels" twice — set WET low before this.
- The hold-MODE clean reset is your safety net out of the chaos.

- Compressed STATE = the "safe" self-oscillation state (it holds itself together).

content:
Accumulator / "mixed eras"
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD
- STABILITY: mild — just off minimum (cumulative aging); moderate ≈ analog feel
- REPEATS: ~11–1 o'clock (pulled back so old layers fade)
- MOD A: optional Dropper (A2)
- MOD B: optional Scrambler (B5) for more adventurous results
- Slot/Bank: STABILITY (either bank) + optional Dropper A2 / Scrambler B5 · MIDI PC 1

## Concept


A loop that ages like a tape machine wearing out in real time. Vintage layers wobble and decay underneath while clear new playing pops fresh on top — the rig's signature degraded wall. The advantage over Frippertronics: you keep playing fresh notes that appear clean while the bed rots.

## How to play it


1. In ADD mode, record a clean loop with STABILITY off as a reference.
2. Turn STABILITY up — mild (just off minimum) for cumulative aging, moderate for an "analog feel."
3. Keep overdubbing. Each additive pass ages more than the last: older layers wobble, lose highs, and get noisier while new layers pop fresh.
4. Pair with REPEATS pulled back (~11–1 o'clock) so old layers fade, giving a continuous time-shift.
5. For something more adventurous, bring in Scrambler.

## Notes


- Use the BLIP Stability slider (see Setup: Additive Assist + Stability slider) to keep flutter and dial out white noise.
- The honest workflow advantage: fresh notes appear clean while the bed disintegrates.

content:
All Slow — NORM half-speed bed under live playing
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: NORM (speed is NOT baked into the dry signal — the looped bed + its overdubs play at half-speed, live playing stays full speed)
- MOD B: HALF-SPEED step (one octave down via the speed step) — documented setting; finer values dial from recipe
- MOD B slot: B4 Stepped Speed (default bank)
- MOD B engage: arcade button — engage Stepped Speed at half-speed
- Slot/Bank: MOD B4 default bank · MIDI PC 3 (Stepped-Speed family) · dial other knobs from recipe (no published values)

## Concept


Record a loop, engage Stepped Speed at half-speed, then begin overdubbing in NORM — everything in the loop, including your new overdubs, plays back at half-speed while your live playing up front stays full speed. Build a slow, doom-y soundscape over time under a live, full-speed banjo/baritone lead. This is behaviour unique to Blooper: in NORM the half-speed is not committed to the dry signal, so the bed ages and slows while your hands stay in real time.

## How to play it


1. Record a loop in NORM.
2. Set MOD B to Stepped Speed (B4) and engage it at half-speed.
3. Begin overdubbing — the bed AND your new overdubs play back at half-speed, but your live playing stays full speed.
4. Build up a slow, doom-y soundscape under a live, full-speed banjo/baritone lead.

## Notes


- Unique-to-Blooper behavior per the official Recording-with-Modifiers guide.
- Because Stepped Speed is time-based, overdubbed audio still lands in unexpected places (head disconnect) — embrace it, or turn the modifier off before precise overdubs.
- Half-speed is the documented setting; finer values dial from recipe.
- Great doom fit: full-speed live over a half-speed aged bed (relates to Daydreaming, but in NORM rather than ADD).
- Honesty flag: half-speed is the documented step — the other knob positions are not published and dial from this recipe.

Turn a held banjo or baritone tone into a synth-style arpeggiated sequence. A ramped Stepped Speed with WIGGLE keeps the pitch range tight and controlled, while SYNC keeps the movement consistent and locked to the loop — a single root note becomes an arpeggiated sequence, hands-free.

2. Set the ramping dips to MOD B + BOUNCE + SYNC + WIGGLE.
3. WIGGLE keeps the pitch range tight/controlled; SYNC keeps the movement consistent and locked to the loop.
4. Hold a banjo root tone and let it arpeggiate.

## Notes


- Single banjo root becomes an arpeggiated sequence, hands-free.
- Sync to the Digitakt for tempo-locked arps.
- Dip switches are physical-only.

Instant doom thickness on a sustained baritone chord. Stepped Speed quantizes to octaves and fifths, so an octave-down setting drops sub-drones tuned beneath the chord — no second instrument needed. Blippertronics / Frippertronics fade-looping
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

- REPEATS: fairly HIGH (all layers subtly fade) → all the way up (max) to LOCK (nothing fades)

## Concept


An endless evolving ambient base — a slowly evolving sustained-loop meditation that breaks up repetition. With REPEATS fairly high, all layers subtly fade so the loop always shifts and moves; once you've built a nice ambient base, max REPEATS to lock it. The "old classic" Frippertronics voice, hands-free.

## How to play it


1. In NORM, build a delay-style base — tap the RECORD footswitch like tap-tempo into the overdubbing state, with a nice long delay time.
2. Set REPEATS fairly HIGH so all layers subtly fade — it always shifts and moves.
3. Improvise over it (bad notes fade away).
4. Once you've built a nice ambient base, turn REPEATS all the way up (max) to LOCK it — nothing fades.

## Notes


- The "old classic" Frippertronics voice — exactly this rig's sustained-wall aesthetic, hands-free.

content:
Build-A-Break — Stepped Trimmer intro/build-up
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- MOD A slot: A3 Stepped Trimmer (default bank)
- MOD A: step off noon — CCW toward 'start 1/32', CW toward 'end 1/32' — to trim in subdivisions (dial by ear, no published value)
- MOD A engage: arcade button; tap on to commit the shortened loop, or move/ramp the knob live to rearrange
- Mode: NORM to audition the shortened loop, ADD to commit
- Slot/Bank: MOD A3 default bank · other knobs dial from recipe (no published values)

## Concept


Stepped Trimmer shortens the loop in musical subdivisions, down to 1/32 steps — an effect similar to shortening a sequence. As the loop tightens into a shorter, more urgent figure it makes a great intro or build-up: trim it down a step at a time to drive energy before the full loop drops back in.

## How to play it


1. Build a loop, then set MOD A to Stepped Trimmer (A3, default bank).
2. Step the knob off noon to trim the loop down in 1/32 subdivisions — CCW toward 'start 1/32', CW toward 'end 1/32'.
3. Use the progressively shorter loop as an intro/build-up — tighten it to drive energy.
4. Manually moving or ramping the knob lets you rearrange/remix the loop on the fly.

## Notes


- Stepped Trimmer's steps are quantized to musical subdivisions, so the result stays rhythmically coherent.
- When using Blooper as a delay, treat Stepped Trimmer like a tap-tempo subdivision control (see Strange Subdivisions).
- Exact knob positions are not published — this is a dialable recipe; dial in the subdivision you want by ear, and the other knobs are dialed from the recipe rather than from published values.

content:
Busy Bee — Stretcher relaxes a busy loop
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: NORM to audition, ADD to commit
- MOD B slot: B4 Stretcher (ALT bank — requires BANK B dip, or load via BLIP)
- MOD B: CCW from noon to slow the loop (up to 4x slower, pitch unchanged) — no published clock positions
- MOD B engage: arcade button — engage Stretcher
- Slot/Bank: MOD B4 ALT bank (BANK B dip or BLIP load) — dialable recipe, no published values

## Concept


Record a deliberately busy, dense loop, then reach for Stretcher — the alt-bank, pitch-independent stretch added in v3.0. Turning the knob counterclockwise from noon slows the loop down (up to 4x slower) while the pitch stays put, so it relaxes rather than detunes. The slowed timing redefines the relationships between the sounds within the loop, opening up "the whole universe of sound between the notes."

## How to play it


1. Record a deliberately busy, dense loop.
2. Engage BANK B and set MOD B to Stretcher (B4), or load Stretcher via BLIP.
3. Turn the knob counterclockwise from noon to slow the loop down (up to 4x slower) — pitch stays put, so it relaxes rather than detunes.
4. Notice how the slowed timing redefines the relationships between the sounds; layer fresh playing over the relaxed bed.
5. Audition in NORM, then switch to ADD to commit the stretched bed.

## Notes


- Stretcher decouples time from pitch (v3.0 feature) — CCW slows up to 4x without dropping the pitch.
- DSP-heavy: mutually exclusive with Pitcher and the Speed modifiers (except reverse). Plan one per loop.
- Pair with Filter to tame the ring-mod artifacts Stretcher can introduce.
- Requires the BANK B dip (or a BLIP load) to reach Stretcher in the alt bank.
- Honesty flag: exact knob clock positions are not published — knob travel beyond "4x slower" dials from this recipe, set by ear.

- MOD A: modifiers + Stability still work in SAMP (e.g. Trimmer so just a sliver plays per trigger)

## Concept


Turn a built-up multi-layer loop into a retriggerable sample alongside the OP-1/Octatrack (benches the CB Onward). Build a complex loop in NORM or ADD, then switch to SAMP — the loop carries over and becomes triggerable, with effects still applied (which is unique to Blooper).

## How to play it


1. Build a complex multi-layer loop in NORM or ADD first.
2. Switch the mode toggle to SAMP — the loop carries over.
3. Trigger with the RIGHT footswitch; hold RIGHT to toggle loop vs one-shot (right LED green = one-shot).
4. Modifiers and Stability still work in SAMP — e.g. set Trimmer so just a sliver plays per trigger.

## Notes


- WARNING: Do NOT tap the RECORD (LEFT) footswitch in SAMP — it instantly wipes everything.
- The bridge that lets a Blooper wall become a triggerable sample with the hardware samplers.
- Save the built wall to a MIDI PC slot before performing.

## Concept


Build a strummed chord from a single banjo or baritone root note — no second instrument. Chromatic Speed is quantized to the chromatic scale (always in key), so you can record a loop of root notes and punch in transposed intervals to turn one root into a chord. The single most rig-defining harmony move.

## How to play it


1. In ADD mode, set MOD A to Chromatic Speed (ALT bank A1) — requires the BANK A dip.
2. Record a loop of all root notes.
3. Punch in transposed intervals at different spots — a major 3rd, a 5th, an octave down, and backwards.
4. Use one-shot/punch-in for clean placement.
5. The single-root sequence transforms into strumming through a chord.

## Notes


- Requires firmware v3.0+ (current v3.2) for the ALT bank.
- BANK dip is physical-only, not MIDI-addressable.

Loops that arm and start on the next clock pulse and never drift off the Digitakt 2 clock. When following clock, pressing RECORD arms Blooper — it waits for the next pulse to start, and playback is also synced so there's no phasing.

content:
Clumped Chords — Stepped Speed remixes a loop into chords
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD
- MOD B: adjust speed steps while recording (CW = forward, CCW = reverse) — dialable, no published clock positions
- MOD B slot: B4 Stepped Speed (default bank — quantized to octaves/fifths)
- MOD B engage: arcade button — engage Stepped Speed moves
- Slot/Bank: MOD B4 default bank · MIDI PC 3 (Stepped-Speed family)

## Concept


Adjusting Stepped Speed during Additive recording reconfigures the loop into what sounds like chords — extending, shrinking, and repeating sections along the way. A single melodic loop becomes a clustered, chordal remix of itself, staying in key because the steps land on octaves and fifths.

## How to play it


1. Record a loop with some note/chord movement (a single note or short phrase also works).
2. Set MOD B to Stepped Speed (B4) and enter ADD mode.
3. While overdubbing, step the speed up and down — the loop reconfigures into chord-like clumps as sections extend, shrink and repeat.
4. Because Stepped Speed is quantized to octaves and fifths, the result stays in key.

## Notes


- ADD mode is essential — the speed moves get baked into the loop.
- Stepped Speed is time-based, so the fixed-loop-length rule applies — slowing past the container loses content, speeding repeats it within the container.
- Different from Chord-from-one-root (Chromatic Speed punch-ins) — this is continuous octave/fifth speed remixing rather than chromatic interval punch-ins.
- Cheat-sheet tip: shift a fifth up or down and play alongside the original key (see Harmonious Fifth).
- Honesty flag: exact knob clock positions are not published — the other knobs dial from this recipe.

content:
Cut It Out — Swapper mutes the loop while overdubbing
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD / overdubbing (the mute triggers while overdubbing is engaged)
- MOD B: NOON (mute-on-overdub behavior) · CCW = threshold for immediate muting · CW = gradual fade into silence
- MOD B slot: B6 Swapper (ALT bank — requires BANK B dip; or load via BLIP)
- MOD B engage: arcade button
- Slot/Bank: MOD B6 alt bank (BANK B dip or BLIP) · dial other knobs from recipe (no published values)

## Concept


With the Swapper knob at noon, Swapper mutes your loop whenever overdubbing is engaged — whether you're playing or not. Nice for inserting deliberate silence or getting precise control over what stays in the loop. This is a precision-edit move (punch silence into the loop, carve precise gaps, replace sections) rather than the ambient Rolling Clouds swell.

## How to play it


1. Engage the BANK B dip to access Swapper on MOD B (or load Swapper via BLIP).
2. Set the MOD B (Swapper) knob to noon.
3. Engage overdubbing — the loop mutes whenever you're overdubbing, letting you punch silence into the loop.
4. Play new material into the silence to replace sections, or leave it empty to carve precise gaps.

## Notes


- This is a precision-edit move (insert silence / control parts) rather than the ambient Rolling Clouds swell — more precise than punching record on/off by hand.
- Counter-clockwise of noon sets a threshold for immediate muting; clockwise sets a gradual fade into silence (manual).
- Requires the BANK B dip (or a BLIP load) to put Swapper on MOD B — physical-only setup.
- Knob at noon is the documented position; the surrounding behavior dials from recipe — no published values for the other knobs.

content:
Daydreaming Half-Speed Octave-Down Grind
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD
- MOD B: octave-down (CCW = reverse, CW = forward; pick forward octave-down for the grind)
- MOD B slot: B4 Stepped Speed
- STABILITY: ~10 o'clock (tape-wobble grit)
- MOD B (Filter): optional Filter (B6) CCW to darken
- REPEATS: max (hold the dropped loop)
- Slot/Bank: MOD B4 default + STABILITY + optional Filter B6 · MIDI PC 3 (Stepped-Speed family)

## Concept


Thom Yorke's "very distinctive grinding vocal" finale on Daydreaming — a dense vocal loop switched to half-speed playback, dropping it an octave. Translated to a banjo/baritone/VG loop that drops an octave into a grinding sub-drone. The downsample artifact of pitching the loop down IS the grinding quality. Designed to emulate (Radiohead used an EHX 45000).

## How to play it


1. In ADD mode, build a loop (a vocal-like sustained banjo/VG phrase, or layered overdubs for density like Thom's stacked vocals).
2. Set MOD B to Stepped Speed (B4) octave-down — CCW for reverse, CW for forward; pick the forward octave-down for the grind.
3. Lean into the downsample grind with mild STABILITY (~10 o'clock) for tape-wobble grit.
4. Optionally add Filter (B6) CCW to darken.
5. REPEATS max to hold the dropped loop.

## Notes


- Where Big Time/MOOD do a half-speed move on the wet, Blooper does it to a committed loop you keep playing fresh over — exactly Thom's workflow (let the dense loop run, then drop it an octave while the live part continues).
- Mono-fine; the Chroma Console / H90 re-spread downstream.

provenance.description: Thom Yorke's grinding vocal finale on Daydreaming — a dense loop dropped an octave via Stepped Speed octave-down, the downsample artifact IS the grind (Radiohead, A Moon Shaped Pool).

content:
Distinct Layers — re-tap to commit independently recallable layers
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: NORM (clean capture) → ADD for the effects-printed final layer
- LEFT footswitch: re-tap to commit each layer — the record→playback transition is what sets a layer; whatever you hear at playback becomes that layer
- LAYERS: navigate the committed stack (8 levels of undo/redo; peel from the TOP only)
- REPEATS: turned down between ideas if you want fully unrelated capsules (so old material fades) — dial to taste, no published value
- Slot/Bank: LEFT footswitch re-tap + LAYERS knob · footswitch/workflow technique (applies to whichever loop slot you're building)

## Concept


Andy Othling's core layering technique: instead of circling and stacking on one layer, deliberately re-tap the LEFT footswitch to commit each idea as a separate layer (bed / stacking / chords / melody / effects pass). This is how you get independently-recallable layers and navigate them with the LAYERS knob — the foundation of Loop Capsules.

## How to play it


1. Record layer 1 (a bed), then re-tap the LEFT footswitch into playback to commit it.
2. Re-tap to record layer 2 (stacking), commit; layer 3 (chords underneath); layer 4 (melody on top); a final layer with effects applied (switch to ADD for that effects-printed pass).
3. Don't just keep circling one layer — each record→playback transition is what creates a distinct, recallable layer.
4. Navigate between committed layers with the LAYERS knob (you can only peel from the top of the stack).

## Notes


- Andy: "I could have kept stacking on one layer... but I wanted to get all those layers distinct."
- You cannot pull out one layer in isolation — the LAYERS knob is undo/redo: navigating back + pressing record erases everything above (use it to fork).
- Limit: 8 discrete undo/redo points (1–7 independent, 8–16 lumped).
- No published knob values — this is a footswitch/workflow technique. Treat REPEATS (and any other knob) as a dialable recipe set to taste.

From Andy Othling (Lowercase Noises) Office Hours stream.

content:
Down Low — Pitcher slams high material down octaves
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD (Pitcher keeps loop length identical — non-time-based, overdub-safe)
- MOD A: deep CCW toward −3 octaves (speed and loop length unchanged) · the deeper the knob, the lower the octave
- MOD A slot: A2 Pitcher (ALT bank — requires BANK A dip; or load via BLIP)
- MOD A engage: arcade button
- Slot/Bank: MOD A2 alt bank (BANK A dip or BLIP) · DSP-heavy, exclusive with Stretcher and the Speed mods · dial other knobs from recipe (no published values)

## Concept


The deeper extremes of Pitcher are great for sound design: record some high-pitched / bright material, then pitch it way down (toward −3 octaves) for huge, transformed sub textures. Because Pitcher is non-time-based, the loop length never changes and speed is unaffected — this is the ADD-mode "safe zone," so heads stay in sync while you keep overdubbing fresh material on top. Pitching high material down preserves more detail than pitching low material up.

## How to play it


1. Record some high-pitched / bright material (the brighter and busier, the more there is to slam down).
2. Engage the BANK A dip and set MOD A to Pitcher (A2), or load Pitcher via BLIP.
3. Turn the MOD A knob deep counter-clockwise toward −3 octaves to slam the loop down low — speed and loop length stay put.
4. Because Pitcher leaves loop length unchanged, overdub fresh material on top safely in ADD while the dropped loop runs underneath.

## Notes


- Pitcher is the ADD-mode "safe zone" — loop length never changes, so heads stay in sync while overdubbing.
- Pitching high material down preserves more detail than pitching low material up — record bright, end heavy.
- DSP-heavy: mutually exclusive with Stretcher, and it does not combine with the Speed modifiers (reverse excepted).
- Requires the BANK A dip (or a BLIP load) to put Pitcher on MOD A — physical-only setup.
- Exact pitch position dials from recipe — no published values; sources say "deeper extremes / way down," range ±3 octaves.

Factory cheat-sheet recipe (Pitcher card, 'Down Low').

content:
Drone Pattern
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- MOD B: CW = repeating sequence, CCW = random; higher = more chopping
- MOD B slot: B5 Scrambler
- MOD B engage: engaged (toggle on/off to regenerate)
- Slot/Bank: MOD B5 default bank · MIDI PC 11

## Concept


Turn a sustained baritone or banjo drone (or any steady source) into a groovy rhythmic pattern. Scrambler chops the loop, with jump points locked to a 16-slice grid so they support the original rhythm. This is Scrambler — the KNOBs co-designer's favorite modifier.

## How to play it


1. Record an ambient or steady source — for example a couple of sustained chords.
2. Set MOD B to Scrambler (B5) and engage to chop into a pattern.
3. Dial the knob: CW for a repeating sequence, CCW for random; higher for more chopping.
4. Toggle on/off to regenerate a new arrangement (jump points re-roll on the 16-slice grid).

## Notes


- Sync the grid feel to the Digitakt clock (see Clock-synced blooping) so the groove feels intentional.

content:
Dry Kill — wet-only loop in a parallel/aux path
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- DRY KILL dip: ON (wet/loop only at output)
- MODE: any (this is a routing setup, not a sound recipe)
- Routing: place Blooper in a parallel/aux send (stereo mixer or H90 routing) rather than the main series chain to keep the dry path stereo
- Other knobs: dial from recipe — no published values

## Concept


Engage the DRY KILL dip to remove the clean signal from Blooper's output, leaving only the wet loop. This lets Blooper live in a parallel/aux path (or keep the rig's dry chain stereo) so the looped wall is mono/wet while the dry signal stays untouched elsewhere — the documented mitigation for Blooper's mono collapse.

## How to play it


1. Engage the DRY KILL dip so only the loop comes out of Blooper.
2. Route Blooper as a parallel/aux device (via a mixer or the H90's routing) so its mono wet loop sits alongside an untouched stereo dry path.
3. Capture and play loops as a wet-only layer that doesn't fold the whole rig to mono.
4. If left in the main series chain instead, accept that the rig is mono from Blooper onward whenever powered.

## Notes


- DeepResearch §5: as wired in series, the rig is mono from Blooper's input onward; DRY KILL + a parallel path is the way to keep the dry chain stereo.
- The dip is physical-only, not MIDI-addressable.
- This is a setup/routing patch, not a sound recipe — no knob values are published, so all other controls are a dialable recipe rather than sourced settings.

content:
Filter-fades-on-repeat
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD
- REPEATS: rolled back (delay setting); leave recording
- MOD B: very slightly engaged toward low-pass (CCW); further CCW = faster/heavier filtering per pass
- MOD B slot: B6 Filter
- Slot/Bank: MOD B6 default bank · MIDI PC 10 (shares Filter family)

## Concept


A delay where each repeat gets progressively darker. With Blooper set as a delay and recording, a slightly-engaged low-pass Filter prints the effect each pass, so every repeat darkens further. A staple ambient move into the H90's bigger spaces.

## How to play it


1. In ADD mode, set Blooper as a delay — REPEATS rolled back, leave it recording.
2. Engage MOD B Filter (B6) very slightly toward the low-pass side (CCW).
3. As it records, it prints the effect each pass, so every repeat darkens.
4. Turn the Filter knob further CCW for faster/heavier filtering per pass.

## Notes


- Knob positions are relative (from Andy's livestream), not clock-face.
- A staple ambient move into the H90's bigger spaces.

content:
Filter + Stability
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- MOD B: Filter — CCW = low-pass, CW = high-pass, noon = none
- MOD B slot: B6 Filter
- MOD B engage: engaged
- STABILITY: engaged (adds wow/flutter/noise/roll-off)
- Slot/Bank: MOD B6 default bank + STABILITY · MIDI PC 10

## Concept


Intensify the vintage/lo-fi effect by narrowing the frequency range and adding resonance. Filter narrows the band and adds resonance while Stability adds wow, flutter, noise, and roll-off — together they compound into deep lo-fi. In ADD, Filter gradually introduces resonant chime and can self-oscillate into ringing resonance.

## How to play it


1. Set MOD B to Filter (B6) and engage it — CCW for low-pass, CW for high-pass, noon for none.
2. Engage STABILITY for wow/flutter/noise/roll-off.
3. Together they narrow the band and add resonance for compounding lo-fi.
4. In ADD, watch for self-oscillation as Filter introduces resonant chime per pass.

## Notes


- Stack under the Chroma Console's degradation for layered lo-fi.
- Watch self-oscillation in ADD mode.

content:
Flickering grains

- MOD A: either extreme (CW consistent, CCW random; at max = granular)
- MOD A slot: A2 Dropper
- REPEATS: down for a dissolving granular delay variant

A fluttering granular feel dominated by silence with pieces of audio poking through. Turn Dropper to either extreme and the loop becomes a sparse grain cloud. The drop pattern recalculates each time the modifier is toggled on, so you can tap on/off to audition patterns.

## How to play it


1. Set MOD A to Dropper (A2), knob to either extreme — CW for consistent, CCW for random; at max it goes granular.
2. Tap the modifier on/off to re-roll and audition new drop patterns.
3. Variant: turn REPEATS down for a dissolving granular delay.

- A mono-fine texture; great Blooper-source material to feed the Chroma Console / H90 for stereo grain clouds.

content:
Forward/Reverse Sweep — one note swept up then back
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD
- MOD B slot: B4 Stepped Speed (default bank — quantized)
- MOD B: set so the loop alternates forward/reverse on the note — dialable, no published clock position
- REPEATS: up — dialable, no published clock position
- STABILITY: up — introduces growing instability over time; dialable, no published clock position
- Tempo (tap): tap a LONG tempo to set a long loop length
- Slot/Bank: MOD B4 default bank + STABILITY · MIDI PC 3 (Stepped-Speed family)

## Concept


Tap a long tempo, turn REPEATS up, and set the quantized pitch modifier (Stepped Speed) so a single recorded note plays forward and then backwards — constantly sweeping up to it and back. Running it in ADD mode with STABILITY up makes the sweep progressively less stable over time, so it slowly decays into a wobbling drone rather than holding a clean cycle.

## How to play it


1. Tap in a long tempo to set a long loop, and turn REPEATS up.
2. Play a single note into the loop.
3. Set the quantized pitch modifier (Stepped Speed) so the loop sweeps the note forward then backward, constantly.
4. In ADD with STABILITY up, the sweep gets less stable over time — let it decay into a wobbling drone.

## Notes


- Andy's words: "plays it forward and then backwards… constantly sweeping up to it and then back" and "less stable over time because we're in Additive mode and stability's up."
- A long tap tempo gives the sweep room to breathe.
- Honesty flag: exact knob / REPEATS / STABILITY positions are not published — dial from this recipe.

In ADD with STABILITY up it gets progressively less stable over time, decaying into a wobbling drone. From Andy Othling (Lowercase Noises) Office Hours stream (verbatim quotes).

content:
Go-To-Sleep Random Stutter
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- MOD B: CCW of noon = random (Jonny's random generator); deeper CCW = more chopping; CW = repeating sequence (fixed Feral Glitch mode)
- MOD B slot: B5 Scrambler
- MOD B engage: engage to chop; toggle on/off to regenerate a new random arrangement
- REPEATS: up
- VOLUME: 12 o'clock
- Slot/Bank: MOD B5 default bank · MIDI PC 11 (shares Scrambler family) or its own slot

## Concept


Jonny Greenwood's randomized stutter/glitch from "Go To Sleep" and "There There." His Max/MSP patch ran a random generator that looped chunks of audio for an "x" amount of time, decided randomly. Blooper's Scrambler is the near-1:1 hardware equivalent — a 16-slice grid, random or fixed. Designed to emulate; Radiohead's actual method is a Max/MSP patch, not a Blooper.

## How to play it


1. Record a dense source first — play a lot of notes (banjo/VG arp), exactly as Jonny "plays a lot of notes so the patch always has something to loop."
2. Set MOD B to Scrambler (B5), knob CCW of noon = random (Jonny's random generator); deeper CCW = more chopping.
3. Engage to chop into the pattern; toggle on/off to regenerate a new random arrangement (the patch's re-roll).
4. For the fixed mode of the Feral Glitch, set Scrambler CW = repeating sequence instead.
5. REPEATS up, VOLUME 12. Jump points lock to the 16-slice grid so they support the rhythm.
6. DRY KILL dip ON = the Feral's kill-dry toggle (glitch-only output); leave it off to blend dry + stutter like the LS-2 in/out.

## Notes


- Sync the grid to the Digitakt clock (see Clock-synced blooping) so the random stutter feels intentional, like the patch's tempo-aware chunks.
- For "occasional disturbance" rather than constant chop, use Skip Protection — same Scrambler, lowest random setting.

content:
Harmonious Fifth — Stepped Speed a fifth up or down
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: NORM to layer the shift over the clean loop, or ADD to commit
- MOD B: step to a fifth up (CW) or down (CCW) — Stepped Speed quantizes to octaves/fifths by design; exact step position not published
- MOD B slot: B4 Stepped Speed (default bank)
- MOD B engage: arcade button — engage the shift
- STABILITY: dial from recipe — no published value
- REPEATS: dial from recipe — no published value

## Concept


Shift the loop a fifth up or down with Stepped Speed and play the shifted version alongside the original key — a harmonious but slightly more complex melodic relationship from one source, with no second instrument. Stepped Speed lands on octaves and fifths by design, so a fifth is the sweet harmonic interval to explore against the original key.

## How to play it


1. Record a phrase, then set MOD B to Stepped Speed (B4).
2. Step the MOD B knob until the loop sits a fifth up (CW) or down (CCW) — Stepped Speed quantizes to octaves and fifths.
3. In NORM the shifted version plays over the clean loop for instant harmony; in ADD it bakes in.
4. Play a fresh live lead over the now-harmonized bed.

## Notes


- KNOBs' explicit tip: a fifth is the sweet harmonic interval to explore against the original key.
- Stepped Speed is time-based — content can be lost or doubled if the speed change implies a different length than the fixed loop container.
- Stepped Speed has one extra octave of range compared to the smooth/chromatic speeds.
- Exact step positions are not published; the MOD B step, STABILITY, and REPEATS values above are a dialable recipe, not sourced settings.

Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

- Mode: NORM to audition the condensed loop, ADD to commit the drum-like figure
- MOD B: CW from noon to condense (up to 4x faster, pitch unchanged) · full CW = ring-mod-ish · dial by ear, no published value

Condensing a loop with the Stretcher (rotating clockwise from noon) emphasizes its percussive aspects, so you can audition any loop as a drum pattern — the "hidden drums" inside a sustained source. content:
Kid-A "Loops Mistreated" Aging Wall
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD
- STABILITY: up — mild → moderate analog feel (older layers wobble, drift out of phase)
- REPEATS: ~11–1 o'clock (pulled back so old layers fade → continuous time-shift)
- MOD A: Dropper (A2) mild for granular crumble (Aphex/Autechre artifacts left uncorrected)
- MOD A slot: A2 Dropper
- Slot/Bank: STABILITY (either bank) + optional Dropper A2 · MIDI PC 1 (shares Accumulator family)

## Concept


The Kid A method verbatim — "loops mistreated, stretched, pulled out of phase… everything breathes wrong on purpose." Build a loop, then let it rot and drift like a tape machine failing while you keep playing clean over it. This is essentially the Accumulator patch aimed squarely at the Kid A aesthetic — the most on-lens of the Radiohead Blooper patches.

## How to play it


1. In ADD mode, record a clean loop (banjo/VG/Rhodes-like phrase) with STABILITY off.
2. Turn STABILITY up — mild to moderate "analog feel" — so each pass ages; older layers wobble, lose highs, and drift out of phase ("breathes wrong").
3. Keep overdubbing; pull REPEATS back (~11–1 o'clock) so old layers fade → continuous time-shift.
4. Add Dropper (A2) mild for granular crumble (Aphex/Autechre rhythmic artifacts left uncorrected).
5. Use the BLIP Stability slider to bias toward flutter, not white-noise hiss.

## Notes


- Fresh notes appear clean while the bed rots — exactly Ed cutting up the Rhodes in real time over a mistreated loop.
- The "pulled out of phase / breathes wrong on purpose" line is the user's making aesthetic, so this is the most on-lens of the Radiohead Blooper patches.

content:
"Let Down" Octave-Stack Arpeggio Builder
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD
- STABILITY: off (keep the stack clean and chimey)
- MOD A: +1 octave (CW; length unchanged = the ADD-safe shift); optional 3rd pass at a 5th or octave
- MOD A slot: A2 Pitcher (ALT bank)
- REPEATS: max (all layers ring as the cascade)
- Slot/Bank: MOD A2 ALT bank (requires BANK A dip) · MIDI PC 14 (ALT-A harmony family)

## Concept


The literal "Let Down" move — Jonny doubled his arpeggio an octave higher, then Ed added a third layer. Blooper builds that stack from ONE recorded arpeggio: print it, overdub an octave-up copy, then a third pass — the doubled/tripled Spector wall from a single line. Designed to emulate (Radiohead used overdubs, not a Blooper).

## How to play it


1. In ADD mode, record the clean arpeggio (banjo/guitar, bright) — keep STABILITY off so the stack stays clean and chimey, matching Big Time TB1's HiFi voicing.
2. Set MOD A to Pitcher (ALT bank A2) at +1 octave (CW; length unchanged = the ADD-safe shift) — requires the BANK A dip.
3. Punch in an overdub pass → now you have the original plus an octave up.
4. Optional third pass at a 5th or octave again (the "Ed Jazzmaster third layer").
5. REPEATS max so all layers ring as the cascade.

## Notes


- This is the real doubled-octave layer the King-of-Gear / PoeticWax breakdown describes — pair it with Big Time TB1 running the multi-tap cascade over the stack for the full jangle wall, into a long hall (St Catherine's ballroom).
- Keep it clean and bright here — the jangle is the hook, so resist the degrade tie-breaker on this one patch.

Loop Capsules
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- REPEATS: all the way down (to fade) → all the way up (after fade) to record new layer
- LAYERS: move between the two totally distinct layers; ramp (RANDOM) to auto-shuffle
- Slot/Bank: LAYERS + REPEATS knobs · each capsule navigable in one MIDI PC loop

## Concept


Capture distinct ideas (a C section vs a G section) on separate layers and navigate or shuffle between them with the LAYERS knob — generative arrangement with no modifiers needed.

## How to play it


1. Record a loop.
2. Turn REPEATS all the way down.
3. Engage overdubbing.
4. Once the audio has faded, turn REPEATS all the way up.
5. Record new sounds.
6. Go into playback, then use the LAYERS knob to move between the two totally distinct layers.
7. Auto-shuffle: ramp the LAYERS knob (RANDOM).

## Notes


- You can only peel from the TOP of the stack (8 levels of undo/redo); navigating back and recording forks the loop and erases layers above.

content:
Manual Stretch — scan a time-stretch across the loop
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD (or one-shot Record) to bake the scan in — Trimmer is time-based
- MOD A: park right of noon, rotate CLOCKWISE to scan the stretch (CCW of noon = abrasive 'crumbs' shortening)
- MOD A slot: A3 Stepped Trimmer
- MOD A engage: arcade button engaged
- Slot/Bank: MOD A3 default bank · MIDI PC 12

## Concept


With the Stepped Trimmer just right of noon, rotating the knob clockwise introduces a manual time-stretching effect as you scan across the loop — scrubbing the recorded material like dragging tape past the playhead. It's a deliberate coding byproduct the designers kept because they liked it, and it's recordable in Additive.

## How to play it


1. Set MOD A to Stepped Trimmer (slot A3, default bank).
2. Park the knob just right of noon and engage the arcade button.
3. Slowly rotate clockwise to scan a manual time-stretch across the loop.
4. Record the move in ADD (or a one-shot Record) to bake the stretch in, or ramp the knob for hands-free movement.

## Notes


- This is the deliberate "clockwise = time-stretch" quirk KNOBs describes — a byproduct of how Trimmer was coded, kept because they liked it.
- Counterclockwise of noon is the abrasive "crumbs" shortening side instead.
- Distinct from the alt-bank Stretcher (true pitch-independent stretch) — this is the default-bank Trimmer's stretch quirk.
- Cheat-sheet tip: pair Trimmer with Scrambler to speed up Scrambler's pattern for bursts of activity (see the Jumbled Bursts seed).
- No published knob values beyond "right of noon, clockwise" — treat the remaining knobs as a dialable recipe to taste; only the Trimmer slot and clockwise-scan direction are sourced.

content:
Momentary-record a reverb sliver
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: SAMP
- LEFT footswitch: HOLD = momentary record (records only while held; release to stop) — but tapping LEFT wipes the loop
- RIGHT footswitch: trigger; hold RIGHT toggles loop vs one-shot
- Slot/Bank: SAMP-mode footswitches · park grabbed sliver in a free MIDI PC slot

## Concept


Grab a split-second sliver of a sustained reverb pad and trigger it. In SAMP, holding the LEFT footswitch records only while held, so you can freeze a reverb pad (Andy uses an Old Blood Noise Dark Star) and momentary-record just a sliver to retrigger.

## How to play it


1. In SAMP mode, freeze a sustained reverb pad upstream.
2. HOLD the LEFT footswitch for momentary record — it records only while held; release to stop.
3. Trigger with the RIGHT footswitch; hold RIGHT to toggle loop vs one-shot.

## Notes


- WARNING: tapping LEFT in SAMP wipes the loop — only HOLD it.
- Capture stereo-dependent reverb tails before Blooper, since SAMP plays back mono — let the Chroma Console / H90 re-spread.

content:
Multi-Generational Resampling — re-capture the degraded loop
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: build in NORM/ADD (with STABILITY) → SAMP to trigger → back to NORM/ADD to re-record the next generation
- STABILITY: engaged on the first loop; increase per generation so each re-capture ages further — set by ear, no published values
- RIGHT footswitch: in SAMP, triggers the carried-over loop so you can re-record its aged output
- LEFT footswitch: RECORD — re-record the triggered output into a fresh loop; in SAMP this wipes the loop, so re-capture deliberately
- EXT RECORD: external footswitch into the EXT jack — hands-free re-capture between generations
- Slot/Bank: mode toggle NORM/ADD ↔ SAMP plus STABILITY — dialable recipe, no published knob values

## Concept


Andy Othling's DAW resampling philosophy mapped onto the pedal: build a loop, switch to SAMP and trigger it, then re-record that triggered (already-aged) output back into a fresh loop through more STABILITY. Each pass is a new "generation," so by the third or fourth re-capture you're hearing a sampling of a sampling of a sampling — the original sound several degradations removed. STABILITY does the aging, SAMP/Carryover does the re-triggering, and the LEFT (RECORD) footswitch closes the loop on the next generation. The "recorded-wrong" aesthetic, native to Blooper.

## How to play it


1. Build a loop in NORM/ADD with STABILITY on so it ages.
2. Switch to SAMP (Carryover) and trigger the loop with the RIGHT footswitch to hear it back.
3. Re-record that triggered output into a fresh loop in NORM/ADD, adding more STABILITY this generation.
4. Repeat — each generation degrades further, so you end up hearing the third/fourth sampling of the original.
5. Let downstream pedals (Chroma / H90) re-stereo and reverb the final degraded wall.

## Notes


- Method maps Andy's DAW resampling idea ("you're hearing the fourth sampling of it") onto Blooper's ADD-Stability + SAMP-Carryover.
- Honesty flag: the original quote in the source is about Primal Tap / VSS-30, not Blooper-specific — the *method* transfers, the attribution does not. This is a designed mapping, not a sourced Blooper preset.
- Honesty flag: no published knob values — increase STABILITY per generation by ear; everything else dials from this recipe.
- Watch out: hitting RECORD (LEFT) in SAMP wipes the loop — re-record into a new pass deliberately rather than over the carried-over sample.

Stacking re-sampling generations so you're hearing the third or fourth pass of the sound — the 'recorded-wrong' aesthetic, native to Blooper (artist: Andy Othling / Lowercase Noises, Sound Methods interview; method mapped to Blooper, honesty-flagged).

Structured surprise — overdubs land in unpredictable spots across the full loop. Trimmer shrinks the loop to a small play window; record overdubs into that window, then turn Trimmer off and the whole loop and the overdubs could be anywhere. Generative/chance arrangement with no ramping.

content:
Mystery Slicing — ramped Stutter, new slice each time
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- MOD A slot: A3 Stutter (ALT bank — requires BANK A dip, or load via BLIP)
- MOD A engage: re-engage to grab a fresh slice size (the ramp re-rolls per toggle)
- RAMP knob (= VOLUME knob while ramping): ramp speed — set to taste (no published value)
- Mode: NORM or ADD
- Slot/Bank: MOD A3 ALT bank (requires BANK A dip) + physical ramping dips (Bounce or Random)

## Concept


Stutter pairs nicely with ramping so that each time you turn it on the slices are a different size — a generative, ever-changing stutter that never repeats the same way twice. Because the ramp is moving the Stutter knob for you, the slice size lands somewhere new every time you re-engage, giving you an always-fresh beat-repeat / DJ-scratch rhythm.

## How to play it


1. Engage BANK A so Stutter sits on MOD A (A3), or load Stutter onto the slot via BLIP.
2. Set the ramping dips to automate MOD A — use BOUNCE for continuous back-and-forth, or RANDOM for the most varied slice sizes.
3. Set the RAMP knob (the VOLUME knob while ramping) for the ramp speed.
4. Each time you toggle Stutter on, the ramp lands the slice at a different size.
5. Toggle on/off through a passage for an always-changing stutter rhythm or a DJ/beat-repeat scratch effect.

## Notes


- Generative by design — the slice size re-rolls per engage thanks to the ramp position.
- Requires the BANK A dip and the ramp dips — both physical-only setups (the ramping dips are not MIDI-addressable; this is a fixed-setup decision, not a per-song recall).
- Combine with manic on/off toggling for a fake time-stretch (see Pseudo-Stretching).
- Random gives the widest spread of slice sizes; Bounce keeps the motion sweeping continuously.
- Honesty flag: ramp speed/flavor and the other knobs dial from this recipe — no published values.

content:
Reverb-Trail Capture — PLAY/DUB straight-to-dub
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: NORM or ADD
- LEFT footswitch: tap to record initial loop; tap again to set endpoint — Blooper auto-continues into overdubbing the second layer; tap again to drop into playback
- REPEATS: high for sustained layers — to taste, no published value
- STABILITY: low for clean capture — to taste, no published value

## Concept


Set the PLAY/DUB dip so a finished initial recording drops straight into overdubbing the second layer instead of playback. This is ideal for capturing ambient reverb trails: hit record, play a chord, and the decaying reverb tail keeps getting captured into the loop without a manual mode switch. The manual explicitly recommends this configuration for ambient music.

## How to play it


1. Set the PLAY/DUB dip to the Dub position (straight-to-overdub after the first recording).
2. Tap RECORD (LEFT footswitch) and play a sustained chord — ideally with an upstream reverb/pad feeding Blooper — then tap again to set the endpoint.
3. Blooper drops straight into overdubbing the second layer; the reverb trail keeps being captured seamlessly with no manual mode switch.
4. Build an ambient bed from decaying tails, then tap RECORD again to drop into playback when ready.

## Notes


- Dub mode is explicitly recommended in the manual for ambient music — it lets reverb trails be captured smoothly into the loop instead of cutting off at playback.
- Pairs with Andy Othling's momentary-record-a-reverb-sliver technique (distinct mechanism — SAMP-mode momentary record) and the existing Momentary-record patch.
- The PLAY/DUB dip is a fixed-setup decision, NOT MIDI-addressable / not a per-song recall.
- REPEATS/STABILITY are to taste — no published values; the load-bearing setting here is the dip.

content:
Precise Glitch Placement — record a glitch into one exact spot
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD
- LEFT footswitch: begin overdubbing the instant the target note plays
- MOD A: engage a modifier (e.g. Trimmer/Scrambler) briefly to make the glitch, then stop · dial from recipe — no published values
- MOD B: alternate modifier source for the glitch burst · dial from recipe — no published values
- Slot/Bank: any modifier slot · technique applies to whichever loop slot you're building

## Concept


Because the loop length is fixed and the record head is respected, you can plant any additive material at a specific moment in the loop: start overdubbing exactly when a target note plays, create the glitch, and when the loop comes back around the glitch lives permanently in that exact spot. This is KNOBs' precise-placement technique — the two-headed model keeps the record head steady, so it lays audio down wherever it currently is.

## How to play it


1. Enter ADD mode with a loop already playing.
2. Wait for the exact note/moment you want to replace; start overdubbing (LEFT footswitch) right then.
3. Make the glitch — a quick Trimmer/Scrambler burst on MOD A/B, or a played sound.
4. Stop overdubbing. When the loop comes around, the glitch is permanently fixed at that spot.

## Notes


- Relies on the steady record head + fixed measure (the two-headed "anomaly" model) — the record head lays down audio wherever it currently is, so a precisely-timed punch lands precisely.
- Related to the existing Punch-in patch, but this one is specifically about replacing one exact note/moment rather than general punch-ins.
- No published knob values — this is a placement technique. The MOD A/B settings are a dialable recipe: pick a modifier, engage it briefly, then stop. Dial the rest to taste.

content:
Pseudo-Stretching — Stutter fakes real-time stretch
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: NORM — tap a short tempo, then leave Blooper in the RECORDING state (do not advance to playback)
- MOD A: stutter slice size (CCW = stutter what just happened / longest; CW = what's coming up / shortest)
- MOD A slot: A3 Stutter (ALT bank — requires BANK A dip; or load via BLIP)
- MOD A engage: arcade button (engage to hold the stutter; toggle on/off for the manic fake-stretch)
- Slot/Bank: MOD A3 alt bank (BANK A dip / BLIP) · dial other knobs from recipe (no published values)

## Concept


Mimic real-time stretching by tapping in a short tempo in Normal mode, turning on Stutter, and leaving Blooper recording. The loop-within-a-loop stutter held over time reads as a stretched, suspended texture — a fake time-stretch with no pitch artifacts, just a held, smeared slice that keeps re-triggering while the record head wanders.

## How to play it


1. Engage BANK A so Stutter is on MOD A (slot A3 in the alt bank), or load Stutter via BLIP.
2. In NORM, tap in a short tempo (this sets a short loop measure).
3. Turn on Stutter and leave Blooper in the recording state — do not advance to playback.
4. The held loop-within-a-loop reads as a real-time-stretch / suspended texture.
5. Alternatively, manically toggle Stutter on/off during playback for the same fake-stretch feel.

## Notes


- Stutter is time-based — it desyncs the record/play heads while engaged.
- Counter-clockwise stutters what just happened (longest slice); clockwise stutters what's coming up (shortest slice) — per the manual.
- Pairs nicely with ramping so each engage gives a different slice size (see Mystery Slicing).
- Requires the BANK A dip (or a BLIP load) to put Stutter on MOD A; the exact slice-knob position is not published — dial from recipe.

content:
Rainbow Machine shimmer
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD
- REPEATS: up (delay base); raise for more cascade
- MOD B: octave-up = cascade up (shimmer); octave-down = cascade into sub-drone
- MOD B slot: B4 Stepped Speed (quantized octave)
- STABILITY: added for a chorus-y quality
- MOD B (Filter): optional Filter (B6) to darken each pass
- Slot/Bank: MOD B4 default + STABILITY + optional Filter B6 · MIDI PC 3 (shares Stepped-Speed family)

## Concept


Shimmer that cascades up octave by octave each repeat — or down for a sub-drone. Set Blooper as a delay and use Stepped Speed (the quantized octave, which Andy distinguishes from A1's unquantized octave) in ADD so the shift cascades. In NORM the shift is fixed with no cascade; ADD makes it cascade.

## How to play it


1. In ADD mode, set Blooper as a delay (REPEATS up).
2. Set MOD B to Stepped Speed (B4): octave-up so each repeat cascades up (shimmer), or octave-down to cascade into a sub-drone.
3. Add STABILITY for a chorus-y quality.
4. Raise REPEATS for more of the cascade.
5. Optionally stack Filter (B6) to darken each pass.

## Notes


- Knob positions are relative (from Andy's livestream).
- The reverse-fifths/octaves variant gives a descending reversed drone.

content:
Repair Me
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD
- RAMP knob (= VOLUME knob while ramping): fairly SLOW
- VOLUME: ride by holding RIGHT footswitch (feedback/self-oscillation expected)

The sound of a tape machine on the edge of death — a loop that is sometimes pure and clean, sometimes wobbly and disheveled, occasionally volatile. This is the strongest "recorded-wrong" degrade fit on the sheet and the doom/decay centerpiece of the rig.

## How to play it


1. In ADD mode, set the ramping dips to STABILITY + BOUNCE + RANDOM.
2. Set the RAMP knob (the VOLUME knob while ramping) fairly SLOW.
3. Loop a wall, then let the slow random Stability ramp ride the line between clean and broken.
4. Layer fresh banjo over the wobble.
5. Expect feedback and self-oscillation — ride VOLUME by holding the RIGHT footswitch.

## Notes


- From the manual (p.45 — "tape machine on the edge of death").
- Dip switches are physical-only, NOT MIDI-addressable, so this ramp setup is a fixed-setup decision, not a per-song recall.

content:
Reverse-Bloom Loop
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD (to print a clean reversed layer back into the wall)
- MOD B: CCW = reverse (loop runs in reverse; decaying tail now swells in)
- MOD B slot: B4 Stepped Speed
- REPEATS: max (FADE none)
- Slot/Bank: MOD B4 default bank, knob CCW · MIDI PC 3 (Stepped-Speed family)

## Concept


The other Daydreaming move — Thom samples ringing glockenspiel notes and reverses them so each note that rang out now gently fades IN. Also covers Jonny's reversed guitar (Backdrifts) and A Moon Shaped Pool's "sample-something-then-reverse-it" approach. Radiohead's reverse is a captured-then-reversed sample, not a swelling reverse-delay pedal — Blooper's reversed loop is the honest hardware match.

## How to play it


1. Capture a ringing pluck/swell (banjo, VG pad, or a reverb tail grabbed in SAMP from upstream).
2. Play the loop backwards: set MOD B to Stepped Speed (B4), knob CCW (= reverse) so the loop runs in reverse — the decaying tail now swells in.
3. For a clean reversed layer printed back into the wall, do it in ADD and overdub the reversed pass on top of the forward loop (the "sample-then-reverse-and-layer" method).
4. Pair with FADE (none) / REPEATS max.

## Notes


- Radiohead's reverse is a captured-then-reversed sample, not a swelling reverse-delay pedal — capture → reverse → layer is the honest hardware match.
- For the swelling-in attack on a single note, also see the MOOD Slip reverse.
- Feed into the H90 hall so the reversed blooms diffuse.

content:
Reverse Octave Cascade — every repeat reversed and an octave down
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD (the pitch/reverse step bakes into each repeat)
- MOD B: reverse + octave-down — CCW past noon into reverse, stepped to the octave-down interval (set by ear; no published clock position)
- MOD B slot: B4 Stepped Speed (default bank — quantized pitch)
- MOD B engage: arcade button — engage Stepped Speed move
- REPEATS: up (so the cascading repeats accumulate) — dialable, no published clock position
- STABILITY: optional — add for a chorus-y degrade (dialable to taste)
- Slot/Bank: MOD B4 default bank (quantized) · MIDI PC 3 (Stepped-Speed family)

## Concept


Andy Othling's cascade: in ADD with the quantized pitch modifier (Stepped Speed) set to "reverse octave down," every repeat plays reversed and an octave below the one before it. Stacked up, the repeats tumble into a descending, backward sub-drone — and because the step is quantized it lands on fifths as well as octaves, so it stays musical. Andy is careful to distinguish the two pitch modifiers: "modifier one is unquantized octave, four is quantized pitch" — this cascade wants the quantized one (Stepped Speed, B4).

## How to play it


1. Build a loop and set MOD B to Stepped Speed (B4) — the quantized pitch modifier.
2. In ADD mode, set the knob to reverse + octave-down (CCW past noon into reverse, stepped to the octave-down interval).
3. Turn REPEATS up so the cascading repeats accumulate.
4. Each repeat now plays reversed and an octave (or a fifth) below the previous one — a descending, backward sub-drone.
5. Optionally add STABILITY for a chorus-y degrade as the cascade builds.

## Notes


- Use the quantized pitch modifier (Stepped Speed, B4), not the unquantized octave one — Andy: "modifier one is unquantized octave, four is quantized pitch." The cascade comes from the quantized stepping.
- The cascade needs ADD — the pitch/reverse step has to bake into each repeat. In NORM the shift is fixed (one octave, no cascade).
- Honesty flag: exact knob position is not published — set "reverse octave down" by ear (CCW past noon into reverse, then to the octave-down step). It lands on fifths too. REPEATS and STABILITY are dialed from this recipe, not from published values.

It lands on fifths too. From Andy Othling's (Lowercase Noises) Office Hours stream.

content:
Rolling Clouds — Swapper swelling/fading ambient bed
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD (record the swells into the loop)
- MOD B: RIGHT side (FADE mode = swelling/fading landscape); noon/left = interactive muting — see Cut It Out / Twitchy Swapper
- MOD B slot: B6 Swapper (ALT bank)
- MOD B engage: engage and let it run while overdubbing
- Slot/Bank: MOD B6 ALT bank (requires BANK B dip, or BLIP-load Swapper) · other knobs dial from recipe — no published values

## Concept


Use the right (FADE-mode) side of Swapper in Additive mode to create a soft landscape of swelling and fading sounds — an ambient bed builder that gently breathes parts of the loop in and out. Swapper is an interactive/envelope-controlled mute-and-swap modifier: its right side gives the fade/landscape behavior, while noon/left is the interactive muting used elsewhere. This is the factory cheat-sheet's named "Rolling Clouds" recipe.

## How to play it


1. Engage the BANK B dip so the alt bank's Swapper is available on MOD B (or load Swapper into a Mod slot via BLIP).
2. Set the Swapper knob (MOD B) to its right (FADE-mode) side.
3. Enter ADD mode and let it run while overdubbing — parts of the loop swell and fade into a soft landscape.
4. Layer sustained baritone/banjo for a continuously breathing ambient wall.

## Notes


- Swapper is an interactive/envelope-controlled mute-and-swap modifier; the right side is the fade/landscape behavior, the noon/left side is interactive muting (see Cut It Out / Twitchy Swapper).

- Exact knob position beyond "right side" is not published; treat the other knobs as a dialable recipe rather than sourced values.

content:
Starter — Stopper run in reverse to begin a loop
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: ADD (Blooper keeps recording while stopped — print the start)
- MOD B: CCW of noon = melting tape-stop (further = longer to stop) · CW of noon = gradual volume fade-out · after stopping, adjust to change the start behavior
- MOD B slot: B5 Stopper (ALT bank — requires BANK B dip; or load via BLIP)
- MOD B engage: arcade button (latch to stop; disengage = reverse 'start')
- Slot/Bank: MOD B5 alt bank (BANK B dip or BLIP) · dial other knobs from recipe (no published values)

## Concept


Disengaging Stopper causes the effect to happen in reverse — a "Starter." Use a tape-stop to halt the loop, then release Stopper to ramp it back to life. Adjust the knob once stopped to give a different speed/effect on the start. Blooper keeps recording while stopped, so the start can be printed.

## How to play it


1. Engage the BANK B dip, set MOD B to Stopper (slot B5), and place the knob counter-clockwise of noon (tape-stop side) or clockwise (volume fade).
2. Engage Stopper to halt the loop — the further CCW, the slower the melting stop.
3. While stopped, adjust the knob to set a different start speed/effect.
4. Disengage to "start" the loop in reverse — and since Blooper keeps recording while stopped, the start can be baked into the loop in ADD.

## Notes


- Stopper's tape-stop side (CCW) is time-based (desyncs the heads); the fade-out side (CW) is non-time-based.
- Can self-oscillate / run away in ADD mode — ride VOLUME.
- Rapidly toggling Stopper on/off makes a manual tremolo / melting vibrato (see Vibrodrops).
- Requires the BANK B dip (or a BLIP load) to put Stopper on MOD B — physical-only setup.
- Exact knob positions beyond CCW/CW of noon dial from recipe — no published values for the other knobs.

Strange Subdivisions — Stepped Trimmer as delay tap subdivisions
Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: NORM (delay base — audition the subdivided window)
- RECORD footswitch: tap-tempo the record footswitch to set the delay time, then leave it recording
- REPEATS: rolled back below max for delay/fade behavior — only fades while recording (dial by ear, no published value)
- MOD A slot: A3 Stepped Trimmer (default bank, 1/32 steps)
- MOD A: step off noon to subdivide the delay in 1/32 increments — acts like a subdivision selector (dial by ear, no published value)
- Slot/Bank: MOD A3 default bank · other knobs dial from recipe (no published values)

## Concept


When you use Blooper as a delay, treat Stepped Trimmer like a unique form of standard tap-tempo subdivisions. Tap a tempo, then step the loop down in 1/32 increments to carve odd, dotted, and triplet-style delay subdivisions out of that one tapped tempo — a subdivision selector that stays musical because every step is quantized.

## How to play it


1. Set Blooper up as a delay: tap-tempo the RECORD footswitch to set the time, pull REPEATS below max (delay/fade behavior), and leave it recording.
2. Set MOD A to Stepped Trimmer (A3, default bank).
3. Step the MOD A knob off noon to shorten the delay window in 1/32 subdivisions — it acts like a subdivision selector on the delay.
4. Combine with Scrambler to speed the pattern up for bursts of jumbled activity.

## Notes


- Stepped Trimmer quantizes to 1/32, so the subdivisions stay musical.
- REPEATS only fades while recording; in playback the loop never fades (it is a manual looper). Backing off REPEATS turns Blooper into a high-quality digital delay.
- Pairs with Scrambler for jumbled / bursting delays (cheat-sheet tip).
- Exact step positions and REPEATS value are not published — this is a dialable recipe; dial the subdivision you want by ear, and the other knobs are dialed from the recipe rather than from published values.

Device: Chase Bliss Blooper

Settings:
- Mode: NORM (audition) → ADD or one-shot Record (print the halt)
