- MOD A slot: A1 Smooth Speed (default bank)
- MOD A engage: arcade button (latch)
- Slot/Bank: MOD A1 default bank · dial other knobs from recipe (no published values)

## Concept


With Smooth Speed set close to real-time speed, engage the modifier and immediately bring the knob to noon to create a rubbery effect like a tape machine slowing to a halt. The single most iconic Smooth Speed move and the literal opposite end of the Glacier recipe.

## How to play it


1. Set MOD A to Smooth Speed (slot A1, default bank).
2. Position the MOD A knob close to real-time speed (clockwise of noon).
3. With the loop playing, engage the arcade button and immediately sweep the knob down to noon.
4. The loop rubberizes and halts like tape slowing to a stop.
5. To keep it in the loop, do this in ADD (or one-shot the pass); note Smooth Speed is time-based so the record/play heads desync while it runs.

## Notes


- Smooth Speed is time-based — overdubbing under it records a different part of the loop than you hear (two-headed anomaly).
- Counter-clockwise of noon on Smooth Speed engages reverse playback (manual); expect to wander out of tune as the speed drops.
- Pair with the Starter trick (Stopper alt-bank) for a stop-then-start gesture, or use Glacier for the near-stopped drone instead of a full halt.

Swapper is very sensitive at maximum — just touching the guitar strings triggers it. Take advantage of that to create twitchy, dynamics-triggered interruptions that replace parts of the loop based on how hard you play. Recording in ADD bakes the envelope-driven swaps right into the loop.

1. Engage BANK B and set MOD B to Swapper (or load Swapper via BLIP).
2. Turn the Swapper knob (MOD B) to max — the highest sensitivity (SENS).
3. Play — even light string touches trigger the swap, interrupting and replacing parts of the loop.
4. Record in ADD to bake the twitchy, dynamics-driven interruptions into the loop.

## Notes


- Envelope-controlled: the swaps respond to your picking dynamics — great for replacing parts of a loop interactively in ADD.
- Requires the BANK B dip (or a BLIP load) to reach the alt-bank Swapper — physical-only setup, no MIDI PC for the alt slot here.
- The "max sensitivity" position is the documented tip; the surrounding knob values dial from recipe — no published values.

content:
Amp Pusher — double-boost into the amp
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: BOOST (diode-free, clearest, loudest)
- GAIN 1: low — push the AMP, not the pedal (nudge up for low-gain OD); dial from recipe, no published value
- VOL 1: set as the smaller always-on lift, or as the bigger kick — whichever role this channel takes (dial from recipe)
- TONE 1: to taste (dial from recipe)
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: BOOST (diode-free, clearest, loudest)
- GAIN 2: low to match Ch1 — push the AMP (nudge up for low-gain OD); dial from recipe, no published value
- VOL 2: set LOUDER or QUIETER than VOL 1 so the two channels give a two-stage lift (dial from recipe)
- TONE 2: to taste (dial from recipe)
- TREBLE BOOSTER: MIDDLE (off) for the pure clean version; engage on Channel 1 for the 'edge/richer' variant
- PRESENCE: DOWN

## Concept

The manual's own AMP PUSHER recipe: BOOST mode on BOTH channels, one set louder than the other, so the pedal's job is to make your AMP's own overdrive the focus rather than supplying its own clipping. BOOST is the diode-free, clearest, loudest circuit on the AM — "a clean boost capable of low-gain overdrive… the clearest sound and the loudest overall volume" (manual) — so stacking two gives you clean headroom that tips into edge. Optionally engage the treble booster on Channel 1 and/or push GAIN for a second, richer flavor: one clean transparent boost and one with hair.

## How to play it

1. Set BOTH channels to BOOST with similar settings; keep GAIN low (push the AMP, not the pedal — or nudge up for low-gain OD).
2. Set one channel's VOL louder than the other so you have a smaller always-on lift and a bigger kick.
3. Stack both to push a tube amp into its own natural breakup.
4. For a second, richer flavor, engage the treble booster on Channel 1 and/or push GAIN: now one boost is clean/transparent and the other has edge.

## Notes

- Manual-named recipe + CB's documented "both-Boost amp-pusher" starting point: the modes and the "one louder" intent are quoted; no exact knob numbers are published — dial VOL/GAIN from the recipe.

content:
Andy's Organic Stack — heavy OD pushed by an end boost
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: OVERDRIVE (right side — heavier foundation)
- GAIN 1: dial from recipe — heavier OD foundation (Andy gives modes, not clocks)
- VOL 1: dial from recipe to taste
- TONE 1: dial from recipe to taste
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: BOOST (left side — the dynamic end boost; clips less than OD)
- GAIN 2: dial from recipe — push level into the amp, not the pedal
- VOL 2: dial from recipe — enough to drive the amp into overdrive
- TONE 2: dial from recipe to taste
- PRESENCE: DOWN (on a spanky/bright guitar, hold footswitch + reduce presence to ~25% to smooth it)
- TREBLE BOOSTER: MIDDLE (off) to start

## Concept

AndyDemos' "organic" approach to the Brothers AM: use Channel 1 (right) as a heavier OVERDRIVE foundation and Channel 2 (left) as a BOOST sitting at the END of the chain. Because the BOOST mode clips less than the OVERDRIVE, it stays more dynamic — and rather than piling on the pedal's own saturation, it pushes the amp itself into overdrive. That "let the amp do the overdriving" move is what makes it sound organic, and it's the deliberate contrast to Andy's other 'saturation' DIST→OD stack.

## How to play it

1. Set Channel 1 (right side) to OVERDRIVE as a heavier foundation.
2. Set Channel 2 (left side) to BOOST — because it clips less, it's more dynamic than running another OD.
3. Run them stacked: the end BOOST pushes the amp itself into overdrive for the "organic" sound (utilize the amp, not the pedal's saturation).
4. On a spanky/bright guitar, hold the footswitch and reduce presence to ~25% to smooth it.

## Notes

- AndyDemos-quoted: the modes and the role of each channel are quoted; there are no exact clock values — dial GAIN/VOL from the recipe to taste.
- "Organic" = let the amp do the overdriving, with the BOOST at the end acting as a dynamic pusher (contrasts with Andy's 'saturation' DIST→OD stack, which leans on the pedal's own clipping).
- In Andy's layout: right = Channel 1, left = Channel 2.
- MASTER dip ON is optional but helps keep overall level controlled once the end boost is engaged.
- No published knob values — phrased as a dialable recipe by design.

Andy's Saturation Stack — distortion fed by overdrive
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: OVERDRIVE, right channel — adds the extra gain feeding Channel 2
- GAIN 1: ~halfway (Andy: 'about halfway on both' to stay detailed when stacked) — otherwise dial from recipe
- VOL 1: push into Channel 2 — dial from recipe
- TONE 1: to taste — dial from recipe
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: DISTORTION, left channel — the saturated output
- GAIN 2: ~halfway (Andy: 'about halfway on both' to stay detailed when stacked) — otherwise dial from recipe
- VOL 2: master — dial from recipe
- TONE 2: to taste — dial from recipe
- PRESENCE: ~25% down on a spanky guitar (hold footswitch + reduce presence), else DOWN
- Both channels: ON — Channel 1 (OD) pushes Channel 2 (DIST)

## Concept

AndyDemos' "saturation" approach for when you want more compression and saturation instead of more volume: DISTORTION on the left channel (Channel 2) with OVERDRIVE on the right (Channel 1) feeding it all the extra gain. It doesn't add a volume boost — it adds gain and compression so everything sounds meatier and bigger. The counterpart to Andy's organic boost-at-end stack: this one chases saturation and compression, that one chases dynamic amp push.

## How to play it

1. Set Channel 2 (left) to DISTORTION and Channel 1 (right) to OVERDRIVE.
2. Stack both — the OVERDRIVE feeds extra gain into the DISTORTION.
3. Aim for more gain and compression, NOT more volume — Andy notes it makes everything "meatier and bigger" without a volume jump.
4. Run gain ~halfway on both to stay detailed; turn the MASTER dip on so the stack adds saturation, not level.

## Notes

- AndyDemos-quoted: the modes and the "more gain/compression not volume" intent are quoted; "about halfway on both" is the only knob hint Andy gives — otherwise dial from recipe. No published values; treat all clocks as a dialable recipe.
- The counterpart to Andy's organic boost-at-end stack: this one chases saturation/compression, that one chases dynamic amp push.
- More compression compounds on an already-squished source (e.g. after a Muff) — go easy if stacking downstream of a fuzz.
- Slot: intended as a MIDI preset (suggested).

content:
Banjo-Lead Cut Recovery
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- TREBLE BOOSTER: DOWN (classic Rangemaster, upper-mid emphasis)
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: OVERDRIVE (or BOOST for cleaner)
- GAIN 1: 10–11 o'clock (low — articulation not crunch)
- VOL 1: noon
- TONE 1: 1 o'clock
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: off (or low-OD Tightener under it)
- PRESENCE 1: brought UP noticeably (hold Ch1 footswitch + TONE 1) — the documented 'opens it out' move

## Concept

The single most rig-specific patch: claw the Gold Tone banjo's articulation and cut back AFTER the Hizumitas has darkened it, so the banjo-as-lead survives into the Longsword and the End Board's granular/reverb stages. The banjo needs articulation and level here, NOT more saturation — a treble booster into an already-overdriven signal (the Muff) is exactly where it gives a "vocal" lead (Mick Taylor / TPS).

## How to play it

1. Set the TREBLE BOOSTER DOWN (classic Rangemaster, upper-mid emphasis) into Channel 1 in OVERDRIVE (or BOOST for cleaner), GAIN 1 low at ~10–11 for articulation not crunch.
2. Bring PRESENCE 1 UP noticeably (hold Ch1 footswitch + TONE 1) — the documented "opens it out" move; or engage PRES LINK 1 so TONE 1 sweeps tone+presence together for a more dramatic, open control.
3. Internal trims: back Input-Impedance CCW (buffers upstream); adjust the treble/presence trim in conjunction with the top tone knob for banjo cut.
4. Optionally run a low-OD Tightener on Channel 2 underneath, or leave Ch2 off.

## Notes

- Designed starting points, not found settings.
- Lead with the booster and Presence, not gain — the banjo is already loud and bright pre-Muff; the job is restoring what the Muff rolled off so the lead reads through the downstream walls.
- Slot: intended as a MIDI preset (suggested).

content:
Boost Mode Clean — diode-free headroom & cleanup
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- CHANNEL MODE: BOOST (no diodes = max headroom, open) — single channel
- GAIN: low for a transparent clean lift; push hard for low-gain overdrive (dial from recipe, no published value)
- VOL: set the amount of lift you need (dial from recipe)
- TONE: to taste (dial from recipe)
- PRESENCE: DOWN
- TREBLE BOOSTER: MIDDLE (off); flip DOWN for a Rangemaster-style cut variant

## Concept

The AM's BOOST mode used by itself. Unlike OVERDRIVE and DISTORTION, BOOST has no clipping diodes in its path — "no diodes… a bunch more headroom and an open sound" — making it the cleanest, loudest, and most open circuit on the pedal, capable of low-gain overdrive only when pushed hard. It's also the most dynamic and touch-responsive mode: roll your guitar volume down or pick lighter and it cleans up beautifully. Used standalone it's a transparent clean boost / make-up gain stage, and it's the same building block underneath the AMP PUSHER and COMBO stacking recipes.

## How to play it

1. Set one channel to BOOST — the diode-free circuit with the most headroom and the most open, dynamic response.
2. Keep GAIN low for a transparent clean boost / make-up gain; push GAIN hard if you want a touch of low-gain overdrive.
3. Set VOL for the lift you need.
4. Roll your guitar volume down to hear it clean up — BOOST/OD are the most touch-responsive modes.

## Notes

- Documented mode behavior is quoted ("no diodes, more headroom, open" and the cleanup/touch-response); no exact knob numbers are published — dial GAIN/VOL/TONE from the recipe.
- The cleanest and loudest mode — also the building block for the AMP PUSHER and COMBO stacking recipes.
- PG review: cleans up well with picking and volume rolls in BOOST/OD, and avoids muddiness at low volumes.
- MASTER dip is optional — useful only if you stack this loud BOOST into another stage; not needed standalone.

content:
Booster Trim Setup — tune the Rangemaster after a buffer
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- TREBLE BOOSTER: DOWN (classic Rangemaster — while setting trims)
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: BOOST or OVERDRIVE (so you can hear the booster)
- GAIN 1: dial from recipe — no published clock values
- VOL 1: dial from recipe — no published clock values
- TONE 1: dial from recipe — no published clock values

## Concept

The Brothers AM's treble booster has three official internal trimmers that Chase Bliss documents and blesses: Input Impedance, Output, and Bias. These are not a mod — they are the intended way to fit the Rangemaster-style booster to your rig. The load-bearing one is Input Impedance: when buffered pedals sit upstream, backing it counter-clockwise from its default fully-CW makes the booster "behave much better after a buffer." Output sets how hard the booster drives the KOT-style front end (CW = harder, CCW = more unity), and Bias sets headroom and how symmetrical the Rangemaster break-up is. This is a setup/utility patch for dialing booster character, not a performance preset — and since no exact trim settings are published beyond the defaults and directions, you tune it by ear.

## How to play it

1. Pop the back cover. Set the TREBLE BOOSTER DOWN (classic Rangemaster) and run Channel 1 in BOOST or OVERDRIVE so you can hear the booster.
2. If buffers sit in front of the AM, back the Input-Impedance trim CCW from its default fully-CW so the booster behaves well after a buffer.
3. Use the Output trim to set drive into the KOT: CW hits it harder, CCW for a more unity feel.
4. Use the Bias trim for headroom / how symmetrical the Rangemaster break-up is. Make tiny movements with a small flathead — easy to damage.

## Notes

- CB-official + manual: the three trims, their defaults, and their directions are quoted; no exact settings are published beyond the defaults/directions — dial by ear. Front-panel knob clocks are NOT sourced, so treat GAIN/VOL/TONE 1 as a dialable recipe.
- The Input-Impedance-after-a-buffer adjustment is the load-bearing one when buffered pedals sit upstream (relevant in this rig — CB Clean + Colour Box buffer the front end).
- These mirror the real King of Tone / Prince of Tone internal trims — a blessed tweak, not a mod. Fragile: tiny moves only, small flathead, easy to damage.

## Concept

The manual's two-channel template that mimics a classic two-channel amp: a low-gain OVERDRIVE on Channel 1 and a mid-gain DISTORTION on Channel 2 — two distinct stages sharing a common KOT character. Tap both footswitches at once to SWAP between them, so you have a rhythm-clean and a lead-dirty channel under your feet without stacking. 1. Set Channel 1 to OVERDRIVE at low gain (rhythm channel) and Channel 2 to DISTORTION at mid gain (lead/dirty channel).
2. Use one channel at a time — tap BOTH footswitches at once to swap between them.
3. Because the two modes clip differently, set each channel's VOL so the rhythm and lead levels are balanced.
4. Leave the treble booster MIDDLE (off) unless the lead needs more cut, then flip it DOWN (Rangemaster).

- Manual-named recipe ("Finding Your Sound"): modes are quoted; no exact knob numbers exist in any primary source — dial GAIN/VOL from the recipe.

- Watch the mode-to-mode level jump: distortion is more compressed than overdrive; balance with VOL.
- MASTER dip off — each channel's own VOL sets its level when used solo, since you're swapping rather than stacking.

content:
Clean-Up Lever — Gain 1 down, Volume up via expression
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: OVERDRIVE (the gain being cleaned up)

- VOL 1: dial from recipe — no published value

## Concept

That Pedal Show's clever external-control move: assign expression so it controls Channel 1's GAIN and Channel 2's MASTER volume at the same time, so a single sweep lets you clean up — turn the gain DOWN while the output volume keeps your level up. A foot-controlled clean-up that drops saturation without losing level, exploiting the KOT's strong cleanup behavior. Channel 1 (OVERDRIVE) is the gain being cleaned up; Channel 2 carries the MASTER (VOL 2) that the same sweep holds or raises.

## How to play it

1. Turn the MASTER dip ON so VOL 2 is the global master.
2. In the CONTROL dip bank, assign the expression pedal to control GAIN 1 and VOL 2 together (TPS's "two CCs from one expression input" idea on a MIDI controller).
3. Sweep the expression pedal toward 'clean' to roll GAIN 1 down while the master volume keeps your level up.
4. Use it like a foot-operated clean-up: less saturation, same or more level, on the fly.

- TPS-quoted: the "gain of side one + master of side two so you can clean up" assignment is quoted; no exact knob numbers — dial from recipe.
- On a Morningstar/MIDI controller: set expression rules at the BANK level (not preset), use a Ring-Active TRS-to-TRS cable, and the 'Select Exp Message' trick to drive two CCs from one input.
- Distinct from the Ramped Drone Swell (which ramps saturation UP into Channel 2): this is a cleanup-DOWN lever that preserves level.

- CHANNEL 1 MODE: BOOST (the pusher), on
- GAIN 1: low — dial from recipe, no published value
- VOL 1: raise gradually — this is how hard Ch1 pushes Ch2; dial from recipe, no published value
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: BOOST (the output), on
- GAIN 2: low — open, loud boost-drive, not a high-gain wall; dial from recipe, no published value
- VOL 2: global output (MASTER on) — set for final stage level; dial from recipe, no published value
- PRESENCE: DOWN to start (hold footswitch + TONE to set)

## Concept

Chase Bliss's canonical boost-stacking recipe, listed in the manual as "COMBO": set BOTH channels to BOOST and use Channel 1 to push Channel 2 for a versatile, loud, open-sounding drive. VOL 1 becomes the "how hard do I push" knob, Channel 2 is the output stage, and GAIN stays low on both so the result is open and loud rather than a saturated wall. CB explicitly recommends turning the MASTER dip on while exploring boost stacking, so VOL 2 becomes the global master and you can crank VOL 1 without disruptive volume jumps — the canonical fix for the VOL-1 level-snap trap.

## How to play it

1. Set BOTH channels to BOOST and turn both on.
2. Turn the MASTER dip ON so VOL 2 is the global master.
3. Gradually raise VOL 1 — this pushes Channel 2 harder for a louder, more open drive — without disruptive level jumps (MASTER absorbs them).
4. Set VOL 2 for your final stage level. Keep GAIN low on both channels for the open, loud character; bring PRESENCE up only if the tone closes in.

## Notes

- CB's own canonical boost-stacking recipe: the channel modes and MASTER-dip guidance are quoted, but no exact knob numbers are published — dial VOL/GAIN from the recipe. This is a dialable recipe, not a found/measured setting.
- The MASTER dip is load-bearing — without it, popping Channel 2 off snaps output to VOL 1's (loud) setting.
- Open and loud rather than saturated — distinct from the distortion-stack walls and from amp-pusher (which leans on the AMP).
- Slot: intended as a MIDI preset (suggested).

Dan's Overdrive Boost

Dan Steinhardt's (That Pedal Show) decade-long, road-tested King-of-Tone setting: OVERDRIVE on Channel 1 always on, with Channel 2 in BOOST used purely to add harmonics plus a small mid lift when kicked in. A transparent, reliable always-on for guitar/baritone, and a great "honest user" baseline before tailoring for the modeled VG-800 source.

## How to play it

1. Run Channel 1 (OVERDRIVE) always on as the core voice.
2. Kick Channel 2 (BOOST) in for harmonics and a small mid lift — VOL 2 only ~1 o'clock; Dan keeps it small, not a big volume jump.
3. If the tone sounds closed-in or chewy, bring PRESENCE UP "quite considerably" — Dan's on-air "changed the game" move (raise via hold-footswitch + TONE).
4. MASTER dip ON recommended so the Ch2 kick stays level-controlled.

## Notes

- Modes and the presence-up move are quoted; knob clocks are inferred starting points.
- The Presence reveal is the headline takeaway — it's the same move used to claw banjo cut back.

content:
Distortion Mode Standalone — hard-clip on one channel
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- TREBLE BOOSTER: MIDDLE (off) to start, or to taste
- CHANNEL MODE: DISTORTION — single channel on, run solo
- GAIN: to taste — keep BELOW max for the cleanest version (max brings heavily-colored compression); no published clock
- VOL: turned UP to compensate — distortion clips more and is naturally quieter than boost/OD; no published clock
- TONE: to taste — no published clock
- PRESENCE: DOWN to start, then to taste

## Concept

The AM's DISTORTION mode on its own: harder, more aggressive clipping with more compression and saturation than overdrive, while still retaining clarity. Because it clips more, it is naturally quieter and more compressed than boost or overdrive — a clipping side effect you compensate for with VOL. A single-channel hard-clip voice for a thicker, more saturated drive that stays mid-present and is never scooped.

## How to play it

1. Set one channel to DISTORTION and run it solo (single channel on).
2. Dial GAIN to taste — keep it below max for the best behavior; the highest gain brings heavily-colored compression.
3. Turn VOL up to compensate: distortion clips more and is naturally quieter/more compressed than boost or overdrive.
4. Set TONE and PRESENCE to taste (PRESENCE DOWN to start); leave the treble booster MIDDLE (off) or set it to taste.
5. Engage HI GAIN (LED goes red, ~25% more gain) only if you want it hotter; MASTER dip optional.

## Notes

- Documented mode behavior: the hard-clipping character, the natural level drop, and the "retains clarity" note are quoted from primary sources; no exact knob numbers are published — dial GAIN/VOL/TONE/PRESENCE from the recipe.
- Always mid-present, never scoopy — it cuts even at high gain.
- PG flags heavily-colored compression at the highest gain levels; the sweet spot is below max ("you don't need maximum gain").

content:
Expander — OD opened up by a bright boost
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: OVERDRIVE, always on (the foundation)
- GAIN 1: dial from recipe — no published value
- VOL 1: dial from recipe — no published value
- TONE 1: to taste
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: BOOST, kicked in to expand
- GAIN 2: dial from recipe — no published value
- VOL 2: dial from recipe — no published value
- TONE 2: turned UP (brighter) — this is what opens the OD out
- PRESENCE: DOWN to start

## Concept

The manual's EXPANDER stacking idea: Channel 1 in OVERDRIVE as the foundation voice, Channel 2 in BOOST with its TONE turned up so the second channel enhances the first — amplifying and OPENING it up rather than adding distortion. Kick Channel 2 on when you want more intensity and openness without more grit. The bright BOOST opens and amplifies the OD; it does not add clipping.

## How to play it

1. Set Channel 1 to OVERDRIVE as your always-on foundation voice.
2. Set Channel 2 to BOOST with TONE 2 turned up (brighter).
3. Kick Channel 2 on when you want more intensity and openness WITHOUT adding distortion — it amplifies and opens up Channel 1.
4. Use the MASTER dip so the Channel 2 kick (with VOL pushing) stays a controlled lift and doesn't throw stage level.

## Notes

- Manual-named stacking recipe (EXPANDER): modes and "TONE up" are quoted; no exact knob numbers are published — dial GAIN/VOL from the recipe.
- Distinct from OVERLOADER / 2-IN-1 (which uses BOOST to oversaturate the OD): here the bright BOOST opens the OD up rather than pushing it into more clipping.
- TONE-up on the boost channel is the key differentiator — it's what "opens it out."

content:
Bury Channel 2 — remote TS footswitch toggle
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: your always-on voice (e.g. BOOST or OVERDRIVE)
- GAIN 1: dial from recipe — no published value
- VOL 1: dial from recipe — no published value
- TONE 1: to taste
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: your kick-on voice (BOOST lift or OVERDRIVE), toggled by the remote footswitch
- GAIN 2: dial from recipe — no published value
- VOL 2: dial from recipe — no published value
- TONE 2: to taste
- PRESENCE: to taste
- MIDI JACK: used as TS external-footswitch input — normally-open momentary footswitch via a TS (mono) cable takes control of Channel 2's bypass automatically

## Concept

The Brothers AM's MIDI jack does double duty: with a TS (tip-sleeve, mono) cable it becomes an external-footswitch input that bypasses Channel 2. Plug any normally-open momentary footswitch in and it automatically takes control of Channel 2's on/off — no MIDI rig required. That lets you bury the AM somewhere awkward on a crowded board (or off to the side) while keeping its second channel footswitchable from anywhere. Set Channel 1 as your always-on voice and Channel 2 as the kick-on (a BOOST lift or an OVERDRIVE), and the remote stomp becomes your lead/rhythm toggle.

## How to play it

1. Set Channel 1 as your always-on voice and Channel 2 as the kick-on (boost/OD) you want to toggle remotely.
2. Plug a normally-open momentary footswitch into the MIDI jack using a TS (tip-sleeve, mono) cable — it automatically takes control of Channel 2's bypass.
3. Stomp the remote switch to toggle Channel 2 on/off from anywhere on the board.
4. Turn the MASTER dip on so the remote toggle is a controlled level change rather than a jump.

## Notes

- Documented feature: the MIDI jack's TS external-footswitch function (bypasses Channel 2, normally-open momentary, TS cable) is quoted from the source material; the tone is your choice — dial the knobs from the recipe, no published values.
- Useful for burying the AM in a crowded board while keeping its lift footswitchable, with no MIDI rig required.
- Don't use a TRS cable here — the TS (mono) cable is what selects the footswitch function (a TRS cable is for actual MIDI).
- MASTER dip on recommended so the remote Channel 2 toggle doesn't throw stage level.

content:
Hi-Gain Classic OD — +25% on the KOT voice
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: OVERDRIVE (the classic KOT voice)
- GAIN 1: dial from recipe — your normal OD setting (no published clock)
- VOL 1: dial from recipe — rebalance after HI GAIN adds level
- TONE 1: dial from recipe to taste
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: OVERDRIVE (identical to Channel 1)
- GAIN 2: dial from recipe — match Channel 1
- VOL 2: dial from recipe — match Channel 1 / rebalance
- TONE 2: dial from recipe — match Channel 1
- PRESENCE: DOWN to start
- TREBLE BOOSTER: MIDDLE (off)

## Concept

AndyDemos' way to get more out of the classic overdrive: run OVERDRIVE on both sides with identical settings, then flip the HI GAIN dip to add roughly 25% gain to all modes on that channel — the bypass LED turns from green to red to confirm it's active. As Andy puts it, it's "a cool way of getting a little bit more out of a pretty classic-sounding overdrive pedal." It's a hotter take on the standard King of Tone voice without touching the knobs — the same OD character, just pushed harder. HI GAIN here is the documented King of Tone internal-mod option, brought out to a dip switch.

## How to play it

1. Set your channel(s) to OVERDRIVE with your normal settings (run both sides identical to A/B them cleanly).
2. Flip the HI GAIN dip ON for the channel you want hotter — it adds ~25% gain to all modes; the bypass LED turns from green to red.
3. Compare with HI GAIN off to hear the extra gain on the classic OD voice.
4. Rebalance VOL if the extra gain bumps the level.

## Notes

- AndyDemos + Doug Hanson + CB-quoted: the ~25% gain figure and the LED-turns-red behavior are quoted; no exact knob numbers — dial GAIN/VOL/TONE from recipe to taste.
- HI GAIN is per channel and saves with presets; it's documented as a King of Tone internal-mod option brought to the dip switch.
- Distinct from the BAD BROS preset (both HI GAIN dips cranked into a wall) and from the DISTORTION + HI GAIN metal use — this is HI GAIN on the clean classic OD voice.
- No published knob values — phrased as a dialable recipe by design.

Joel's Rangemaster Boost
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- TREBLE BOOSTER: DOWN (classic Rangemaster)

Joel Korte's stated personal favorite space ("I live in it a lot"): the classic Rangemaster treble booster ON going into BOOST mode — open, headroomy, with "a little bit of hair." A bright, cutting always-on, and the cleanest, brightest way to get the banjo to read again after the Muff.

content:
KOT Recipe Concepts — blues breakup & transparent rhythm crunch
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- TREBLE BOOSTER: MIDDLE (off) / very low — let the TONE do the cut, not the booster
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: OVERDRIVE — the King of Tone voice for both concepts
- GAIN 1: BLUES: low / edge-of-breakup. RHYTHM CRUNCH: modest. Dial by ear — no published AM values
- VOL 1: to taste / unity (dial from recipe)
- TONE 1: BLUES: moderate. RHYTHM CRUNCH: a touch brighter for articulation. Dial by ear
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: RHYTHM CRUNCH only: a clean/boost channel ahead of the OD
- PRESENCE: DOWN to start (hold footswitch + TONE to set); raise if closed-in

## Concept

Two dial-from-ear voicing CONCEPTS pulled from a published King of Tone settings guide and recast for the AM's controls. (1) BLUES: a warm, vocal, edge-of-breakup voice that cleans up with pick attack and guitar volume, and growls when you dig in. (2) TRANSPARENT RHYTHM CRUNCH: a tight, articulate crunch that firms up the low end and adds bite while staying out of the way of the guitar's natural tone. The honest framing matters here — the guide's actual Volume-A/Volume-B/Drive/Tone numbers are for the ORIGINAL Analogman King of Tone, not the Brothers AM, so this seed keeps only the relative directions (low/modest drive, lower vs higher tone), never the wrong-pedal clock numbers.

## How to play it

1. BLUES: set Channel 1 to OVERDRIVE at low / edge-of-breakup gain with a moderate TONE — back off your picking and it cleans up, dig in and it growls; vocal and dynamic.
2. RHYTHM CRUNCH: run a clean/boost channel into an OVERDRIVE channel at modest gain with a slightly brighter TONE — it tightens the low end and adds bite while staying transparent.
3. Use the TONE knob (not the treble booster) for articulation here so the crunch stays uncolored.
4. Dial entirely by ear: do NOT copy the source's number values — they're for the original KOT, not this pedal.

## Notes

- HONESTY: the Guitar Chalk guide prints specific Volume-A/Volume-B/Drive/Tone numbers for the ORIGINAL Analogman King of Tone — verified, NOT the Brothers AM. The AM has no such numeric scale (GAIN 1/2, VOL 1/2, TONE 1/2 + booster/modes/dips), so the numbers are deliberately omitted; only the relative-direction CONCEPTS are kept.
- Edge-of-breakup territory partly overlaps existing voices — kept as a compact, clearly-labelled "dial-by-ear blues/rhythm" concept reference rather than two separate number-bearing patches.
- If you want the booster-flavored versions, layer the Rangemaster from the treble-booster patches on top.

content:
Moment Maker — specialty channel + always-on
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- TREBLE BOOSTER: MIDDLE (off) for the always-on channel; UP (bright) or DOWN (Rangemaster) feeds the specialty channel's sparkle
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: OVERDRIVE — the dependable always-on voice
- GAIN 2: low/medium — dial from recipe (no published value)
- VOL 2: level-match to the specialty channel so the swap isn't a jump — dial from recipe
- TONE 2: to taste — dial from recipe (no published value)
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: BOOST — the airy/nostalgic specialty voice (brighter/cleaner)
- GAIN 1: low/clean for an open, airy voicing — dial from recipe
- VOL 1: level-match to the always-on channel — dial from recipe
- TONE 1: brighter than Ch2 for sparkle — dial from recipe
- PRESENCE: start DOWN (raise via hold-footswitch + TONE if needed)

## Concept

The manual's MOMENT MAKER two-channel idea: keep one channel as your reliable always-on sound and reserve the other for an airy, nostalgic, specialty voice you bring in only for a moment. The two channels become a workhorse and a special-occasion tone rather than a stacked pair — Channel 2 in OVERDRIVE as the dependable rhythm/lead voice, Channel 1 set up as a distinct brighter/cleaner specialty sound (e.g. BOOST with the treble booster engaged for sparkle).

## How to play it

1. Set one channel as your dependable always-on voice (main rhythm/lead tone) — e.g. Channel 2 OVERDRIVE at low/medium gain.
2. Set the other channel for a distinct specialty sound — airy/nostalgic, e.g. Channel 1 BOOST with the treble booster engaged for sparkle, or a brighter/cleaner voicing.
3. Use the always-on channel by default; tap both footswitches to swap into the specialty voice for a single moment, then swap back.
4. Balance each channel's VOL so the swap isn't a jarring level change. Start PRESENCE DOWN and raise only if the tone is closed-in.

## Notes

- Manual-named recipe: the concept is quoted, but the specialty voice is open-ended — so all knob values are dial-from-recipe, with no published numbers.
- This is a workflow/role idea, not a fixed tone — treat the specialty channel as a blank slate for whatever "moment" you need.
- DIPs: none required. Consider flipping MASTER on if levels jump between the two voices.

content:
Momentary Boost — hold-to-engage lift
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- MOTOBYP dip (accent channel): ON — that channel's footswitch engages only while held (momentary)
- MASTER dip: ON (recommended) so the held accent is a controlled lift, not a level explosion
- ACCENT CHANNEL MODE: BOOST for a clean held lift, or DISTORTION for a momentary saturation hit
- VOL (accent channel): sets the size of the accent — dial from recipe, no published value
- GAIN (accent channel): sets how much drive the held hit adds — dial from recipe, no published value
- OTHER CHANNEL MODE: your normal always-on tone (MOTOBYP off on this one)
- PRESENCE: start DOWN

## Concept

Use the MOTOBYP ("momentary to bypass") dip so a footswitch engages its channel only while held — a hold-down momentary boost or kill. Set the accent channel as a BOOST (clean lift) or DISTORTION (saturation hit) with MOTOBYP on, and you get an on-the-fly accent: stomp-and-hold for a lead lift or a momentary saturation hit, release to drop back instantly. The other channel runs your normal always-on tone, untouched.

## How to play it

1. Turn the MOTOBYP dip ON for the channel you want as a momentary accent.
2. Set that channel to BOOST (for a clean held lift) or DISTORTION (for a momentary saturation hit). Dial its VOL/GAIN to size the accent.
3. Run your normal tone on the other channel (leave its MOTOBYP off).
4. Stomp and HOLD the accent footswitch for the lift; release to drop back instantly. Keep MASTER on so the held accent stays a controlled lift rather than a level jump. Start PRESENCE DOWN.

## Notes

- Documented feature: MOTOBYP (hold-to-engage momentary bypass) is quoted across sources; the tone you put on the channel is open, so all knob values are dial-from-recipe with no published numbers.
- Great for quick on-the-fly boosts where you don't want a latched state — Guitar.com calls out the momentary mode for "quick on-the-fly boosts."
- Can also be used as a momentary KILL depending on routing.
- MASTER on is recommended here so the held accent is a controlled lift, not a level explosion.

content:
Piera's Beano-into-KOT — thick & crunchy / Marshall-ify a Fender
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- TREBLE BOOSTER: DOWN (classic Rangemaster / Beano Boost)
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: OVERDRIVE (the King of Tone voice — Piera's favorite is booster INTO the KOT)
- GAIN 1: enough for crunch but below max — dial from recipe (no published values)
- VOL 1: to taste (dial from recipe)
- TONE 1: to taste (dial from recipe)
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: off, or a low BOOST underneath

## Concept

Mike Piera's (Analog Man) own stated favorite: the Beano Boost / Rangemaster treble booster running INTO the King of Tone — "it's thick and crunchy." This is the pairing the whole pedal is architected around — the booster is fixed at the front, feeding Channel 1. Piera also notes the treble boost "can turn a Fender amp somewhat into a Marshall" — a midrange-forward grind. Run the Rangemaster into Channel 1 in OVERDRIVE (the KOT voice) for Piera's signature thick, crunchy lead.

## How to play it

1. Set the treble booster DOWN (classic Rangemaster / Beano Boost).
2. Set Channel 1 to OVERDRIVE — the booster feeds the King of Tone circuit, Piera's stated favorite pairing.
3. Dial GAIN 1 for a thick, crunchy lead; keep below max for the touch response. Into a clean Fender turned up, this leans the amp toward a Marshall-like grind.
4. Plug near the front / straight from guitar (low input impedance dislikes buffers ahead); if buffered upstream, back the internal Input-Impedance trim CCW.
5. If the tone feels closed-in, raise PRESENCE (hold the footswitch + turn TONE).

## Notes

- Artist-stated: Piera names the Rangemaster/treble boost INTO the King of Tone as his favorite — "thick and crunchy"; and "adding the treble boost can turn a Fender amp somewhat into a Marshall." No knob numbers are published in any source — controls above are a dialable recipe, not sourced values.
- Distinct from Joel's Rangemaster Boost (booster into BOOST mode) — Piera's is booster into the OVERDRIVE/KOT voice.
- The whole pedal is architected around this pairing (booster fixed at front, linked to Channel 1).

content:
Piera's Boost-Into-OD — more dirt, same volume
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: BOOST (feeds the OD's input first via the AM's fixed series order)
- VOL 1: moderate — slam the OD's input, don't raise master (dial from recipe)
- GAIN 1: to taste — how hard the boost hits the OD (dial from recipe)
- TONE 1: to taste (dial from recipe)
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: OVERDRIVE (receives the boosted signal)
- GAIN 2: set for your OD voice (dial from recipe)
- VOL 2: to taste — your OD/master level (dial from recipe)
- TONE 2: to taste (dial from recipe)
- PRESENCE: DOWN to start, bring UP if the saturated voice gets closed-in

## Concept

Mike Piera's (Analog Man) alternate King-of-Tone stacking philosophy: run the BOOST *into* the OVERDRIVE rather than after it, to push more distortion out of the OD channel WITHOUT a big jump in overall volume. This is the move for players who already have the level they need but want more saturation — the deliberate counterpart to the boost-after-OD thickener. In the AM's fixed series (Channel 1 → Channel 2), setting Channel 1 to BOOST and Channel 2 to OVERDRIVE makes the boost slam the OD's input for you.

## How to play it

1. Set Channel 1 to BOOST and Channel 2 to OVERDRIVE — the boost hits the OD's input first (the AM's series order does this for you).
2. Keep the boost's VOL moderate so it slams the OD rather than raising master volume.
3. Set GAIN 2 for your OD voice; the boosted input will push more saturation through it.
4. Result: more distortion/saturation from the OD with little additional volume.
5. Choose this vs boost-after-OD based on whether you want more GAIN (this) or more VOLUME (boost-after).

## Notes

- Artist-stated (Mike Piera, Guitar World): "others like to run the boost into the overdrive to add more distortion without too much additional volume" — no knob numbers are published, so all values here are a dialable recipe, not sourced settings.
- This is the gain-leaning counterpart to the boost-AFTER-OD approach (boost after the dirt = thicken + volume), covered by the existing Dan's Overdrive Boost patch. A separate DIST←OD pairing is the heavier "saturation stack" voice if you want more than the OD channel gives.
- The MASTER dip is optional: leave it off to keep this purely a gain change; turn it on only if you want VOL 2 to act as a global master and hold output put.
- Great for tightening into a higher-gain lead voice while staying at stage level.

content:
Post-Muff Tightener (always-on default)
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- TREBLE BOOSTER: MIDDLE (off); flip DOWN/Rangemaster only when banjo needs cut
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: BOOST (or very low OVERDRIVE), only channel ON
- GAIN 2: 9 o'clock (low — tighten, not gain)
- VOL 2: carefully level-matched so Hizumitas-engaged vs AM-engaged is unity (global master)
- TONE 2: noon then to taste
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: OFF
- PRESENCE 2: nudged UP slightly (hold Ch2 footswitch + TONE 2) to recover upper-mid cut the Hizumitas darkened

## Concept

The rig's everyday always-on job: tighten, re-level, and add cut to the Hizumitas Muff wall WITHOUT adding more gain. Hands a clean, predictable line level to the Longsword and the whole time/tape chain. The 2-IN-1 idea executed as a low-gain single-channel tightener — the AM should be on more often than not, and the whole point is no extra gain, just EQ, level, and a rounded-off decay handed cleanly downstream.

## How to play it

1. Run Channel 2 only (BOOST, or very low OVERDRIVE) with GAIN 2 low at ~9 — goal is tighten, not gain.
2. Carefully level-match VOL 2 so Hizumitas-engaged vs AM-engaged is unity.
3. Nudge PRESENCE 2 up slightly (hold Ch2 footswitch + TONE 2) to recover the upper-mid cut the Hizumitas darkened.
4. Keep the MASTER dip ON (VOL 2 is global master — prevents the VOL-1 level-snap trap, keeps downstream level stable).
5. Optionally turn PRES LINK 2 ON for a more open, full-range response on the modeled VG-800 source.

## Notes

- These are designed starting points, not found settings — the manual prints diagrams, not numbers.
- Flip the treble booster DOWN/Rangemaster only when the banjo needs cut.
- PRES LINK is the move for the modeled source.
- Slot: intended as a MIDI preset (suggested).

content:
Pres Link Open — full-range/synth voicing
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- CHANNEL MODE (channel in use): BOOST (most open / most headroom) or OVERDRIVE for grit
- GAIN: modest — keep the wide-band source clear, not squished (dial from recipe)
- VOL: dial from recipe to taste
- TONE: your single open/dark-to-bright control once PRES LINK is on — sweep to the most open, full-range response (dial from recipe)
- PRESENCE: now slaved to TONE via PRES LINK (no longer set independently)
- TREBLE BOOSTER: MIDDLE (off) to keep it neutral, or to taste

## Concept

Chase Bliss's own recommendation for full-frequency sources — synths, modeled and divided signals. Engage the PRES LINK dip on the channel you're running and the TONE knob now controls TONE and PRESENCE together, giving a more open, transparent, full-range response from a single, more dramatic tone control. This is the documented move for the modeled VG-800 output and any synth or wide-bandwidth source: BOOST keeps the most headroom and stays open, while OVERDRIVE adds grit if you want it.

## How to play it

1. Engage the PRES LINK dip for the channel you're running — now TONE controls TONE and PRESENCE simultaneously.
2. Set that channel to BOOST (most open) or OVERDRIVE for some grit.
3. Sweep the TONE knob to find the most open, full-range response — CB recommends this for full-frequency instruments like a synth.
4. Keep GAIN modest so the wide-band source stays clear, not squished.

## Notes

- CB-recommended: the PRES LINK behavior and the "use it for full-frequency/synth sources" recommendation are quoted; no exact knob numbers — dial from recipe.
- On the modeled VG-800 source, BOOST + PRES LINK is the documented move for the most open, full-range response.
- PRES LINK "makes for a more dramatic tone control" — a wider tonal sweep from one knob. Distinct from Pres-Link Tone Sweep (which chases the dramatic single-knob move as a performance tool).
- No published knob values — phrased as a dialable recipe by design.

content:
Pres-Link Tone Sweep — dark-to-bright in one knob
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- CHANNEL MODE: DISTORTION (Joel's demo) for the most dramatic sweep; any mode works
- GAIN: up — the higher the gain, the more dramatic the dark→bright sweep; dial from recipe, no published clock
- TONE: the single dark→bright control (now sweeping TONE + PRESENCE together via PRES LINK); dial from recipe
- VOL: dial from recipe
- PRESENCE: follows TONE while PRES LINK is ON — no separate setting
- PRES LINK: ON (the dip that links TONE + PRESENCE for the dramatic single-knob sweep)
- EXP/CV: optional — assign to TONE via the CONTROL (right-side) dips so your foot sweeps dark→bright

## Concept

Chase Bliss's demonstrated PRES LINK trick: turn the PRES LINK dip on so TONE and PRESENCE move together, collapsing two tone controls into one dramatic knob that sweeps from very dark to very bright. Joel Korte demos it in DISTORTION with the gain way up (CB Technical Demo) — the same TONE knob takes you across the whole tonal range in a single move. It's a performance-minded voicing: one knob (or one expression sweep) does the big tonal moves on a hard-clipped voice. Related to, but distinct from, the full-range/synth PRES LINK patch — this one chases the dramatic single-knob tone sweep as a performance tool.

## How to play it

1. Turn the PRES LINK dip ON for your channel — TONE and PRESENCE now move together.
2. Set the channel to DISTORTION with the gain up (Joel's demo) for the most dramatic effect.
3. Sweep the TONE knob: it now goes from very dark to very bright in one move.
4. For a performance move, assign an expression pedal to TONE on the CONTROL (right-side) dip bank so your foot does the dark→bright sweep — a filter-sweep-like effect on a hard-clipped voice.

## Notes

- CB-quoted: the PRES LINK behavior and the dark→bright demo (DISTORTION, gain up) are quoted; no exact knob numbers are published — dial GAIN/TONE/VOL from the recipe.
- Related to but distinct from the full-range/synth PRES LINK patch: this one chases the dramatic single-knob tone sweep as a performance tool, not the full tonal range for synth-like voicing.
- Pairs well with expression-over-TONE for a filter-sweep-like effect on a hard-clipped voice; on a Morningstar/MIDI controller, set expression rules at the BANK level, not the preset level (documented gotcha).

content:
Presence-Up — open out the closed/chewy tone
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- CHANNEL MODE: OVERDRIVE (or any — this is a presence move layered on whatever voice)
- GAIN: to taste (dial from recipe)
- TONE: to taste — and used to SET presence: hold that channel's footswitch and turn TONE
- PRESENCE (per channel): brought UP from the default fully-down — hold that channel's footswitch + turn its TONE knob (up for cut/air, down to soften harsh highs); no published value, dial from recipe
- TREBLE BOOSTER: to taste

## Concept

The headline hidden-control move from the King of Tone world, surfaced on the AM. Presence ships fully down — closed, mid-focused, chewy — and bringing the hidden PRESENCE up "changes the game" and opens the tone right out. On the original KOT this was an internal trim pot; here you hold the channel's footswitch and turn its TONE knob to set it. Some players wrote the KOT off until they found this. Treat it as a general "open it out / add air or tame harshness" patch for any voice that feels boxed-in — the standalone technique, layered on whatever drive you're running.

## How to play it

1. Start with whatever overdrive/boost voice feels closed-in, mid-focused, or chewy.
2. Hold that channel's footswitch and turn the TONE knob — this sets the hidden PRESENCE (ships fully down; was an internal trim on the original KOT).
3. Bring PRESENCE up noticeably until the tone "opens out" and the top end/clarity return; reduce it to soften harsh highs.
4. Don't overdo it (Mick noted Dan went a touch far). Or engage PRES LINK to set presence with TONE on the fly, or drive it via MIDI.

## Notes

- KOT/TPS/CB/PG-quoted: presence ships fully down, was an internal trim on the original KOT, and presence-up "opens it out / changed the game" — but no numeric value is published, so dial it from the recipe rather than a fixed clock.
- Joel's caveat: he prefers presence down and got confused mid-development whenever it was accidentally up — this is a deliberate move, not a default.
- Generalizes the presence reveal; the banjo-specific version is Banjo-Lead Cut Recovery and Dan's Overdrive Boost folds it in — this is the standalone technique.

content:
Ramped Drone Swell
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: OVERDRIVE (or DISTORTION) as the bed
- GAIN 2: 11 o'clock
- VOL 2: master
- TONE 2: noon
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: BOOST, on (the ramp target)
- GAIN 1: starts low (swept up by EXP/CV)
- TREBLE BOOSTER: MIDDLE or DOWN
- PRESENCE: DOWN
- EXP/CV: sweep heel→toe into a held chord to bloom the drone (assigned to GAIN 1 / VOL 1 via CONTROL dips)

## Concept

A drone-build tool: swell the saturation/intensity of the push into Channel 2 under a sustained banjo/baritone chord, WITHOUT a level spike, before the Longsword and the End Board chew on it. The signature sustained-wall builder — Channel 2 (OVERDRIVE/DISTORTION) is the bed, Channel 1 (BOOST) is the ramp target, and an expression pedal or 0–5V CV sweeps the push.

## How to play it

1. Set Channel 2 (OVERDRIVE or DISTORTION) as the bed; Channel 1 (BOOST) on as the ramp target with GAIN 1 starting low.
2. Assign EXP (or 0–5V CV) → GAIN 1 (or VOL 1) via the CONTROL dip bank (right side); set polarity so HEEL = no push, TOE = full push; SWEEP dip to taste.
3. Keep the MASTER dip ON so the ramp adds saturation/intensity, not a level jump.
4. Sweep heel→toe into a held chord to bloom the drone.

## Notes

- Designed starting points, not found settings.
- CONTROLLER GOTCHA — on a Morningstar/MIDI controller, set the expression rule at the BANK level, not the preset level, and use a TRS-to-TRS cable with the omniport "Ring Active." If the swell isn't responding, that bank-vs-preset config is the first thing to check.
- Slot: intended as a MIDI preset (suggested).

content:
Recorded-Wrong Re-Clip
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- TREBLE BOOSTER: UP (brighter/strident — shaves lows, adds the 'wrong' edge, stacks well with downstream effects)
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: DISTORTION
- GAIN 1: 1–2 o'clock
- VOL 1: 1 o'clock (push into Ch2)
- TONE 1: 1 o'clock
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: DISTORTION or OVERDRIVE
- GAIN 2: 1 o'clock
- VOL 2: master
- PRESENCE: high or PRES-LINKed for the brittle, over-bright character

## Concept

Lean INTO the rig's "recorded-wrong" aesthetic: re-clip the already-modeled, already-saturated VG-800 + Muff signal with hard-clipping DISTORTION + HI GAIN so the heavily-colored compression PG warns about becomes the FEATURE — a squished, gated, mis-biased wall feeding the granular/tape stages downstream. The compression is the point; let the granular/tape stages feed on it.

## How to play it

1. Set the TREBLE BOOSTER UP (brighter/strident — shaves lows, adds the "wrong" edge, stacks well with downstream effects per AndyDemos).
2. Channel 1 = DISTORTION with HI GAIN 1 ON, GAIN 1 ~1–2, VOL 1 ~1 pushing into Channel 2.
3. Channel 2 = DISTORTION or OVERDRIVE, GAIN 2 ~1, VOL 2 as master.
4. Turn PRES LINK on a channel + sweep TONE for the dramatic dark→bright move (CB tech demo demos this in DISTORTION with gain way up).
5. Run PRESENCE high or PRES-LINKed for the brittle, over-bright character; keep MASTER dip ON.

## Notes

- Designed starting points, not found settings.
- Honest flag — this intentionally runs OPPOSITE the rig's usual low-gain-tightener advice. Use it as a deliberate effect (post-punk brittle wall, doom squish), not the default. Embrace the "heavily colored compression at the highest gain levels" as the texture.
- Slot: intended as a MIDI preset (suggested).

content:
Sunny Skies (full 3-circuit stack)
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- TREBLE BOOSTER: ENGAGED — start DOWN (Rangemaster), or UP (bright) to taste; NOT middle
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: DISTORTION
- GAIN 1: noon
- VOL 1: 11 o'clock (the push into Ch2)
- TONE 1: 1 o'clock (bright/focused)
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: OVERDRIVE
- GAIN 2: 11 o'clock
- VOL 2: noon
- TONE 2: 1 o'clock (bright/focused)
- PRESENCE 1: DOWN to start
- PRESENCE 2: DOWN to start; raise if chewy
- Slot/Bank: Onboard P2 (default bank)

## Concept

The "mixture of everything" factory preset — all three circuits in series for a bright, focused, charged voice: treble boost into DISTORTION (Ch1) into OVERDRIVE (Ch2). Shows off what the full `BOOST → CHANNEL 1 → CHANNEL 2` series stack does. Bright and forward; useful when you want the AM to actually be the dirt rather than just shape the Muff.

## How to play it

1. Engage both channels with the treble booster on — Ch1 feeds Ch2.
2. VOL 1 at ~11 sets the push into Channel 2.
3. Expect a level jump vs P1 (distortion clips differently) — rebalance with VOL 2 or set the MASTER dip ON.
4. If it sounds chewy, raise PRESENCE 2.

## Notes

- Modes are quoted; all knob clocks are inferred starting points (manual prints diagrams, not numbers).
- CB lists the treble boost as ON for this preset — pick DOWN/classic Rangemaster or UP/bright per taste, but not MIDDLE.

content:
TPS Boost-After-Dirt — lift another overdrive
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- TREBLE BOOSTER: MIDDLE (off) for a neutral lift, or DOWN (Rangemaster) for extra cut
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: BOOST (no diodes — most headroom, most open); used as the boost after another already-dirty drive
- GAIN 1: low — clean lift (dial from recipe)
- VOL 1: set for the lift amount (dial from recipe)
- TONE 1: to taste (dial from recipe)
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: off (single-channel boost after dirt)

## Concept

That Pedal Show's demonstration of the famous King of Tone boost trick: set another drive (e.g. a Bluesbreaker) dirty, then place the AM's BOOST after it — the boost lifts the already-overdriven signal and "gives it all the love," with a frequency that gets you heard 100%. The KOT principle: a clean boost AFTER a dirt pedal increases volume and cut without adding much distortion. This is the generic boost-after-another-pedal move; the rig-specific Clean Push into the Longsword is its own patch. Note: the AM has more bottom end than a Prince of Tone, per TPS.

## How to play it

1. Get a good dirty sound from another overdrive earlier in your chain (TPS used a Bluesbreaker).
2. Set one AM channel to BOOST and place the AM after that dirt.
3. Use the BOOST to lift the already-overdriven signal — it adds volume and cut, not much distortion, and "gives it all the love."
4. Keep GAIN low; this is a clean lift. Add the Rangemaster (booster DOWN) if you want even more cut.

## Notes

- No published knob numbers — controls are a dialable recipe, not sourced values. TPS-quoted character + the analogman.com principle (boost-after-dirt trick) are what's quoted; the clocks are starting points to dial in.
- This is the generic "boost after another pedal" move; the rig-specific Clean Push into the Longsword already exists as its own patch — this is the general technique.
- Analogman's own framing: a clean boost AFTER a dirt pedal increases volume without adding much distortion (vs INTO a dirt pedal, which adds distortion).

content:
TPS Vocal Lead — treble booster into an overdriven channel
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- TREBLE BOOSTER: DOWN (classic Rangemaster — the vocal-lead voice); UP for a brighter cut through a dark/humbucker rig
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: OVERDRIVE (or DISTORTION) — already overdriven is where the booster shines
- GAIN 1: up enough to be clearly overdriven before the booster hits it — dial from recipe, no published clock
- VOL 1: to taste — dial from recipe, no published clock
- TONE 1: to taste — dial from recipe, no published clock
- PRESENCE 1: raise if the tone is closed-in (hold Ch1 footswitch + TONE 1) — the documented 'opens it out' move
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: off, or a low boost

## Concept

That Pedal Show's key treble-booster insight: a treble booster into a clean amp can be unpleasant, but into a channel that's ALREADY overdriven it comes into its own and takes you to a really vocal lead tone — Mick Ronson / Brian May territory. Engage the booster on Channel 1, push Channel 1 into overdrive/distortion, and lean on the booster for a singing, cutting lead. This is the general lead principle; the rig-specific banjo version lives in Banjo-Lead Cut Recovery.

## How to play it

1. Set Channel 1 to OVERDRIVE (or DISTORTION) and get it clearly into breakup first — the booster is unpleasant into a CLEAN amp but sings into an already-overdriven channel.
2. Engage the treble booster on Channel 1 — DOWN (classic Rangemaster) for the vocal voice, UP for more cut through a dark/humbucker rig.
3. Play leads — you're after the singing, vocal Mick Ronson / Brian May tone.
4. If it sounds closed-in or chewy, bring PRESENCE up (hold the Ch1 footswitch + turn TONE 1) or engage PRES LINK 1 to open it out.

## Notes

- TPS-quoted + PG humbucker-cut note: the "booster into an already-overdriven channel = vocal lead" principle, the presence-up reveal, and the top-end+booster cut for dark humbucker rigs are all quoted; no exact knob numbers exist in any primary source — dial GAIN/VOL/TONE from the recipe.
- Distinct from Banjo-Lead Cut Recovery (which targets banjo articulation at low gain in a specific rig): this is the general lead-voice principle that wants the channel already overdriven.
- Expect a higher noise floor with the booster on — normal when emphasizing upper-mids/treble.

content:
Treble-Booster A/B — two booster voices into a boost
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- TREBLE BOOSTER: A/B between DOWN (classic Rangemaster, upper-mid) and UP (brighter/strident, shaves lows, adds sparkle)
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: BOOST (bare-bones — lets the booster voices speak)
- GAIN 1: cranked a bit while A/Bing (exact clock not published — dial from recipe)
- VOL 1: noon
- TONE 1: noon
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: off (single-channel)
- PRESENCE: DOWN

## Concept

AndyDemos' bare-bones method for hearing the two treble-booster flavors side by side: put the booster at the front into Channel 1 in BOOST mode and A/B the two voices. The classic Rangemaster voice (DOWN) has an upper-mid emphasis (Marshall-ish bite); the other voice (UP) shaves off even more low end and is brighter, more strident, and adds clean high-end sparkle — great for opening up dark humbucker rigs and for stacking with other effects. A learning/utility patch for picking your booster flavor before committing it to a song.

## How to play it

1. Set Channel 1 to BOOST and leave Channel 2 off — bare-bones so the booster voices come through clearly.
2. Toggle the TREBLE BOOSTER DOWN (classic Rangemaster) and play — note the upper-mid emphasis (Marshall-ish bite).
3. Toggle the TREBLE BOOSTER UP and play — note it shaves more low end and is brighter, more strident, with clean high-end sparkle (good for dark humbuckers).
4. Pick the voice you want; the bright/UP voice stacks especially well with other effects downstream.

## Notes

- AndyDemos + Guitar.com-quoted: the two booster voices and their character (upper-mid Rangemaster vs bright/sparkle) are quoted; knob clocks are NOT published — this is a dialable recipe, so crank GAIN 1 a bit while A/Bing per Andy rather than treating any clock value as sourced.
- MIDDLE = OFF (pure classic KOT, no Rangemaster) — the third toggle position, included for completeness.
- Use this as the A/B utility, then feed the chosen voice into Joel's / Piera's booster patches.

content:
Whole-Stack Scene — one PC recalls the AM with the board
Device: Chase Bliss Brothers AM

Settings:
- CHANNEL 2 MODE: per the chosen song tone — dial from recipe (no published value)
- GAIN 2: per the chosen tone — no published values
- VOL 2: per the chosen tone (optionally the global master via MASTER dip) — no published values
- TONE 2: per the chosen tone — no published values
- CHANNEL 1 MODE: per the chosen song tone — dial from recipe (no published value)
- GAIN 1: per the chosen tone — no published values
- VOL 1: per the chosen tone — no published values
- TONE 1: per the chosen tone — no published values
- TREBLE BOOSTER: per the chosen tone — saves with the preset
- PRESENCE: per the chosen tone — presence saves with the preset
- MIDI channel: shared CB-stack channel (default ch.2)
- Save: hold a footswitch ~3 sec (or send a PC while holding both footswitches) to store the preset
- Onboard recall: footswitch = left/right preset; both/middle = LIVE

## Concept

A MIDI/preset integration patch rather than a single tone. Beyond the 4 onboard presets, the Brothers AM can store a large bank of drive settings over MIDI. The trick: save the AM's preset to the SAME Program Change number that the rest of the Chase Bliss board uses for a given song, on a shared MIDI channel. Now one Program Change from your sequencer recalls a whole-stack scene — the AM's drive setting fires alongside every other CB pedal, no per-pedal recall needed. Everything saves with the preset: all AM controls, every dip state (modes, HI GAIN, MASTER, BANK, PRES LINK), and presence. Optionally repurpose VOL 2 as a global master (MASTER dip) so the recalled scene has one output control. The tone you save is whatever the song needs — use any of the other AM patches as your starting voice.

## How to play it

1. Dial the AM to the drive tone a given song needs (use any of the other patches as the starting tone — this patch supplies the routing, not the knob values).
2. Put the AM on the shared CB-stack MIDI channel (default 2) and save its preset to the SAME Program Change number the rest of the CB pedals use for that song (hold a footswitch ~3 sec, or send a PC while holding both footswitches).
3. Now a single Program Change from your sequencer recalls the AM's preset alongside the whole board — a one-PC scene per song; the dip states AND presence recall too.
4. Optionally set the MASTER dip so VOL 2 acts as a global master, giving the recalled scene one output control.
5. Remember the AM gets MIDI over the ring-active 1/4" TRS jack via a powered Chase Bliss MIDIbox — power the MIDIbox.

## Notes

- Documented integration, dialable tone: the PC-recall behavior, the shared-number whole-stack scene, the uniform CB-stack CC map, dips-and-presence-save-with-preset, the master-volume MASTER dip, and the MIDIbox requirement are all documented. The actual tone you save is your choice — dial the knobs from recipe; no knob values are published here, so none are presented as sourced.
- Common gotcha: forgetting to power the MIDIbox. The AM takes TRS-MIDI, not native 5-pin DIN or USB.
- Sources differ on the exact MIDI preset count (commonly cited around ~122/128 beyond the 4 onboard) — treat it as "a large bank" rather than a hard number. The uniform CB-stack CC map applies for remote control of individual params within the scene.

All AM controls AND dip states (modes, HI GAIN, MASTER, BANK, PRES LINK, presence) save with the preset. content:
Adaptive Envelope — Stay-Out-of-the-Way Comp
Device: Chase Bliss Clean

Settings:
- Release: in Hidden Options = Envelope Type select: ADAPTIVE or COMBO (normally L Fast 50ms / Mid User 650ms / R Slow 1.5s)
- Attack: sets the SLOWEST attack bound — the envelope adapts faster within it (dial to taste from your comp recipe)
- Dynamics: to taste (dial from underlying comp recipe)
- Sensitivity: by LED (dial from underlying comp recipe)
- Wet: to taste (dial from underlying comp recipe)
- Dry: to taste (dial from underlying comp recipe)
- EQ: to taste (dial from underlying comp recipe)
- Mode: to taste
- Physics: to taste

## Concept

A behind-the-scenes responsiveness tweak that layers under any comp recipe. In Hidden Options, switch the envelope follower's ENVELOPE TYPE from the default Analog to **Adaptive** (or **Combo**). Adaptive makes attack/release dynamically adjust to your playing loudness — it helps fast playing keep its energy and stays out of the way, where Analog is smoother but more static. **Combo** pairs Analog attack with Adaptive release for the best of both: the responsiveness of Adaptive with the accuracy of Analog. With an adaptive type, ATTACK and RELEASE now set the *slowest possible* speeds, and the envelope adjusts faster within that range based on how hard you play.

## How to play it

1. Start from any comp recipe you like (e.g. Tight & Lively for funk/fast dense playing).
2. **Hold both footswitches** to open Hidden Options.
3. Set the **Release toggle (= Envelope Type in Hidden Options)** to **ADAPTIVE** for a reactive follower, or **COMBO** for Analog-attack + Adaptive-release.
4. Treat your ATTACK/RELEASE settings as the *slowest* bounds; the envelope will adapt faster within them based on your playing.
5. Use under fast/dense passages to keep energy without over-squishing; A/B against Analog to hear the smoother-but-static contrast.

## Notes

- Mode selection is a documented manufacturer feature; the **comp knob values here are a dialable recipe, not published settings** — borrow exact values from whatever comp patch you layer this under, then just flip the Envelope Type.
- Manual: "Adaptive is good at staying out of the way and helps faster playing maintain its energy, but it's not quite as smooth as Analog."
- Combo = "responsiveness of Adaptive with the accuracy of Analog."
- Layers under any other comp patch — pairs especially well with Tight & Lively for funk / fast dense playing.
- All CUSTOMIZE dips OFF; only the Hidden Options Envelope Type changes.

provenance.title: Adaptive Envelope — Stay-Out-of-the-Way Comp
provenance.description: A Hidden Options responsiveness tweak — switch the envelope follower to Adaptive (or Combo) so attack/release dynamically adjust to your playing loudness, helping fast/dense passages keep their energy while staying out of the way. Layers under any comp recipe. Manufacturer feature per the Clean manual's Envelope Type section.

content:
Always-On Huge Fuzz Feeder
Device: Chase Bliss Clean

Settings:
- Sensitivity: HIGH (by LED, hot enough that quiet notes still move it)
- Dynamics: noon-1:00 (hard limiting)
- Wet: 1:00-2:00 (hot, to slam the next pedal)
- Dry: OFF
- Attack: 9:00 (fast)
- EQ: noon (off)
- Release: Mid (User 650ms)
- Mode: Mid (Manual)
- Physics: Mid (stable)
- Slot/Bank: MIDI-recallable doom-feeder preset alongside the fuzz-board scene

## Concept

A hard-limiting feeder designed to slam the MXR 108 / Hizumitas / Longsword evenly so that even quiet picking triggers full downstream saturation — the "always massive" doom voice. High Sensitivity plus limiting flattens dynamics into a hot, consistent drive level.

## How to play it

1. **Set Sensitivity by ear to the left LED first** — run it HIGH, hot enough that quiet notes still move it.
2. Dynamics ~noon–1:00 (hard limiting).
3. Wet ~1–2:00 (hot, to slam the next pedal); Dry off.
4. Attack ~9:00 (fast); EQ noon; toggles at Mid.

## Notes

- **HONEST:** Wet here is comp make-up gain, not a pristine clean boost — plenty hot to slam the fuzz but not transparent.
- To let the fuzz BREATHE with your attack instead, back Dynamics DOWN out of limiting (toward 10:00 comp). Don't over-compress into the Hizumitas (Big-Muff style) if you want the dynamic bloom.
- All dips OFF.
