content:
Tube Sag — Sputtering Overload
Device: Chase Bliss Clean

Settings:
- Dynamics: final quarter of the sweep (Sag zone, past 3:00)
- Sensitivity: fairly high so digging in triggers the sag
- Wet: BOOST to compensate for the level loss
- Attack: moderate
- Release: Mid (User ~650ms) — moderate
- Dry: to taste for body
- EQ: to taste
- Bypass FS (hold): HOLD to momentarily max out Clean's Sag effect — slam full sputter on the fly

## Concept

Past 3:00, Dynamics leaves compression behind and enters Sag — Clean's simulated overloaded-tube state. Per the manual, "your signal falls out, falters, and sputters as you play harder." Push Dynamics into the last quarter of its sweep, set Sensitivity fairly high so digging in trips the sag, and boost Wet to recover the lost level. The result is a touch-sensitive "broken" clean that reacts to dynamics like a starved amp: it holds together when you ease off and collapses when you dig in. For a performed version, just HOLD the BYPASS footswitch to slam max Sag in the middle of a phrase.

## How to play it

1. Turn Dynamics past 3 o'clock into the Sag zone (last quarter of the sweep).
2. Raise Sensitivity so hard picking triggers the falter.
3. Boost Wet to recover the volume that Sag eats.
4. Dig in to make it sputter; ease off and it recovers.
5. Or HOLD the BYPASS footswitch to slam max Sag on the fly during a phrase.

## Notes

- Manual: Sag "simulates an overloaded tube. Your signal falls out, falters, and sputters as you play harder."
- Holding the BYPASS footswitch momentarily maxes out Clean's Sag effect — a performable "fall apart" gesture (no preset change needed).
- More useful on guitar than bass — Sag responds to higher frequencies, so boomy lows react poorly (compressorpedalreviews).
- Distinct from the Sag Swell / Slapback and Sag electric-piano patches — this targets the raw sputtering-overload character plus the BYPASS-hold gesture, not swells or the three-voices trick.
- PHYSICS adds to it for more instability (see the Physics-wobble patch).
- The sag zone is published as "past 3:00 / last quarter"; the Sensitivity, Wet and Attack amounts are a dialable recipe, not published numbers — set them by ear and by the LED.

A touch-sensitive "broken" clean that reacts like a starved amp; or hold the BYPASS footswitch to slam max Sag on the fly. Manufacturer-described tone (manual SAG section + bypass-hold gesture) — the sag zone is published as "past 3:00", the exact amounts are dialable.

3. Set the hidden **Aux Onset** (Wow knob in the hidden menu) for how fast it grabs.
4. Seed a drone, freeze it, then solo banjo over the held bed.

## Notes

- Existence + play-over are confirmed by the manual and the 4-version owner comparison; the exact dip combo is community-confirmed via manual-excerpt searches.
- THE move for the sustained-wall aesthetic.
- Saveable to an onboard preset (freeze scene).

content:
Banjo Bowed-Pipe Doom Drone
Device: Chase Bliss Lost & Found

Settings:
- ROUTING: L<R series (Right into Left)
- R slot mode: 5B Sympathetic Resonator
- L slot mode: 1B Useful Ambience (halo)
- MODIFY (R feedback): 4:00–5:00 (MAXED — resonates forever)
- TIME (R onset): noon
- MODIFY (L feedback): 1:00
- TIME (L size): 2:00 (large)
- BLEND: 2:00 (toward the reverb / 2nd-effect mix in series)
- MIX (RAMP): 2:00–3:00
- FREEZE (HOLD R footswitch): PITCH FREEZE — locks the drone
- Slot/Bank: Preset bank 2 (BANK dip)

## Concept

Banjo plinks feed the Sympathetic Resonator (R slot, 5B) with feedback maxed so it resonates forever into a glassy/vibraphone bowed-pipe drone. Holding the R footswitch hits PITCH FREEZE to lock the drone as a sustained doom wall. The drone then runs `L<R` (Right into Left) into Useful Ambience (1B) as an internal reverb halo. This is the rig's banjo-as-lead-into-drone signature move — a Swans-style sustained drone wall.

## How to play it

1. Set ROUTING to `L<R` (Right slot feeds Left).
2. Play sustained banjo notes/chords into the Resonator — feedback MAXED makes them resonate forever.
3. **HOLD the R footswitch = PITCH FREEZE** to lock the drone into a sustained wall.
4. Sweep the ALT octave (start at −1) **during the ring** for expression — octave only does something when swept mid-ring.
5. The Useful Ambience halo (L slot) blooms over the top; BLEND ~2:00 toward the reverb sets its mix in the series chain.

## Notes

- **DESIGNED, not found** — no owner published this exact recipe.
- Onset (TIME on the Resonator) is barely audible on shipping units — leave it ~noon.
- ALT octave only does something when swept during the ring (not a static setting).
- TRAILS on so the frozen pad survives bypass; LATCH on so the FREEZE hold latches.
- Don't stack against the Microcosm / Dark Star / Etherealizer reverb downstream — that's why the halo is kept internal here. Feeds the Microcosm a moving, sustained texture.

Glue Only (Comp/Saturator Utility)
Device: Chase Bliss Lost & Found

Settings:
- Channel: turn ONE channel on
- MODIFY: EXACTLY NOON (= no effect; channel passes only GLUE)
- ROUTING: irrelevant (single channel)
- MIX (RAMP): noon = WET VOLUME unity (hold right footswitch + turn MIX to trim)
- Slot/Bank: Any (utility)

## Concept

The genuine utility setting the rig's old shorthand gestured at — run the hidden end-of-chain GLUE compressor/saturator on its own, with NO effect engaged. *"You can use GLUE on its own as a bonus effect... turn on either channel and set its MODIFY knob at 12:00."* Useful to gently saturate/glue the stereo bus before the Microcosm's input. This is the **only** honest "utility" use of this pedal — L&F is a 12-mode multi-fx, not a utility, and is not run always-on here.

## How to play it

1. Turn **ONE** channel on, set its MODIFY knob to **EXACTLY NOON** (= no effect; the channel passes only GLUE).
2. Engage **GLUE** via the hidden option (hold **both** footswitches): low ~9–10:00 = gentle compression; higher = compresses, then overloads into saturation.
3. ROUTING is irrelevant (single channel).
4. Set MIX to noon for WET VOLUME unity (hold the right footswitch + turn MIX to trim).

## Notes

- This is the **only** honest "utility" use of this pedal — the brief's "character preamp/gate" framing was the rig's old incorrect shorthand.
- **MODIFY-at-noon = no effect** is the #1 "is it broken?" trap.
- Useful to gently saturate/glue the stereo bus before the Microcosm's input.
- Leave SPREAD / UNSYNC as the rig needs.

provenance.title: Glue Only (Comp/Saturator Utility)
provenance.description: Factory utility (CB "Glue" GLUE-alone trick) — run GLUE alone as a standalone compressor → saturator to even level spikes / add cohesion before the Microcosm, with NO effect engaged; the one genuine utility use of this 12-mode multi-fx.

content:
Grain Doubler (Clock-Locked Grain Mill)
Device: Chase Bliss Lost & Found

Settings:
- ROUTING: L+R parallel
- Both slots mode: 4B Grain Tumbler (requires L SWAP on)
- L SWAP: on (so the left slot can host a right-channel mode)
- TIME (slot A): 11:00 (shorter loop / single bouncing playhead)
- MODIFY (slot A feedback-into-buffer): 1:00 (grains accumulate)
- ALT (slot A grain fade): 2:00 (smoother/ambient)
- TIME (slot B): 1:00–2:00 (longer loop + more playheads)
- MODIFY (slot B): 12:00–1:00
- ALT (slot B): 10:00 (glitchier)
- BLEND: noon
- MIX (RAMP): 1:00
- FREEZE (LATCH + HOLD): freezes a repeatable grain pattern
- Slot/Bank: Preset bank 2 (BANK dip)

## Concept

CB's named factory Combo — *"custom clusters of interwoven grains."* Both slots run Grain Tumbler (4B) in parallel, clock-locked from the Digitakt, giving the Microcosm's grain engine even rawer material. Because it is non-reverb, it won't stack with Dark Star / Etherealizer downstream. Slot A is the shorter, accumulating, ambient voice; slot B is the longer, multi-playhead, glitchier voice.

## How to play it

1. Set ROUTING `L+R` parallel, enable **L SWAP** so the left slot can host a right-channel mode.
2. Slot A: TIME ~11:00 (single bouncing playhead), MODIFY ~1:00 (grains accumulate), ALT ~2:00 (smooth).
3. Slot B: TIME ~1–2:00 (longer loop, more playheads), ALT ~10:00 (glitchier).
4. **FRESH-VS-FROZEN move:** LATCH + HOLD one slot to freeze a background grain pattern, play live over it on the other slot, then nudge TIME for new clock-quantized patterns.
5. Sync to the same master clock as Big Time / Blooper (`cb-stack-*` files).

## Notes

- UNSYNC off — incoming MIDI clock auto-overrides UNSYNC and locks both slots.
- GLUE ~10–11:00 evens grain spikes before the Microcosm.

provenance.title: Grain Doubler (Clock-Locked Grain Mill)
provenance.description: Factory combo (CB "GRAIN DOUBLER") — two independent granular voices (both slots = Grain Tumbler) interwoven and clock-locked from the Digitakt, feeding the Microcosm's grain engine even rawer material; non-reverb, so it won't stack with Dark Star/Etherealizer downstream.

content:
Knobs Chunky-Glue Swell
Device: Chase Bliss Lost & Found

Settings:
- ROUTING: single channel (or L+R with R parked)
- L slot mode: 1A Slow-verb
- MODIFY (L): 1:00 (toward A — pre-diffusion feedback)
- TIME (L): 1:00–2:00 (larger size)
- MIX (RAMP): 1:00–2:00 (diffused tail runs louder-than-dry by design)
- FREEZE (HOLD footswitch): INFINITE — freezes the swell as a pad
- Slot/Bank: Preset L (live recallable)

## Concept

The de-facto signature setting — the Chase Bliss / Knobs flagship sound. A Slow-verb (1A) swell is pushed hard with the hidden GLUE compressor/saturator until it overloads into a thick, compressed wall: *"Very ambient shoegaze reverb that swells in... sprinkled with GLUE — it's like chunky glue."* The GLUE-heavy overload is the whole move. Run as a single channel (or L+R with R parked).

## How to play it

1. Engage the L slot (Slow-verb). Play sustained chords and let the swell bloom in.
2. Set ALT (diffusion) ~3:00 so the tail is fully smeared.
3. **Push GLUE HARD ~2–3:00 until it overloads** — this is the "chunky glue" character.
4. **HOLD the footswitch = INFINITE** to freeze the swell as a sustained pad and play over it.

## Notes

- De-facto signature setting — Knobs (Joel Korte's collaborator) is the closest this pedal has to a named user.
- **Honest:** not a touring-artist credit, it's CB's own launch demo.
- The Slow-verb's diffused tail is louder-than-dry by design, so MIX ~1–2:00 keeps the wet present.
- Nudge EQ slightly CCW to tame mud as GLUE overloads.

provenance.title: Knobs Chunky-Glue Swell
provenance.description: The Chase Bliss × Knobs flagship sound (Ref Joel Korte's collaborator) — an ambient Slow-verb swell pushed hard with GLUE into a thick, compressed/overloaded "chunky glue" wall; the closest thing to a signature-artist setting this pedal has.

content:
Light Sleeper (Recorded-Wrong VHS Swell)
Device: Chase Bliss Lost & Found

Settings:
- ROUTING: L>R series
- L slot mode: 2A Orchestral Swell
- R slot mode: 6B Gen Lite
- MODIFY (L pitch interval): UNISON (or oct-down for a synthy non-pitched swell)
- TIME (L swell/attack): 1:00 (removes the pick attack)
- TIME (R wow↔flutter): toward MAX = slow wow
- MODIFY (R depth): 12:00–1:00
- BLEND: 2:00 (toward Gen Lite — sets degrade amount)
- MIX (RAMP): FULL (CB marks this Combo *)
- FREEZE (HOLD R footswitch): TAPE STOP — slowdown gesture
- Slot/Bank: Preset R (live recallable)

## Concept

CB's named factory Combo and the most "recorded-wrong" of them — *"A VHS-era dream sequence that blends heavily digital and analog sounds together."* A digital Orchestral Swell (2A) is set to UNISON (or oct-down) for a synthy non-pitched swell, then smeared through Gen Lite (6B, a mini Generation Loss MkII) for tape wow and crinkle. Runs `L>R` series, MIX FULL.

## How to play it

1. Set ROUTING `L>R` series, MIX FULL.
2. Play sustained chords — TIME(L) ~1:00 removes the pick attack so the swell reads as orchestral/synthy.
3. Set MODIFY(L) to UNISON (or oct-down) for a non-pitched swell.
4. Gen Lite degrades it: TIME toward MAX = slow wow, ALT ~10–11:00 = failure/crinkles.
5. BLEND ~2:00 toward Gen Lite sets the degrade amount.
6. **HOLD the R footswitch = TAPE STOP** for a slowdown gesture.

## Notes

- SPREAD **OFF** so Gen Lite reads as believable tape rather than per-side chorus.
- Gen Lite ≈ a mini Generation Loss MkII — don't also hammer the full Gen Loss on Board 3 at once (double-degrade).
- GLUE ~10–11:00 tames swell spikes.

provenance.title: Light Sleeper (Recorded-Wrong VHS Swell)
provenance.description: The most "recorded-wrong" factory combo — a digital Orchestral Swell smeared through Gen Lite (mini Generation Loss) into a VHS-dream-sequence drone for the Microcosm; CB's "VHS-era dream sequence that blends heavily digital and analog sounds."

content:
Orchestral Resonance (Banjo Pipe Drone)
Device: Chase Bliss Lost & Found

Settings:
- ROUTING: L+R parallel
- L slot mode: 2A Orchestral Swell (native — no SWAP)
- R slot mode: 5B Sympathetic Resonator (native — no SWAP)
- MODIFY (L pitch interval): oct-up for shimmer or unison for a synth pad
- TIME (L swell): 12:00–1:00
- MODIFY (R feedback): 2:00–3:00 (HIGH — longer ring)
- TIME (R onset): noon (very subtle)
- BLEND: noon (balance both voices)
- MIX (RAMP): FULL (CB marks *)
- Slot/Bank: Preset bank 2 (BANK dip)

## Concept

CB's named factory Combo and Knobs' favorite mode — *"keen tracking and two flexible, layered voices."* Sustained banjo/baritone chords become two layered pitch-tracked voices: the Orchestral Swell (2A, oct-up shimmer or unison pad) layered in parallel with the Sympathetic Resonator (5B, long glassy ring). Banjo-as-lead into a glassy drone, cleanest on slow chordal input. Both modes live on native channels, so no SWAP is needed.

## How to play it

1. Set ROUTING `L+R` parallel, MIX FULL.
2. Play slow sustained banjo/baritone chords — pitch modes track cleanest here.
3. Orchestral Swell: choose MODIFY = oct-up (shimmer) or unison (synth pad).
4. Sympathetic Resonator: MODIFY feedback HIGH (~2–3:00) for a longer ring; sweep the ALT octave **during resonance** for expression.
5. BLEND ~noon balances the two voices.

## Notes

- Pitch modes track cleanest on slow sustained banjo/baritone — fast banjo rolls will artifact (on-aesthetic).
- Resonator onset (TIME) is very subtle on shipping units — leave ~noon.
- Use EQ CCW if the banjo plink gets shrill.

provenance.title: Orchestral Resonance (Banjo Pipe Drone)
provenance.description: Factory combo (CB "ORCHESTRAL RESONANCE"; Knobs' favorite mode) — turns sustained banjo/baritone chords into two layered pitch-tracked synth/pipe voices (Orchestral Swell + Sympathetic Resonator); banjo-as-lead into a glassy drone, cleanest on slow chordal input.

content:
Random Event (Live Mode-Shuffle)
Device: Chase Bliss Lost & Found

Settings:
- ROUTING: L+R parallel
- Both slots modes: on-aesthetic pair (e.g. Grain Tumbler + Spectral Modulator, or Gen Lite + Sympathetic Resonator)
- BLEND: noon
- MIX (RAMP): noon–1:00
- CC112 (Random L Mode): draw MIDI ramps/triggers in Digitakt/Deluge automation
- CC113 (Random R Mode): draw MIDI ramps/triggers in Digitakt/Deluge automation
- CC114 (Random Both Modes): draw MIDI ramps/triggers in Digitakt/Deluge automation
- 6A Ensemble HOLD = RANDOM: smooth, non-cyclical movement instead of an LFO
- Save as preset (PC): so a fixed scene can also be recalled
- Slot/Bank: Preset L or R (recall a frozen version on cue)

## Concept

The patch that earns the rig's "Random" tag — constantly-shifting mode/variant combos drawn live from the Digitakt or Deluge, a controlled-chaos texture event feeding the Microcosm. Load both channels with on-aesthetic modes, run `L+R` parallel, then drive the pedal's Random-mode CCs from the controller so it keeps jumping to new combinations. The randomness is recallable / clock-synced — controlled chaos, not noise — and a frozen version can be saved to recall on cue.

## How to play it

1. Load BOTH channels with on-aesthetic modes (e.g. Grain Tumbler + Spectral Modulator, or Gen Lite + Sympathetic Resonator).
2. Set ROUTING `L+R` parallel, BLEND ~noon, MIX ~noon–1:00.
3. **Drive from the controller:** CC112 = Random L Mode, CC113 = Random R Mode, CC114 = Random Both Modes — draw MIDI ramps/triggers in the Digitakt's CC automation (or the Deluge automation view) so the pedal jumps to new mode/variant combos.
4. **Alternatively** arm BOUNCE across L MODIFY + R MODIFY (Control-bank dips) for hands-free knob churn; MIX (RAMP) sets speed.
5. **6A Ensemble HOLD = RANDOM** gives smooth, non-cyclical movement instead of an LFO.
6. **SAVE as a preset (PC)** so a fixed scene can also be recalled on cue.

## Notes

- **DESIGNED, not found** — Bay Mud demonstrates the technique in a no-talking jam; exact CC ramp values are not spoken (they're the standard L+F CCs per the MIDI manual).
- This is the patch that earns the rig's "Random" tag.
- The randomness is recallable / clock-synced — controlled chaos, not noise.

provenance.title: Random Event (Live Mode-Shuffle)
provenance.description: DOUG-designed — the rig's "Random" tag in action; constantly-shifting mode combos drawn live from the Digitakt/Deluge (CC112/113/114) for a controlled-chaos texture event feeding the Microcosm, with a frozen version saved to recall on cue.

content:
Shoegaze Special
Device: Chase Bliss Lost & Found

Settings:
- ROUTING: L>R series
- L slot mode: 1A Slow-verb
- R slot mode: 6A Ensemble Expander
- MODIFY (L): 1:00 (toward A, moderate pre-diffusion feedback)
- TIME (L): 1:00 (medium size)
- MODIFY (R Ensemble depth): 11:00
- TIME (R Ensemble LFO): 10:00
- BLEND: 1:00 (toward the chorus / 2nd-effect mix in series)
- MIX (RAMP): 1:00–2:00
- Slot/Bank: Preset L (live recallable)

## Concept

CB's named factory Combo and on-aesthetic starting point — *"A swirling, living ambience that is both surreal and loaded with emotion."* The L slot's Slow-verb provides the diffused reverberant bed, and the R slot's Ensemble Expander (≈ 4 voices, Juno-chorus LFO) smears it into swirl. Runs `L>R` series with native channels (Slow-verb = L1, Ensemble = L6, so no SWAP). It sits at the front of Board 2, feeding the Microcosm a shoegaze/post-punk wash from sustained chords.

## How to play it

1. Engage the L>R series chain — play sustained banjo/baritone chords to build the reverberant bed.
2. Let the Slow-verb's pre-diffusion feedback (MODIFY ~1:00) and large smear (ALT diffusion ~2–3:00) bloom.
3. The Ensemble Expander on the R slot adds the swirl — leave it at ~4 voices with a slow LFO.
4. Use BLEND (~1:00, toward the chorus) to set how much of the 2nd effect's mix lands in the series chain.

## Notes

- For doom weight, push MODIFY(L) higher (more feedback) and EQ CCW to darken (cut highs).
- GLUE ~10:00 adds light cohesion to the wet wall.
- Sits at the front of Board 2 → into the Microcosm.
- **Honesty:** Modes + routing = CB Field Guide verbatim; the exact MODIFY / TIME / ALT / BLEND clock positions are suggested starting points (DOUG's), not in the Combo doc.

provenance.title: Shoegaze Special
provenance.description: CB's on-aesthetic factory combo — a swirling reverberant bed (Slow-verb into Ensemble Expander) feeding the Microcosm, for shoegaze/post-punk wash from sustained banjo/baritone chords.

content:
Spectral Mill (Resynth into Microcosm)
Device: Chase Bliss Lost & Found

Settings:
- ROUTING: L+R parallel
- L slot mode: 3B Spectral Modulator
- R slot mode: 6B Gen Lite (needs L SWAP on, or run Spectral solo)
- L SWAP: on (to host Gen Lite in the right slot; both modes live on left channel natively)
- MODIFY (L notch depth): 1:00
- TIME (L sawtooth-LFO rate): 9:00–10:00 (SLOW — glacial sweep)
- ALT (L resonance/clipping): 2:00 (digital-distortion grit; normalizes upper partials)
- Gen Lite (R, if paired): full wet, TIME toward wow, ALT crinkles ~10:00
- BLEND: 11:00 (toward Spectral)
- MIX (RAMP): 1:00–2:00
- Slot/Bank: Preset bank 2 (BANK dip)

## Concept

Instead of feeding the Microcosm dry guitar, this gives its grain engine far richer raw material — a constantly-moving resynthesized signal. The Spectral Modulator (3B) does glacial filter sweeps (slow sawtooth LFO) with a resonance/clipping edge for digital-distortion grit, optionally paired with Gen Lite (6B) for extra ruin. This is the art-rock studio-as-instrument glitch-texture move (Radiohead glitch/granular).

## How to play it

1. Set ROUTING `L+R` parallel. To pair Gen Lite, enable **L SWAP** so the left slot can host a right-channel mode (or run Spectral Modulator solo and skip the swap).
2. Set TIME(L) ~9–10:00 for a glacial sawtooth-LFO sweep.
3. Push ALT(L) ~2:00 for the resonance/clipping grit (normalizes upper partials → digital distortion).
4. If pairing Gen Lite: full wet, TIME toward wow, ALT crinkles ~10:00.
5. Follow with the downstream reverbs to make it shine.

## Notes

- **DESIGNED, not found.** Spectral Modulator is the standout "resynthesis" texture for this rig.
- SPREAD on puts the L/R spectral processing on opposed LFOs.
- UNSYNC off → LFO syncs to clock (~3:00 ≈ one cycle/beat, noon ≈ once/bar/side).
- Pair with Gen Lite for extra ruin, or run solo.

provenance.title: Spectral Mill (Resynth into Microcosm)
provenance.description: DOUG-designed — feeds the Microcosm a constantly-moving resynthesized signal (Spectral Modulator + Gen Lite) instead of dry guitar; glacial spectral filter sweeps + digital-distortion grit for the art-rock studio-as-instrument glitch-texture move (Radiohead glitch/granular).

content:
Stereo Pinging Phaser (Bounce Sweep)
Device: Chase Bliss Lost & Found

Settings:
- ROUTING: single channel
- L slot mode: 3A Pinging Phaser
- TIME (LFO speed): 11:00
- MODIFY (pole count): the swept param (2–64 poles)
- ALT (feedback): 1:00 (needs some feedback to speak)
- MIX (RAMP) = ramp/bounce SPEED: slow = intermittent stereo pinging, fast = aggressive
- FREEZE (HOLD): PAUSE — freezes the LFO so you can set poles (2–64) by hand
- Slot/Bank: Preset bank 2 (BANK dip)

## Concept

A hands-free evolving stereo phaser from Mark Johnston's "Secret Weapons" walkthrough. Mode 3A (Pinging Phaser) runs with an armed BOUNCE on the L MODIFY knob so the pole count sweeps min↔max continuously, throwing "intermittent stereo pinging." It's a motion/random-leaning texture for the Microcosm that isn't yet another reverb. With BOUNCE armed, the MIX (RAMP) knob sets the ramp/bounce speed.

## How to play it

1. Set ROUTING to single channel, load 3A Pinging Phaser on the L slot.
2. SPREAD on (essential for the stereo effect).
3. Set TIME (LFO speed) ~11:00, ALT (feedback) ~1:00 (it needs some feedback to speak).
4. **Arm BOUNCE** on the L MODIFY knob (Control-bank ramp/bounce dip) so the pole count oscillates min↔max.
5. The **MIX (RAMP)** knob now sets the bounce **SPEED** — slow = intermittent stereo pinging, fast = aggressive.
6. **HOLD = PAUSE** freezes the LFO so you can dial poles (2–64) by hand.

## Notes

- Demoed on **beta firmware**, but the phaser/ramp engines are **not** the ones that changed (only synth/resonator did).
- Changing poles while playing throws "not-intentional but very cool" artifacts — on-aesthetic.
- MIDI clock-syncing the LFO is **not** useful (fastest sync = once/beat); use the free LFO or bounce instead.

provenance.title: Stereo Pinging Phaser (Bounce Sweep)
provenance.description: Community patch (Mark Johnston "Secret Weapons") — a hands-free evolving stereo phaser where an armed BOUNCE sweeps the pole count min↔max for intermittent stereo pinging; a motion/"random"-leaning texture for the Microcosm that isn't another reverb.

content:
Synth Tower (Dual Synth Tracker)
Device: Chase Bliss Lost & Found

Settings:
- ROUTING: L+R parallel
- L slot mode: 5A Impulse Synthesizer (requires L SWAP on)
- R slot mode: 5B Sympathetic Resonator
- L SWAP: on (both modes live on the right channel natively)
- MODIFY (L brightness): 11:00–12:00 (keep darker for doom)
- TIME (L portamento): 10:00
- MODIFY (R feedback): 2:00
- BLEND: noon
- MIX (RAMP): FULL (CB marks *)
- Play style: Play BLOCK CHORDS struck together (rolled chords only voice the last note)
- Slot/Bank: Preset bank 2 (BANK dip)

## Concept

CB's named factory Combo — *"Two different synths following your every move in their own way."* The Impulse Synthesizer (5A) tracks chords with sub-octave weight; the Sympathetic Resonator (5B) adds pipe voices. Drop the ALT octave (−1) on the Resonator for cinematic doom low-end from baritone or Jazz-bass. Runs `L+R` parallel — requires L SWAP on, since both modes live on the right channel natively.

## How to play it

1. Set ROUTING `L+R` parallel, enable **L SWAP**, MIX FULL.
2. **Play BLOCK CHORDS struck together** — rolled chords only voice the last note.
3. Impulse Synth: keep MODIFY (brightness) ~11–12:00 for doom; pick a slow attack (ALT) for pads.
4. Sympathetic Resonator: MODIFY feedback ~2:00, ALT octave −1 for sub weight.
5. BLEND ~noon balances the two synth voices.

## Notes

- Impulse Synth is register-sensitive — play down an octave for fuller tracking.
- **NOT for fast leads** ("it will not keep up").
- For Jazz-bass sub weight, watch GLUE/MIX so the wet doesn't muddy the fundamental.
- GLUE ~11:00 evens the dynamic Impulse Synth.

provenance.title: Synth Tower (Dual Synth Tracker)
provenance.description: Factory combo (CB "SYNTH TOWER") — two different synth voices following each chord (Impulse Synth sub-octave weight + Sympathetic Resonator pipes); cinematic doom low-end from baritone/Jazz-bass when the ALT octave is dropped.

content:
Tape Shifter (Pitched Tape Cascade)
Device: Chase Bliss Lost & Found

Settings:
- ROUTING: L<R series (Right into Left)
- R slot mode: 4A Tape Echo (native — no SWAP)
- L slot mode: 2B Pitch Repeater (native — no SWAP)
- MODIFY (L pitch shift): oct-down (great with GLUE) or up-a-5th (airy)
- TIME (L delay subdivision): noon = beat (left = subdivisions, right = multiples)
- ALT (L number of taps): chop the repeat finer
- TIME (R delay time): stepped/synced
- MODIFY (R feedback): → infinite (never self-oscillates)
- ALT (R stability/tape-age): up = older (HPF + warble)
- BLEND: 1:00–2:00 (Tape Echo mix in the cascade)
- MIX (RAMP): noon–1:00
- Slot/Bank: Preset R (live recallable)

## Concept

CB's named factory Combo — *"A two-stage cascade of synced reflections, where analog-style tape echoes are pitch shifted and repeated."* The Pitch Repeater (2B) pitch-shifts and re-triggers the reflections, then `L<R` (Right into Left) feeds them into a warm Tape Echo (4A). More of a rhythmic/electronic delay than a drone wall, but it earns inclusion as a clock-locked time texture into the Microcosm.

## How to play it

1. Set ROUTING `L<R` (Right slot feeds Left).
2. Pitch Repeater: choose MODIFY = oct-down (great with GLUE) or up-a-5th (airy); set TIME subdivision (noon = beat); use ALT to chop the repeat into finer taps.
3. Tape Echo: set feedback (MODIFY) toward infinite (it never self-oscillates); raise ALT for older, warbly, high-passed tape age.
4. BLEND ~1–2:00 sets the Tape Echo's mix in the cascade.
5. Latch a new chord loudly to trigger the buffer dump-and-refill (a feature on new chords, a surprise on held drones).

## Notes

- More rhythmic/electronic delay than drone wall (hence no signature tag), but a clean clock-locked time texture.
- UNSYNC off — clock-locked; MIDI clock overrides anyway.
- SPREAD on splits the echo L/R.
- The Tape Echo dumps-and-refills its buffer on a loud new chord — a feature for latching a new chord, a surprise on held drones.

provenance.title: Tape Shifter (Pitched Tape Cascade)
provenance.description: Factory combo (CB "TAPE SHIFTER") — a synced two-stage cascade of pitch-shifted, repeated reflections (Pitch Repeater) running into a warm Tape Echo; a rhythmic clock-locked delay texture for ambient/electronic-leaning passages into the Microcosm.

content:
Balance Beam — degraded-but-in-tune Tape loop
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- Looper MODE: Tape
- CLOCK: lower to introduce grit/character
- Looper MODIFY: raise to speed the loop back up to its recorded speed

## Concept

A "recorded-wrong" tape loop that stays at its **original pitch/speed** but gains aliasing vibe — exactly the degrade-without-detuning trick this rig wants. Set Looper MODE = **Tape**, **lower CLOCK** to introduce grit/character, then **raise MODIFY** to speed the loop back up to its recorded speed → "same speed as you recorded it, but more vibe."

## How to play it

1. Set Looper MODE = **Tape** and capture a loop.
2. **Lower CLOCK** to introduce grit and aliasing character.
3. **Raise MODIFY** to bring the loop back up to its recorded speed — degraded but in-tune.
4. Set LENGTH to taste.

## Notes

- Inverse move = slow CLOCK + 2×/4× MODIFY for the gritty-Tape sound (gritty-tape-loop).
- Perfect for banjo/baritone beds. Turn **CLASSIC** on for deteriorating loops.

provenance.title: Balance Beam — degraded-but-in-tune Tape loop

Classic Mode — degraded "recorded-wrong" base layer

Settings:
- CLOCK: noise-full — turning down adds noise
- Looper MODE: micro-loops gradually deteriorate/distort over time; Tape LENGTH chops the loop instead of shortening it
- Wet MODE: Reverb trails get resonant/ringy; Slip aliased/uneven crunch; Delay TIME adds rubbery pitch-bends

## Concept

A global tone shift that restores all the MkI flaws — the most directly on-aesthetic toggle for drone/doom/shoegaze degradation. Flick the **CLASSIC** dip ON (controls are identical; sound/response differ): CLOCK is noise-full (turning down adds noise); micro-loops gradually deteriorate/distort over time; Reverb trails get resonant/ringy (mild feedback); Slip gets aliased/uneven crunch; Delay TIME adds rubbery pitch-bends; Tape LENGTH **chops** the loop instead of shortening it.

## How to play it

1. Flick the **CLASSIC** dip ON.
2. Run any recipe — the degraded character layers under it automatically.
3. For MkI "hold-to-record, release-to-play": CLASSIC on + **NO DUB** on + overdub engaged + **LATCH** off.
4. Flash **firmware 1.1** for the original cloudy/wispy Stretch inside Classic.

## Notes

- Not a single patch — a global "degraded" switch to layer under any recipe.
- **Dip settings save with presets**, so bake CLASSIC into both stored slots.

content:
Clock-Decay Character Shift
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- Wet MODE: Reverb
- Wet TIME: up enough to sustain
- Wet MODIFY: anywhere (CW = washed, CCW = distinct taps)
- CLOCK: turn down (CCW) live while the tail decays — scale: 2k…3k…4k…6k…(12k noon)…16k…24k…32k…48k…64k

## Concept

CLOCK is tone, time and quality in one knob. Play a single note and, **while the reverb decays, turn CLOCK down (CCW)** — the character of the tail changes as you sweep. Play another note and it sounds different again. Continue CCW (toward 4k/3k/2k) and "things get real textural." This is the single most impactful gesture on the pedal.

## How to play it

1. Set Wet MODE = **Reverb**, TIME up enough to sustain, MODIFY wherever you like (CW = washed, CCW = distinct taps).
2. Play a single note.
3. While the reverb tail decays, **turn CLOCK down (CCW)** — listen to the character shift.
4. Play another note; continue CCW toward 4k/3k/2k for heavy texture.

## Notes

- Low CLOCK = heavy aliasing/downsampling ("computer noises"); high = hi-fi. CLOCK scale: 2k…3k…4k…6k…(12k noon)…16k…24k…32k…48k…64k.
- Lowering 64k→32k half-speeds both channels together.
- Flick the **SMOOTH** dip for a continuous bend instead of stepped 4ths/5ths.

provenance.title: Clock-Decay Character Shift
provenance.description: CLOCK as tone + time + quality in one — re-pitch and degrade a reverb tail as it decays; the single most impactful gesture on the pedal.

content:
Clock Reveal — sweep CLOCK live under a decaying note
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- Wet MODE: Reverb
- CLOCK: start high (hi-fi), then turn down (CCW) live as the tail decays — scale: 2k…3k…4k…6k…(12k noon)…16k…24k…32k…48k…64k

## Concept

This is the manual's explicit single-note reveal exercise. Play one note into the **Reverb** and, while the tail decays, slowly rotate **CLOCK** counter-clockwise from a high (hi-fi) setting down through 12k (noon) → 6k → 4k → 3k → 2k. The character morphs dramatically — pure to crunchy, then on into heavy aliasing/downsampling that the manual calls "real textural" and "computer noises." Because CLOCK is "tone, length, and quality all in one," the same sweep also changes loop length/resolution, but with Wet MODE = Reverb the headline effect is hearing the sample rate fall in real time.

## How to play it

1. Set **Wet MODE = Reverb** and start with **CLOCK** high (hi-fi).
2. Play a single sustaining note or chord.
3. While the reverb tail rings out, slowly turn **CLOCK** counter-clockwise.
4. Play another note and notice how much the character has changed; continue CCW for heavy aliasing / "computer noises." (Flick **SMOOTH** for a continuous bend instead of stepped 4ths/5ths.)

## Notes

- The CLOCK scale numbers (2k…64k) and the live-sweep gesture are documented directly in the manual — these are sourced, not invented.
- CLOCK is "tone, length, and quality all in one," so this sweep also changes loop length/resolution, not just brightness.
- Low CLOCK = heavy aliasing/downsampling ("computer noises"); high = pure/hi-fi. Community reports CLOCK moves in perfect 4ths/5ths unless SMOOTH is on, and goes grittily lo-fi without tape-style hiss.
- Differs from the existing clock-decay patch by being the manual's explicit single-note reveal exercise; pairs with SMOOTH for pitch-bend sweeps.

provenance.title: Clock Reveal — sweep CLOCK live under a decaying note
provenance.description: The manual's signature 'Try this' gesture and arguably the single most impactful move on the pedal — play one note into the Reverb and, while it decays, slowly turn CLOCK counter-clockwise so the character morphs from hi-fi to crunchy, then on into 'real textural' aliasing and 'computer noises.' You hear the sample rate fall in real time. The CLOCK scale numbers below are published in the official manual (pp.18–21 'Try this'), not invented.

content:
Clock-Synced Loop Layer + bass/baritone sub-drone (rig patch d)
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- Looper MODE: Tape (LENGTH set by CLOCK)
- Wet MODE: Delay
- Wet TIME: a quarter-note feel
- Wet MODIFY: 1:00 (piling repeats)
- CLOCK: sets loop length; keep HIGHER for the sub-drone variant to preserve low-end
- Looper MODIFY (sub-drone variant): octave-down
- MIDI clock (CC51 follow / CC53 / CC54): feed from the rig master to lock to Big Time / Blooper

## Concept

An in-time loop locked to the rig and committed to Blooper; plus a sub-drone from bass/baritone without thinning the fundamental. Tape loop length set by CLOCK with SYNC tying the Micro-Looper to the Wet Delay, fed by MIDI clock so the loop locks to the rig and can be captured in time then committed downstream.

## How to play it

1. Set Looper MODE = **Tape** (LENGTH set by CLOCK); engage **SYNC** (hidden — Wet MODE toggle LEFT) so the Micro-Looper syncs to Wet.
2. Set Wet MODE = **Delay**, TIME to a quarter-note feel, MODIFY 1:00 (piling repeats).
3. Feed **MIDI clock** from the rig master so the loop locks to Big Time / Blooper (send CC51>0 to follow; CC53/CC54 set divisions).
4. Capture in time, then commit to Blooper downstream.
5. **Sub-drone variant:** set Tape MODIFY octave-down, but keep **CLOCK higher** to preserve low-end (aggressive low-CLOCK downsampling thins bass fundamentals).

## Notes

- SYNC + MIDI-clock parts are factory features; the knob feels are inferred — dial by ear.
- Mike Gordon (Phish) documented running bass through MOOD MkII (Equipboard, user-maintained — not official).

content:
DRY KILL — wet-only output / volume-as-swell
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- DRY KILL (dip switch): on
- MIX (blend knob): becomes a wet-only fader — 0 = silence, 100 = full wet/loop; no published value, set to taste
- Wet / Looper mode: any wet/loop texture — DRY KILL works with any mode

## Concept

Flip the **DRY KILL** dip on and MOOD's clean signal is pulled out of the output entirely, so what you hear is **100% wet**. That re-purposes the **MIX** knob: instead of blending dry↔wet it becomes a pure wet **0–100 fader**. All the way down is *silence* (there's no dry to fall back on); rolling it up swells in nothing but wet/loop texture. Great for running MOOD in a parallel FX loop, or for volume-swell-style wet-only entrances — but it's a surprising silence trap on stage, so know it's on before you commit. Exact knob positions aren't published; treat MIX as a dialable wet level rather than a fixed value.

## How to play it

1. Flick the **DRY KILL** dip on.
2. Set up any wet/loop texture (any Wet or Looper mode works).
3. Use **MIX** as a wet-only fader: all the way down = silence; roll up to swell pure wet/loop in.
4. Reach for it when MOOD lives in a parallel FX loop, or when you want only the effect with no dry blend.

## Notes

- ⚠️ With DRY KILL on and **MIX** down you get **silence** — there's no dry signal to fall back on. Surprising live; re-check before a performance.
- DRY KILL removes the clean signal **even when bypassed** (per the spec sheet).
- Turns **MIX** from a dry↔wet blend into a pure wet level control.
- **No published knob values** — MIX is a dialable wet-only recipe (0 = silence, up = more wet), not a fixed setting.

Useful for parallel-FX-loop use and volume-swell-style wet-only entrances, but a surprising silence trap live. A factory dip-switch feature documented in the official video manual pt.2 + community walkthrough + manual p.44.

Attack-controlled stutter/freeze where your picking carves into a held bed. Set Looper MODE = **Env**, **crank MODIFY (sensitivity MAX)**, and set LENGTH for the slice size. 5. **Go fully quiet** to freeze and repeat the last slice. Lower CLOCK for aliasing.

## Notes

- The manual's own gesture behind Perry Frank's "Reverb + Env" dynamic drone (reverb-env-dynamic-interactive).

## Concept

From-scratch first sound: a few notes become an evolving textural bed (banjo/baritone or any input). This is the manual's literal "good default to do your own thing" — start neutral at noon across all six effect knobs, then drop CLOCK into the grit zone to add character. "You should be a texture now."

## How to play it

1. Start with BOTH channels bypassed and **all dips OFF**. Set all six effect knobs (Wet TIME/MODIFY, looper LENGTH/MODIFY) ~noon; CLOCK ~noon; MIX ~noon; ROUTING = **IN+micro-loop**.
2. Play a few notes, then turn ON the Micro-Looper.
3. Turn ON the Wet Channel to "smear it."
4. In order: roll **CLOCK down** to the lower-third (illustration ~6k) for grit; then move each MODIFY; finally bring up TIME and LENGTH.

## Notes

- This is the orientation patch — **don't store it**. It's neutral-noon as a launch pad, not a destination.
- The whole point is the gesture: noon everything, then drop CLOCK into the grit zone and start sculpting from there.

Gritty Tape Loop
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- Looper MODE: Tape
- CLOCK: slower (combine with faster playback speed)
- Looper MODIFY: octave-quantized playback speed — .5x / 1x / 2x / 4x, forward or reversed (toward 2x/4x)
- Looper LENGTH: shortens the slice CCW

## Concept

Grit and vibe in a tape-style micro-loop. Combine a **slower CLOCK** with a **faster playback speed** (MODIFY toward 2×/4×). MODIFY is octave-quantized: **.5× / 1× / 2× / 4×**, forward or reversed. LENGTH shortens the slice CCW. The slow clock degrades the loop while the fast playback keeps it moving.

## How to play it

1. Set Looper MODE = **Tape**.
2. Lower **CLOCK** to introduce grit.
3. Push **MODIFY** toward 2×/4× (octave-quantized) for faster playback.
4. Set **LENGTH** for the slice size (CCW shortens it).

## Notes

- Add **CLASSIC** for deteriorating MkI loops. Heavily cited across the notes.
- The inverse trick (slow CLOCK + raise MODIFY back to recorded speed) is Balance Beam (balance-beam-tape-loop).

content:
Kid-A Mistreated Micro-Loop (CLASSIC + Tape)
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- Looper MODE: Tape
- CLOCK: lower for grit/aliasing (Balance Beam move)
- Looper MODIFY: raise to bring the loop back up to recorded speed (degraded but in-tune)
- Looper LENGTH: to taste
- Wet MODE: Reverb (layer over the loop for the wash)

## Concept

Kid A's "loops mistreated, stretched, pulled out of phase — everything breathes wrong on purpose." A tape micro-loop that deteriorates and detunes as it runs, made playable: capture a phrase with **CLASSIC** on, then use the **Balance Beam** move (lower CLOCK for grit/aliasing, then raise MODIFY back to recorded speed) → "same speed, but more vibe" — degraded but in-tune, the mistreated-loop sound without falling out of key.

## How to play it

1. Set Looper MODE = **Tape** and turn the **CLASSIC** dip ON (the single most on-aesthetic switch — loops gradually deteriorate/distort over time).
2. Capture a phrase.
3. Apply Balance Beam: **lower CLOCK** for grit/aliasing, then **raise MODIFY** to bring the loop back up to its recorded speed (degraded but in-tune).
4. For "pulled out of phase," let CLASSIC + low CLOCK drift it. LENGTH to taste.
5. Layer the Wet **Reverb** over it for the wash.

## Notes

- This is the Kid A method made playable: Ed cut up the Rhodes in real time over loops — here you capture, then mistreat the loop live while playing fresh over the top.
- Commit the result to Blooper (SYNC + downstream) for a kept layer.

content:
LATCH — hands-free freeze / overdub
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- LATCH: on (binary dip — HOLD now latches instead of momentary)
- LEFT footswitch (freeze / wet): HOLD to freeze the wet channel — with LATCH it stays frozen when you lift your foot; long-press again to release
- RIGHT footswitch (overdub / looper): HOLD to overdub — with LATCH it stays engaged hands-free; long-press again to deactivate

## Concept

Turn the HOLD function of each footswitch into a latch instead of a momentary action. With the **LATCH** dip on, a long-press (HOLD) on the **LEFT** footswitch freezes the wet channel — or a HOLD on the **RIGHT** footswitch engages overdub — and it stays engaged after you lift your foot. Long-press the same footswitch again to deactivate. Without LATCH the hold is momentary: the freeze or overdub stops the moment you release. This is the difference between performing over a sustained frozen pad with both hands free and having to pin a switch down through the entire passage.

## How to play it

1. Flick the **LATCH** dip switch on.
2. HOLD the **LEFT** footswitch to freeze the wet (or **RIGHT** to overdub) — it now stays engaged when you lift your foot.
3. Play freely over the latched freeze, or keep building overdubs hands-free.
4. Long-press the same footswitch again to deactivate the latched state.

## Notes

- Without LATCH the hold is momentary — the freeze/overdub stops "as soon as I let go." LATCH is the practical choice for performance "so you don't have to hold it down the whole time."
- Pairs with **NO DUB** (which requires overdub left engaged — LATCH keeps the RIGHT footswitch on for you) and with overdub-density build patches.
- This is a binary on/off dip toggle, not a continuous knob — there are no numeric settings here, so nothing in this patch is an unsourced dial position.

- Exists specifically so V1 owners can recover the original shorter loop feel if the doubled length doesn't suit their workflow.
- Pairs with **Classic Mode** for a faithful V1 micro-looper feel.
- Saves per-preset like all hidden options.
- This is a binary hidden toggle (HALF vs FULL) rather than a continuous knob value — no numeric settings are involved, so nothing here is an unsourced dial position.

content:
MISO — mono-in to stereo-out split
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- MISO (dip switch): on
- Input cable: TS (mono)
- Output cable: TRS (stereo)
- SPREAD (dip switch, optional): on to widen/animate the stereo image per mode
- STEREO WIDTH (hidden, Wet TIME): set to taste — no published value

## Concept

Feed MOOD a single mono instrument and get a **true stereo output**. The **MISO** dip splits a mono input into a stereo out (**TS cable in, TRS cable out**), so a mono guitar/banjo/bass can drive MOOD's stereo wet and looper engines and land in a stereo rig. Note: **MISO is what creates stereo from mono** — SPREAD only *widens* stereo that already exists. This is a routing/IO switch, not a tone recipe — no knob values are involved.

## How to play it

1. Run a **TS (mono)** cable into MOOD's input and a **TRS (stereo)** cable out of its output.
2. Flick the **MISO** dip switch on.
3. Play — your mono source is now split to a stereo output through MOOD's stereo engines.
4. (Optional) Engage **SPREAD** to widen/animate the stereo image per mode; set **STEREO WIDTH** (hidden, Wet TIME) to taste.

## Notes

- **MISO CREATES stereo** from a mono source; **SPREAD only WIDENS** existing stereo — don't confuse the two.
- With a stereo input already present, leave MISO **off**.
- Rig flag: a mono Blooper immediately downstream will re-collapse any stereo image — wide stereo has to land at a later stereo stage.
- This is an I/O routing feature; the only adjustable here is the optional **STEREO WIDTH** (hidden Wet TIME), which has **no published value** — dial it to taste.

content:
NO DUB — pseudo-live micro-looper effect
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- CLOCK: higher tracks live playing more closely; move while overdubbing to build different-speed harmonies (dial from recipe — no published clock-face values)
- Looper MODE: Tape / Stretch / Env to taste
- Wet MODE: optional — blend a wet channel under the live looper
- RIGHT footswitch (overdub): must stay ENGAGED for NO DUB to do anything — hold, or use LATCH to keep it on

## Concept

Turn the always-listening Micro-Looper into a near-live wet/granular effect rather than a sustaining loop. Flicking the **NO DUB (Refresh)** dip drops looper feedback to zero, so the loop refreshes instead of piling up — the channel tracks your current playing instead of holding old material. The higher the **CLOCK**, the more tightly it tracks. While overdubbing you can also move CLOCK to pin notes at the positions you played them but at different speeds, building harmonies. The result is a pseudo-real-time granular/pitch effect instead of a held loop.

## How to play it

1. Flick the **NO DUB (Refresh)** dip switch on.
2. Engage the Micro-Looper and **HOLD the RIGHT footswitch** to keep overdub engaged (set **LATCH** on so you don't have to keep holding it).
3. Turn **CLOCK** up — the higher it is, the more closely the looper tracks your live playing.
4. While overdubbing, freely move **CLOCK**: notes stay where you played them but play back at different speeds, building harmonies.
5. Play — the looper now behaves as a pseudo-live wet/granular effect (feedback at zero, refreshing) instead of a sustaining loop.

## Notes

- ⚠️ Overdub MUST stay engaged for NO DUB to do anything — without it, nothing changes.
- ⚠️ NO DUB and FADE are mutually exclusive: "no dub, no fade."
- In **Classic Mode** + NO DUB + overdub engaged + LATCH off you get the MkI "hold-to-record, release-to-play" behavior (in CLASSIC, NO DUB mutes loop output while overdubbing).
- No published knob values — CLOCK position is a dial-by-feel tradeoff between tracking tightness and grit. Treat the controls above as a recipe, not sourced settings.

The NO DUB (Refresh) dip drops looper feedback to zero so the loop refreshes instead of piling up, letting the channel track your current playing — the higher the CLOCK, the tighter it tracks. While overdubbing, move CLOCK to pin notes at their played positions but at different speeds, building harmonies. content:
Overdub Density Build — stack the micro-loop
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- RIGHT footswitch (Micro-Looper): tap to capture a micro-loop; HOLD to overdub more material onto it (or set LATCH so it stays engaged)
- Looper MODE: flip between passes — Tape ⇄ Stretch ⇄ Env; the loop is NOT erased when you change modes
- Looper MODIFY: dial each engine to taste per pass (dial from recipe — no published knob values)
- CLOCK: shared loop/grain speed — set to taste per pass (dial from recipe — no published clock-face values)
- MIX: balance the stacked loop against your live signal (dial from recipe — no published values)

## Concept

Use the MkII's new overdubbing to pile sound after sound onto a captured micro-loop, building massive evolving textures that were impossible on V1. Capture a loop with a tap of the **RIGHT footswitch**, then **HOLD** that footswitch to overdub more material on top — with **LATCH** on it stays engaged hands-free. The key move is that you can switch the looper **MODE** toggle between **Env / Tape / Stretch** *after* capture without erasing the loop, so each overdub pass can be a different engine. Layer a few **Stretch** passes especially and you "turn just about anything into an infinitely interesting texture."

## How to play it

1. Capture a micro-loop with a tap of the **RIGHT footswitch**.
2. **HOLD** the **RIGHT footswitch** (or set **LATCH** on) to engage overdub and play more material onto the loop.
3. Between passes, flip the looper **MODE** toggle to a different engine (**Tape ⇄ Stretch ⇄ Env**) — the loop is not erased.
4. Layer several passes (a few **Stretch** overdubs especially) to build a dense, infinitely evolving bed.

## Notes

- Overdubbing + Stretch is the documented route to "turn just about anything into an infinitely interesting texture."
- Switching loop modes after capture does NOT erase the loop — exploit that for multi-engine layers.
- Add **FADE** (hidden) for overdubs that slowly evolve/replace; remember **FADE** and **NO DUB** are mutually exclusive.
- ⚠️ No published knob values — CLOCK, MODIFY, and MIX positions are dial-by-feel per pass. Treat the controls above as a recipe, not sourced settings.

Crucially you can switch freely between Tape/Stretch/Env after capture without erasing the loop, so each overdub pass can be a different engine. Real-Time Reverse Swell (Daydreaming / Backdrifts)
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- Wet MODE: Slip
- Wet MODIFY: CCW of noon = REVERSE
- Wet TIME: sampling size — LOW (~10–11:00) = instant reverse per note; HIGH (~1–2:00) = reversed phrases that follow behind you
- CLOCK: noon (or down for grit)
- MIX: to taste
- LEFT footswitch (Wet / freeze): freeze for a held reversed bed under a live lead

## Concept

Radiohead's signature reverse-bloom — Thom reversing ringing glockenspiel notes so they "fade in" (Daydreaming), and Jonny's reversed guitar (Backdrifts). MOOD's Slip does it live, in real time, while you sustain. **MODIFY CCW of noon = REVERSE** (the Unperson-confirmed reverse); **TIME = sampling size** (low for instant reverse on each note, high for reversed phrases that follow behind you, the glockenspiel "fades in" feel).

## How to play it

1. Set Wet MODE = **Slip**, MODIFY CCW of noon for reverse.
2. Set TIME: low (~10–11:00) for instant reverse on each note, high (~1–2:00) for reversed phrases that trail you.
3. Play a ringing pluck (banjo / VG pad) — it returns reversed, swelling in.
4. Add the **CLASSIC** dip for aliased crunch. CLOCK noon (or down for grit), MIX to taste.
5. **Freeze** (hold LEFT FS) for a held reversed bed under a live lead.

## Notes

- All 🟣 designed-to-emulate — no MOOD artist setting is documented and Radiohead never used one; this chases the *result* (Slip = the reverse method). Clock-face numbers are inferred starting points, dial by ear.

content:
Replace Trick — clear space & punch in glitches
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- RIGHT footswitch (Micro-Looper bypass): tap to bypass the Micro-Looper Channel — while bypassed it erases the loop and records live input in its place; tap back to playback to keep the new material
- Looper MODE: Tape / Stretch / Env to taste (dial from recipe — no published values)
- CLOCK: sets loop length/speed as usual (dial from recipe — no published knob values)

## Concept

The Micro-Looper's bypass doubles as a **replace** function. The instant you bypass the channel it starts erasing the existing loop and recording your input in its place — so bypassing isn't just "off," it's a live overwrite. That makes it a fast way to clear a section or punch in glitch stabs. It's distinct from **overdub** (which layers new material onto the loop) because **bypass replaces** what was there.

## How to play it

1. Have a micro-loop playing.
2. **Bypass the Micro-Looper Channel** (RIGHT footswitch) — it immediately starts erasing the loop and recording your live input in its place.
3. **Hold it bypassed** to clear space, or **punch quickly** for glitch stabs.
4. **Re-engage playback** to lock in the new/replaced material.

## Notes

- Manual "Overdubbing" p.31: "Replace."
- Distinct from overdub (which layers onto the loop) — bypass replaces what was there.
- ⚠️ Sourced from the official manual only (not yet corroborated by an in-repo transcript); no published knob values. Treat CLOCK / MODE above as a recipe, not sourced settings.

content:
Reverb Wash vs Multi-Tap Clusters
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- Wet MODE: Reverb
- Wet TIME: decay/size — CCW short, CW long
- Wet MODIFY: smear — MIN = multi-tap clusters, MAX = washed reverb, mid = hybrid

## Concept

The foundational reverb map. **MODIFY is smear**: at MIN you hear distinguishable multi-tap delay clusters; at MAX it washes out into reverb; in the middle you get "semisolid hybrids." A twist of MODIFY can also split the sound into flitty grains. **TIME** sets decay/size (CCW short, CW long). Everything frozen or rhythmic downstream depends on knowing where MODIFY lives.

## How to play it

1. Set Wet MODE = **Reverb**.
2. Set TIME for the decay/size you want (CCW = short, CW = long).
3. Sweep MODIFY: MIN for distinct multi-tap clusters, MAX for a washed reverb, mid for semisolid hybrids.
4. For granular textures, give MODIFY a twist to split the sound into flitty grains.

## Notes

- This is the reference map for every reverb-based patch — learn where MODIFY transitions from taps → wash → grains, because freeze and rhythmic moves build on it.

Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- Wet MODE: Delay
- Wet MODIFY: feedback near max (back off ~1:00 to avoid full self-oscillation)
- Wet TIME: slowly rotate clockwise once audio is repeating

## Concept

Recording a stretch into a delay-looper pile-up. With Delay **MODIFY (feedback) near max** the repeats pile up like a looper; back off to ~1:00 to avoid full self-oscillation. Once audio is repeating, **slowly rotate TIME clockwise** — the stretching effect gets recorded into the loop itself.

## How to play it

1. Set Wet MODE = **Delay**.
2. Set MODIFY (feedback) near max so repeats stack into a loop — pull back to ~1:00 if it tips into runaway self-oscillation.
3. Play until the audio is repeating on its own.
4. **Slowly rotate TIME clockwise** — the stretch bakes permanently into the looping repeats.

## Notes

- Clean stretch unless **CLASSIC** is on (which adds rubbery pitch).
- Delay is the **only** mode that passes audio between the two channels.

content:
Shimmer Pad
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- MIX: 2:00
- CLOCK: 2:00
- Wet TIME: 3:00
- Wet MODIFY: 2:00
- Wet MODE: Reverb
- Looper LENGTH: 1:00
- Looper MODIFY: 2x (octave up)
- Looper MODE: Tape
- ROUTING: IN+micro-loop

## Concept


Classic shimmer effect built from two MOOD channels working together: the **Reverb** provides a long, washed-out pad, and the **Tape micro-looper at 2x speed (octave up)** adds the bright, crystalline shimmer overtone. Routing is set to `IN+micro-loop` so the Wet reverb processes both your dry signal and the octave-up loop together, creating the feedback-shimmer illusion.

## How to play it


1. **Engage both channels.** Play a chord or sustained note — the Micro-Looper captures it and plays it back an octave up, which feeds into the Reverb wash.
2. **Hold the LEFT footswitch** to freeze the reverb into an infinite shimmering pad.
3. **Play over the frozen bed** — new notes add fresh shimmer layers on top.
4. **For evolving texture**, hold the RIGHT footswitch to overdub new material into the micro-loop while frozen.

## Notes


- **CLOCK at 2:00** keeps it clean and hi-fi — shimmer wants clarity, not grit. Drop to noon if you want a darker, degraded shimmer.
- **SMOOTH dip on** so Clock sweeps don't step audibly if you adjust live.
- **SPREAD on** scatters the reverb taps across the stereo field for width. Note that Blooper downstream will collapse this to mono — this patch is best heard through the H90/Chroma Console path or on headphones.
- **TRAILS on** so the shimmer pad sustains when you bypass.
- **Hidden TONE rolled to 1:00** tames any ice-pick frequencies from the octave-up content.
- Tape MODIFY is set to the 2x detent (one click CW of noon) for a clean octave-up. Push to 4x for a more extreme, synth-like two-octave shimmer.

content:
Slip Pseudo-Sitar & Glitch Trails
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- Wet MODE: Slip
- Wet TIME: sampling size — HIGH = harmonized phrases trail you (drone/sitar feel); LOW = instant pitch-shifter response, glitchier reverse-flavored stutters (dial by ear — no published value)
- Wet MODIFY: playback speed/direction in semitone steps — off neutral for sustained pitch-shifted harmonies, CCW of noon = reverse (dial by ear — no published value)

## Concept

Slip's continuous auto-sampling and pitch-shifting, run **live (not frozen)**, makes pseudo-sitar drones and glitchy reverse-flavored trails — whimsical harmonies that follow behind your playing. **TIME = sampling size**: high produces harmonized phrases that trail your notes (the drone/sitar feel); low gives an instant pitch-shifter response with glitchier, reverse-flavored stutters. **MODIFY = playback speed/direction in semitone steps** (CCW of noon = reverse). Great as interstitial/ambient filler between songs or under a solo. Distinct from the frozen-Slip glitch-synth and the doom Slip-reverb-smear: here Slip runs live, not frozen.

## How to play it

1. Set Wet MODE = **Slip**.
2. Use a higher **TIME** so harmonized phrases follow behind your notes (drone/sitar feel).
3. Set **MODIFY** off neutral for sustained pitch-shifted harmonies (semitone steps).
4. Lower **TIME** for an instant pitch-shifter response and glitchier, reverse-flavored stutters.
5. Optionally engage **SPREAD** for auto-panned drama; use as ambient filler between songs or under a solo.

## Notes

- Effects Database notes Slip is favored for pseudo-sitar sounds and glitchy/delayed reverse effects in solos and ambient pads between songs.
- Live (un-frozen) Slip distinguishes this from the frozen-Slip glitch-synth patch and the doom Slip-reverb-smear.
- ⚠️ No published numeric values — the sitar/interstitial framing is the sourced part, all settings are by ear. Treat the control descriptions as a dialable recipe, not measured positions.

content:
SPREAD — per-mode affected stereo image
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- Wet MODE: any (Reverb = scattered taps, Delay = ping-pong, Slip = smooth pan)
- Looper MODE: any (Env = pans over threshold, Tape = R-forward/L-reversed, Stretch = slow pan)
- CLOCK: sets pan/scatter speed together with the active mode's time control (dial to taste — no published values)
- STEREO WIDTH (hidden — Wet TIME): hold both footswitches + turn Wet TIME to set how wide the spread is (dial to taste)
- SPREAD SOLO (hidden — ROUTING): optional — spread only one channel instead of both

## Concept

SPREAD is the fastest way to make any mode wide and moving. It does **not** turn stereo on (MOOD is stereo by default — MISO handles a mono source); it **widens and animates the existing image**, and every mode has its own take on it. Reverb scatters its taps across the field, Delay ping-pongs L↔R (mirroring your input pan depth), Slip / Env / Stretch auto-pan, and Tape plays the right channel forward while the left channel runs in reverse. One dip, six distinct stereo behaviors.

## How to play it

1. Confirm you have a stereo image (stereo in, or MISO on for a mono source).
2. Flick the **SPREAD** dip on.
3. Pick a mode and play: Reverb taps scatter, Delay ping-pongs L↔R, Tape plays right-forward / left-reversed, Slip / Env / Stretch pan.
4. Hold both footswitches and turn **Wet TIME** to set **STEREO WIDTH**; use **SPREAD SOLO** (hidden, ROUTING) to spread only one channel.

## Notes

- No published clock-face values — controls above are a dialable recipe; the active mode's time control plus CLOCK set the pan/scatter speed, and Wet TIME (held) sets the width.
- SPREAD enhances/widens existing stereo — it does **not** turn stereo on (that's MISO).
- Tape's L-reversed / R-forward split is a distinctive, documented per-mode behavior worth exploiting for a wide degraded bed.
- Reviewers note the clean Delay ping-pong is "an absolute treat in a wide stereo rig."
- Rig flag: a mono downstream pedal collapses the spread — keep wide SPREAD for stereo-capable downstream stages.

SPREAD does not enable stereo (MOOD is stereo by default) — it widens and animates the existing image, the fastest way to make any mode wide and moving. (Factory dip feature — official video manual pt.2 + manual pp.36-39; demo review guitar.com — no published clock-face values, so dial from the recipe.)

content:
SPREAD SOLO — spread one channel only
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- SPREAD dip: on (required for any spread behavior)
- LEFT + RIGHT footswitches (hidden access): HOLD both until the LEDs go green, then move ROUTING
- ROUTING: flip toward the channel you want spread; MIDDLE = both channels spread (default)

## Concept

SPREAD normally scatters/ping-pongs both channels in stereo at once — all or nothing. This hidden option lets you apply SPREAD to **just one channel** while the other stays centered. Keep a mono/centered micro-loop legible but run it through a ping-pong **Delay**, or ping-pong the **Reverb** while **Stretch** stays a normal centered stereo. With the SPREAD dip on, enter hidden options (hold both footswitches until green) and move the **ROUTING** toggle toward the channel you want spread; the **MIDDLE** position spreads both (the default behavior).

## How to play it

1. Engage the **SPREAD** dip.
2. **Hold both footswitches** until the LEDs go green (hidden-options mode).
3. Move the **ROUTING** toggle toward the channel you want spread (MIDDLE = both get spread).
4. Exit; now only the chosen channel ping-pongs/scatters while the other stays centered — e.g. a mono micro-loop passed through a ping-pong delay.

## Notes

- Great for keeping a captured loop legible/centered while the wet effect animates around it.
- MIDDLE position spreads both channels (this is the default).
- Documented example: keep a mono micro-loop but pass it through a ping-pong delay.
- Honesty: this is a routing/toggle recipe — there are no published knob values to dial. The community walkthrough notes the spread side can also be set via the wet **MODE** toggle; flipping ROUTING toward a channel is the manual-documented path. Verify by ear which channel scatters.

A hidden option (official video manual pt.2 + community walkthrough; manual pp.14–17) that frees you from all-or-nothing spread.

content:
STEREO WIDTH — set the wet pan width
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- LEFT + RIGHT footswitches (hidden access): HOLD both until the LEDs go green, then turn Wet TIME
- Wet TIME (in hidden menu): CCW = narrow/near-mono, CW = wider; default mid
- SPREAD (back dip): must be ON for width to do anything
- MISO (back dip): engage first if your source is mono

## Concept

Dial exactly how wide the Wet Channel's stereo image spreads when **SPREAD** is engaged — from squished/near-mono to fully glorious wide. This is a hidden option set with the **Wet TIME** knob: at minimum the wet image is "squished completely," at maximum it backs out "sounding glorious." Think of it as the precision companion to the SPREAD dip — SPREAD turns the spread on, STEREO WIDTH says how much. Default is mid.

## How to play it

1. Engage the **SPREAD** dip (and **MISO** first if your source is mono).
2. **Hold both footswitches** until the LEDs go green (hidden-options mode).
3. Turn the **Wet TIME** knob: CCW narrows the wet image toward mono, CW opens it up wide.
4. Exit the hidden menu; **Wet TIME** returns to its normal time/decay duty.

## Notes

- Has **no audible effect unless SPREAD is on**.
- Use a narrower width when a mono stage sits downstream so the collapse is less jarring; go wide only when a stereo stage follows.
- Default is mid.

content:
Stretching 101 + Frozen Grain Wall
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- Looper MODE: Stretch
- Looper MODIFY: start MAX → slowly rotate toward NOON; NOON = frozen (infinitely repeats current slice). ⚠️ MAX = no effect
- Looper LENGTH: start MAX → gradually rotate down to minimum for stretching; once frozen, sizes the held grain (high = clearer phrase, low = blurry/grainy)
- CLOCK: lower = grainier

## Concept

The single best sustained-wall move: classic grainy time-stretch, then one frozen grain held into an infinite drone. Set Looper MODE = **Stretch**, both MODIFY and LENGTH to MAX, then slowly rotate MODIFY toward NOON for "good ol' stretching." **FROZEN: MODIFY exactly at NOON** stops the progression and infinitely repeats the current slice; LENGTH then sizes the held grain.

## How to play it

1. Set Looper MODE = **Stretch**. Set **both MODIFY and LENGTH to MAX**.
2. **Slowly rotate MODIFY toward NOON** — once it's moving slowly, **gradually rotate LENGTH down to minimum** → "good ol' stretching."
3. To FREEZE: set **MODIFY exactly at NOON** — this stops progression and infinitely repeats the current slice.
4. Use **LENGTH** to size the held grain: high = clearer/repeating phrase, low = blurry/grainy.

## Notes

- ⚠️ **MODIFY at MAX outputs no effect** regardless of LENGTH.
- Lower CLOCK = grainier; firmware 1.1 restores MkI Stretch character inside CLASSIC.
- **Slot L = "Frozen Grain Wall"** (with Reverb freeze layered, CLASSIC on). Perry Frank's Reverb+Stretch "sprawling epic" lives here (reverb-stretch-sprawling-epic).

provenance.title: Stretching 101 + Frozen Grain Wall
provenance.description: The single best sustained-wall move — classic grainy time-stretch, then MODIFY exactly at noon freezes one grain into an infinite drone. The basis of Slot L. (Perry Frank's Reverb+Stretch epic.)

content:
SYNC (in-time captures, clock-lockable)
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- LEFT + RIGHT footswitches (hidden access): HOLD both (LEDs green), then move the Wet MODE toggle
- MIDI clock (CC51 follow / CC53 div wet / CC54 div loop): feed clock to lock to Big Time / Blooper / Digitakt

## Concept

Tying one channel's timing to the other; capturing rhythmic ideas in time, then committing downstream (Blooper). A hidden option: hold **both footswitches** (LEDs green), then move the **Wet MODE toggle**. **LEFT** = Micro-Looper synced to Wet (loop length set by Wet TIME — great for in-time capture). **MIDDLE** = unsynced. **RIGHT** = Wet synced to Micro-Looper (Wet TIME steps in rhythmic relation to the loop). Combine with MIDI clock to lock to Big Time / Blooper / Digitakt.

## How to play it

1. **Hold both footswitches** until the LEDs go green (hidden-options mode).
2. Move the **Wet MODE toggle**: LEFT = loop follows Wet, MIDDLE = unsynced, RIGHT = Wet follows the loop.
3. For external lock, feed MIDI clock from the rig master (send CC51>0 to follow; CC53 = wet division, CC54 = loop division).
4. Capture in time, then commit downstream to Blooper.

## Notes

- ⚠️ MIDI clock is **ignored in Synth Mode**, and a stray MIDI Note auto-engages Synth Mode — watch this when the Digitakt sequences it (CC51 clock-follow, CC53/CC54 divisions).

content:
Synth Mode — play CLOCK with MIDI notes
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- MIDI Note input (via Chase Bliss MIDIbox): send a Note to auto-engage Synth Mode — Note transposes the wet output (no published note-to-pitch table; explore by ear)
- CLOCK: becomes pitch control in Synth Mode; move the knob physically to exit back to normal/clock-synced behavior
- Synth output mode: Open (constant drone), On/Off (gate sustain), or ADSR (enveloped) — set over MIDI
- ADSR + portamento + velocity: Attack/Decay/Sustain/Release, portamento and velocity are user-set over MIDI (no factory numbers — dial from recipe)
- Exit (CC59): send CC59 to leave Synth Mode (or physically move CLOCK)

## Concept

Play MOOD's CLOCK — and thereby its pitch and character — straight from a MIDI keyboard or sequencer. Sending any MIDI **Note** auto-engages **Synth Mode**: CLOCK becomes pitch control and the note input transposes the wet output, so you can "play" a frozen pad or drone as a monophonic granular synth. Synth Mode adds Attack/Decay/Sustain/Release, portamento, velocity, and three output modes (Open / On-Off / ADSR). It's a strong move for sequenced, pitched degradation — but watch the gotcha: Synth Mode silently overrides MIDI clock sync. New to MkII, flagged in Doug Hanson's demo.

## How to play it

1. Connect a MIDI controller/sequencer through a Chase Bliss **MIDIbox** (converts MIDI to the 1/4" TRS MOOD expects).
2. Capture or freeze a sustained pad/drone as source material.
3. Send a **MIDI Note** — MOOD auto-engages **Synth Mode**, CLOCK becomes pitch control, and the note input transposes the wet output.
4. Choose an output: **Open** (constant drone), **On/Off** (gate sustain), or **ADSR** (enveloped); dial Attack/Decay/Sustain/Release plus portamento and velocity over MIDI.
5. Exit Synth Mode with **CC59** — or physically move the **CLOCK** knob — to restore normal / clock-synced behavior.

## Notes

- ⚠️ MIDI clock is **IGNORED** in Synth Mode — a stray Note from a sequencer (e.g. a Digitakt) silently knocks MOOD out of clock sync. Watch for this when sequencing a stack.
- No published note-to-pitch table and no factory ADSR numbers — the controls above are a dialable recipe; explore by ear / set everything over MIDI.
- Full setup details live in the separate MOOD MkII MIDI manual (not the main pedal manual).
- Doug Hanson's demo flags this as new-to-MkII: "play MOOD's CLOCK with a MIDI controller by sending MIDI notes."

Powerful for sequenced, pitched degradation — but it silently overrides MIDI clock sync. (Factory MIDI feature, new to MkII; no published note-map or ADSR numbers.)

content:
The Unperson — dry input over a reverb-soaked loop
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:

## Concept

Playing dry over a drenched loop — "beautiful ambient setup," ideal with synth / OP-1 / VG-800 sources. Set ROUTING = **micro-loop only** so the Wet hits only the loop while your input stays dry, with Wet MODE = **Reverb** on the loop. Run a loop, then use **DIRECT MICRO-LOOP / FADE** (hidden) to push the loop into the background.

## How to play it

1. Set ROUTING = **micro-loop only** and Wet MODE = **Reverb**.
2. Capture a loop (synth / OP-1 / VG-800 source) — the Reverb soaks the loop only.
3. Play dry on top — your live input bypasses the Wet path.
4. Use **DIRECT MICRO-LOOP / FADE** (hidden) to push the soaked loop into the background under your dry playing.

## Notes

- Directly rig-relevant — VG-800/OP-1 are perfect looper food here.
- Demoed with Vong Replay synth, Mutable Rings, and OP-1 as sources.

content:
TONE — wet hi-cut to darken / V1 voicing
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- Both footswitches (hold): hold until LEDs turn green to enter the hidden-options menu
- Wet MODIFY (in hidden menu = TONE/hi-cut): fully CW = brightest (default); turn CCW to roll off highs; near max CCW the cut is drastic — set by ear, not by eye

## Concept

Tame the MkII's brighter, more-present wet voicing with a hidden high-cut filter, pushing the wash back toward the darker/mellower original MOOD sound or simply sitting it under a mix. It's a simple but drastic-at-max low-pass on the Wet Channel, set with the Wet MODIFY knob inside the hidden options menu — the documented gentle way to keep MOOD's degraded wash from getting harsh before downstream stages.

## How to play it

1. Hold both footswitches until the LEDs turn green (hidden-options menu).
2. Turn the Wet MODIFY knob counter-clockwise to roll off highs (CW = brightest/default).
3. Stop where the wash sits under your mix or matches the darker original-MOOD voicing.
4. Exit by releasing/tapping out; the Wet MODIFY knob returns to its normal smear/feedback duty.

## Notes

- No published clock-face / numeric value for the cut — this is a dialable recipe set by ear. The cut is gentle in the lower range but drastic near max, so listen, don't set it by eye.
- Default is fully CW (brightest); on-camera the cut at max was drastic ("took all the highs out").
- This is the documented gentle way to keep MOOD's degraded wash from getting harsh before downstream stages.

content:
Freeze Double-Time x SYNC — looper + frozen-delay layers
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- Looper MODE: Tape/Stretch — capture loop 1 first
- Wet MODE: Delay
- Wet TIME: delay length — vary for different secondary-loop lengths (dial from recipe)
- Wet MODIFY: feedback (dial from recipe)
- LEFT footswitch (Wet / freeze): HOLD to freeze the Delay into a second micro-loop

## Concept

Run **two independent loop layers simultaneously**: the Drolo Micro-Looper holds one captured loop while a **frozen Delay** holds a second, acting as a secondary micro-loop. Two clocks of repetition at once. What sets this apart from a plain double-time freeze is the **SYNC** hidden option — set it so the frozen delay's TIME steps relate to the loop length, locking the two layers rhythmically into one combined groove.

## How to play it

1. Capture a micro-loop with the **Micro-Looper** (Looper MODE = **Tape/Stretch**) — this is loop 1.
2. Set Wet MODE = **Delay**, play a phrase into it, then **HOLD the LEFT footswitch** to freeze the delay into a second loop.
3. Adjust **Delay TIME** to try different secondary-loop lengths.
4. In the hidden menu, set **SYNC** (Wet MODE toggle, RIGHT) so the frozen delay locks rhythmically to the micro-loop length — two synced loop layers.

## Notes

- The manual's "Freeze Idea: Double Time" explicitly suggests pairing with the **SYNC** hidden option — that combination is what this patch captures beyond the plain double-time freeze (see sibling patch freeze-idea-double-time).
- A frozen delay behaves as a **secondary micro-loop**, independent of the Micro-Looper channel.
- **No published knob values** — TIME, MODIFY, and the loop lengths are by feel / locked by SYNC. Treat the controls above as a dialable recipe, not sourced settings.

Vary Delay TIME for different secondary lengths and engage the hidden SYNC option so the frozen delay locks rhythmically to the loop length. From the official manual's 'Freeze Idea: Double Time' recipe (pp.22–23) plus the SYNC hidden option (p.17).

content:
Trail Catcher (bake ambience into the loop)
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- ROUTING: includes Wet on the loop (run the micro-loop through the Reverb)
- Wet MODE: Reverb
- RIGHT footswitch (Micro-Looper): briefly turn the Micro-Looper OFF and back ON to resample the reverb trails into the loop

## Concept

Resampling reverb trails permanently into a micro-loop. Run a micro-loop through the Reverb (ROUTING includes Wet on the loop), then briefly turn the **Micro-Looper OFF and back ON** — it resamples the reverb trails into the loop. Because the looper records while bypassed/always-listening, any Wet or upstream effect is baked in permanently.

## How to play it

1. Set ROUTING so the micro-loop runs through the Reverb, and Wet MODE = **Reverb**.
2. Let the loop pick up reverb trails.
3. **Briefly turn the Micro-Looper OFF and back ON** — the reverb trails are resampled into the loop.

## Notes

- ⚠️ **Plan the moment — it's permanent.**
- Nuance: while **overdubbing**, Wet effects are NOT recorded (clean input only); baking happens only in the bypassed always-listening state.

content:
TRAILS — keep the wash on bypass
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- TRAILS dip: on — Wet modes fade out smoothly after bypass rather than stopping instantly

## Concept

Let the Wet Channel smoothly fade out after you bypass the pedal instead of cutting dead, so toggling the effect mid-performance doesn't kill the vibe. The recommended default-on dip for ambient/drone work where an abrupt cut would break the spell. Behavior is identical to MkI TRAILS.

## How to play it

1. Flick the **TRAILS** dip on.
2. Build a wet wash / freeze.
3. Bypass the pedal mid-passage — the wet tail fades out smoothly instead of cutting off.
4. Leave **TRAILS** on as your default for ambient sets so toggling never kills the wash.

## Notes

- No knob values — TRAILS is a behavior toggle, not a dialed setting. Dial the Wet Channel itself to taste.
- Power-user preference: "I like to have trails engaged… so it keeps a smoother effect… I don't want it to kill the vibe."
- Same behavior as MkI TRAILS.
- The looper is separate — TRAILS governs the **Wet Channel** fade; in true-bypass the looper doesn't run at all.

A factory dip-switch feature documented in the official video manual pt.2 and the community hidden-options walkthrough (no knob values — it's a behavior toggle).

content:
True-Bypass mode (footswitch toggle)
Device: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

Settings:
- LEFT + RIGHT footswitches (true-bypass toggle): tap BOTH footswitches 3× to enter true-bypass; tap either footswitch to exit back to buffered bypass
- All three LEDs: blink red to confirm true-bypass is active

## Concept

By default MOOD sits in buffered bypass with trails. Tapping **both footswitches three times** in quick succession flips it into hard **true-bypass**, pulling the pedal entirely out of the signal path — all three LEDs blink red to confirm. The catch: the always-listening Micro-Looper does **not** run in true-bypass, so its continuous capture stops working. Tap either footswitch to exit back to buffered bypass with trails. There are no knob values here — this is a footswitch gesture, not a knob recipe.

## How to play it

1. Tap both footswitches three times in quick succession.
2. Confirm: all three LEDs blink red — you're now in true-bypass.
3. Use it when you want MOOD entirely out of the chain.
4. Tap either footswitch to exit and return to buffered bypass with trails.

## Notes

- This patch has **no published knob values** — it's a footswitch gesture/toggle, not a dialable knob recipe.
- ⚠️ The Micro-Looper does **NOT** run in true-bypass — if you rely on always-listening capture, stay in buffered bypass.
- Default is buffered bypass with trails (keep **TRAILS** on so toggling mid-performance doesn't kill the wash).
- Same gesture also lives in the hidden/reset family — don't trigger it by accident.
