"Bouncy Thermae" Pitch-Sequenced Banjo Lead (clock-locked)
Artists: Radiohead
Instrument: banjo
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, Chase Bliss Big Time, Hologram Chroma Console, Eventide H90, MXNHLT PORTA424

A melodic hook where the *repeats are the melody* — single banjo notes stepped through a scale by the centerpiece, locked to the rig clock so it sits in a sequenced arrangement. ⭐ signature-fit.

This is a 🟣 designed integration of owned-gear patches; no artist ever played *this* chain. The Taste-ref names the sound it chases, and the per-unit patch sheets carry their own provenance.

## Signal path


EBM-5 banjo (GK-5) → **VG-800 (#3 GR-300 Thick-Synth Lead)** → Clean (#2 Transparent Enhancer) → [Board 2 thru] → **Big Time (#7 Bouncy Thermae, Factory #4)** → Chroma → **H90 (#25 PrismShift Self-Generating Stereo Arp Bed, Mix low)** → PORTA424 → tape. *(Big Time sits 2nd on Board 3; H90 is later on Board 3 — order preserved.)*

## Per-unit


- VG-800 **#3 GR-300 Thick-Synth Lead** — `PITCH A = +12` (or +7/+5), `COMP SW ON` extends the hexa-VCO decay (the banjo fast-decay fix), `ENV MOD` for pick-triggered wah. Recall GK **#1 EBM5 BANJO**.
- Clean **#2 Transparent Enhancer** — slow Attack keeps the pluck attack uncompressed so the GR-300 transient triggers the Thermae steps cleanly; the cleanest banjo-as-lead base.
- Big Time **#7 Bouncy Thermae (Factory #4)** — MODE Short, STATE Compressed, SCALE Octave (or Oct+4+5 = maps to tap subdivisions), MOTION Square; **SCALE IGNORE optional ON** for cleaner sine + scaled steps. Feed single notes; repeats arpeggiate into octave ladders.
- H90 **#25 PrismShift Self-Generating Stereo Arp Bed** — from factory "Sequential Chimes"; **Spread = FULL** so arps pan L↔R, slow Step Length for an ambient bed under the Big Time sequence; Mid voice stays live/playable. Mix low (the bed, not the lead).

## Routing


Mono banjo front; Big Time MISO to stereo. **DT2 (or 61SL) is clock master.** Big Time slaved: subdivision via CC54, p-lock COLOR/TIME via CC14–19 from the DT2 for grid-quantized moves (Big Time #2 method). H90 tempo-sync its delay components to the same MIDI clock. 61SL #5 (Big Time Centerpiece Performance Template) can ride TIME/WET live without diving into the pedal. Keep TILT EQ above noon — defined banjo transients are what the Thermae steps fire on.

## Sound


A self-arpeggiating banjo melody that climbs scale-quantized octave ladders in time, with a slow stereo PrismShift chime bed cascading underneath — a sequenced, glassy, banjo-driven hook.

Taste-ref: art-rock-studio-as-instrument (sequenced/stepped pitched delay; CB Thermae lineage) + the electronic-groove-first lean of letting a locked figure generate melody.

## Play


Play *less* than you think — sparse single plucks. The Big Time SCALE stepping and the H90 self-generating arp do the density. Use Big Time STEP MODE (tap LEFT) to manually walk the pitch for a composed run, or leave it on the clock for hands-free.

Crap-Amp Demo Grind
Artists: Car Seat Headrest, Modest Mouse
Instrument: baritone/VG-800
Gear: Chase Bliss Clean, Longsword, JHS Kilt v10, Chase Bliss Generation Loss, MXNHLT PORTA424, JHS 424, UA Apollo x8

A dry, mid-forward, demo-grade rhythm grind — old-pedal-into-a-practice-amp character on baritone/VG-800, under a groovebox kick, printed to four-track. A 🟣 DOUG-designed integration (EAE Stormbringer voice re-pointed at the cluster; no artist used these boxes).

## Signal path


baritone/VG-800 → CB Clean → Longsword → JHS Kilt v10 → [End] CB Generation Loss → PORTA424 → JHS 424 → tape. (Digitakt/MPC kick clocks the part underneath.)

## Per-unit


- **CB Clean** — **#7 Always-On Huge Fuzz Feeder** so even quiet picking triggers the downstream grind evenly (or **#6 Baritone Drone Sustainer** if the baritone needs taming first).
- **Longsword** — **#LSW-LF1 Crap-Amp Vintage Grind (Stormbringer-lean)** (Level/Drive ~1–2:00, Mid boosted at 1 kHz, DIODE silicon, SHIFT up). EAE's own "old distortion pedal into a practice amp" voice. Keep it DRY.
- **JHS Kilt v10** — **#KLT-LF1 Telephone Demo-Crunch (thin/console-overload)** (Gain 10–11:00, Tone 1:00, Low-Cut up = deliberately thin/telephone). Pushes the warts audible.
- **CB Generation Loss** — **#30 Brittle Mid-Forward AM-Jangle Bed (GL-LF2)** (Model 7–9, thin/narrow) for the small-speaker demo character, or **#1 Subtle Tape Age**.
- **PORTA424** — **#12 Bedroom 4-Track Demo Print** (9V, trashy) — the 4-track grit terminus.
- **JHS 424** — **#13 Demo-Is-The-Song 4-Track Grit (424-LF1)** (Gain 1/2 12:00, under the gate) → Apollo.

## Routing / sync


Mono throughout (baritone/VG → mono board → mono tape). **Don't crank both tape boxes** — split the destruction: if PORTA424 is at 9V/trashy, keep 424 light, or vice versa. Groovebox is clock master (MPC or DT2); the grind part is played live over it, not sequenced.

## Sound


Thin, honking, mid-forward demo crunch on the baritone — the sound of a half-broken dirt box into a small amp, captured to cassette. Sits as a rhythm bed, not a lead.

## Play


Set the grind, play the rhythm part dry over the groovebox kick. For a brittle stab section, swap Kilt for the gated path in the Half-Broken DS-2 Gated Stab Beat chain. Ride instrument volume for the clean↔hair dynamic (the Kilt cleans up beautifully with the guitar volume).

**Taste-ref:** lo-fi-prolific-volume — CSH/Modest Mouse "old distortion pedal into a practice amp" demo grind. 🟣 designed (EAE Stormbringer voice re-pointed at the cluster; no artist used these boxes).

Crescendo Drone Arc
Artists: Swans
Instrument: baritone/banjo (GK-5 → VG-800)
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, MXR M173 Classic 108 Fuzz, EarthQuaker Devices Hizumitas, Longsword, OBNE Dark Star V3, Walrus Audio QI Etherealizer, Chase Bliss Big Time, Eventide H90, Chase Bliss Generation Loss, Novation 61SL MkIII, Elektron Digitakt 2, Akai MPC Sample

The Swans crescendo as a **whole-board performance** — rise from near-silence to a pulverising sustained wall via repetition + layering + a late dynamic slab. Pairs a dark low wall (baritone) with brittle icy stabs over a frozen drone bed, building to "four church choirs." The arc IS the patch; resist set-and-forget. (Gira uses *no pedals* — volume + sustain + overtones + layering — so the whole rig chases the *result* of physics, not a setting.)

This is a **designed integration** — no artist ever used this exact chain. Real method = Gira's no-pedals loud-amp wall (Gibson Lucille + GK 1000 bass head + Mesa 4x12s) + Westberg's Ibanez AS-200 → DS-1 → Dyna Comp → Orange Thunderverb — none of this rig. ⚠️ the wall is the *result* of physics (sustain + bass weight + freeze-layering + a dynamics arc), not a single patch; "four church choirs" = freeze/Multiply + freeze pads, not live instruments. 🟣 designed.

## Signal path


baritone/banjo (GK-5 → **VG-800** baritone + banjo lead) → **CB Clean** (dynamic swell from near-silence) → **MXR 108** (grinding bite) → **Hizumitas** (sustaining chordal wall) → **Longsword** (drone-bed feeder / late op-amp slab) → Board 2 → **Dark Star V3** (near-silence frozen drone bed, Board-2 terminus) → **QI Etherealizer** (galaxy-wash crescendo freeze + oscillate) → Board 3 → **Big Time** (oceanic freeze + one-stomp climax) → **H90** (cavernous Blackhole freeze) → tape.

*Under it:* Digitakt/MPC motorik 16ths via the 61SL clock.

## Per-unit (staged as the arc)


- **(1) Near-silence —** **Dark Star V3 #32 DS-PP2 Swans Near-Silence Frozen Drone Bed** (Mix 1, Decay 12, Filter 11–12 dark warm, Crush 11 barely-there, **Aux = Hold**: strum a baritone/banjo drone, freeze it into a barely-audible static bed) + **QI #30 QI-PP1 Swans Galaxy-Wash Crescendo** short-press Freeze (the barely-audible grain start). **VG-800 #7 Doom Baritone Wall (−7 STEP)** or **#5 VIO Bowed Swell Drone** as the source; **CB Clean #12 Dynamic Volume Swell** to bring it up from silence (Wet = Swell In ~noon–1:00). ⚠️ Dark Star Hold passes new notes bone-dry — swell in via the dry path / expression.
- **(2) Pulse —** clock-locked motorik 16ths from **Digitakt/MPC** under **Longsword LS-PP3 Swans Crescendo Drone-Bed Feeder** (DIODE center · Drive ~10:00 smooth bloom · Low/High ~11:00 softened · Mid SHIFT down 300 Hz ~1:00 body · Boost OFF — a *stable* bed you swell up). **61SL = clock master** drives the kraut pulse.
- **(3) Grind + stabs —** **MXR 108 #13 108-PP1 Westberg Grinding Bite** (OUTPUT ~12:00 to unity · FUZZ ~12–1:00 mid-gain grind · BUFFER ON) feeding **Hizumitas #13 HZ-PP1 Swans Sustaining Chordal Wall** (Volume ~1:00 · Sustain ~2:00 just shy of max so a chord still reads *as a chord* · Tone ~1:00 bass side = the "warm guitar/bass hum"). Brittle icy stabs over the warm bed = **108 #14 108-PP2 Icy Brittle Stab** (FUZZ 2–3:00 into the gate · **BUFFER OFF** = thin/gated/crackly) on the bright VG/banjo line, OR **Hizumitas #15 HZ-PP3 Joy Division Dark Treble-Cut Rhythm** for the darker option. Gira's "icy stabs over warm hum."
- **(4) Crescendo —** kick the **Hizumitas wall** to full + the **VG-800 baritone**, then **QI #30 QI-PP1** long-press **Freeze** (Space → 100%) + hold **Tap/Osc** (delay self-oscillates into a saturated snowball over several seconds) = the overwhelming wall. Add **Big Time #4 Oceanic Drone Bed** (FREEZE a chord into a non-degrading pad) and/or **Big Time #10 One-Stomp Climax (OVERLOAD ramp)** (hold RIGHT in Long → ramps COLOR+FEEDBACK to a wall, release to collapse). **H90 #6 Blackhole Freeze Drone** locks the cavernous bed under it = "four church choirs."
- **(5) Collapse/fade —** release the freezes; **Gen Loss #6 Tape-Stop Doom Cadence** (Aux = Stop) can halt the whole wet voice into a dying repeat that Big Time catches.
- **(Late slab variant) —** for the BC,NR-adjacent "kick the door in," **Longsword LS-PP1 Op-Amp Sabbath Slab** (Boost footswitch ON as the door-kick) and/or **Hizumitas HZ-PP2 Big-Muff Sabbath Slab** — park off until the climax.

## Routing / sync


The arc is a **dynamics performance, never a static patch.** **61SL = clock master** drives the motorik 16ths (Digitakt/MPC). Board 2 stays **Stereo, trails on** (Dark Star Board-2 terminus). ⚠️ **RIG-CRITICAL: pad/reamp the VG-800 line level before the Qi** (no level switch — it clips hot). ⚠️ **Dark Star Hold + QI Freeze pass new notes bone-dry** — swell the live wall up *over* the frozen beds via CB Clean's dynamic swell / a volume pedal, not by re-triggering into the freeze. Let ONE box own the big space per moment (Dark Star early, then QI + H90 at the peak) — don't max three reverbs (mud). The crescendo build is **WET/FEEDBACK riding up**, not added notes. Watch Big Time WET before OVERLOAD (it's "scary loud"); hold MODE to panic-reset.

## Sound


A barely-audible frozen baritone drone that a kraut pulse emerges under, warm sustaining chordal walls layering up with icy brittle stabs on top, building over minutes via repetition + freeze-layering into an overwhelming, self-oscillating, cavernous wall — four church choirs — then collapsing. Cold and crushing.

## Play


Strum a baritone drone → **Dark Star Aux = Hold** + **QI short-press Freeze** to seat the barely-audible bed. **CB Clean dynamic-swell** the live source up from silence. Start the motorik pulse (61SL/Digitakt). Layer the 108-grind → Hizumitas wall, drop brittle stabs on top. At the peak: **QI long-press Freeze → hold Tap/Osc**, **Big Time OVERLOAD hold**, **H90 Blackhole Freeze** — let the wall consume. Then release everything (or **Gen Loss Aux=Stop** tape-halt) for the collapse. Five to seven minutes of one chord, repeated, growing.

## Taste-ref


Swans — "The Seer" / "Bring the Sun" sustained crescendo walls (Gira/Westberg volume + sustain + overtones + layering, "four church choirs"); the dynamics arc from near-silence to pulverising wall.

Dark Star Frozen Bed + Live Wall Swelling Up From Near-Silence
Artists: Swans
Instrument: baritone (Jazzmaster via GK-5 → VG-800)
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, EarthQuaker Devices Hizumitas, Walrus Audio QI Etherealizer, OBNE Dark Star V3, Chase Bliss Big Time

The "Bring the Sun" begin-from-a-drone architecture — a barely-audible frozen bed, then the live wall swells up over it from near-silence into a crescendo. Two layers of sustain at once. Designed integration; Swans layer real instruments over minutes on a loud stage — the freeze + swell manufactures the static "many sustained voices" bed and the rise in the box.

## Signal path


Baritone JM (GK-5 → **VG-800 #5 VIO Bowed Swell Drone**) → **CB Clean #6 Baritone Drone Sustainer** + **Clean #12 Dynamic Volume Swell** (the near-silence build) → Hizumitas #13 (HZ-PP1, the live wall, kicked in over the bed) → (Middle board) → **Walrus QI** parallel → **OBNE Dark Star V3 #32 (DS-PP2) Swans Near-Silence Frozen Drone Bed** (Aux = Hold) → (End board) → Big Time bypassed → tape.

## Per-unit


- **VG-800 #5:** VIO removes the pick attack for an attackless drone.
- **Dark Star DS-PP2 (#32):** **Mix 1 (mostly wet) · Decay 12 · Multiply 12 · Filter 11–12 (slightly dark/warm) · Crush 11 (light bit-crush, "barely there") · Lag 1**, **Aux = Hold** to freeze a baritone/banjo chord into a static barely-audible bed.
- **Clean #6 / #12:** the AUX swell (#12) bows the *live* Hizumitas wall up from silence over it. Stereo, trails on (Dark Star is the Board-2 terminus, #28).

## Routing


Stereo from Dark Star onward. **GOTCHA (DS-PP2):** while Hold is engaged, new notes pass BONE-DRY — that's fine here, because the live wall (Hizumitas) is a separate dry-forward voice swelling in over the frozen bed; don't expect to re-trigger the frozen reverb. Build the bed FIRST (freeze), then swell the wall.

## Sound


A near-silent static drone bed under a slowly-rising saturated wall — the literal Swans crescendo architecture. Taste-ref: Swans "Bring the Sun" — drone-barely-audible → instruments stacked over minutes.

## Play


(1) Strum baritone, freeze it into the Dark Star bed (Aux Hold), barely audible. (2) Engage Clean's swell and bow the Hizumitas wall up from near-silence. (3) Repeat the chord, let it consume. (4) Collapse. This is a *performance arc*, not a static patch.

content:
Detuning Modulated Verb
Artists: Radiohead, Hammock
Instrument: baritone
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, OBNE Dark Star V3, Strymon Big Sky, Chase Bliss MOOD MkII

A modulated reverb that drifts and detunes under a sustained source — the queasy, warbling pad (Hammock's "more warble"), not a static hall. The modulated-detuning-verb brief. This is a 🟣 DOUG-designed integration; no artist used this exact pedal chain, the Taste-ref names the sound it chases.

## Signal path


Baritone JM (GK-5) → **VG-800** (VIO bowed swell) → **CB Clean** → [Board 1] → **Dark Star V3** (chorused-detune crushed wash) **and/or** [Board 3] → **Big Sky** (Detune Verb / Falling Shimmer) → tape.

## Per-unit


- **VG-800 — #5 VIO Bowed Swell Drone** (attackless, `NORMAL MIX OFF`) — a smooth bowed source is ideal for a detuning verb to grab; or **#11 Organ Drone** for a thicker pad.
- **CB Clean — #6 Baritone Drone Sustainer** (full-range envelope to tame the boom; slow release to extend into a bed).
- **Dark Star V3 — #27 Crushed ambient wash** (Pitch 1 detune up / Pitch 2 detune down = chorused width, Crush 9 heavy sample-rate, Filter 11) **or #7 Detune / chorus width** (a smidge off the center notch + Lag-wiggle for chorus). This is the on-Board-2 detuning verb.
- **Big Sky (End-board version) — #12 "Detune Verb"** (Shift1 −10 cen / Shift2 +10 cen, INPUT, MOD off = clean detune) **or #11 Falling Shimmer** (both voices −10%, REGEN — a continuously sinking, queasy wall) **or #2 Drone Wall (Cloud, freeze)** with **MOD 1:00** for slow movement.

## Routing


Stereo. Run the detune on **either** Dark Star (Board 2) **or** Big Sky (Board 3), not both — two detuned verbs beat against each other into seasickness (use that on purpose only if you want chaos). Keep MOD speed **slow** (Big Sky #1's "avoid fast/seasick" note).

## Sound


A reverb that visibly *moves* — pitches drifting ±10 cents, chorusing against themselves, the tail sinking or warbling. The "recorded-wrong" detune without bright shimmer.

## Play


Bow-swell the VIO source in (instrument volume or Clean's Dynamic Swell #12) → let the detuning verb bloom → ride Big Sky **MOD** or Dark Star **Pitch 2** by hand for live drift. For the Ful Stop bed specifically, layer **MOOD TB3** (frozen reverb + CLOCK-down drift) underneath.

**Taste-ref:** art-rock-studio-as-instrument — Radiohead "Ful Stop" unison-drift wash; Hammock's detuned-verb "more warble" philosophy (Big Sky #23).

Digitakt Crushed Loop → Console → Tape
Artists: Daft Punk, LCD Soundsystem
Instrument: synth (Digitakt loop)
Gear: Elektron Digitakt 2, Chase Bliss Clean, JHS Colour Box V2, Chase Bliss Generation Loss, MXNHLT PORTA424, JHS 424, UA Apollo x8

A locked Digitakt loop whose timbre opens and closes over a long build, run through the Neve console front end and printed to cassette — the filter-house move wearing a recorded-wrong coat. A 🟣 DOUG-designed integration; the sidechain is an LFO/limiter approximation (no true sidechain key on the DT2; Clean fakes it on the bus), flagged.

## Signal path


Digitakt 2 (main out, stereo) → CB Clean (end-of-chain bus role) → JHS Colour Box V2 (XLR/line, PAD on) → CB Generation Loss → PORTA424 → JHS 424 → tape.

## Per-unit


- **Digitakt 2** — **#32 Filter-House Loop (open/close cutoff sweep)** as the timbre engine: 2–4-bar loop, LOOP ON, multimode FILTER low + RES high-not-screaming, **LFO → FILTER FREQUENCY** triangle very slow (one cycle over many bars) + a touch of **BIT REDUCTION** for SP-1200 grit; pair **#23 Ambient Send-FX** (ping-pong delay ~88 / dark reverb ~90) for depth. Clock-master template = **#29 DT2 MIDI / Clock-Master Rig Template**.
- **CB Clean** — **#13 Pseudo-Sidechain Bus Limiter** (Ricky Tinez) end-of-chain so a hot kick ducks the whole bus = the dance pump without a sidechain jack (Dry down, cut lows so bass doesn't over-trigger). Requires redeploying Clean to a stereo end slot.
- **JHS Colour Box V2** — **#10 Drum-Bus / Stereo-Loop Crush** (XLR input mandatory, PAD ON, HI for crush / LO for glue, HI-PASS ~9:00 so the low end doesn't pump) — the broken-console saturation on the loop bus.
- **CB Generation Loss** — **#10 Filtered Lo-Fi / "AM Radio" Small-Speaker Bed** (Model 7–9, band-limited, mid-forward) so the loop sits like a broken radio, OR **#1 Subtle Tape Age** for lighter patina.
- **PORTA424** — **#1 Always-On Cassette Print** (Trim 9:00, 18V) for clean cassette glue, or **#12 Bedroom 4-Track Demo Print** if you want the grit obvious.
- **JHS 424** — **#1 Subtle Always-On Tape Print** (Gain 1 9:00, Gain 2 10:00) — finish + mono-commit to Apollo; let PORTA424 carry tone.

## Routing / sync


**Digitakt = clock master** (CLOCK + TRANSPORT SEND on); its LFO-on-cutoff is the build, locked to the grid. The Colour Box is a **MONO device** — sum the DT2 stereo to mono into it (or process the bus mono). Clean redeployed to a **stereo end slot** for the pseudo-sidechain to pay off; the kick run a touch hot so it pushes the bus down each hit. Don't crank both tape boxes — PORTA424 = the tape here, 424 = level only.

## Sound


A four-on-the-floor (or motorik) loop that breathes open across minutes, ducking on the kick, saturated through a broken Neve and dulled to a small-speaker cassette bed — groove-first but recorded-wrong.

## Play


Start the loop, ride the DT2 filter cutoff open over the build (or let the slow LFO do it), bring layers in with **#25 Hands-Free LAST/NOT-LAST Auto-Fill** so the box plays its own transitions while both hands ride pedals. Foot the Colour Box from glue (LO) to crush (HI) at the drop.

**Taste-ref:** electronic-groove-first (Daft Punk filter-house / LCD pump) filtered through the lo-fi degrade arc. 🟣 — the sidechain is an LFO/limiter approximation (no true sidechain key on the DT2; Clean fakes it on the bus), flagged.

Filter-House Build
Artists: Daft Punk, LCD Soundsystem
Instrument: synth/sampler + banjo/baritone (VG-800)
Gear: Novation 61SL MkIII, Elektron Octatrack MkII, Akai MPC Sample, Elektron Digitakt 2, Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, MXR M173 Classic 108 Fuzz, EarthQuaker Devices Hizumitas, Chase Bliss Big Time, MXNHLT PORTA424, JHS 424, UA Apollo x8

Groove-first, additive, filter-house — a 2–4-bar loop locked and never changed while **filter cutoff automation opens it over a long build**, a bouncing acid bass underneath, the four-on-the-floor pump, SP-1200 grit, a glided Da-Funk banjo lead, into the centerpiece delay and tape. The LCD "lock one loop, add layers across minutes" build + the Daft Punk "vary the timbre, not the notes" filter sweep, with the cued **Dance Yrself Clean** explosion as a Part switch.

This is a **designed integration** — no artist ever used this exact chain. Real method = CS-60/SH-101/808/909 & Juno-106/MKS-80/TB-303/SP-1200 in Pro Tools/Logic — none of this rig. ⚠️ pump = emulation; vocoder/talkbox = not achievable. 🟣 designed.

## Signal path


*Sequence/clock plane* — **61SL MkIII** (clock master + filter-cutoff ride) → **Octatrack MkII** (the locked loop + crossfader filter sweep) + **MPC Sample** (909/808 backbone) + **Digitakt** (optional).

*Audio* — Octatrack/MPC stereo out → Apollo bus (the loop/drum body); **VG-800** banjo/baritone lead + acid bass → **CB Clean** → MXR 108 → **Hizumitas** (the overdriven-guitar read for the Da Funk lead) → Board 3 → **Big Time** (clock-locked tempo-synced delay, the centerpiece) → **PORTA424 → JHS 424** tape → Apollo print.

## Per-unit


- **61SL MkIII** — **#14 Filter-Cutoff Ride + Pump-CC Template** (enc1 → filter CUTOFF CC = the slow open/close build · fader1 → a pump-CC / a CC ramp that ducks on each beat · enc2 → RESONANCE · Fader Pickup ON · **SL = clock master, Tx On**). Drives the VG-800 SYNTH cutoff (CONTROL ASSIGN, CC#1–31 window) or the OT's FX cutoff CC. For the explosion, layer **#15 Dance-Yrself-Clean Cued-Explosion Session** (Part 1 sparse vamp held ~3 min → cued Part 2 slam on the downbeat).
- **Octatrack MkII** — **#28 Filter-House Crossfader Open/Close** (disco/funk loop or a resampled banjo/VG figure on a Flex track, LOOP ON · FX1 = multimode resonant filter, FX2 = delay · **Scene A = filter CLOSED, Scene B = filter OPEN** — throwing the crossfader A→B *is* the build · slow LFO → cutoff under it · **Lo-Fi bit reduction for SP-1200 grit**) + **#30 One-Loop Additive Long Build** (lock ONE loop, never change it; add tracks across minutes; stage the explosion as a cued Part switch). Pump via **#29 4-on-the-Floor Sidechain-Pump Loop** (input compressor or LFO-ramp → AMP volume, WAVE=RAMP, synced 1/4, retrigged on the kick step). ⚠️ no true sidechain key — the pump is faked.
- **MPC Sample** — **#29 4-on-the-Floor 909/808 Kit + Cowbell** (tuned to the song key so it locks to the baritone sub · Swing 54–58% for the dirty-909 shuffle · Transient FX on the kick) and/or **#30 Resample-the-Synth-for-Drums** (synthesize the kit from a VG-800/OP-1 voice and resample it in = the "Get Innocuous!" DFA method, AC50-mapped). ⚠️ Resample is silent the first try — do it twice. Run **MPC as clock master OR slave carefully** — fw1.2.1 MIDI-slave distorts; on fw1.3.x verify, else let the MPC follow.
- **VG-800** — **#34 Da Funk Band-Passed Portamento Lead** for the banjo lead (SYNTH/SOLO, portamento ON = the slide in 4ths, FILTER CUTOFF mid + TOUCH SENS up = the band-passed wah) + **#35 Around-the-World Acid Filter-Bass** in BASS mode for the bouncing baritone bass (FILTER CUTOFF ~50 low, RESO ~60 high, FILTER DECAY ~25 snappy pluck). Ride the bass cutoff open over the build (or let the 61SL/OT do it).
- **CB Clean** — **#13 Pseudo-Sidechain Bus Limiter** if you want the whole VG/loop bus to pump with the kick (Dry down, Dynamics into limiting, fast/fast, cut lows so bass doesn't over-trigger — Ricky Tinez's documented house move) — best when Clean is redeployed to a stereo end slot; or keep #1 *Home Base* at the front for the lead.
- **MXR 108 + Hizumitas** — **108 #5 Stacked Fuzz Booster** (low fuzz, high output) → **Hizumitas #5 Balanced Mid-Forward Lead** so the Da Funk banjo lead reads like an overdriven guitar (the MS-20 / Juno-into-Fat-Cat colour). Only on the lead — not the loop.
- **Big Time** — **#2 Lo-Fi Rhythmic Groove (clock-locked)** (MODE Short · STATE Compressed · 0.5X ON for SP-1200-ish crush · TIME = MIDI clock via CC54 dotted-8th/16th · CLUSTER multi-tap = the groove · FEEDBACK ~35% articulate · SPREAD ping-pong). The tempo-synced stereo delay (1/8 L, dotted-1/8 R) the filter-house sources call for. ⚠️ MPC distorts when slaved on fw1.2.1 — run MPC master or Big Time master, not both.
- **PORTA424 #1 + JHS 424 #1** — tape glue on the bus for the SP-1200-at-45rpm grit lineage.

## Routing / sync


**61SL = clock master (Tx On)**, 24 PPQN to the OT, MPC, Digitakt and (via CC54) Big Time — one tempo for the four-on-the-floor; everything follows. **Never Tx AND Rx clock at once; feed clock on USB or DIN, not both.** The OT crossfader is the live filter-house controller (Scene A↔B), the 61SL enc1 the alternate cutoff ride. The pump is the **emulation** (LFO-ramp on track volume / OT input comp — no DAW-style sidechain key). The build is **arrangement** (add layers / cued Part switch) for LCD, **filter sweep** for Daft Punk — do both. Saturate the drop arp (Hizumitas) for the Dance-Yrself-Clean explosion. ⚠️ **No vocoder/talkbox on the rig** — the robot-voice option (VG-800 #36, filter-modulated carrier) only fakes the *result*.

## Sound


A locked disco/banjo loop that opens from a filtered murmur to a full-spectrum four-on-the-floor groove over minutes, pumping on the kick, an acid baritone bass bouncing under it, a glided overdriven banjo lead on top, tempo-synced ping-pong delay, SP-1200 grit, printed to tape — then a cued explosion slams the full kit + a saturated saw arp in on the downbeat.

## Play


61SL starts the room. Lock the OT loop and *never touch the notes* — only the filter. Throw the crossfader (or ride enc1) to open the cutoff over the build; bring MPC layers in one at a time. At the boundary, fire the **cued Part switch (OT-E3 / 61SL-E2)** to slam the explosion in on the downbeat. Carry the Da Funk banjo lead on the VG-800 (melody in 4ths, portamento). Ride Big Time WET for dub throws.

## Taste-ref


Daft Punk — "Around the World" / "Da Funk" filter-house, acid-pluck bass, glided band-passed lead; LCD Soundsystem — "All My Friends" one-loop additive build, "Dance Yrself Clean" withhold-then-explosion; the DFA resample-the-synth-for-drums method.

Frozen Grain Wall
Instrument: baritone
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, Chase Bliss MOOD MkII, Hologram Chroma Console, Eventide H90, Strymon Big Sky

One frozen grain held into an infinite drone you build a whole intro/outro on — the sustained-wall workhorse, all from one pedal's two channels, then widened. This is a 🟣 DOUG-designed integration; no artist used this exact pedal chain, the Taste-ref names the sound it chases.

## Signal path


Baritone / banjo → **CB Clean** → [Boards 1–2 light] → [Board 3] → **MOOD MkII** (Stretch grain + Reverb freeze) → **Chroma Console** (re-expand + light tape) → **H90 / Big Sky** (hall, low Mix) → tape.

## Per-unit


- **VG-800 — #29 ORGAN → Blooper Capture Drone** (steady waveform, no rotary) — a dead-steady drone is the best stretch/grain source.
- **CB Clean — #6 Baritone Drone Sustainer** (limiting ceiling + slow release = a sustained bed).
- **MOOD MkII — #18 Stretching 101 + Frozen Grain Wall** (Stretch: both MODIFY+LENGTH max, rotate MODIFY toward **noon to FREEZE** a single grain; LENGTH sizes the held grain) layered with **#12 Freeze Pad** on the Wet Reverb channel. Save it to **Slot L "Frozen Grain Wall"** with **#29 CLASSIC** dip on for grit. This is the **Perry Frank Reverb+Stretch "sprawling epic"** (#32).
- **Chroma Console — #13 Ambient Diffusion Bed** (the re-expander) + a light **#2 Subtle Tape Glue** (keep CASSETTE light — don't double the tape if Gen Loss is running).
- **H90 — #6 Blackhole Freeze Drone** at low Mix, or **Big Sky #3 "For Days"** (max-decay Cloud) as the failover — one diffuser only.

## Routing


MOOD's **SPREAD width collapses into the mono Blooper/Chroma path** — keep wide intent for after the Chroma re-expansion. Use **MOOD LATCH** dip so the Freeze holds hands-free. Re-check MOOD **LEVEL BALANCE (#26)** between the two channels (they're not auto-balanced).

## Sound


A grainy, smeared, infinitely-held wall — granular fuzz at the edges, a steady organ drone at the core — that you play a live melody over.

## Play


Hold a chord → tap MOOD's Micro-Looper to capture → **HOLD LEFT FS** to freeze the reverb into a pad → rotate MODIFY to noon to lock a single stretched grain → play over the held wall. Slowly turn **CLOCK down (#2)** for a degrading, detuning drift as it sustains.

**Taste-ref:** post-punk-texture-dynamics — sustained-crescendo drone walls (Swans-adjacent); the MOOD sheet's "sprawling epic" / sustained-wall workhorse.

Frozen Granular Pad, Banjo Lead On Top
Artists: Yvette Young, Bon Iver, Sufjan Stevens
Instrument: banjo
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, Walrus Audio QI Etherealizer, OBNE Dark Star V3, Chase Bliss Big Time, Hologram Chroma Console, Eventide H90, MXNHLT PORTA424

The Yvette-Young workflow translated to banjo-as-lead — capture a chord into a frozen granular pad on Board 2, then play a banjo lead over the self-sustaining bed. The cleanest "lead over a held wall" chain. ⭐ signature-fit.

This is a 🟣 designed integration of owned-gear patches; no artist ever played *this* chain. The Taste-ref names the sound it chases, and the per-unit patch sheets carry their own provenance.

## Signal path


EBM-5 banjo (GK-5) → **VG-800 (#6 CRYSTAL Shimmer Pad** for the bed *or* **#4 SOLO Lead** for the live lead — see Play) → Clean (#12 Dynamic Volume Swell) → [Board 1 → Board 2] → **QI Etherealizer (#4 Frozen Banjo/Baritone Pad → Dark Star)** → **Dark Star V3 (#24 Frozen banjo bed)** → [Board 3] → **Big Time (#4 Oceanic Drone Bed, WET low)** → Chroma → **H90 (#28 PrismShift/Polyphony Freeze Pad)** → PORTA424 → tape.

## Per-unit


- VG-800 **#6 CRYSTAL Shimmer Pad** — `SUSTAIN 90–100` glassy bell drone as the bed source; `NORMAL MIX OFF` (let the model own it). Switch to **#4 SOLO Lead** (or just dry banjo through a less-saturated model) for the line you play *over* the freeze.
- Clean **#12 Dynamic Volume Swell** — AUX swell (LATCH for toggle); Wet = Swell In ~noon, Dry = Swell Out ~noon. The banjo pluck *bows in* like a bowed note, feeding the granular pad pre-swelled material.
- QI **#4 Frozen Banjo/Baritone Pad** — Grain Cloud, short-press **Freeze** to loop the grain buffer; **Space modest (10–11:00)** so the Dark Star owns the space; **Tone LPF** to tame the banjo 2–4 kHz spike. ⚠️ RIG-CRITICAL: pad/reamp the VG-800 line level before the Qi (no level switch — it clips hot; use the bench EHX Effects Interface).
- Dark Star V3 **#24 Frozen banjo bed** — Mix mostly wet, **Aux = Hold**, short Lag so the fast banjo transient speaks before the wash blooms; LPF side if octave content ice-picks. Stereo, trails on (Board-2 terminus, #28 global config).
- Big Time **#4 Oceanic Drone Bed** — MODE Long, low COLOR / high FEEDBACK climb, **WET set low** (the manual warns twice about runaway); this thickens the held bed, doesn't front it.
- H90 **#28 PrismShift/Polyphony Freeze Pad** — freeze the bed; the **PrismShift Mid voice stays live/playable** so the lead still rings through the frozen pitched pad.

## Routing


Mono banjo (Board 1) → stereo from CE-2W onward into Board 2; QI runs **Parallel** by default. ⚠️ **Dark Star Aux=Hold passes new notes BONE-DRY** — that is *good* here: the dry banjo lead sits in front of the frozen wash. Lean on the dry path + the H90/Chroma for the lead's own ambience. No clock needed (this is a held/ambient chain) — but the 61SL #4 (Whole-CB-Board Scene Recall) can recall the whole Board-3 state for the song part in one PC.

## Sound


A static, glassy, granular cathedral bed that never decays, with a clear bowed-in banjo melody floating on top — the lead present and dry-forward, the wall infinite behind it.

Taste-ref: indie-folk-confessional (the freeze-pad-and-jam, halo-around-one-voice intimacy) + post-punk-texture-dynamics (the sustained wall). Approximation: the QI grain cloud is a *fixed* pitched cloud, not a played MIDI harmony — it chases the result, not the Prismizer method.

## Play


Strum/roll one banjo chord → Clean swells it in → short-press QI **Freeze** to capture the grain pad → engage Dark Star **Aux Hold** to lock the wash → switch the VG-800 to the lead voice and solo over the frozen bed. To release, tap Freeze/Hold off; trails keep the wash ringing.

Half-Broken DS-2 Gated Stab Beat
Artists: Car Seat Headrest
Instrument: banjo/baritone/VG-800
Gear: Chase Bliss Clean, JHS Colour Box V2, JHS 424, MXNHLT PORTA424

The deliberately spitty, gated, "keeps-breaking" demo-stab texture — used as a rhythmic element where the choke IS the groove, locked to a glitch beat. A 🟣 DOUG-designed integration. This is the chain that deliberately crosses the JHS 424 Gain-2 ~3:00 gate (the one documented threshold).

## Signal path


banjo/baritone/VG-800 → CB Clean → JHS Colour Box V2 → JHS 424 (gated) → PORTA424 → tape. (Octatrack/MPC glitch beat clocks it.)

## Per-unit


- **CB Clean** — **#3 Tight & Lively** (fast attack/release) so the stabs stay tight before the gate.
- **JHS Colour Box V2** — **#4 Honk / Telephone (mid-stacked radio voice)** (all three SHIFTs to midrange, boosted) for the brittle telephone stab, OR **#2 Console Crunch** to pre-shape.
- **JHS 424** — **#14 Half-Broken DS-2 Gated Crunch (424-LF2)** — Gain 1 1:00, **Gain 2 4:00 (PAST the 3:00 gate)**, Bass 10. Pick attack and note-offs do the gating = the half-failing dirt box. **NOT for sustained drones** — that brittleness is the whole point here.
- **PORTA424** — **#1 Always-On Cassette Print** (light, 18V) — because the 424 is the stage destroying, keep the PORTA424 clean (the one-stage-destroys rule).

## Routing / sync


**This is the chain that deliberately crosses the JHS 424 Gain-2 ~3:00 gate** (the one documented threshold — cited on the 424 sheet). Because the 424 gates hard, **keep the PORTA424 clean** so only one stage destroys. Mono. Octatrack/MPC runs the glitch beat as clock master; the gated stabs are played or sequenced in time so the choke lands on the grid.

## Sound


Tight, aggressive, spitting gated crunch — single notes and chord stabs crack lo-fi then choke off, brittle and percussive, sitting like a broken-drum-machine element inside the beat.

## Play


Program or play stabs on the grid; the note-offs gate them. Pair under the Octatrack **#34 / OT-E3 Postal-Service-style un-pumped glitch beat** or the MPC **#31 Glitchy Beep-Beat** for the clattery, dry-forward bed. Use as a section element, not a whole song (it chokes sustain).

**Taste-ref:** lo-fi-prolific-volume — CSH Boss DS-2 "keeps breaking" spitty/gated dirt box; post-punk/art-rock brittle stabs. 🟣 designed.

Hizumitas Fuzz → Big Time — One-Note Oceanic Wall
Artists: Swans
Instrument: baritone guitar / banjo
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, EarthQuaker Devices Hizumitas, Chase Bliss Generation Loss, Chase Bliss Big Time, Chase Bliss MOOD MkII, Chase Bliss Blooper, Hologram Chroma Console, Eventide H90, MXNHLT PORTA424

The honest minimal centerpiece: hold ONE note on a sustaining fuzz and let Big Time's feedback + diffusion build an endless oceanic drone bed — the smallest possible signature chain. A single held note swells into a slowly-climbing, defined fuzz wall that never quite resolves; FREEZE turns it into an infinite pad you solo over.

🟣 DOUG-designed integration. No artist used this exact chain — the per-unit patch refs carry their own provenance, and the Taste-ref names the sound it chases.

## Signal path


Baritone JM / banjo (GK-5) → VG-800 → **Clean #7 Always-On Huge Fuzz Feeder** → EQD Hizumitas (mono) → **Generation Loss** → **Big Time IN-L (auto-MISO) #9 Hizumitas Fuzz Wall** → MOOD → Blooper → Chroma → **H90 #2 Blackhole Infinite Ambient Pad** → PORTA424 → tape.

The only "real artist signal-order" invoked is the general **fuzz-before-delay** standard — a documented pedal-order best-practice (EQD / JHS / Reverb signal-chain guides), not an artist-specific path.

## Per-unit


- **Clean #7 Always-On Huge Fuzz Feeder** — but back Dynamics DOWN out of limiting (toward 10:00) per the patch's own note, so the Hizumitas blooms with your attack instead of being slammed flat. Clean stays mono here (front of Board 1).
- **Big Time #9 Hizumitas Fuzz Wall** — MODE Long (not the patch's default Long/varies — use Long so FREEZE holds a non-degrading pad), STATE Compressed (holds the sustaining fuzz, stops runaway), VOICING Focus (shaves highs+lows → keeps the muff wall defined), COLOR LOW ~25–35% (the fuzz already saturates), TILT pushed UP (cut low mud), FEEDBACK ~60%, WET ~45%. SPREAD widen. The Hizumitas Filter knob pre-shapes scooped↔thick before the delay.
- **H90 #2 Blackhole Infinite Ambient Pad** — the downstream hall the wet feeds into for the doom wall.

## Routing


Mono fuzz → **IN-L auto-engages MISO** (mono-in / stereo-out) — the clean way to fan a mono fuzz into a stereo delay field. No clock needed (free-running drone). Favor **DRY KILL ON** (Big Time Options) if you want the wet-only bed to stay out of the dry print. Gain-staging: keep COLOR modest — too much COLOR + a hot fuzz makes the limiter clamp to porridge.

## Sound


A single held note swells into a slowly-climbing, defined fuzz wall that never quite resolves; FREEZE turns it into an infinite pad you solo over.

**Taste-ref:** post-punk/experimental (Swans crushing sustained crescendos); the drone/doom making-aesthetic at its most minimal.

## Play


Hold one note, let the wall build, then **hold Big Time's RIGHT footswitch to FREEZE** the bed (non-degrading infinite pad) and play melody/banjo over the held wall. To collapse, tap RIGHT to unfreeze or **hold MODE to panic-reset** to a clean delay.

Holy-Trinity Granular Pad
Artists: Bon Iver
Instrument: banjo
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, Hologram Microcosm, Walrus Audio QI Etherealizer, OBNE Dark Star V3, Eventide H90

The rig's headline lush ambient bed — a glacial granular wash that blooms into a wide stereo reverb-pad you solo a banjo lead over. The Board-2 texture stage at full song. This is a 🟣 DOUG-designed integration; no artist used this exact pedal chain, the Taste-ref names the sound it chases.

## Signal path


Banjo (GK-5) → **VG-800** (Organ/Crystal pad) → **CB Clean** (always-on) → [Board 1 stereo send] → **Microcosm** (Haze grain-wash) → **QI Etherealizer** (frozen grain cloud) → **Dark Star V3** (stacked-octave reverb terminus) → [stereo to Board 3] → **H90** light hall → tape.

## Per-unit


- **VG-800 — #6 CRYSTAL Shimmer Pad** (bell drone, `SUSTAIN 90–100`, `NORMAL MIX OFF`) or **#11 Organ Drone + Rotary** (`SUSTAIN 100`) — a steady continuous-waveform source is the best grain fodder. Onboard REV/DLY off; pad the line out before Board 2.
- **CB Clean — #6 Baritone Drone Sustainer** (or **#1 Home Base** for banjo) — set SENSITIVITY by the left LED first; just glue/level, EQ at noon (tone is the Colour Box's job).
- **Microcosm — #11 Haze Grain-Wash Map (variation B/D)** with **#27 Ambient Smear Wash** clock-face as the dial-in (Activity ~1:00, Shape ~1, Filter 11–12, Space ~3:00, Mix ~1:00). The grain event-generator; keep Filter back to tame the banjo top.
- **QI Etherealizer — #4 Frozen Banjo/Baritone Pad → Dark Star** (Flow **Parallel**, Grain Cloud, Space **10–11:00 only** so the Dark Star owns the space, Tone ~1:00 to roll the ice-pick). Hit a chord → **short-press Freeze** (#18 gesture) → grain cloud loops.
- **Dark Star V3 — #5 Pad Factory (opposed-octave split)** or **#4 Stacked-octave pad** (Pitch 1 −1 oct / Pitch 2 +1 oct, Decay high, Crush just below noon for light degrade, Spread full CW). Use the **#16 "a in Dark"** trick to seat unity. Board-2 terminus config **#28** (Stereo, trails on).
- **H90 — #4 Blackhole Low Orbit Resonance** at low Mix (a sub-heavy hall to seat the bloom), or bypass and let Dark Star be the whole space.

## Routing


Stereo from Board 1 onward. Run QI **Parallel** so the live banjo stays present on top of the frozen cloud. **Don't max two reverbs** — QI Space modest, Dark Star owns the wide space, H90 only a low-Mix seat. No clock needed (this is a free-running pad). Pad/reamp the VG-800 into the QI (no level switch — clips hot).

## Sound


A diffuse granular shimmer that widens into an orchestral octave-split reverb pad — huge, slow, glassy, with a defined banjo lead floating on top.

## Play


Strum/hold the VG pad → let the Microcosm grain-wash build → short-press QI **Freeze** to lock the grain cloud → solo a banjo lead over the held bed. Sweep QI **Tone** down by hand (#20) for movement (the QI has no EXP jack). To go bigger, **long-press QI Freeze** (#13) to ramp Space to 100% — but then pull Dark Star back so you don't double the verb.

**Taste-ref:** indie-folk-confessional — Bon Iver / U.F.O.F. spectral wash around a single voice; the cluster index's "orchestral wash around one voice" chain.

iPhone-Intimate Close Wash
Artists: Sufjan Stevens, Big Thief
Instrument: banjo
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, Hologram Microcosm, Walrus Audio QI Etherealizer, Hologram Chroma Console, MXNHLT PORTA424

The opposite of a wall — a faint, close, in-the-room wash sitting *behind* a present, dry fingerpicked banjo. Cassette warble and a halo, never a hall. The intimate-wash brief. This is a 🟣 DOUG-designed integration; no artist used this exact pedal chain, the Taste-ref names the sound it chases.

## Signal path


Banjo (GK-5) → **VG-800** (clean fingerpicked banjo) → **CB Clean** → [Board 1] → **Microcosm** (faint glacial Haze) → **QI Etherealizer** (faint wash, mostly dry) → [Board 3] → **Chroma Console** (CASSETTE intimate degrade) → tape (PORTA424).

## Per-unit


- **VG-800 — #32 Sufjan Fingerpicked Banjo Lead** (5th excluded = "4-string guitar," bright/clean, `NORMAL MIX` moderate so the real pluck/finger noise stays) or **#33 iPhone-Intimate Clean Acoustic Bed**.
- **CB Clean — #1 Home Base** / **#5 Banjo Transient Tamer** — gentle glue, keep the source present and dry-forward (this chain is *not* about squashing it into a wall).
- **Microcosm — #29 Glacial Halo Bed (Haze)** (Mix **~11:00**, sits BEHIND the dry voice — the halo-not-hall move; Filter 11–12 to tame the banjo top).
- **QI Etherealizer — #29 iPhone-Intimate Faint Wash** (Flow Parallel, **Mix/Dry HIGH** mostly dry, Grain Mix ~10:00 faint, Space 9:00 a halo not a hall, Tone ~11:00).
- **Chroma Console — #31 iPhone Voice-Memo Cassette Capture** (TEXTURE CASSETTE ~10–11:00, SWEETEN ~9–10 so the source still reads present, VIBRATO + DRIFT subtle warble, **MIX ~65–70%**). Pick **this OR Gen Loss** as "the tape" — don't double it.

## Routing


Stereo, but everything stays **mostly dry** — Mix knobs low across the board so the banjo stays close and present. Chroma Buffered+Trails, both outs. No freeze, no big space. This is the restraint chain.

## Sound


A close-mic'd banjo with a faint pitched haze and a hint of cassette wow/flutter behind it — like an intimate take captured on the wrong, slightly worn machine.

## Play


Fingerpick rolling banjo arpeggios; keep the dry forward and let the haze/cassette sit *under* it. Resist the urge to freeze — the point is intimacy, not a wall. If you want a touch of glue, add **Chroma #32 Live-Room Slapback** (EchoBoy-style, one-two repeats) instead of more wash.

**Taste-ref:** indie-folk-confessional — Sufjan *Carrie & Lowell* iPhone-Voice-Memos intimacy / Big Thief "Not" close-and-dry; the cluster index's "Sufjan banjo + intimate room" chain.

**Approximation flag:** the degrade is the intimate iPhone/cassette kind, NOT doom fuzz — a deliberate lens choice per the indie-folk cluster index; dry stays close.

Keys Rig
Artists: Peter Gabriel, Prince, The Police
Instrument: keys
Gear: Novation 61SL MkIII, Caroline Somersault, Boss CE-2W

61-key controller through two compact modulation pedals. Gabriel's synth pads get lo-fi wobble from the Somersault; Prince's keys get classic chorus from the CE-2W. Two pedals, minimal footprint, big texture.

## Signal Path


### 1. Novation 61SL MkIII
Semi-weighted 61-key controller. Drives soft synths (Arturia V Collection, Native Instruments Komplete) via USB, or hardware synths via 5-pin MIDI DIN. Audio comes from the synth source (plugin output from interface, or hardware synth audio out) — the Novation itself produces no audio.

### 2. Caroline Somersault
Lo-fi modulation with character. [Vibrato mode](guide:Caroline%20Somersault/vibrato-mode) adds pitch wobble to pads — instant VHS-era Gabriel/Tears for Fears texture. The chorus side is warm and imperfect, not pristine — it degrades the signal slightly, which keeps keys from sounding too "produced." Havoc footswitch for momentary pitch-dive chaos on transitions.

### 3. Boss CE-2W
[CE-2 mode](guide:Boss%20CE-2W/ce-2-mode) for classic 80s synth chorus — the same circuit that defined the era these artists come from. On electric piano patches (Rhodes, Wurli from V Collection), this is the sound. On pads, it widens the stereo image without overwhelming. CE-1 mode for deeper, more dramatic chorus on ambient parts.

## Routing


Audio path: synth/plugin output → Somersault → CE-2W → back to interface (or PA).

If running soft synths, route a stereo output from your interface (e.g., [RME Babyface Pro FS outputs 3-4](guide:RME%20Babyface%20Pro%20FS/output-routing)) through the two pedals and return on separate inputs. This keeps the pedal color on keys only, not your whole mix.

For hardware synths (OP-1 Field, etc.), run their audio out through the same two pedals before hitting the interface.

## The Vibe


- **Gabriel pads**: Somersault vibrato slow + CE-2W chorus — warped, wide, atmospheric
- **Prince keys**: Somersault off, CE-2W CE-2 mode — clean chorus on stabs and comps
- **Police keys**: Both on, subtle settings — shimmery movement under guitar

Let Down Cascading Wall
Artists: Radiohead
Instrument: banjo (GK-5 → VG-800)
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, Chase Bliss Generation Loss, Chase Bliss Big Time, Chase Bliss Blooper, Eventide H90, MXNHLT PORTA424, JHS 424, UA Apollo x8

The OK Computer marquee — Jonny's cascading arpeggio *doubled an octave up + a third Jazzmaster layer* into a Phil-Spector wall, the 5/4-against-4/4 Reich phasing, dying into the St Catherine's ballroom reverb. One banjo/guitar arpeggio line becomes a shimmering, tape-warped, octave-stacked multi-tap cascade in a long hall. The one chain that **resists the degrade tie-breaker** — the jangle is the hook, so it stays bright.

This is a **designed integration** — no artist ever used this exact chain. Radiohead's actual method = Telecaster + Jazzmaster layers tracked in the St Catherine's ballroom (no pedals of this rig). 🟣 designed — never an artist chain.

## Signal path


banjo (GK-5 → **VG-800** Ondes/clean lead voice) → **CB Clean** (light comp, always-on) → *[skip the fuzz wall]* → Board-2 thru → **Generation Loss** (light tape flutter) → **Big Time** (5-against-4 cascade, ping-pong) with **Blooper** running an octave-up overdub stack underneath → **H90** (St Catherine's ballroom hall) → **PORTA424 → JHS 424** tape print → Apollo.

## Per-unit


- **VG-800** — #3 *GR-300 Thick-Synth Lead* or a clean bright **E.GUITAR** model for the Telecaster-arpeggio attack; feed a single bright arpeggio line. (For the gliding "How to Disappear" colour instead, swap to **TB1 Ondes-Martenot lead voice**, portamento ON — but Let Down wants the bright Tele jangle, not the glide.)
- **CB Clean** — #2 *Transparent Enhancer* (the ~2:1 thicken-don't-squash base, slow Attack so the pick stays uncompressed). Keep it gentle — the jangle needs its attack.
- **Generation Loss** — #2 *Vintage But Not Broken* nudged toward #1 *Subtle Tape Age* (Wow ~10:00, Flutter just up, Saturate ~9:00, Failure off, Dry Small) = the Kid-A "breathes wrong" tape warp arrives *before* the cascade, gently, without dropouts. Keep hidden Hiss low + HUM BYP so it doesn't stack noise into the print.
- **Big Time** — **TB1 "Let Down" Cascading Jangle-Delay** (MODE Short · STATE Compressed · VOICING HiFi · 0.5X OFF · COLOR ~30–35% · **TIME = 5-against-4 tap** vs the 4/4 · CLUSTER ~45–55% · TILT above noon · FEEDBACK ~40% · WET ~40% · **SPREAD ping-pong**). The multi-tap + 5/4 tap is what builds the "two clocks that refuse to agree."
- **Blooper** — **TB2 "Let Down" Octave-Stack Arpeggio Builder** (Mode ADD · record the clean bright arp STABILITY off · MOD A **Pitcher ALT-A2 = +1 oct** · punch-in overdub → original + octave-up · optional 3rd pass at a 5th/octave for the "Ed Jazzmaster" layer · REPEATS max). This is the *real* doubled-octave layer; Big Time TB1's taps cascade over the stack.
- **H90** — #3 *Blackhole Dark Matter Reverse Bloom* is wrong here; use the cluster's **H90-TB3** role via patch #1 *Cavernous Blackhole Drone* pulled back, OR #2 *Blackhole Infinite Ambient Pad* with **long pre-delay ~80–120 ms, decay ~4–6 s, Mix ~25–30%** = the "supernatural natural reverb" of the 3am ballroom, sitting *under* the cascade.
- **PORTA424** — #1 *Always-On Cassette Print* (Input Trim 9:00, 18V for firm lows under the hall, mono-sum the H90 bus). **JHS 424** — #1 *Subtle Always-On Tape Print* (Gain 1 9:00 / Gain 2 10:00, Treble 1:00 de-haze, XLR → Apollo). Tape glue, not grit — keep the jangle intact.

## Routing / sync


Banjo arrives mono into Board 1; **Big Time IN-L auto-engages MISO** (mono-in / stereo-out) so the ping-pong spreads. Clock-lock Big Time to the **Digitakt/MPC MIDI clock via CC54** (set the 5-against-4 as the subdivision relationship by tapping it, or run the dotted-8th and let the arp imply the 5). Blooper is **mono in/out** — its octave stack sums into Big Time, and the **Chroma Console re-expands to stereo** before H90 if you route through it (here we go Big Time → Blooper → H90 directly, stereo from Big Time's MISO). NO dry kill — the dry jangle must stay present. Bright/HiFi voicing throughout; Gen Loss stays subtle so the cascade isn't muddied.

## Sound


A bright, chiming, octave-stacked arpeggio wall that phases against itself (5 vs 4), warped just enough by tape to "breathe wrong," ringing into a long ballroom hall and printed to cassette. Spector-wide, supernatural, recorded-in-1997.

## Play


Fingerpick ONE steady bright arpeggio. Punch-in the Blooper octave-up overdub (hold LEFT one-shot) before the section so the stack is printed and rings under your live line. Let Big Time's ping-pong taps do the doubling/tripling illusion. For the build, raise Blooper REPEATS to max so all layers ring; for the outro, ride the H90 mix up. Optional: feed OP-1 **OP1-TB2 ZX-Spectrum bleeps** into Blooper's Scrambler for the dying-modem outro.

## Taste-ref


Radiohead — "Let Down" (OK Computer, 1997): doubled/tripled cascading arpeggios, 5/4-vs-4/4 Steve Reich phasing, St Catherine's ballroom 3am reverb, EMT 140 plate.

Longsword Op-Amp Slab → H90 Catch
Artists: Black Country New Road
Instrument: baritone (Jazzmaster via GK-5 → VG-800)
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, EarthQuaker Devices Hizumitas, Longsword, Chase Bliss Big Time, Eventide H90

The late, sudden "kick the door in" distortion slab — a dynamics build that drops a Sabbath-class op-amp wall into a reverb that catches the wreckage. Tension/release, not set-and-forget. Designed integration; BC,NR's slab is an Op Amp Big Muff / Maxon, so the rig chases the scooped sustaining result, not the exact pedals.

## Signal path


Baritone JM (GK-5 → **VG-800 #8 FILTER BASS Doom Sub** or #7 −7 STEP) → CB Clean (Home Base, leveling) → **Hizumitas #14 (HZ-PP2) BC,NR Big-Muff Sabbath Slab** (off until the drop) → **Longsword #15 (LS-PP1) BC,NR Op-Amp Sabbath Slab** (Boost footswitch = the door-kick) → Big Time bypassed → **H90 #19 Glitch/Stutter Pre-Mangle → reverb** (Preset B catches it) → tape.

## Per-unit


- **Hizumitas HZ-PP2 (#14):** **Volume max · Sustain max · Tone ~2:00** (the scooped slab voice), parked OFF until the second-half climax.
- **Longsword LS-PP1 (#15):** **DIODE down (silicon squared brick) · Drive ~2–3:00 · Level ~2:00 (rebalance — silicon is loud) · Low ~1:00 · High ~10:00 · SHIFT down (300 Hz Sabbath body) · Boost footswitch ON as the climax stomp** (it is the rig's *most accurate* op-amp-distortion unit).
- **H90 #19:** Glitch/Stutter into a reverb Preset B = the "recorded-wrong" destruction catching the slab.

## Routing


Mono Board 1. The whole chain is a **dynamics arc**: verse = quiet (slab pedals off, just Clean + a dry VG bed), climax = both fuzz/distortion stomps kick in. Watch Longsword output (silicon is the loudest stage — rebalance Level). Pull Low toward noon if the bottom flubs.

## Sound


Restrained → sudden overwhelming scooped slab, then the reverb shreds the tail into glitch. Taste-ref: Black Country, New Road — "Basketball Shoes" / "Sunglasses" late distortion slab.

## Play


Hold the build with only Clean + a VG bed; at the drop, stomp Hizumitas HZ-PP2 then Longsword Boost together for the door-kick; release to collapse. A late, partial, sudden drop — half the rig amps up, not one blow-out.

MPC-Master Groove → Big Time Rhythmic Delay
Artists: Daft Punk, LCD Soundsystem
Instrument: drums/sampler
Gear: Akai MPC Sample, Elektron Digitakt 2, Elektron Octatrack MkII, Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, Chase Bliss Big Time

A groove-led song where the **MPC is clock master** (the fw-safe arrangement), its four-on-the-floor kit drives the tempo, and Big Time's multi-taps lock to the groove as the rhythmic centerpiece delay — with the kick ducking the delay bus for the house "breathe." A pumping four-on-the-floor groove where the delay taps lock dotted-8th against the kick; the acid bass's filter opens over the build.

🟣 DOUG-designed integration. No artist used this exact chain — the per-unit patch refs carry their own provenance, and the Taste-ref names the sound it chases.

## Signal path


**MPC Sample** (clock MASTER) → MIDI → Big Time (follows) + DT2/Octatrack; MPC audio + VG-800 acid bass → Board 1 → Clean → **Big Time #2 Lo-Fi Rhythmic Groove** → CB stack → tape. (MPC drum bus optionally → **Clean #13 Pseudo-Sidechain Bus Limiter** for the pump.)

## Per-unit


- **MPC #29 4-on-the-Floor 909/808 Kit + Cowbell** — tuned to song key (kick=root), Swing 54–58%, Transient FX on the kick. The tempo engine.
- **MPC #31 Glitchy Beep-Beat** (optional B-section) — the un-pumped Postal Service counterpoint when you want the groove to drop out.
- **Big Time #2 Lo-Fi Rhythmic Groove (clock-locked)** — MODE Short, STATE Compressed, MOTION Off, 0.5X ON, CLUSTER ~⅓–½ (the multi-tap groove), FEEDBACK ~35% (articulate not washy), WET ~40%, subdivision via **CC54** (dotted-8th/16th). p-lock COLOR/TIME via CC14–19 from a sequencer for grid-quantized moves.
- **VG-800 #VG-E2 Around-the-World Acid Filter-Bass** — baritone as the bouncing acid bass under the kit.

## Routing


**MPC = clock master** (its MIDI-slave distortion bug means it should NOT be slaved). Big Time CC111=0 follows the MPC; CC54 sets the subdivision against the kit. **The pump is faked, not true sidechain** — either route the MPC drum bus through **Clean #13** (hot kick ducks the bus) for a hardware pump, or fake the duck on the loop with the Elektron **LFO-ramp** (DT2-E2 / OT-E2). Big Time itself is *not* in the sidechain — it just locks its taps to the grid.

## Sound


A pumping four-on-the-floor groove where the delay taps lock dotted-8th against the kick; the acid bass's filter opens over the build.

**Taste-ref:** electronic / groove-first (Daft Punk filter-house + LCD four-on-the-floor pump). ⚠️ **Approximation:** the rig has no true DAW sidechain key — the pump is an LFO-ramp / bus-limiter fake (flagged in DT2-E2/OT-E2 and Clean #13). The delay locking to the groove is real (CC54).

## Play


Start the MPC; ride Big Time **WET/CLUSTER** to swell the delay in for the chorus; switch to MPC #31 (drop the pump) for a breakdown, then slam the kit back in.

content:
Octatrack Capture-and-Destroy Break
Instrument: drums/sampler (MPC or Digitakt into Octatrack)
Gear: Akai MPC Sample, Elektron Octatrack MkII, JHS Colour Box V2, Chase Bliss Generation Loss, MXNHLT PORTA424, JHS 424, UA Apollo x8

Sample the live drum/loop bus into the Octatrack, slice it, re-sequence it into a break the source never played, then crossfade clean-loop ↔ filter-swept-crushed-and-frozen — a performable recorded-wrong groove with one hand on the fader. A 🟣 DOUG-designed integration.

## Signal path


MPC Sample (or Digitakt) → Octatrack MkII inputs A/B → OT main out → JHS Colour Box V2 (line/XLR) → CB Generation Loss → PORTA424 → JHS 424 → tape.

## Per-unit


- **Octatrack MkII** — **#24 Fast Resampling Capture-and-Destroy** to grab the bus into a buffer at **LEVEL 127** (the anti-generation-loss rule), then **#11 Cuckoo Slice-Kit-from-a-Recording** to slice + keyboard-play it, **#12 LFO → STRT Slice-Walk** (RMP / SPD 33 / ×2 / DEPTH 16 / SYNC TRIG → dest STRT) to auto-march the 8 slices. Perform with **#15 Scene-Crossfade Performance** (Scene A = dry loop / Scene B = filter swept + Lo-Fi crushed + freeze-delay feedback high) and **#18 Beat-Repeat / Stutter Freeze** (master Delay LOCK=1, FB=127) for glitch-collapse stabs.
- **JHS Colour Box V2** — **#10 Drum-Bus / Stereo-Loop Crush** on the OT main out (PAD ON; HI for crush). For obvious console-fuzz stabs, **#3 Broken Console Preamp Fuzz** as a moment.
- **CB Generation Loss** — **#11 Demo-Crunch Cassette** (Model 7/10, DROP BYP on for a *consistent* warble) or **#31 Drunk-Drivers Dropout Demo (GL-LF3)** (Failure ramp + Bounce) when you want the dropout left audible as the hook.
- **PORTA424** — **#4 Mid-Voltage Edge-of-Breakup Workhorse** (Trim 12–1:00) — obvious-but-controlled cassette grit on the break.
- **JHS 424** — **#1 Subtle Always-On Tape Print** — finish + mono-commit (keep it light; PORTA424 carries the grit).

## Routing / sync


**OT must be clock MASTER to live-loop / live-resample reliably** (Pickup overdub misbehaves when OT is a MIDI clock slave). MIXER **DIR AB = 0** when running the bus through a Thru/Flex so you don't comb-filter dry-against-processed; capture via **CUE or scene-lock master Comp MIX=0** to avoid re-compression on resample. The OT main out is stereo → mono-sum into the Colour Box. The crossfader **Scene 1 empty = clean fader home** (PRESET MKII convention) so far-left = the untouched loop.

## Sound


A sliced, re-pitched, conditionally-mutating break that you can throw from clean to a filter-swept, bit-crushed, beat-frozen smear in one fader move, then degrade and print to cassette. Generative on its own — never loops identically.

## Play


Capture 4 bars, slice 16/auto, let the STRT-LFO walk the slices; ride the crossfader A↔B for the build, punch **[P/T8]** for stutter-freeze fills, fire a Gen Loss **#8 Momentary FAIL Punch-In** as chaos punctuation that the downstream Big Time/tape catches.

**Taste-ref:** lo-fi-prolific-volume break-flip craft + electronic-groove-first slice-mangle; the recorded-wrong groove as a live instrument. 🟣 designed.

Ondes-Martenot Bowed Banjo Lead
Artists: Radiohead, Jonny Greenwood
Instrument: banjo
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, Chase Bliss Big Time, Chase Bliss MOOD MkII, Hologram Chroma Console, Eventide H90, MXNHLT PORTA424

Turn the banjo into a gliding, swelling, *singing* monophonic lead — no pick attack, long ducking trails — the Ondes-Martenot lead feel on the banjo voice. A lead that floats, not strikes. ⭐ signature-fit.

This is a 🟣 designed integration of owned-gear patches; no artist ever played *this* chain. The Taste-ref names the sound it chases, and the per-unit patch sheets carry their own provenance.

## Signal path


EBM-5 banjo (GK-5) → **VG-800 (#5 VIO Bowed Swell Drone** with portamento, *or* **VG-TB1 Ondes-Martenot lead voice** from the art-rock index) → **Clean (TB1 Ondes-Martenot Bowed-Swell)** → [Board 2 thru / light] → [Board 3] → **Big Time (TB3 Ondes-Martenot Lead Delay)** → MOOD (#12 Freeze Pad, light) → Chroma → **H90 (#9 Shimmer Drone — exp-pedal → Pitch Decay → Freeze)** → PORTA424 → tape.

## Per-unit


- VG-800 **#5 VIO Bowed Swell Drone** — VIO GUITAR with `LEAD EMPHASIS` up + `SLOW GEAR`/`SOUND HOLD` to remove the pick attack; `NORMAL MIX OFF`. Add **portamento/glide** (the VG-TB1 ribbon-glide) for the seamless pitch slide. Recall GK **#1 EBM5 BANJO**.
- Clean **TB1 Ondes-Martenot Bowed-Swell** — AUX Dynamic Swell; Hidden: Wet = Swell In ~noon–1:00 (slowish bowed attack), Dry = Swell Out ~noon. Sensitivity set so only intended notes bow in. The hard banjo pluck *bows in* like the Ondes' intensity key.
- Big Time **TB3 Ondes-Martenot Lead Delay** — MODE Long, STATE Compressed (sagging trails that duck under the attack then bloom), VOICING Focus (vocal-like), CLUSTER low (~15% — the *line* is the melody), MOTION Sine slow+shallow, FEEDBACK ~50% long singing trails.
- MOOD **#12 Freeze Pad** (light) — optional held ambient pad under the lead; LATCH so it holds hands-free, TRAILS on so toggling doesn't kill the wash.
- H90 **#9 Shimmer Drone (staff move)** — expression pedal → Pitch Decay, sweep up to bring shimmer tails in, push past 100 to Freeze before the pitch-loop clash; the reliable shimmer-drone-behind-a-lead.

## Routing


Mono banjo → VG-800 (glide + slow-gear swell) → Clean (the swell engine). This chain is **dynamics-and-glide first** — the swell comes from Clean, the glide from the VG-800 portamento, the long singing tail from Big Time. Keep CLUSTER low on Big Time so the single line stays a melody, not a wash. Map an expression pedal to H90 Pitch Decay (or to Big Time COLOR/FEEDBACK) for a hand-ridden swell/recede. No clock required; this is a free-time lead.

## Sound


A bowed-in, gliding banjo line with no audible pick attack, trailing long compressed echoes that duck around each note and bloom after — voice-like, "nothing closer to singing."

Taste-ref: art-rock-studio-as-instrument — Jonny Greenwood's Ondes-Martenot leads ("How to Disappear Completely," "The National Anthem," Kid A): intensity-key swell + ribbon glide. The rig *approximates* the Ondes: swell from Clean, glide from VG-800 portamento, the instrument is the banjo — not a real Ondes.

## Play


Pick a note and let Clean bow it in (no audible attack); slide between notes for the VG-800 portamento glide; ride the expression pedal to swell the H90 shimmer tails in behind the line. Hold MOOD Freeze (LATCH) for a held pad under a sustained passage.

One-Stomp Build → Drop — OVERLOAD Climax Over a Swelled Banjo Lead
Artists: Swans, Radiohead
Instrument: banjo
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, Chase Bliss Big Time, Chase Bliss MOOD MkII, Hologram Chroma Console, Eventide H90

A whole dynamic arc on the centerpiece alone: a banjo lead swells in clean, the part builds, then **one footswitch detonates the climax into a wall** and release collapses it — the Swans/post-punk near-silence-to-overwhelming move with no extra pedals. A bowed-banjo lead over clean trails that, on the stomp, ramps COLOR+FEEDBACK toward max into a self-oscillating wall; release drops it back to the singing trails.

🟣 DOUG-designed integration. No artist used this exact chain — the per-unit patch refs carry their own provenance, and the Taste-ref names the sound it chases.

## Signal path


Banjo (GK-5) → VG-800 (#VG-E1 portamento lead, optional) → **Clean #12 Dynamic Volume Swell** (+ **Clean TB1 Ondes-Martenot Bowed-Swell**) → drive → **Big Time #10 One-Stomp Climax (OVERLOAD ramp)** → MOOD → Chroma → **H90 #6 Blackhole Freeze Drone** → tape.

## Per-unit


- **Clean #12 Dynamic Volume Swell** (or **TB1 Ondes-Martenot Bowed-Swell**) — the banjo pluck auto-swells in (violined attack, no volume pedal), so the lead enters like a bowed Ondes voice feeding the delay pre-swelled material. AUX footswitch engages it.
- **Big Time #10 One-Stomp Climax (OVERLOAD ramp)** — MODE **Long** (OVERLOAD only works in Long), STATE Saturated, COLOR ~35% (headroom for the ramp), TILT pushed DOWN (boost lows → longer/louder tails feeding the climb), FEEDBACK ~55% base (the ramp takes it to max), WET set **conservatively** (the manual warns twice it's "scary loud"). SPREAD widen.
- **H90 #6 Blackhole Freeze Drone** — catch the climax tail and lock it as a held wall downstream.

## Routing


Mono banjo → IN-L (MISO). Can run free or clocked — if clocked, keep the SL/DT2 master so the swell timing sits on the grid. **Safety net:** the OVERLOAD wall is loud — set WET low before performing, and **hold MODE to panic-reset** Big Time to a clean delay if it runs away.

## Sound


A bowed-banjo lead over clean trails that, on the stomp, ramps COLOR+FEEDBACK toward max into a self-oscillating wall; release drops it back to the singing trails.

**Taste-ref:** post-punk / experimental (Swans' near-silence → overwhelming crescendo); art-rock Ondes-Martenot lead voice on the banjo (Radiohead Kid A leads, via Big Time TB3 / Clean TB1).

## Play


Swell the banjo lead in (Clean AUX), build the part, then **hold Big Time's RIGHT footswitch → OVERLOAD ramps into the wall**; release to collapse. For an infinite ending, throw the tail into H90 #6 Freeze instead of releasing. **Hold MODE = panic reset** out of the chaos.

One-Stomp Feedback Climax
Artists: Swans
Instrument: baritone (Jazzmaster / banjo via GK-5 → VG-800)
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, MXR M173 Classic 108 Fuzz, EarthQuaker Devices Hizumitas, Chase Bliss Generation Loss, Chase Bliss Big Time, Eventide H90

A performative feedback climb — one footswitch detonates a held chord into a climbing, self-oscillating wall, release to collapse. The build/drop as a single gesture. Designed integration chasing the post-punk/doom pulverising crescendo.

## Signal path


Baritone JM / banjo (GK-5 → VG-800 #7 −7 STEP) → CB Clean #7 (huge fuzz feeder) → 108 #9 → Hizumitas #3 Doom Wall → (End board) → CB Generation Loss (light) → **CB Big Time #10 One-Stomp Climax (OVERLOAD ramp)** → **H90 #15 Wormhole Hyperspace Wall** (Warp on a latching footswitch) → tape.

## Per-unit


- **Big Time #10:** MODE **Long** (OVERLOAD only works in Long), STATE Saturated, **COLOR ~35% (headroom for the ramp), FEEDBACK ~55% base, TILT EQ pushed DOWN** (boost lows → longer/louder tails feeding the climb), **WET set conservatively** (the ramp is "scary loud").
- **H90 #15 Wormhole:** Warp Factor 10, Stability DOWN (more pitch-wobble), Length UP, **Warp assigned to a LATCHING footswitch** so you hold it and ring out.

## Routing


Stereo from the End board. **Safety:** the Big Time manual warns about volume twice — set WET low before this; **hold-MODE = panic-reset** to a clean delay out of the chaos.

## Sound


A held chord that ramps into a climbing, pitch-warping, self-oscillating wall and falls back when released. Taste-ref: post-punk crescendo / doom feedback climb (Swans pulverising crescendo).

## Play


Hold the chord, then **hold Big Time's RIGHT footswitch** → OVERLOAD ramps COLOR+FEEDBACK toward max into a wall; simultaneously stomp the H90 Wormhole Warp latch for the rising hyperspace swell; release Big Time to collapse. Hold-MODE bails you out.

Onward Glitch → Big Time — Clocked Stutter-into-Delay
Artists: Radiohead
Instrument: banjo
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, MXR M173 Classic 108 Fuzz, Chase Bliss Onward, Chase Bliss Big Time, Chase Bliss MOOD MkII, Hologram Chroma Console, Eventide H90, Elektron Digitakt 2, Novation 61SL MkIII

A minimal two-box centerpiece where one glitch pedal supplies the *event* and Big Time supplies the *space* — angular stutters smeared into rhythmic multi-tap tails, all on one grid. Banjo plucks shatter into angular repeating fragments that the delay fans into a rhythmic, slightly-crushed cloud sitting over a frozen sub-octave pad.

🟣 DOUG-designed integration. No artist used this exact chain — the per-unit patch refs carry their own provenance, and the Taste-ref names the sound it chases.

## Signal path


Banjo (GK-5) → VG-800 → Clean (#1 Home Base) → MXR 108 (spitty fuzz, optional) → **CB Onward #17 Two-Personality Patch** (Board 2 placement / pre-Big-Time send) → **Big Time #1 Crushed Analog** (clocked) → MOOD → Chroma → H90 → tape.

## Per-unit


- **Onward #17 Two-Personality Patch** — a hands-free locked **FREEZE sub-drone** underneath + a live **PLAYBACK-error GLITCH** tracking your banjo on top. The glitch side is what Big Time multi-taps; the freeze side is the pad under it.
- **Big Time #1 Crushed Analog (Factory #7)** — but lock TIME to clock and lean on CLUSTER: MODE Short, STATE Compressed (keeps the stuttered taps articulate in a dense mix — borrow from #2 Lo-Fi Rhythmic Groove), CLUSTER ~⅓–½ (the multi-tap pattern echoing the glitches), 0.5X ON (12-bit crush), COLOR ~40%, FEEDBACK ~45%, WET ~40%, SPREAD ping-pong (the added taps fan L/R).

## Routing


**Clock them together** so glitch timing and delay subdivision lock to one grid — Onward syncs its GLITCH timing to MIDI clock; Big Time locks TIME via **CC54** subdivision (dotted-8th or 16th). Set Big Time SCALE Off/Chromatic so clock snaps delay to the quarter. Run the **DT2 (or 61SL) as clock master** driving both (DT2 #29 MIDI/Clock-Master template; 61SL #3 per-pedal CC template can also retrigger Onward's Glitch via **CC108** clock-quantized). Pick ONE master — never loop clock. Stereo from Onward into Big Time's stereo ins.

## Sound


Banjo plucks shatter into angular repeating fragments that the delay fans into a rhythmic, slightly-crushed cloud sitting over a frozen sub-octave pad.

**Taste-ref:** art-rock / studio-as-instrument (Radiohead "Ful Stop" glitch-rhythm; reverse/glitch delays as the hook).

## Play


Lock the Onward freeze sub-drone hands-free, then play banjo so the live glitch tracks it; **CC108 from the 61SL retriggers the Glitch in time** for punch-ins. Big Time's CLUSTER fader is the live "more/less taps" control.

content:
Prismizer Halo Bed
Artists: Bon Iver
Instrument: banjo
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, Walrus Audio QI Etherealizer, OBNE Dark Star V3, Eventide H90

The rig's approximation of the Bon Iver / Prismizer vocal halo — a pitched harmony cloud hovering around a single held banjo/voice, with a played diatonic voice underneath. A halo bed, flagged honestly as the result, not the method. This is a 🟣 DOUG-designed integration; no artist used this exact pedal chain.

## Signal path


Banjo (GK-5) → **VG-800** (one played diatonic harmony voice) → **CB Clean** (present) → [Board 1] → **QI Etherealizer** (Prismizer-halo grain-freeze cloud) → **Dark Star V3** (dual-pitch shimmer pad) → [Board 3] → **H90** light hall → tape.

## Per-unit


- **VG-800 — #31 Banjo Halo Harmony Drone** (`ALT TUNE MODE = HARMONY`, `+1 oct` or a USER-SCALE diatonic 3rd/5th in the song's key; `NORMAL MIX ~30%` keeps the dry banjo under the harmony) — the closest the rig gets to the Prismizer's *played* harmony (one fixed interval).
- **CB Clean — #5 Banjo Transient Tamer** — keep the source present and articulate (the "dry voice" in front of the cloud).
- **QI Etherealizer — #27 Prismizer Halo Freeze Cloud** (Flow Parallel, Grain Cloud, Playback **x2** +1 oct bright prism-up layer, Chorus Tri Rate 9 Depth 11 = the long-glide slur stand-in, Space 10–11:00). Play a chord → **short-press Freeze** = the grain cloud loops as a pitched cloud.
- **Dark Star V3 — #29 Halo Shimmer Pad (dual-pitch glide)** (Pitch 1 +1 oct L / Pitch 2 detune just off unity R via the "a in Dark" trick; Crush ~12 clean, Filter ~1 HPF glassy, Mix mostly wet but UNDER the dry voice) — two fixed pitched voices echoing the halo's pitched copies.
- **H90 — #8 Shimmer Subtle Octave Wash** (+1 AND −1 oct, low Mix) to seat the cloud, optional.

## Routing


Stereo, QI **Parallel** (live banjo present on top, like the dry vocal). Pad/reamp the VG-800 line into the QI. Space modest on the QI; Dark Star owns the width. For the "715 hit-it-harder" distortion, push the VG-800 / Board-1 source hot before the (padded) input.

## Sound


A held banjo note surrounded by a pitched-up harmony cloud and two chorused octave voices — a "choir of one banjo," with the dry played line and a fixed diatonic harmony underneath.

## Play


Play the harmony-voiced banjo chord → short-press QI **Freeze** to lock the pitched cloud → solo a banjo lead over it; the Dark Star adds the two fixed pitched copies. For the genuine article, run the in-the-box **Antares Harmony Engine (PRZ-TB1, index-only)** on the banjo instead — the pedals only approximate it live.

**Taste-ref:** indie-folk-confessional — Bon Iver "22 (OVER S∞∞N)" / "715 - CRΣΣKS" Prismizer/Messina vocal halo; the cluster index's "vocal halo on the rig (approximation)" chain.

**Approximation flag:** the real Prismizer is a MIDI-played, formant-shifted, polyphonic 4-note harmony cloud; the QI gives a fixed/drifting pitched cloud, the Dark Star two fixed voices, the VG-800 one played interval — all chase the RESULT, not the METHOD. No artist used this pedal chain.

QI Galaxy-Wash Crescendo + Dark Star Shimmer Wall
Artists: Swans
Instrument: baritone (Jazzmaster via GK-5 → VG-800)
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, EarthQuaker Devices Hizumitas, EHX Effects Interface, Walrus Audio QI Etherealizer, OBNE Dark Star V3, Chase Bliss Big Time

The "let the Qi take over" pole — capture a baritone drone, freeze it, ramp Space to 100%, oscillate the delay into a saturated snowball, and seat it in a Dark Star shimmer wall. The most texture-forward wall here; pure Middle-board granular crescendo into the End board. Designed integration; Swans build the crescendo over minutes on a loud stage — the freeze + oscillate manufactures the rise-and-overwhelm in the box.

## Signal path


Baritone JM (GK-5 → **VG-800 #6 CRYSTAL Shimmer Pad** or #29 ORGAN drone) → CB Clean #6 (sustain the bed) → Hizumitas #10 Synth-Filter Decay Sweep (a morphing source) → (Middle board) → **EHX Effects Interface** (pad/reamp the VG line — RIG-CRITICAL) → **Walrus QI #30 (QI-PP1) Swans Galaxy-Wash Crescendo** → **OBNE Dark Star V3 #25 Infinite Shimmer Drone** (Aux = Hold) → (End board) → Big Time bypassed → tape.

## Per-unit


- **QI QI-PP1 (#30):** Flow **Series**, Grain Mix ~2:00 **Phrase Sample**, **Playback x.5 (−1 oct, baritone weight)**, Delay Mix noon / Feedback ~2:00, Space ~2–3:00, full wet — the performance is short-press **Freeze** (grain loop) → long-press **Freeze** (Space → 100%) → **hold Tap/Osc** (saturated snowball crescendo); **Tone-by-hand** is the expression substitute (no EXP jack).
- **Dark Star #25:** **Mix 2–3 · Decay 4–5 (near infinite) · Multiply 1–2 · Filter 1 (HPF, glassy) · Pitch 1/2 +1 oct · Crush 12 (clean) · Lag 11**, **Aux = Hold**, Stereo/trails.

## Routing


Stereo from the QI onward (true stereo). **Two rig-critical cautions, both documented:** (1) the QI has **no level switch and clips hot** — pad/reamp the VG-800 line via the EHX Effects Interface BEFORE the QI (QI #30 / #23). (2) **Don't stack two maxed reverbs** — keep the QI's Space crescendo as the event and the Dark Star as the seating space, or run the Dark Star LPF-side if the octave-up shimmer ice-picks the banjo.

## Sound


A baritone drone that rises from a frozen grain loop into a galaxy-sized oscillating wash, seated in an infinite glassy shimmer wall. Taste-ref: Swans "Bring the Sun" / "The Seer" — rise-from-quiet pulverising crescendo (shimmer-wall lean).

## Play


Capture the drone → short-press QI Freeze (barely audible) → long-press Freeze to ramp the reverb → hold Tap/Osc to oscillate the delay into the crescendo; ride the QI Tone by hand. Freeze the Dark Star bed under it for the infinite shimmer tail.
