Reverse-Bloom Loop Bed
Artists: Radiohead
Instrument: banjo
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, Chase Bliss MOOD MkII, Chase Bliss Blooper, Hologram Chroma Console, Eventide H90

A backwards swelling bed — captured plucks/tails flipped so each note fades *in*, then diffused into a big hall. The granular/reverse-bed brief, built from a committed loop (not a swelling reverse-delay). This is a 🟣 DOUG-designed integration; no artist used this exact pedal chain, the Taste-ref names the sound it chases.

## Signal path


Banjo / VG pad → **CB Clean** → [Boards 1–2 light] → [Board 3] → **MOOD MkII** (real-time reverse, optional) → **Blooper** (reversed loop) → **Chroma Console** (mono→stereo re-expand) → **H90** (hall) → tape.

## Per-unit


- **VG-800 — #6 CRYSTAL Shimmer Pad** or **#5 VIO Bowed Swell** — ringing, decaying notes reverse best (the tail becomes the swell-in).
- **MOOD MkII — #10 Slip as Real-Time Reverse** (MODE Slip, MODIFY CCW of noon = reverse; TIME high = reversed *phrases* that follow you) for a live reversed entrance before you commit it.
- **Blooper — TB4 Reverse-Bloom Loop** (Stepped Speed B4, knob **CCW = reverse**; the decaying tail swells in) — or capture a forward loop in **#6 Clean drone loop** then overdub a reversed pass in ADD. Mono in/out — degrade and rebuild here.
- **Chroma Console — #13 Ambient Diffusion Bed** (DOUBLER + SPACE + LPF FILTER, Buffered+Trails, both outs connected) — its structural job is to **re-expand the mono Blooper loop to stereo** before the H90.
- **H90 — #1 Cavernous Blackhole Drone** at moderate Mix, or **#18 Cosmic Web Reverse-Grain Pad** (reverse-pitched grains into reverb) for a doubled reverse character. Print the tail to tape.

## Routing


Blooper is **mono in/out** (4th on Board 3) — let the **Chroma re-stereo it** (Buffered+Trails, both outs, re-calibrate when you swap banjo/baritone/VG-800). Optionally clock Blooper to the Digitakt (Blooper #27, CV CLOCK dip / MIDIbox) so the loop arms on the next pulse.

## Sound


Notes that arrive backwards — swelling in from nothing — looped into an evolving bed, then smeared wide and deep by the hall. Glassy, disorienting, oceanic.

## Play


Play a ringing phrase into MOOD Slip to hear it reverse live → capture the reversed pass to Blooper (left FS RECORD → ADD) → drop to playback and solo fresh banjo over the backwards bed. Feed the reversed blooms into the H90 hall so they diffuse.

**Taste-ref:** art-rock-studio-as-instrument — Radiohead "Daydreaming" reversed-glockenspiel / "Backdrifts" reversed guitar (the result; Blooper TB4 / MOOD TB1 chase it on this rig).

**Approximation flag:** the reverse here is a captured-then-reversed *sample* (the honest hardware match per Blooper TB4), not a swelling reverse-delay.

Ruined-Cassette Drop
Artists: Car Seat Headrest, Swans
Instrument: drums/sampler (groovebox bus + heavy source)
Gear: JHS Colour Box V2, Longsword, Chase Bliss Generation Loss, Chase Bliss Big Time, MXNHLT PORTA424, JHS 424

The blown-out climax of a degraded groove — the whole bus collapses into one ruined-cassette bounce as a moment, then collapses back. The most "recorded-wrong" stack in the file. A 🟣 DOUG-designed integration + **explicit approximation flag** (no vocal path).

## Signal path


groovebox bus + heavy source → JHS Colour Box V2 (or Longsword) → CB Generation Loss → CB Big Time → PORTA424 → JHS 424 → tape.

## Per-unit


- **JHS Colour Box V2** — **#16 Broken-Console Screamed Crush (CBX-LF2)** (HI · STEP 5 max · PRE-VOL maxed · EQ flat then TREBLE up) — the genuine broken-console fuzz; OR **Longsword #LSW-LF2 Glitchy 8-Bit Broken Slam** (Level/Drive/Boost MAX, silicon) for the squared/gated sputter.
- **CB Generation Loss** — **#9 Total Destruction (moment climax)** (Wow/Flutter 2:00+, Saturate + Failure maxed, VHS Model 1–3, Noise on) — a nauseating-on-purpose full meltdown, a *moment* not a tone.
- **CB Big Time** — **#10 One-Stomp Climax (OVERLOAD ramp)** (MODE Long, hold RIGHT footswitch → OVERLOAD ramps COLOR+FEEDBACK to a wall; WET set LOW first — "scary loud"; hold MODE = panic-reset out).
- **PORTA424** — **#14 Blown-Out Screamed-Mic Crush (P424-LF3)** (Trim MAXED, 9V) — the overloaded-cheap-mic crush terminus.
- **JHS 424** — **#4 Gated-Fuzz Monster** (Gain 2 4:00, PAST the gate) for total collapse, OR keep it light if PORTA424 is already maxed (don't double-destroy unless you want the full porridge for the single climax).

## Routing / sync


This is the one place the **don't-crank-both-boxes rule is deliberately broken** — for a single climax you *can* stack both PORTA424 maxed + 424 gated for total collapse (flagged: it goes to undifferentiated mush, so use it as one moment). Groovebox clock master; trigger the drop on a cued pattern boundary. **APPROXIMATION:** CBX-LF2 / P424-LF3 port the *screamed-into-a-cheap-mic vocal* character to a string/groovebox source — **this rig has no vocal path**, so it is a character analogy, not Toledo's actual vocal chain. Flagged.

## Sound


A speaker-ripping, gated, blown-out cassette meltdown that swells in on the OVERLOAD ramp and falls apart — the drop where the whole degraded groove eats itself, then snaps back to the verse.

## Play


Run the groove clean-ish into the verse; at the drop, foot the Colour Box (or Longsword) max-fuzz, hold the Big Time RIGHT footswitch for the OVERLOAD ramp, and let Gen Loss Total Destruction + the maxed tape stage detonate. Release / hold MODE to collapse back. Use once per song — the hiss + pitch-warp fatigue fast.

**Taste-ref:** lo-fi-prolific-volume — CSH screamed-into-laptop-mic overloaded-vocal *character* (ported to a string/groovebox source); post-punk/Swans brittle-density climax. 🟣 designed + **explicit approximation flag** (no vocal path).

Sampler Resample Loop — Big Time Texture → Samplers → Back Through Big Time
Artists: Car Seat Headrest, Radiohead
Instrument: drums/sampler
Gear: Chase Bliss Big Time, TE OP-1 Field, Elektron Digitakt 2, Akai MPC Sample, EHX Effects Interface, Eventide H90

The "recorded-wrong" generation-loss loop with Big Time at both ends: print a Big Time texture into a sampler, mangle it, then stream it back through Big Time so one delay is the song's glue — the OP-1-sketch → MPC-beat → Digitakt-sequence → all-through-Big-Time workflow. A frozen Big Time wall, sampled and crushed, played back as a chromatic/poly choir, then re-delayed by the same pedal — degradation stacked until it sounds captured on the wrong machine.

🟣 DOUG-designed integration. No artist used this exact chain — the per-unit patch refs carry their own provenance, and the Taste-ref names the sound it chases.

## Signal path


(capture) Big Time wet out → **OP-1 / DT2 / MPC sampler in**; (mangle in the box) → (return) sampler out → EHX Effects Interface (line→instrument, for the OP-1) → **Big Time** as a stereo aux/insert → CB stack → H90 → tape.

## Per-unit


- **Big Time #4 Oceanic Drone Bed (freeze-and-solo)** — build a wall, **hold RIGHT FS to FREEZE** a non-degrading infinite pad; *this frozen bed is the thing you sample.* MODE Long, STATE #!&%/Saturated, COLOR ~25–30%, FEEDBACK ~80%, DIFFUSE high. Keep WET conservative (it's loud).
- **OP-1 #21 Andreas Roman one-note polyphonic sampler** — sample the frozen Big Time bed as ONE note, then play it polyphonically across the keys (the "broken synth choir" engine). Re-print to Porta tape for stacked degrade. (~20 s cap; bounce-volume +8 to match.)
- **DT2 #17 Optoproductions Resample-the-Master Mangle Loop** — alt path: record Big Time's output (`INPUT = MAIN INPUT`) → Grid-slice → Comb → bit-crush → resample again. ⚠️ disable `TO MAIN` while resampling re-amped audio or it feeds back.
- **MPC #13 Resample to Bake FX** + **#14 Bake-the-Grit (SP1200)** — capture Big Time off the rear inputs → Chop→Transients → bake vintage-emulator/LoFi via Resample (⚠️ silent first try — do it twice). DJ-Shadow logic: a Big Time sample bank nobody else has.

## Routing


**OP-1 needs the EHX Effects Interface** (its line out goes farty/muddy straight into instrument-level gear) — route OP-1 → Effects Interface → Big Time. DT2/MPC put out healthy line level → feed straight in; set Big Time **COLOR low** for line sources (already hot) and use **DRY KILL** so Big Time returns wet-only into the aux path. On the return pass keep one clock master (whoever's driving the song).

## Sound


A frozen Big Time wall, sampled and crushed, played back as a chromatic/poly choir, then re-delayed by the same pedal — degradation stacked until it sounds captured on the wrong machine.

**Taste-ref:** lo-fi / prolific (Car Seat Headrest cassette-degrade) crossed with art-rock studio-as-instrument (the looped-and-layered build); banjo-as-lead can play the resampled choir.

## Play


FREEZE a Big Time bed → sample it on the OP-1/DT2/MPC → mangle → drop the sampler line back through Big Time. One delay, the whole song's glue.

content:
Stripped Guitar Board
Artists: Peter Gabriel, Prince, The Police, mk.gee
Instrument: guitar
Gear: TC Electronic Polytune 3, JHS 424, Oxford Drive, Strymon Deco V2, Boss BF-3, Eventide H90, Strymon Iridium

Same artist DNA — Gabriel, Prince, Police, mk.gee — in a leaner rig. No Big Time, Clean, or MOOD. The Deco V2 and H90 do the heavy lifting: Deco covers tape chorus and slapback, H90 runs dual delay + reverb engines simultaneously.

## Signal Path


### 1. TC Electronic Polytune 3
Tuner + buffer.

### 2. JHS 424
The pedal version of mk.gee's Tascam 424 preamp trick. Simpler than the PORTA424 — one knob of lo-fi tape-style gain. Push it for committed grit up front.

### 3. Oxford Drive
British Marshall-voiced distortion. Covers Prince's dirtier rhythm crunch and Gabriel-era Peter Hammill-style aggression. The ShredMaster lineage gives it a focused midrange that cuts without fizz — roll the gain back for funky edge, push it for leads.

### 4. Strymon Deco V2
The Swiss army knife of this board. [Tape saturation side](guide:Strymon%20Deco%20V2/tape-saturation) adds warm compression (replaces Clean's role). [Doubletracker side](guide:Strymon%20Deco%20V2/doubletracker) does:
- **Chorus**: Wide, through-zero flanging — covers The Police territory alongside BF-3
- **Slapback**: Short tape echo for Prince rockabilly-funk moments
- **Flange**: Deep tape-flange sweeps
Stereo output from here forward.

### 5. Boss BF-3
Dedicated flanger for Andy Summers textures that Deco can't cover simultaneously. [Ultra mode](guide:Boss%20BF-3/ultra-mode) for dramatic jet sweeps, [Standard mode](guide:Boss%20BF-3/standard-mode) for subtle movement. Gate/Pan mode does rhythmic stereo effects — useful for Gabriel-style production tricks.

### 6. Eventide H90
Dual engines replace Big Time + reverb duties. Run [delay in Preset A + reverb in Preset B](guide:Eventide%20H90/dual-preset-routing) simultaneously:
- **Delay**: TimeFactor algorithms for 80s rack delay (Gabriel/Police era). TapeEcho for warm repeats, ModDelay for chorus-on-repeats.
- **Reverb**: Blackhole for massive Gabriel pads, [Plate](guide:Eventide%20H90/plate-reverb) for tighter Prince-style room. MangledVerb adds distorted reverb textures (mk.gee territory).
The H90's routing flexibility (series, parallel, dual) means you can run delay-into-reverb or keep them independent per song.

### 7. Strymon Iridium
Same role as Rig A — amp sim at the end. Round for clean, Chime for jangle.

## Routing Notes


- Mono through JHS 424 → Oxford Drive, then stereo from Deco V2 onward
- H90 is center-positive 12V power — do NOT daisy-chain, use its included adapter
- H90 + Deco V2 both have MIDI — two pedals, full preset recall
- Fewer pedals = simpler power, smaller board

## The Vibe


- **Prince funk**: JHS 424 light, Oxford Drive low gain, Deco slapback, H90 tight plate
- **Police shimmer**: Deco chorus + BF-3 flange stacked, H90 ModDelay
- **Gabriel pads**: Deco saturation warm, H90 Blackhole + long delay, expression pedal on decay
- **mk.gee raw**: JHS 424 pushed hard, Oxford Drive stacked, H90 MangledVerb

Twin-Fantasy Bedroom Beat Wall
Artists: Car Seat Headrest
Instrument: banjo/VG-800 + MPC drums
Gear: Akai MPC Sample, Chase Bliss Clean, JHS Colour Box V2, Oxford Drive, Strymon Deco V2, Chase Bliss Generation Loss, Chase Bliss Big Time, MXNHLT PORTA424, JHS 424, UA Apollo x8

The "the demo IS the song" dense bedroom wall — an MPC-driven crunchy-dry beat under a banjo/VG-800 part, layered "as big as possible," every wart left audible, double-cassette-printed. A 🟣 DOUG-designed integration; Toledo used a laptop DAW + bundled mic, not pedals — this chases the *result*, not the signal path.

## Signal path


- **Drum/loop backbone:** MPC Sample → Apollo bus (its own degrade baked in) → summed into the End-board print.
- **Melodic part:** banjo/VG-800 → CB Clean (always-on) → JHS Colour Box V2 → Oxford Drive (relocated front) → Strymon Deco V2 → [End board] CB Generation Loss → CB Big Time → PORTA424 → JHS 424 → tape (PORTA424/424 print).

## Per-unit


- **MPC Sample** — runs **#14 Bake-the-Grit Resample (SP1200/MPC60 Authentic Crush)** on the breaks (pitch up +6 → Vintage Emulator SP1200 → Resample → tune back −6) + **#15 LoFi (Bitcrush + Decimate)** latched with **#16 Color (Cassette)** on a couple of hits (DIBIA$E's latch); finger-drummed with **#28 Dilla Feel (Quantize-Off micro-timing)** so it never machine-guns.
- **CB Clean** — **#1 Home Base (Safe Space)**, the always-on leveler; bump to **#5 Banjo Transient Tamer** when the banjo carries the part so plucks behave like guitar before the dirt.
- **JHS Colour Box V2** — **#15 Crunchy-Dry Direct-In (CBX-LF1)** — "boost a quiet source until it clips" = Toledo's recorded-quiet-then-boosted crunch. HI · STEP 3 · PRE-VOL 1:00 · MASTER set LAST. Keep it DRY downstream.
- **Oxford Drive** — **#OXF-LF1 Crunchy-Dry Demo Crunch (DS-2 character)** ('91 / Si / Gain 11–12:00 / Bass 8:00 / Contour 9:00 / Treble 1:00). **Relocate ahead of the fuzzes** (or guitar/banjo-only into the End board) so its fixed-mid filter isn't collapsed by the wall.
- **Strymon Deco V2** — **#16 Cassette Demo Fatten + Wobble (DEC-LF2)** — Voice cassette, bounce doubler, to layer the part "as big as possible" before the ruin.
- **CB Generation Loss** — **#29 Laptop-Bounce Cassette Demo (GL-LF1)** (Model 7 Dictatron-EX, Wow/Flutter 9:00, Saturate 11:00, Failure 9:00 with DROP BYP on, Dry Small). Keep hidden Hiss low + HUM BYP so it doesn't stack a 2nd noise floor into the print.
- **CB Big Time** — **#1 Crushed Analog (Factory #7)** — murky/saturated vintage echo right after Gen Loss; COLOR modest (the source is already degraded), 0.5X ON for the 12-bit crush.
- **PORTA424** — **#12 Bedroom 4-Track Demo Print (P424-LF1)** (Trim 12–1:00 the breakup gate, Treble 10:00, 9V trashier).
- **JHS 424** — **#13 Demo-Is-The-Song 4-Track Grit (424-LF1)** (Gain 1 12:00, Gain 2 12:00 — **well under the 3:00 gate**), XLR → Apollo, mono-commit.

## Routing / sync


**MPC = MIDI clock MASTER** (mandatory — MIDI-slave distortion on fw1.2.1; MPC master also keeps Big Time from distorting when slaved). Big Time follows via **CC111=0**; subdivision via **CC54**. Mono melodic path → Big Time IN-L auto-engages **MISO** (mono-in/stereo-out). H90 not in this chain; the stereo End bus mono-sums into PORTA424's mono input, then JHS 424 mono-commits to the Apollo. **Pick one tape box to destroy** — here PORTA424 carries the demo grit (9V), JHS 424 stays light (just level + XLR). Gain-staging: Colour Box MASTER set last (biggest jump); Deco is a gain device (level-match on engage).

## Sound


A dense, dry, mid-forward bedroom wall — crunchy direct-in part doubled and fattened, drums crushed to 12-bit SP1200 grit, the whole thing bounced through two cassette stages so chords smear and single notes bloom. Warts as identity.

## Play


Lay the MPC beat, hold the banjo/VG part and layer multiple passes (resample on the OT or MPC for the "as big as possible" stack). Footswitch the Oxford in for the dirty sections; ride Colour Box PRE-VOL by hand for the recorded-quiet-then-boosted swell into clipping. Leave everything DRY — no long verb.

**Taste-ref:** lo-fi-prolific-volume — Car Seat Headrest, *Twin Fantasy* / "Something Soon" bedroom-DAW degrade ("the demo is the song"). 🟣 chases the result; Toledo used a laptop, not pedals.

Vocal-Halo Banjo
Artists: Bon Iver, Sufjan Stevens
Instrument: banjo (GK-5 → VG-800)
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, Hologram Microcosm, Walrus Audio QI Etherealizer, OBNE Dark Star V3, Hologram Chroma Console, Eventide H90

The modern-folk signature — Bon Iver's Prismizer/Messina **vocal halo** (a pitched harmony cloud around one voice) recreated on the rig as a **banjo-as-lead** with a played diatonic harmony voice, a frozen pitched grain cloud around it, a dual-pitch shimmer pad, all kept **close and dry-forward** (halo, not hall) with intimate iPhone-cassette degrade — never doom fuzz. This is the live-rig **approximation** of the halo; the genuine article is the in-the-box Antares Harmony Engine (PRZ-TB1, index-only).

This is a **designed integration** — no artist ever used this exact chain. The real method = laptop + 2× Auto-Tune + Eventide H8000 (the Messina) / Antares Harmony Engine / Deering banjo / SM7 / iPhone — none of this rig. The **whole chain chases the RESULT, not the METHOD** (no MIDI-played, formant-shifted, polyphonic halo on the rig). 🟣 designed.

## Signal path


banjo (GK-5 → **VG-800** halo-harmony voice) → **CB Clean** (present, light comp) → *[fuzz wall bypassed]* → **Microcosm** (granular harmony onset-cloud) → **QI Etherealizer** (Prismizer-halo grain freeze) → **Dark Star V3** (dual-pitch shimmer pad, Board-2 terminus, stereo) → Board 3: **Chroma Console** (iPhone-cassette intimate degrade) → **H90** (faint room) → tape.

## Per-unit


- **VG-800** — **#31 Banjo Halo Harmony Drone** (recall GK SETTING #1 EBM5 BANJO · INST = E.GUITAR or VIO · `ALT TUNE MODE = HARMONY`, `HARMONY = +1 oct` or a USER-SCALE diatonic 3rd/5th, KEY set to the tune · `NORMAL MIX ~30%` so the dry banjo stays under). ⚠️ **Approximation:** ONE fixed played interval, not the 4-note MIDI-played formant-shifted cloud — the cloud comes downstream. For the lead voice itself use **#32 Sufjan Fingerpicked Banjo Lead** (5th string excluded).
- **CB Clean** — #2 *Transparent Enhancer* or **#5 Banjo Transient Tamer** (tames the violent banjo attack so notes behave like guitar). Keep the source present/dry-forward — the voice stays close.
- **Microcosm** — **#29 Glacial Halo Bed (Haze)** or **#30 Banjo Fingerpick Onset-Halo** (Strum B / Mosaic A): Filter ~noon (tame the 2–4 kHz), **Mix ~11:00 — modest, halo-not-hall** so the granular pitch-cloud sits *behind* the present banjo. Global Config = Stereo in, Line, Buffered+Trails. ⚠️ a granular pitch-cloud, not played harmony.
- **QI Etherealizer** — **#27 Prismizer Halo Freeze Cloud** (Flow Parallel · Grain Cloud, Playback **x2** = the bright prism-up layer · Chorus Tri, Depth ~11 = the long-glide slur stand-in · Space 10–11:00 modest · Tone ~1:00 to roll the ice-pick · play a chord → **short-press Freeze** = the cloud loops, play the lead over it). ⚠️ **RIG-CRITICAL: pad/reamp the VG-800 line level before the Qi** (no level switch — it clips hot; use the bench EHX Effects Interface). ⚠️ fixed pitched cloud, not MIDI-played 4-note harmony. For the "715 hit-it-harder" distortion, push the source hot into the padded input.
- **Dark Star V3** — **#29 Halo Shimmer Pad (dual-pitch glide)** (Stereo, trails on · Pitch 1 = +1 oct (L) · Pitch 2 = detune just off unity (R), seated with the "a in Dark" off-noon trick · **Crush ~12 clean** (intimate lane, not doom) · Filter HPF glassy so the up-voice floats · Mix mostly wet but UNDER the dry voice). ⚠️ two fixed pitched voices, not the played 4-note halo.
- **Chroma Console** — **#31 iPhone Voice-Memo Cassette Capture** (TEXTURE CASSETTE ~10–11:00 · CHARACTER SWEETEN ~9–10 so the close source still reads present · MOVEMENT VIBRATO + DRIFT ~9 = subtle "wrong machine" warble · MIX ~65–70%). **Pick this OR Gen Loss as "the tape" — don't double it;** Gen Loss stays bypassed/clean for this chain.
- **H90** — a low-Mix **Room/Plate** (Posen "Room" distant-mic role, Mix ~20%) for a faint halo, not a hall. The space is a halo, never a swallow.

## Routing / sync


Banjo mono into Board 1, kept **present/dry-forward** the whole way (CB Clean + the dry path carry the close voice; every texture box sits *behind* it). **Parallel/Mix-modest** on Microcosm, QI, and Dark Star so none takes over — this is the halo-not-hall discipline. **Dark Star Hold passes new notes bone-dry** — fine here: the dry banjo lead sits in front of the frozen halo. Run **Buffered+Trails on Chroma** with both outs connected for the mono→stereo re-expansion. Let ONE box own the big space (here Dark Star + a faint H90) — don't stack three reverbs (mud). No clock needed; this is a played, rubato chain.

## Sound


A close, dry-forward fingerpicked banjo lead haloed by a pitched harmony cloud and a bright shimmer pad, warbled by an iPhone-in-a-hotel-room cassette degrade, with a faint room around it. A choir-of-one-banjo — intimate, recorded-wrong in the *gentle* way, never doom.

## Play


Recall the VG-800 halo-harmony banjo voice; fingerpick rolling arpeggios. Play a chord → **short-press QI Freeze** to capture the pitched cloud → solo the banjo lead over the frozen halo. Use **Dark Star Aux = Hold** (or the live shimmer) for the static pad; lean on the dry path for the lead since Hold passes dry. Keep everything restrained — the voice stays close. For the *genuine* halo, run **Antares Harmony Engine (PRZ-TB1, index-only)** in the DAW on the banjo and let these pedals only approximate it live.

## Taste-ref


Bon Iver — "22 (OVER S∞∞N)" / "715 - CRΣΣKS" Prismizer/Messina vocal halo; Sufjan *Carrie & Lowell* iPhone-intimate close/dry capture; banjo-as-lead.

VocalShift "Singing Wall" Baritone Drone with 61SL-Played Harmony
Artists: Bon Iver, Sufjan Stevens
Instrument: baritone
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, Eventide H90, Chase Bliss MOOD MkII, Hologram Chroma Console, MXNHLT PORTA424, Novation 61SL MkIII

Harmonize a single sustained baritone (or banjo) drone into a wide, scale-locked, multi-voice "singing wall" — and play the harmony intervals *live* from the keyboard while the lead note is held. A drone that becomes a choir, with the player conducting the harmony. ⭐ signature-fit.

This is a 🟣 designed integration of owned-gear patches; no artist ever played *this* chain. The Taste-ref names the sound it chases, and the per-unit patch sheets carry their own provenance.

## Signal path


Baritone JM (GK-5) → **VG-800 (#5 VIO Bowed Swell Drone** or **#7 Doom Baritone Wall** for weight) → Clean (#6 Baritone Drone Sustainer) → [Board 2 thru] → [Board 3] → **H90 (#31 VocalShiftMIDI Live-Harmony Drone, played from the 61SL)** → **MOOD (TB3 / #12 frozen Reverb pad)** → Chroma → PORTA424 → tape. **61SL (#2 VG-800 Audition & Control + #11 clock)** plays the harmony intervals into the H90.

## Per-unit


- VG-800 **#5 VIO Bowed Swell Drone** (attackless sustained source) or **#7 Doom Baritone Wall** (−7 STEP weight); recall GK **#2 BARI JM**. `NORMAL MIX` low so the H90 harmonizer tracks a clean fundamental.
- Clean **#6 Baritone Drone Sustainer** — limiting + slow release for a sustained, even bed for the harmonizer to lock onto; full-range Envelope Balance.
- H90 **#31 VocalShiftMIDI Live-Harmony Drone** — 4 MIDI-played voices over the held baritone; Root learn, Spread Wide, **Hold** so voices sound only while a MIDI note is held; map Glide/Freeze to footswitches for pitch-rise swells and frozen vowel-drones. (Stack into the H90 wet-only "super-algorithm" trick for a thicker singing wall.)
- MOOD **TB3 (frozen Reverb pad)** / **#12 Freeze Pad** — Reverb washed (MODIFY CW), HOLD LEFT to freeze into an infinite pad; slowly turn CLOCK down for the moving/detuning drift under the harmonized voices.
- 61SL **#2 VG-800 Audition & Control** + **#11 clock master** — plays the harmony intervals into the H90 VocalShiftMIDI; SL = clock master so any synced FX follow one tempo.

## Routing


Baritone drone mono front → stereo into Board 3. The **61SL plays MIDI notes into the H90** (VocalShiftMIDI receives MIDI-note intervals) — route the SL's DIN/USB to the H90's MIDI in; the SL is clock master (Tx on; never Tx and Rx clock at once). The H90 harmonizes the live audio drone to the played intervals. Keep the VG-800 `NORMAL MIX` low and the source clean so the harmonizer tracks. ⚠️ This is **not** the VG-800's own ALT-TUNE harmony (that's one fixed interval, VG #30/#31) — here the *played MIDI* sets the chord live, which is the richer move.

## Sound


One held baritone note becomes a wide, scale-locked 3–4-voice stereo chord — a "singing wall" you conduct from the keyboard — over a slowly-detuning frozen MOOD pad. Drone as choir.

Taste-ref: indie-folk-confessional (the vocal-halo / played-harmony cloud, Bon Iver/Sufjan layered harmony) rendered on the baritone/banjo drone instead of a voice. Honest note: the H90 VocalShiftMIDI is a *real* multi-voice formant harmonizer (not an approximation) — but it is harmonizing a *string drone*, not a sung vocal, so the timbre is the rig's, not Bon Iver's.

## Play


Hold one baritone note (bowed in via Clean / VIO slow-gear) → play harmony intervals on the 61SL → the H90 sings them over the drone → freeze the MOOD pad (HOLD LEFT, LATCH) under it → use the H90 Glide/Freeze footswitches for pitch-rise swells or to lock a frozen vowel-drone. For a banjo variant, swap the VG-800 source to the EBM5 banjo lead and let the harmony cloud halo it.

Washed-Out Ambient Guitar
Gear: Chase Bliss MOOD MkII, Hologram Microcosm, OBNE Dark Star V3, Strymon Big Sky

Guitar -> **Chase Bliss MOOD MkII** -> **Hologram Microcosm** -> **OBNE Dark Star V3** -> **Strymon Big Sky**

## Signal Flow Rationale


1. **Chase Bliss MOOD MkII** (granular texture source)
   - Wet channel on Slip mode to smear incoming notes into drifting micro-loops
   - Drolo side on Stretch for time-warped grain clouds
   - Clock slow; Mix mostly wet — strips attack and creates the initial wash

2. **Hologram Microcosm** (granular layering)
   - Mosaic or Haze engine to scatter the already-softened signal into shimmering fragments
   - Activity knob moderate so grains overlap without chaos
   - Adds melodic movement and spectral shimmer on top of the MOOD's smear

3. **OBNE Dark Star V3** (pad reverb + pitch)
   - Pitch knobs to +1 octave / -1 octave for organ-like depth
   - Crush low, Filter slightly rolled off high-end for lo-fi haze
   - Freeze footswitch to capture and sustain a pad underneath live playing

4. **Strymon Big Sky** (final space)
   - Cloud or Shimmer algorithm, Decay long, Mix ~60-70%
   - Pre-delay short to keep things diffuse rather than distinct
   - Acts as the master "room" that glues everything into one enormous wash

## Tips


- Roll your guitar's tone knob down to ~4-5 for extra softness at the source.
- Use volume swells (volume knob or expression pedal) to remove all pick attack.
- MOOD's freeze/loop can hold a bed while you layer new phrases through the rest of the chain.

---

*Sources: gear/Chase Bliss MOOD MkII/GearProfile.md, gear/Hologram Microcosm/GearProfile.md, gear/OBNE Dark Star V3/GearProfile.md, gear/Strymon Big Sky/GearProfile.md*

Westberg Two-Voice Sustaining Wall
Artists: Swans, Norman Westberg
Instrument: baritone (Jazzmaster / banjo via GK-5 → VG-800)
Gear: Roland VG-800, Chase Bliss Clean, MXR M173 Classic 108 Fuzz, EarthQuaker Devices Hizumitas, Chase Bliss Big Time, Eventide H90

Rebuild Norman Westberg's *documented* Swans wall architecture on owned gear — two stacked dirt voices + compression + a volume swell + repetition into a "vast sustaining chordal" wall. This is a designed integration honoring a documented signal-ORDER, not a claim that Westberg played this chain (Swans use no fuzz; the two-fuzz stack manufactures the loud-amp overtone result).

## Signal path


Baritone JM / banjo (GK-5 → VG-800, dark E.GUITAR model) → **CB Clean #6 Baritone Drone Sustainer** (the Dyna-Comp role + the **#12 Dynamic Volume Swell** for the build) → **MXR 108 #13 (108-PP1) Westberg Grinding Bite** → **Hizumitas #13 (HZ-PP1) Swans Sustaining Chordal Wall** → Big Time bypassed/clean → **H90 #6 Blackhole Freeze Drone** (lock-a-wall staff move) → tape.

## Per-unit


- **Clean #6 / #12:** tames the boomy lows full-range and extends decay into a sustained ceiling (Dynamics ~noon limiting, Release Slow, full-range Envelope Balance); the **AUX swell (#12)** is the documented volume-pedal "build" tool.
- **108-PP1 (#13):** OUTPUT 12:00 / **FUZZ 12–1:00 (mid-gain grind, not maxed)** / BUFFER ON — the DS-1 "aggressive grinding" role.
- **Hizumitas HZ-PP1 (#13):** **Volume ~1:00 · Sustain ~2:00 (just shy of max so a chord still reads AS a chord) · Tone ~1:00 (bass side, the "warm guitar/bass hum")**.
- **H90 #6:** Blackhole, **Freeze = Feedback fully clockwise** on a Performance-Parameter footswitch.

## Routing


Mono through Board 1; the swell is the live build gesture. No clock. The **order is the point** — this mirrors Westberg's cited chain (dirt → comp → volume → amp): here 108 grind + Hizumitas wall = the two dirt voices, Clean = the Dyna-Comp + the volume swell.

## Sound


A chord (not a single note) that blooms into a sustaining, choir-like wall — "four church choirs singing at once" rendered as 108-grind + Hizumitas-smooth + Clean-extend + Blackhole-freeze. Taste-ref: Swans "The Seer" / "Bring the Sun" — Westberg's sustaining chordal wall.

## Play


Pick a chord with "potential," engage Clean's AUX swell so it bows in, repeat the chord letting overtones stack, then stomp the H90 Blackhole Freeze to lock it and play over the top.
